cooking_instructions: Soak the black chana for 6-8 hours, preferable overnight.
Strain it and transfer it to a pressure cooker and let it cook for 5 whistles on a medium flame.

Strain the chana, transfer it to a blender, add the remaining ingredients and blend it to a paste-like texture. Transfer it to a bowl, add salt and besan flour and coriander leaves. Mix it well till the ingredients combine evenly and bind together.
Shape it into patties.
Heat a tawa, add little oil and cook the patties gently  to a golden brown colour on both sides. Handle it gently as it will turn soft at this point. Serve it hot with mint chutney.

title: Cookd Ambur Egg Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes.
In another bowl, add 2 eggs and 1 tbsp of the cookd biryani paste and whisk till it combines. In a pan, add 1 tbsp of ghee and scramble it, keep it aside.
Heat water in a pot, add salt and bring it to a boil. Add the eggs and boil them for 10-12 minutes. Transfer it to a bowl of cold water, peel the shell and keep it aside.
Heat a pot, add the cookd ambur biryani paste. Add water, mix well and bring it to a boil. Add the soaked and strained rice and mix it in.

Cook it on a medium flame, stirring it gently ad regular intervals. Once the rice and water are at level, cover the pot tightly and cook it on a low flame for 10 minutes. Turn off the flame and let it rest for 10 more minutes. Open the pot, sprinkle the scrambled eggs on top, add the seasoning oil, and fluff up the rice.

title: Puthur Jayaram Prawn Tawa Fry
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add the onions and saute till it turns translucent.
Add the tomatoes and masala powders and saute till the raw aroma of the masalas is one and the tomatoes are soft and mashy. Keep the onion tomato mixture aside.
Heat up a tawa, add the prawns and cook it dry till all the water it lets out has evaporated.
Push the prawns to the side, add oil and add  ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder and turmeric powder. Mix it till it combines with the oil and mix the prawns along with it for 2 minutes.
Add the onion tomato mixture and mix till it all combines evenly. Add salt, black pepper and coriander leaves and mix till it combines evenly. Serve it hot with rice.

title: Pondy Style Macaroni
cooking_instructions: In a blender jar add the milk, oil garlic, salt and blend into a smooth paste.
In a pan pour in the oil and add the chilli paste, ginger garlic paste, salt and pepper. Saute for 5 minutes or until well cooked and set aside.
In a large pot pour water, add salt and bring it to a boil, add the macaroni and cook according to the package instructions.
In a kadhai pour in some oil, add the eggs and scramble it, and then add garlic and green chilli.
Add the vegetables and saute for 30 seconds add the chilli sauce, soy and green chilli sauce and mix.
Add the macaroni and mix until well combined. Serve the pasta with the garlic mayonnaise and garnish with some spring onions

title: Salli Gosht
cooking_instructions: Peel and cut the potatoes into matchsticks. Fry the matchstick potatoes in oil until golden brown and set aside.

In a pressure cooker oil, add the whole garam masalas and finely chopped onion and saute until the onions almost turn golden brown then add tomato puree and cook for 3 minutes, add all the powdered spices, salt and  mix thoroughly.
Add the mutton once the oil separates from the tomato puree. Cook the mutton on a high flame for 2-3 minutes then add the apricots, vinegar and jaggery.
Add the water and pressure cook for 4 whistles on a medium flame and let the pressure subside before opening. Garnish with the salli potatoes and serve.

title: Cookd Wedding Egg Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes.
In a bowl, add 2 eggs and add 1tbsp of Cookd biryani paste and whisk it till it combines. Add ghee in a pan, add the egg mixture, scramble it and keep it aside.
Heat water in a pot, add salt and bring it to a boil. Add the eggs and boil them for 10-12 minutes. Transfer it to a bowl of cold water, peel the shell and keep it aside.

Heat a pot, add the cookd ambur biryani paste  and saute on a low flame for a few seconds. Add water,  mix well and bring it to a boil. Add the soaked and strained rice and mix it in. Cook it on a medium flame, stirring it gently at regular intervals.

Once the rice and water are at level, cover the pot tightly and cook it on a low flame for 10 minutes. Turn off the flame and let it rest 10 more minutes. Open the pot, add the seasoning oil, sprinkle the scrambled eggs on top and fluff up the rice.

title: Udupi Potato Fry
cooking_instructions: Cut the potato into cubes and cook until they’re fork tender ( around 5 minutes )
Drain the potatoes and pat dry, deep fry until golden brown and set aside.
In a Kadai add oil and let it heat up, add coconut, shallots, garlic, ginger, fennel seeds, pepper, curry leaves and cumin seeds. Saute until the shallots are cooked and the coconut turns golden.
Blend the mixture into a coarse mixture and set it aside.
In the same kadai add oil, green chillies and curry leaves, add back the paste and cook for 30 seconds. Add the deep fried potatoes and give it a good mixture and check for salt and add if necessary.

title: Angamaly Fish Curry
cooking_instructions: Mix together all the ingredients except the raw mango. Rub and mix it well using your fingers.
Add the raw mango and mix gently to combine. Rest for 15 minutes.

For the coconut milk, add the grated coconut to a mixer jar along with ½ cup of water. Grind it until smooth. Strain it to get the thick coconut milk. Add the remaining coconut to 1 cup of water, and grind it again until smooth. Strain it to get the thin coconut milk.
Place the pot on the stove and heat it up. Add the thin coconut milk and bring it to a boil.
Add the fish pieces, cover and cook on low heat for 5 mins.
Add the thick coconut milk, mix and turn off the heat as soon as bubbles start to appear.
In another pan, heat coconut oil and add the small onion, curry leaves and dry red chilli. Saute until the onion starts to brown. Add this to the fish curry, mix and serve with rice.

title: Tandoori Pasta
cooking_instructions: Heat butter in a pan and add the onion and green chilli. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add ginger garlic paste and all the spice powders. Saute for 2 minutes on low heat.
Add the capsicum and saute for 1 minute. Add the maida and saute for 2-3 minutes.
Add the milk gradually while mixing continuously. Add a little bit of the milk, mix and then only add more milk.
Once all the milk is added, add salt and pepper, and mix. Allow it to simmer for 2-3 mins.

Remove it from the stove. Place a metal bowl inside, with a piece of hot charcoal. Pour a few drops of oil on it, cover it immediately and rest for 2 minutes. After that, remove the charcoal. Cover the sauce and set aside.
For cooking the pasta, bring water to a boil and add salt. Add the pasta and cook for 7-8 minutes.
Remove the pasta and add it to the sauce. Heat it up and and mix until evenly combined. Add grated cheese and coriander leaves, and mix. Remove it from the heat.

This next step is optional. Transfer the pasta to a heat-proof bowl. Sprinkle Mozzarella cheese, coriander leaves and red chilli flakes on top. Bake it in a hot oven at 200°c for 7-8 minutes or until the cheese melts and starts turning golden brown. Remove from the oven, serve hot and enjoy!

title: Karaikudi Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins.
Heat a pan, dry roast the spices required for the karaikudi masala and blend it to a fine powder.
Heat a pot, add oil and ghee. Add cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, cumin and fennel. Let it crackle.
Add the shallots and saute till it turns golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste, coriander leaves, mint leaves and green chilli and saute for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and mix well till the tomatoes become soft.
Add the chicken and mix well. Add the prepared masala and cook it along with the chicken on a medium flame for about 2 minutes.
Add a cup of water, mix well and bring it to a boil. Cover and cook the chicken for 10 minutes.
Add the rice and mix well for a few seconds. Add salt and mix it well. Add 800 ml of water and mix well and bring it to a boil.
Stir it gently till the rice and water are almost at the same level. Add extra water if necessary and add lemon juice.

Cover the pot with foil and seal it tightly with a fitting lid. Keep it on a preheated tawa for dum for 5 minutes on a medium flame and 5 minutes on a low flame. Open the pot, fluff the rice and let it rest for 5 minutes. Serve it hot with raita.

title: Poached Egg Curry
cooking_instructions: For the gravy, heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds, fennel seeds, cardamom, curry leaves, ginger, garlic, green chilli and curry leaves. Saute for 30 seconds.
Add onion and salt. Saute until it turns golden brown.
Turn the flame to low. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, Kashmiri chilli powder, black pepper powder and garam masala powder. Saute for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4-5 minutes on medium heat, until the tomatoes soften. Break the tomatoes using the spoon/spatula.
Add sugar and water, cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Heat water in a pot just until it starts bubbling. Then reduce the flame to low and add the salt and vinegar.
Crack each egg into a bowl. Then add it slowly to the water. Wait for around 10-15 seconds before adding the next egg. Allow it to cook for 3 minutes.
Remove it from the water and add it into the gravy. Cover the lid and turn off the heat. Rest for 3-4 minutes before serving. Open the lid and serve with Idiyappam, chapathi, appam or parotta.

title: Pudhina Chicken
cooking_instructions: Prepare a thick batter with the required ingredients and whisk it till there are no lumps.
Add the chicken cubes to it and mix it till it is coated evenly with the batter.
Heat oil in a kadai. Deep fry the chicken to a golden brown colour and till it is cooked thoroughly. Keep it aside.
Add coriander, mint and green chillies, shallots to a blender. Blend it to a fine paste.
Heat a pan, add oil, add curry leaves, green chilli and chopped onions. Saute on a high flame till the onions turn translucent.
Add the green paste and mix well for about a minute. Add water, mix well and bring it to a boil.
Add salt, red chilli powder and bring it to a boil.
Add the fried chicken and mix it well till it is coated with the masala.
Add the quartered boiled egg and mix well.
Add a mixture of chopped mint and coriander leaves. Serve it hot.

title: Vendakkai Peanut Fry
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the peanuts. Fry on low flame for 3-4 minutes or until it becomes golden brown and crispy. Remove it from the pan and set aside.
In the same oil, add urad dal, chana dal, dry red chilli, garlic and curry leaves. Then add the lady’s fingers and mix.
Add salt and lemon juice, and cook for 5 minutes on high heat. Don’t cover the pan with a lid.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder and cumin powder. Saute for 5 more minutes on medium heat.
Add the fried peanuts and red chilli powder. Cook for 2 more minutes, then remove from the heat and serve with any rice dish.

title: Channa Tikka Masala (Vegan)
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the chickpeas for 6-8 hours (preferable overnight) and strain it. To a pressure cooker, add the chickpeas, water and salt. Pressure cook the chickpeas for 6 whistles and take it off the flame. Let the pressure reduce gradually.
In another pan, add oil, heat it up. Add ginger, garlic and onions. Saute till the onions turn light brown.
Add the tomato puree and masala powders. Mix well. Add water, mix well and bring it to a boil and lower the flame. Cover and cook the tomato puree for 5 minutes.
Add the boiled Chickpeas, mix well. Season the mixture.
Finally add coconut milk and coriander leaves. Mix well. Take it off the flame. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve it hot with rice.

title: Dahi Ke Sholay
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl add the hung curd, onion, ginger, green chilli, and all the masalas. Mix the curd thoroughly and set aside
Cut the edges of the sandwich bread and roll it into a thin sheet.
Apply some water to the bread and add the filling inside. Roll the bread into a cylinder and crimp both the edges.
Fry the bread until golden brown.

title: Jain Paneer Masala
cooking_instructions: In a pan, heat oil and add all the ingredients for the paste. Cover and cook on medium heat for 5 minutes or until the tomatoes have softened fully. Keep stirring at intervals.
Allow the mixture to cool, then grind into a smooth paste.
Heat ghee in another pan and add the capsicum. Saute on high heat for 1 minute. Remove from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan on low heat, add cumin, asafoetida and red chilli powder. Allow it to cook for a few seconds, then add the prepared tomato paste.
Stir well and cook for 5 minutes. Then add water to adjust the consistency, then cover and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add the paneer cubes, sauteed capsicum, garam masala powder and Kasuri methi. Cook for 2 more minutes and then serve!

title: Jaffna Chicken Fry
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the chicken, salt, black pepper powder, and turmeric powder and mix well. Then add lemon juice to it and mix it well again. In a pan pour oil and add the chicken and cook it until it’s 3/4th done, and set aside
In the same pan add fennel seeds, curry leaves,  thinly sliced shallots, green chilli, garlic and ginger
Cook until it turns aromatic and add the powdered spices, add water, curd and cook until the mixture is well cooked.
Add the cooked chicken and coconut milk, cook for two minutes and serve hot

title: Buffalo Chicken Strips
cooking_instructions: Cut the chicken breast into strips and set aside
In a mixing bowl add the Maida, the spices and ginger garlic paste pour in the water and whisk into a smooth batter
Dip the strips into the batter and dust it in the corn flour and deep fry until light golden brown and crispy
In a pan add the butter and let it melt, once melted add the chilli paste and saute.
After 30 seconds add the ginger garlic paste and cook until the raw smell subsides.Add red chilli sauce, soy sauce salt and pepper and cook for a minute
Add the milk and turn off the flame and set aside
Add the sauce to the chicken and toss until well combined and serve

title: Goan Prawn Curry
cooking_instructions: Grind all the ingredients for the paste. Add water gradually, as needed, to form a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pot and add the onion and green chilli. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add tomato, turmeric powder and salt. Saute for 3-4 minutes until the tomato softens.
Add the prepared masala and saute for 3-4 minutes, then add water and mix. Then cover with a lid, reduce the flame to medium-low and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add water and sugar, and bring it to a boil. Add the prawns and cook for 3-4 minutes, depending on the size of the prawns.
Optionally, you can add some coconut milk right before turning off the heat. Stir, remove from the stove and serve with steamed rice.

title: Chocolate Drops
cooking_instructions: Heat water in a pan, bring it to a boil. Place a bowl over the pan, add the chopped chocolate and let it melt completely into a smooth mixture
Line a tray with parchment paper. Spoon the chocolate onto the tray to make it look like discs. Top it off with chopped nuts and sprinkles.
Refrigerate it or freeze it for 10-15 minutes. Wrap it in foil or any wrapper of your choice and enjoy.

title: Vegan Fish Fry
cooking_instructions: Peel the raw banana and cut it into thick slices.
Mix all the ingredients for the marination together. Add water as needed to form a smooth and thick paste. Coat the raw banana in the marination.
Combine the rava with salt in a plate/bowl. Coat the raw banana slices in the rava.
Shallow fry in oil until cooked and crisp on both sides, a total of 6-8 minutes. Serve as a starter or as a side with rice.

title: Orange Jujubes
cooking_instructions:
In a small bowl pour the orange juice and add the gelatine, let it bloom for 10-15 minutes
In a pan add the sugar and water and heat until the sugar is completely dissolved. Add the honey along with the orange peel and cook until it reaches soft ball stage. Strain the mixture and add back to the pan 
Add the orange juice and gelatine mixture and cook for a minute and transfer into greased moulds and set for 3 hours. Once set coat in sugar and serve

title: Creamy Paneer Rice Bowl
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak basmati rice for 20 minutes. Boil the rice until it’s 90 done and let it completely cool.
In a pan add oil, shallow fry the paneer until golden brown.
In a pan add oil, garlic, onion, the mixed herbs and bell peppers, saute until aromatic.
Add cream, milk and mix well.
Add the fried paneer, cheese and season it with salt and black pepper powder.
In a pan add ghee and garlic and saute until aromatic. Add the cooled rice and toss along with some salt and pepper. Add the finely chopped herbs and switch off the flame and toss

title: Eggless Chocolate Brownies
cooking_instructions: Heat water in a pan, bring it to a boil and lower the flame. Place a bowl on top of the pan. (double boiler). Add the chopped chocolate and butter. Mix it till they melt completely into a smooth mixture.
Add condensed milk and sugar. Mix till the sugar dissolves. Take the bowl off the boiler, and let the mixture cool down a little bit.
Sieve in the maida, salt, baking powder and fold in the mixture till all the ingredients combine evenly.
Add milk and mix till it combines with the rest of the mixture and turns into a smooth, thick batter.

Grease a baking pan with butter and line it with parchment paper. Transfer the batter to the baking pan. Tap the pan on the table to clear out the air pockets in the batter. Bake it in a preheated oven at 180 degrees for 30 minutes.

Take it out of the oven and let it cook down for 30 minutes to an hour. It is at this point when the gooey texture inside the brownie and glossy texture on top forms. After 30-40 minutes, cut and serve it warm. Let it cool for longer if you’d like to have it cold.

title: Pink Oats Dosa
cooking_instructions:
Dry roast the oats on low heat until aromatic and crisp. Add it to a mixer jar along with rava and grind it into a powder. Remove it into a bowl.
Add beetroot, green chilli, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander leaves and water to grind. Add it to the oats powder and mix. Add salt & water as needed to get the required consistency. 
To cook, heat a tawa. Pour a ladle of the batter and spread it gently in a circular motion. Pour oil around the edges, cover and cook until it crisps up and starts to turn golden brown slightly. Remove and serve with chutney.

title: Fish Coconut Milk Curry
cooking_instructions: Peel and cut the raw mango.
Heat coconut oil in a pot and add fenugreek seeds. Then add ginger, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves and onion. Saute until the onion turns translucent, around 3 mins.
Add tomato and salt. Saute for 2-3 minutes.

Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder and coriander powder. Saute for a minute and then add water. Bring it to a boil, then simmer for 3-4 mins. Add the raw mango pieces and coconut milk. Mix well and allow it to come to a boil.
Then add the fish pieces, cover and cook for 5 minutes. Add coconut oil and curry leaves, cover with a lid, and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving with rice, appam or parotta.

title: Cookd Dindigul Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak rice for 20 minutes.
In a pressure cooker add the cookd dindigul biryani paste and the chicken. Saute for 30 seconds and pour water and bring it to a boil.

Add the soaked rice to the pressure cooker. Close the cooker and cook for 2 whistles on a medium flame. Let the biryani rest for 10 minutes. Open the pressure cooker, add the seasoning oil, fluff up the rice and serve it hot with raita.

title: Veg Jaipuri
cooking_instructions: Grind the cashew and tomato into a fine paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add the carrot and beans. Saute for 2 minutes. Add the cabbage, capsicum, onion and green chilli. Add salt and saute for 2 more minutes. Remove it from the pan and set aside.
Heat ghee in the same pan. Add cumin seeds, dry red chilli and garlic. Saute for around 30 seconds. Add green chilli, ginger and onion. Saute until the onion turns golden brown.
Add the tomato & cashew puree and mix to combine. Add salt, turmeric powder, coriander powder, Kashmiri chilli powder and cumin powder. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add curd, mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the grated paneer, cooked vegetables, garam masala powder, coriander leaves and butter. Mix and cook for 2 minutes.
Crush a roasted papad, mix and turn off the heat. Serve it garnished with some grated paneer and crushed roasted papad.

title: Black Pepper Tofu
cooking_instructions: Add corn flour, oil, honey, salt and pepper along with some water and whisk into a thick batter. Add cubed tofu and mix thoroughly
Fry the tofu until golden brown and set aside.
In a kadhai or wok add finely chopped garlic, ginger and spring onion whites .
Add cubed bell peppers, onions and saute for 30 seconds, add maple syrup, honey and soy sauce.
Cook for 30 seconds and pour in some water and the cornflour slurry make sure it’s a thick sauce. Add the fried tofu and saute. Garnish with chopped spring onion greens and serve.

title: Bang Bang Paneer
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl add cornflour, soy sauce, milk and whisk into a smooth batter. Add paneer cubes and mix thoroughly making sure the paneer doesn’t break. Let it marinate for 20 minutes.

In the meantime, take a pan pour oil and add garlic and spring onion whites while the oil is cold and cook until they are golden brown. Once golden brown switch off the flame and add chilli flakes and Kashmiri chilli powder and set aside.
Now crumb the marinated paneer cubes and deep fry until golden brown.
In a bowl add mayonnaise, honey, soy sauce, onion powder, kashmiri chilli powder and the prepared chilli oil whisk until well combined and garnish with spring onion greens and coriander. Serve hot!!

title: Pepper Chicken Peratal
cooking_instructions: Dry roast Pepper, Fennel Seeds and Cumin Seeds until aromatic and grind into a powder.
In a Kadai add coconut oil, curry leaves, green chilli, shallots and onions, cook until the onions turn translucent.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook until the raw smell goes away.
Add Chicken, turmeric powder and salt. Add the water and cook for 10 minutes.
Once the chicken is cooked add the ground masala and garam masala and cook for 2 more minutes. Turn off the flame and add the coriander leaves.

title: Arroz Verde (Mexican Green Rice)
cooking_instructions: In a mixer jar add onion, jalapeno, green chillies, garlic and coriander leaves and blend it into a smooth paste.
In a pan pour oil, add the rice and saute until it turns golden then add cumin seeds, oregano and thyme, saute until it turns aromatic (around 30 seconds).
Add the blended paste and saute gently without breaking the grains of rice for 2 minutes.
Add the sweet corn, green peas, salt and mix it well. Pour the stock/ water and increase the flame to high once it comes to a boil reduce the flame to sim and cook for 5-7 minutes covered.
Once the rice is cooked add the lemon juice and switch off the flame. Gently fluff up the rice and serve it hot.

title: Tandoori Chicken Burger
cooking_instructions: For the marination, add all the spice powders to a bowl. Heat up some mustard oil and pour it too.
Mix it and then add ginger garlic paste, lemon juice and curd. Mix well until smooth and evenly combined.
Add the chicken pieces and then mix with the marination.

Place a metal bowl in the centre with a piece of hot charcoal. You can heat it by placing it directly on the gas stove and heating it for around 10 minutes or until it turns white around the edges. Pour oil on the coal, then cover and rest for 5 minutes. Then remove the coal.

To cook the chicken, heat a grill pan/any flat pan and brush it with oil. Place the chicken pieces without crowding the pan too much. Cook for 5 minutes on high heat, flipping it occasionally and brushing with oil. Then reduce the heat to medium and cook for 5 more minutes, flipping occasionally. Remove the chicken from the pan.
For the masala onion rings, mix together the onion rings with chilli powder, chaat masala and lemon juice.
For the chutney, grind together all the ingredients except the curd. Add it to a bowl, add the curd and whisk together until smooth.
To assemble the burger, place the lettuce, chicken pieces, onion rings and mint chutney inside a bun (toasted with ghee). Close and serve.

title: Rava Fried Mushroom
cooking_instructions: For the marination, mix together all the ingredients to combine. Add water as needed to make a smooth paste.
Gently remove the stems from the tops of the mushrooms. We only need the tops for this recipe. Mix to coat it evenly.
In another bowl, add rava and salt. Coat the mushrooms in the rava one by one. Deep fry it in oil on high heat until it forms a crust and turns crispy on the outside, around 2-3 minutes.

title: Lamb Masaaman Curry
cooking_instructions: For the massaman paste, add all the spices to a pan. Dry roast the other spices till it is aromatic and transfer it to a blender. Add a little water and blend it to a thick, coarse paste and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add chopped garlic and saute for a few seconds. Add the onions and saute them for a minute.
Add the potatoes and lamb strips and saute on a medium flame for 10 minutes on a medium flame.
Add the curry paste and mix it till it coats the other ingredients evenly.
Add water, mix it well and bring it to a boil. Cover and cook the mixture for 15 minutes.
Add coconut milk, bring it to a soft boil and simmer the mixture till it starts to become thick. Transfer it to a bowl, garnish it with coriander sprigs and serve it hot with rice.

title: Laccha Pyaz Paratha
cooking_instructions: In a  mixing vessel add atta, kasuri methi, coriander leaves, salt and chilli flakes. Add ghee and water, knead into a smooth chapati dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
In a mixing bowl add sliced onions, green chillies, coriander, cumin powder, chopped coriander leaves and salt, mix and let it set.

Once the dough is rested, portion it into dough balls and roll it into a thin chapati, spread some ghee and add the onion mixture onto the dough and fold it into an accordion and roll it to a paratha.
Add it to a piping hot tawa and cook until the insides are cooked and the crust is crispy. Serve it with your favourite gravy.

title: Sweet Corn Vadai
cooking_instructions: In a blender add the sweet corn and blend into a coarse paste. Transfer the corn into a mixing bowl and add the remaining ingredients. Mix until it’s thoroughly combined splash water it make it into a dough. Shape it into small discs.
Fry the vada until golden brown and serve.

title: Green Fish Fry
cooking_instructions: For this recipe, you can use either whole fish (such as Tilapia, White Pomfret, Pearl Spot, Mackerel) or fish slices (such as Seer fish, Barracuda, Salmon). If using whole fish, make slits on the fish before marinating. Marinate the fish using salt and turmeric powder first. Set aside until you prepare the green marination.
Grind together the ingredients under ‘to grind’ (coriander leaves, mint leaves, green chilli, ginger, garlic and lemon juice) into a smooth paste.
Add it into a bowl, and mix in black pepper powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, salt and cornflour. Add it to the fish and coat it evenly. Refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.

Heat oil in a pan. Over medium heat, add the fish and cook for around 4 minutes on each side (this time will vary depending on size). If it is getting dark too quickly, reduce the heat. Once fried, remove it from the pan. Squeeze some lemon juice and sprinkle some chaat masala on the fish.

title: Instant Upma Mix
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, crackle the mustard seeds. Add the cumin seeds, asafeotida, curry leaves and green chillies. Saute for a few seconds. Add the dals and fry. Add the cashew nuts and fry until golden brown.
Add the rava and reduce the flame to a simmer. Saute until lightly browned and aromatic, about 10 mins. Cool completely and store in an airtight container, in the fridge.

To cook: use ¼ Cup of the mix with 1 Cup of water. Bring to a boil and simmer until thick while stirring continuously, about 2-3 mins. Switch off the flame and keep covered for 5 mins. Add ghee and serve.

title: Cookd Dindigul Mushroom & Soya Chunks Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak rice for 20 minutes.
In a pressure cooker add the cookd dindigul biryani paste and the mushrooms and soya chunks.
Saute for 30 seconds and pour water, let it come to a boil. Add the soaked rice to the pressure cooker.
Close the cooker and cook for 2 whistles on a medium flame. Open the pressure cooker, add the seasoning oil, fluff up the rice and serve it hot.

title: Cookd Dindigul Egg Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak rice for 20 minutes.
Boil 3 eggs and set aside.
In a saute pan add 1 tablespoon of cookd dindigul biryani paste and break 2 eggs. Scramble the eggs and set aside.

In a pot add the cookd dindigul biryani paste and pour water and bring it to a boil. Add the soaked and strained rice. Cover and cook for 12 minutes on a low flame. Open the pot, add the seasoning oil, add the scrambled eggs to the biryani and mix gently. Serve with boiled egg.

title: Cookd Dindigul Mutton Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak rice for 20 minutes.
To  a pressure cooker add the cookd dindigul biryani paste and mutton curry cut and mix for a 30 seconds. Add 1 Cup (250ml) of water. Mix it and let the water start to heat up. Close the cooker and pressure cook the mutton on a medium flame for 7 whistles. Turn off the flame and let the steam reduce gradually. Open the cooker and check if the mutton is cooked. If it isn't, close the cooker and cook it for 2 more whistles if necessary and let the steam reduce gradually
Open the cooker, and ½ Cup (125ml) of water. Add the soaked and strained rice, give it a gentle mix. Cover the cooker and pressure cook it for 2 whistles on a medium flame. Turn off the flame after 2 whistles and let the steam reduce gradually for about 10 minutes. Open the cooker, add the seasoning oil, fluff the rice and serve it hot with raita.

title: Angara Paneer
cooking_instructions: Dry roast the ingredients required to make the angara masala till it is aromatic and blend it to a fine powder.

Heat a pan, add onion and saute till it turns golden brown. Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a few seconds. Add the tomatoes and cook till it turns soft. Add the kashmiri chilli powder and cook on a medium flame for a minute.
Transfer the mixture to a blender, add little water and blend it to a fine paste.

Transfer the mixture to a pan and start cooking it on a medium flame, mixing it regularly. Add water and the ground masala and mix well and bring the gravy to a soft boil. Add the kasuri methi, fried onions and paneer and mix gently till the ingredients combine evenly.
Add salt, ghee and cream, bring the mixture to a simmer. Let the mixture simmer for 10 minutes.
Place a piece of hot coal in a bowl and place it on the gravy. Add a tbsp of ghee, cover it immediately. Let it smoke for 5 minutes. Transfer it to a bowl. Serve it hot.

title: Chicken Fricassee
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken with Salt and Pepper. Heat oil in a pan. Add the marinated Chicken and sear on a high flame it to a golden brown colour on both sides. Take it out of the pan, keep it aside.
In the same pan, melt butter. Add garlic and thyme, saute it for a few seconds. Add the chopped carrot onions and leeks and cook till they shrink.
Add the mushrooms, saute till it cooks completely.

Add the maida, mix it till it turns like roux and cook it till the raw flavour is gone. Add water, mix it till the roux dissolves and bring it to a boil. Cook it till the liquid thickens. Season the sauce. Add the chicken and let it cook in the sauce for 5 minutes.
Add fresh cream to the sauce. Cook it for another minute. Turn off the flame, transfer the dish to a bowl, garnish it with chopped parsley and fresh cream. Serve it hot with Herbed rice or bread.

title: Paneer Ghee Roast Paratha
cooking_instructions: Prepare a soft dough with atta, salt, water and oil. Knead it well. Divide it into equal sized pieces. Shape it and keep it aside, covered.

To prepare the paneer masala, heat a pan, add 1 packet of the mangalore ghee roast and ¼ Cup of water. Bring the gravy to a boil. Add crumbled paneer and mix well. Cook the mixture till it is almost dry and take it off the flame.

Dust some flour on a flat surface. Flatten a dough ball with your palm and add a spoon of filling in the middle. Cover and seal it from end to end. Dust more flour on the dough and roll out the stuffed pedas gently.
Heat a tawa, cook the parathas on a medium flame. Add oil or ghee based on preference while cooking it. Serve it hot with curd or more ghee roast.

title: Caramel Payasam
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins. Add the rice to a mixer grinder and pulse blend into smaller bits (optionally).
In a pan, caramelize the sugar until golden brown/ amber in colour. Add the milk and melt the caramel on a low flame, set aside.
In a large cooker, heat ghee and fry the nuts until golden brown and raisins until puffed and golden.
Add the milk and the rice. Add the cardamom powder and vanilla essence. Pressure cook for 2 whistles and allow the steam to release naturally. Serve warm/cold garnished with nuts/ saffron.

title: Senai Kizhangu Varuval
cooking_instructions: To a pan, add water, salt and turmeric powder. Bring it to a boil. Add the diced senai kizhangu and boil for 4 minutes and strain it immediately.
Heat oil in a kadai and deep fry the senai kizhangu till it becomes golden brown and crispy.
Heat a pan, add oil. Add mustard, fennel, green chillies and curry leaves. Let them crackle.
Add the chopped onions and saute till it turns light brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a few seconds. Add the tomatoes and masalas and mix till the tomatoes turn soft.
Add a little water and mix well. Add the fried senai kizhangu and mix well.

Add the coconut paste, salt and garam masala. mix well. Keep mixing till it becomes a dry and crispy mixture. Keep scraping the residue off the bottom of the pan. Finish with chopped coriander leaves and turn off the flame. Serve it hot along with rice.

title: Street Style Gobi Manchurian
cooking_instructions: Wash cabbage and cauliflower in water. Strain it, drain the water off it and transfer it to a bowl. Add the rest of the ingredients. Add water and mix it well till the cauliflower is coated evenly.
Heat oil in a kadai. Deep fry the cauliflower mixture in chunks till it becomes slightly crispy. Take it off the oil and keep it on a plate with tissue paper to let the oil drain off.
Heat a pan with oil. Add garlic, saute it for a few seconds.
Add water and add the 3 sauces and mix it till it all combines evenly. Add the spices and seasonings.
Add the fried chunks to it, toss it till it is evenly coated. Transfer it to a bowl/plate. Garnish it with chopped onions and coriander leaves. Serve it.

title: Chicken Donne Biryani (Naati style)
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins.
Combine the mint, coriander, green chillies to make the fine green paste.
Heat ghee in a pot, add the whole spices and fry until aromatic. Add the onions and fry until golden brown.
Add the ginger, garlic paste and cook until the raw aroma goes. Add the green paste and cook for about 3 mins. Add the powdered spices and the salt. Cook for a minute.

Add the chicken and cook for 5 mins, until it releases water. Add the water and bring to a boil. Add the rice and simmer until the rice and water reach the same level. Add extra chopped mint and coriander leaves.

Use a banana leaf to sit on the top and then place a fitting lid with some weight, and dum cook for 12-15 mins on a preheated tava/ low flame. Allow it to rest further for 10 mins. Open the pot and gently break the dum. Add some extra ghee on top and serve hot with raita in a donne.

title: Bamboo Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 20 mins.
In a deep pot, add chicken and the rest of the ingredients required for the marination. Mix it all together till they combine evenly. Let it marinate for 1 hour in the same pot.
Keep the pot with the Chicken on the stove and cook it for 10 minutes adding a cup of water.

In another pan, bring water to boil. Add the whole spices, ghee, salt and bring it to a boil. Add the basmati rice and let it cook till it is 70% done (4 minutes). Strain the rice immediately. Reserve some of the water for later.

Wash the bamboo thoroughly. In a bamboo, layer the rice and chicken mixture alternatively and finally top it off with the fried onion, ghee, saffron milk, coriander and mint leaves and kewra water. Add a piece of folded banana leaf on top and press it down slightly. Cover the bamboo with silver foil, and a dough made with maida and water. seal the edges.

In a pressure cooker, add water and bring it to  a boil. Close the cooker and let it start steaming. Don’t put the whistle on top. Place the bamboo on top of the cooker lid and let it steam on a medium flame for 5 minutes and on a low flame for 20 minutes. Take the bamboo out of the pot, open it gently and transfer the biryani to a plate. Serve it hot with raita.

title: Peri Peri Chicken with Egg Corn Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 mins. Cook the basmati rice in an open pot with 1 litre of water and ½  tbsp of salt. Once the rice is 80% done, drain the water and let the rice cool completely.
For the sauce: Combine all the ingredients into a fine paste and set aside.
On the diced chicken, apply some of the marinade and cook on a tava until golden brown and cooked through with some oil.

For the sauce, heat oil in a pot and add the sauce. Cook until the raw flavor goes, add water with the cornstarch to make it into a thick sauce. Add the cooked chicken and toss well. Finish with parsley.
In the pan add some more oil, add finely chopped onion, carrots, beans and capsicum. Saute this for 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, salt, sugar and pepper. Make a hole in the middle, break 2 eggs, scramble and mix well with the vegetables.
Add the cooked rice to the pan. Garnish it with spring onion greens.

title: Garlic Mayonnaise
cooking_instructions: In a blender jar, add the egg, whole garlic cloves and lemon juice. Blitz/Pulse once just to combine the ingredients.

Use any neutral flavored oil for this recipe, such as sunflower oil, canola oil or rice bran oil. Do not use strong flavored oils such as coconut oil or mustard oil. Blend on low speed, and simultaneously pour in the oil in a thin and steady stream. Do not pour in too much oil at once, as this will cause the garlic mayonnaise to split.
Season with salt, to taste. Blend again briefly, just to combine the salt. Use immediately or store in the refrigerator, in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

title: Chettinad Paneer Tikka
cooking_instructions: Dry roast all the spices under chettinad masala until aromatic. Cool them down to room temperature and grind it into a fine powder and transfer into a bowl.

Heat Gingelly oil and add it to the ground chettinad masala. Add hung curd, turmeric powder, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, salt, besan flour and finely chopped curry leaves. Mix well to form a paste.
Add the paneer cubes, onion, deseeded tomato and capsicum. Mix gently to coat the marinade on all veggies and paneer.
Insert the paneer, onion, capsicum and tomato into the skewers.
Grill the paneer on an open flame until all sides are cooked and until you could see charred marks all over the paneer. Brush some ghee over the grilled paneer and serve hot.

title: All Purpose Gravy
cooking_instructions: Soak the cashew in hot water for at least 20 minutes. Grind it into a fine paste to make cashew paste. Set this aside.
Grind the tomatoes into a fine paste. Set this tomato puree aside.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat oil and add the whole spices.
Add the onion and saute until it turns golden brown.
Add the ginger garlic paste and saute for 3 minutes, or until the raw smell goes away. Add the tomato puree and salt. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the red chilli powder, turmeric powder and coriander powder. Cook for 5 minutes on medium heat.

Add the cashew paste and cook until the oil starts floating on top. This step will take around 10 minutes. Stir regularly to make sure it does not stick to the bottom. Allow it to cool down completely. Store this in the refrigerator, airtight for up to 1 week, in a closed container.

title: Veg Diwani Subzi
cooking_instructions: Prepare a smooth paste by blending together fried onions and cashew nuts
Heat oil in a pan, add onions and saute for a minute, add the remaining vegetables and saute them on a medium flame for 5 minutes and keep them aside
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and the spices and let them crackle.
Add ginger garlic paste and saute for a minute on a medium flame. Add tomato puree, green chilli and cook it well on a medium flame for 10 minutes.
Add the masala powders and mix well for 2 minutes.
Add the onion and cashew paste and mix well till it combines evenly. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Add the vegetables and mix well and simmer the gravy for 2 more minutes.
Finally add fresh cream, garam masala and kasuri methi, salt, ghee and mix well. Serve it hot with rice or roti and enjoy.

title: (Super Easy) Mutton Varuval
cooking_instructions: To a pressure cooker, add mutton and the remaining ingredients and mix well till all the ingredients combine evenly.

Add water, place the cooker on the stove and pressure cook it on a medium flame for 7-8 whistles. Check if the mutton is soft and cooked. Cook it down till the mixture is almost dry. Add coriander leaves, mix well and serve it hot with rice or parotta.

title: Mushroom Manchurian
cooking_instructions: To the mushrooms, add cornflour, maida, salt, pepper and water. Mix till the mushrooms are coated well.
Heat oil in a kadai and deep fry the mushrooms till it turns golden brown.
Heat oil in a wok, add ginger and garlic and saute for a few seconds.
Add the onions and capsicum and toss for a few seconds on a high flame.
Add the sauces and mix till it combines evenly.
Add the mushrooms and toss till it is coated evenly with the sauce. Garnish with spring onions and serve it hot.

title: Tawa Pulao (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat some oil in a pan and saute the vegetables for 1 minute.
Add water, cover and cook on low heat for 3 minutes or until softened.
Add the all-purpose gravy and pav bhaji masala, and mix well.
Add rice and salt, mix well to coat. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with raita.

title: Chicken Curry (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Add the all-purpose gravy to a pan and heat it. Add the chicken and saute for 3 minutes.
Add water, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Season with salt, if needed. Serve garnished with coriander leaves.

title: Mix Veg Gravy (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: In a pan, heat oil and add the vegetables. Saute for 3 minutes on high heat.
Add salt and water, cover and cook on low heat for a further 5 minutes, or until the vegetables become soft.
Add the gravy into the pan, and mix. Bring it up to a simmer. Garnish with fresh cream & coriander leaves. Serve with rice or roti.

title: Prawn Gravy (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add curry leaves and the prawns. Saute it for 2 minutes on high heat. Remove it from the pan.
Add the gravy into the pan and heat it up. Add the prawns and mix. Cover and cook on low heat for 2 minutes. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve!

title: Egg Drop Curry (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat the gravy and water in a pan. Bring it to a light boil.
Add 4 eggs around the pan. Sprinkle salt and garam masala powder.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes. Sprinkle coriander leaves on top and serve. Best served with jeera rice!

title: Masala Uthappam (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Grease a tawa with oil. On medium heat Pour the dosa batter and spread it very lightly. It has to be thick.

Cook for around 15 seconds, then spread the gravy over the uthappam. Drizzle ghee around the edges, cover and cook for around 1 minute. Flip and cook for 30 seconds more. Serve garnished with fresh chopped onions and coriander leaves.

title: Bhindi Masala (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add the chopped ladies fingers and salt. Fry until browned, around 4-5 minutes. Remove this from the pan.
To the pan, add the gravy and water. Heat it up, then add the beaten curd and mix. Cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the fried ladies fingers and garam masala powder. Cook for 2 more minutes. Add coriander leaves, mix and serve with chapathi or rice.

title: Egg Bhurji (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add the gravy and heat it up.
Add the eggs and salt. Once it starts to cook lightly, mix it up to scramble. Cook for around 3 minutes. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve!

title: Spicy Tomato Chutney (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Add the gravy into a mixer jar with some water. Grind it into a smooth paste.

Heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and allow it to crackle. Add curry leaves and urad dal, cook on low heat until the urad dal’s colour starts to change lightly. Add this tempering to the chutney and mix. Serve with dosa or idly.

title: Aloo Gobi (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat oil and add the cumin seeds. Once they crackle, add the potato and cauliflower with some salt and water. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the gravy and allow it to heat up for a minute. Squeeze some lemon juice and add some coriander leaves. Mix and serve hot with some rice or chapathi.

title: Soya Masala (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Soak the soya in salt, turmeric powder and hot water. Cover and soak for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan, add the soya, all-purpose gravy and water. Cover and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in garam masala powder and coriander leaves. Serve with rice or chapathi.

title: Paneer Butter Masala (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat butter in a pan and add the paneer. Fry until the colour slightly starts to change on all sides. Remove the paneer from the pan.
Add the gravy and water to the pan. Heat it up and bring it to a gentle boil.
Add paneer, garam masala powder, Kasuri methi and fresh cream. Turn off the heat as soon as it starts boiling.

title: Mutton Curry (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the mutton. Cook for 2-3 minutes on high heat, stirring occasionally.
Add salt, green chilli, coriander leaves, all-purpose gravy, water and garam masala powder.
Cover and pressure cook for 1 whistle on high heat. After 1 whistle, reduce the flame to low and cook for 25 minutes. Allow the pressure to release, and serve with rice or chapathi.

title: Masala Pav (All Purpose Gravy)
cooking_instructions: Heat the all-purpose gravy with water. Remove it into a bowl.

Toast the Pav lightly on both sides. Add some of the mixture on the pav. Optionally, you can top it with some grated cheese, onion and coriander leaves. Fold it and add serve. Add more masala on top, with some grated cheese, onion and coriander leaves. Serve with a lemon wedge.

title: Cauliflower Kuruma
cooking_instructions: Cut the cauliflower into florets. Wash and drain it. Then add salt, turmeric and enough water to cover. Set aside for 10-15 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and add the whole spices (cinnamon, cardamom, clove, fennel seeds, kalpasi). Add the onion and saute until it turns translucent.

Add ginger garlic paste and saute for a minute. Add the green chilli, tomato, salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, black pepper powder and garam masala powder. Saute for 3-4 minutes or until the tomato softens. Drain the cauliflower and add it to the pot. Add water, cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Prepare the coconut paste by grinding all the ingredients into a fine paste.

Add the coconut paste and water. Cover the pot partly with a lid and cook for 5 more minutes. Adjust the amount of salt, add coriander leaves, mix and turn off the heat. Serve with chapathi, Idiyappam or rice.

title: Singapore Chicken & Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak rice for 30 minutes.
In a stock pot or a large pot add the aromatic herbs and spics along with oil and saute until aromatic. Pour water and let it come to a simmer.
Add the chicken legs and simmer it for 20 minutes. Extract the chicken legs carefully and set aside. Strain the stock and use it to cook the rice.

In a pan, add oil, garlic, saute and add the soaked basmati rice. Add in the stock, and add salt. Cover and cook for 12 minutes. Once the rice is done garnish it with coriander leaves, serve it with the chicken and chopped peanuts.

title: Soya Nuggets
cooking_instructions: To a bowl, add soya chunks and hot water and let it soak for 10 minutes. Strain the soya and squeeze the hot water out of it.
To a blender, add the soya and the remaining ingredients and blend till it all combines together and forms a binding texture. Add very little water while blending if it isnt blending well.
Shape it into squares and keep it aside
Prepare a thick batter with maida, salt, pepper and water.
Dip the shaped nuggets in the maida batter and then coat it in the panko crumbs.

Heat oil in a kadai. Make sure the oil is hot before frying the nuggets. Deep fry the nuggets till it turns golden brown and crispy. Transfer it to a place lined with tissue paper to drain off the excess oil. Serve it hot with any dip of your choice.

title: Mor Sambar
cooking_instructions: Add coconut, green chillies, garlic, pepper, jeera, tomato into a mixing jar and blend into a smooth paste and set aside.
In a pressure cooker add the toor dal and ¾ Cup water and cook for 4 whistles on a medium flame and set aside to let it cool.
In a kadai add oil, mustard seeds once it sputters add curry leaves, jeera, dry red chillies, asafoetida and onion.
Saute for 30 seconds and add the drumsticks. Cook the drumsticks for a minute and add the chopped carrots and saute for 30 more seconds.
Add the paste along with ½ teaspoon of turmeric powder and cook for 2 minutes or until the raw flavour disappears.

Pour ¼ Cup water and bring it to a boil, dilute curd with ½ cup water and add it to the sambar along with the boiled toor dal. Add 1 teaspoon of sambar powder and cook until the raw flavour disappears. Mix the sambar thoroughly and adjust for seasoning if necessary.

title: Prawn Vadai
cooking_instructions: Mince the prawns and add all the ingredients together and mix thoroughly.
Grease your palms and shape the mixture into vadai's.
Deep fry the vadai's until golden brown and serve hot.

title: Vaazhakkai Kofta Curry
cooking_instructions: Bring water to boil in a steamer, and steam the vaazhakai for 10 minutes and take it out. Let it cool down and peel off the skin, transfer it to a bowl and mash it well.
Add the remaining ingredients required for the kofta and mix well till all the ingredients combine evenly. Shape them into even sized balls.
Heat oil in a kadai. Deep fry the koftas till it turns golden brown and take it out.
Heat another pan, add oil, cumin,fennel seeds, green chillies, curry leaves and let it splutter.
Add the onions and saute till it turns light brown. Add ginger garlic paste and saute for a minute. Add the masala powders and mix for a minute.
Add the tomato puree, bring it to a boil and simmer it for 10 minutes till it is cooked.
Add water, salt and black pepper, mix well and bring the gravy to a boil.
Add the fried koftas and and cook it in the gravy for two minutes on a low flame. Garnish with coriander leaves, take it off the flame and serve it hot with rice.

title: Chocolate Cold Coffee
cooking_instructions: Mix together the coffee powder, cocoa powder and water until dissolved.
To a blender, add together all the ingredients along with the decoction. Blend for around 30 seconds. Serve it in a glass, garnished with chocolate syrup and kitkat.

title: Honey Chilli Cauliflower
cooking_instructions: To a bowl, add the cauliflower florets, add hot water and soak them for 10 minutes. Let the cauliflower soak for 10 minutes and strain it and put it back in the bowl. Add cornflour, maida, salt, pepper and water and mix well till the cauliflower is coated with the batter.
Heat oil in a kadai and fry the cauliflower till it turns golden brown and crispy. Keep it aside
Heat a pan, add oil, and add chopped garlic. Saute till they turn golden brown.
Add the chilli flakes and let it fry for a second and then add the water.
Add honey and mix well till it combines with the water and becomes a thick sauce.
Add the fried cauliflower, chopper spring onion and toss well till the cauliflower is coated with the sauce. Garnish it with toasted sesame seeds and serve it hot.

title: Jim Jam Biscuit
cooking_instructions: For the cookies: Whisk soft butter, sugar and the vanilla essence until it is pale, soft and fluffy.

Add some milk and whisk well to combine. Add the maida, salt, baking powder and cornstarch and mix well to bring together the dough, do not whisk. Fold together until the dough is uniform. Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 mins.
For the cream: Whisk the butter until soft, add the milk and vanilla essence. Add the powdered sugar and whisk until a smooth and thick cream is obtained. Fill this mixture into a piping bag.
For the Jam: In another piping bag, take some mixed fruit/ strawberry jam and mash it to make it smooth and in piping consistency.
Place it in between parchment paper/ butter paper and roll out to 1 cm thickness.

Use a cookie cutter to cut the desired shape cookies, cut out an even number. On half the cookies, cut out a smaller circle. Use a knife to make the characteristic indent shape if desired and a few holes with a skewer on the base piece. Place them on a parchment paper and bake in a preheated oven at 180c for 10-12 mins, until light golden brown. Allow the cookies to cool fully.

To assemble: On the base cookies, pipe some of the vanilla cream mixture, leaving an indent in the centre. Fill this gap with the jam and place the top piece on top, press gently. Sprinkle some sugar on the jam portion and serve up your childhood memories in every bite!

title: Appalam Kuzhambu
cooking_instructions: Soak the tamarind in water for 15 mins. Set aside. You can continue with the remaining steps while it is soaking.

Heat oil in a pan and add cumin, black peppercorn, fenugreek seeds, garlic and curry leaves. Cook on low heat until the garlic starts to brown lightly. Turn off the heat and allow it to cool down slightly. Then add it to a mixer jar along with tomatoes. Grind it into a paste.
Heat gingelly oil in a pan and crackle mustard seeds. Then add small onion, curry leaves, garlic and salt. Cook for 5 minutes on medium heat, or until the onion and garlic softens.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder and Kashmiri chilli powder. Saute on low heat for 2 minutes.
Add the ground paste and saute for a minute.
Drain and add the tamarind pulp. Cook it on low heat until the oil starts to float on top. Add jaggery and fried appalam, and mix.

title: Karaikudi Kaalan Noodles
cooking_instructions: Bring water to a boil and cook the noodles as per the instruction on the pack. Strain the noodles, add some oil to prevent the noodles from sticking on to each other.
Add all the ingredients under coconut paste and grind into a fine paste using a mixer grinder.
In a pan, add coconut oil, add the finely chopped onion, ginger and garlic and saute for a minute. Add the dried red chili and curry leaves and continue to saute.
Add the chopped mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes. Add the red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and tomato ketchup. Cook this for a minute.
Add the coconut paste and mix well. Add salt and lemon juice.
Add the cooked Noodles and mix without breaking the noodles. Add some more salt, black pepper powder, coriander leaves, mix well and remove from the heat and serve hot.

title: Tawa Chana
cooking_instructions: Soak the chickpea in water for 8 hrs.
In a pressure cooker add 2 cups of water, ½ tsp of salt, soaked chickpea and pressure cook it for 15 mins.
Heat a pan, add all the ingredients under “Tawa masala powder” and dry roast until aromatic.
Once cool, add the dry roasted ingredients to a mixer grinder and grind into a fine powder.
In a Tawa, heat butter, oil, add onion, green chilli and saute till it turns translucent.
Add tomato and cook till the tomatoes are soft and mushy.
Add ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, dry mango powder, chaat masala powder, ground Tawa masala powder, ½ tsp of salt and saute for a minute.
Add ¼ Cup of water and cook the spice powders.
Add the cooked chickpea, ¼ Cup of water, mix well, and stir fry for 5 mins on medium flame.
Add coriander leaves and serve hot with chapati/roti.

title: Thenga Paal Soru
cooking_instructions: Soak the Basmati rice for at least 20-30 minutes. Heat ghee in a pressure cooker and add all the spices.
Add the onion and green chilli, and saute until it turns translucent.
Add the ginger garlic paste and saute for 2 minutes. Add the tomato and saute until the tomato starts to soften, around 3-4 minutes.

Add the water, coconut milk and salt. Mix it well. Add the soaked rice, cover and pressure cook on high flame for 2 whistles. Once the pressure settles, open the cooker and fluff up the rice gently, and serve.

title: Nellai Mutton Kari Kuzhambu
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pot along with the mutton fat on low heat. Add the whole spices (clove, bay leaves, cinnamon) and onion. Saute until it starts to turn golden brown.
Add the ginger garlic paste and coriander leaves. Saute for 2 minutes.

Add the tomato and rock salt. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the tomato starts to soften. Add the turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, red chilli powder, fennel powder and black pepper powder. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add the mutton and saute for 3-4 minutes on high heat.
Grind together the coconut and roasted peanuts. Add this to the mutton.

Transfer this to a pressure cooker. Add water, cover and pressure cook for 1 whistle on high heat. Then reduce the heat and cook it for 25 minutes on low heat. Open the lid. If needed, heat it to thicken the gravy even further. Mix in coriander leaves and serve.

title: Chicken Thanni Kuzhambu
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the whole spices and curry leaves. Saute for a few seconds.
Add the onion and saute for 2 minutes. Add the tomato and fried gram. Saute until the tomato starts to soften.

Add the turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and chicken masala. Saute for 3-4 minutes on medium heat, then turn off the heat. Once it cools down, grind it into a paste adding water as required.
Heat oil in another pot and add fennel seeds, curry leaves and onions. Saute until the onions turn translucent.
Add ginger garlic paste and saute for 2 minutes. Add the chicken, turmeric powder and water. Bring it to a boil.

Add salt and the prepared masala paste. Once it boils, reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 20 minutes. Add water as needed to adjust the consistency. Simmer for 2-3 more minutes. Sprinkle coriander leaves and turn off the heat.

title: Prawn Moilee
cooking_instructions: Mix the prawns with salt, turmeric powder and black pepper powder. Heat oil in a pan and pan-fry for 2 minutes on each side. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Heat oil in another pan and add fenugreek seeds. Add garlic, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves and onion. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder and salt. Saute for a minute.
Add thin coconut milk (2nd press). If you don’t have it, combine water and coconut milk together. Add the prawns and simmer for 2 minutes.

Add the coconut milk, black pepper powder and vinegar. Stir it and immediately add tomato slices and coconut oil on top.Turn off the heat immediately. Cover and rest for 5 minutes. It will thicken and the flavours will mingle together. Serve hot with appam, Idiyappam or rice.

title: Aloo Bhuna
cooking_instructions:
For Masala:
In a pan, add salt to taste, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, black peppercorns, black cardamom,  green cardamom, cloves, dry kashmiri red chillies and dry roast it on medium flame or until the spices turn fragrant. Grind into a fine powder. Keep it aside

For Gram Flour Mixture:
In a pan, add ghee, once it's hot, add green chillies, gram flour and saute until the rawness is gone. Add carom seeds, prepared masala and mix well. Turn off the flame and keep aside for further use.

For Aloo Bhuna:
Heat a pan, add oil, add bay leaf, black peppercorns, green cardamom let it crackle. Add onion and saute until it turns light brown.
Add coriander powder, turmeric powder and saute for a minute. Add tomato and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add curd, Kashmiri red chili powder, salt to taste and mix well.
Add baby potatoes, water and mix it well.

Cover and cook for 10 minutes on a medium flame. Stirring occasionally. Once the potatoes are 80% cooked, add prepared gram flour mixture and mix till the gravy starts to thicken. Finish it with some coriander leaves and ghee, and transfer it to a serving bowl. Garnish it with coriander sprig and chili oil. Serve hot with roti.

title: Kasi Halwa
cooking_instructions: Cut the ash gourd, peel it and remove the seeds. Grate it and using a muslin cloth, squeeze out the water into a bowl. Set the squeezed water and the ash gourd aside.
In a pot, heat the ghee and fry the cashew on low heat. Once it is golden brown, remove it from the pot.
Into the same ghee, add the grated ash gourd. Cook for 5 minutes or until most of the water has evaporated. Add the squeezed water and cook again until the water has evaporated.
Add the sugar and saffron. Continue cooking until the sugar has dissolved completely.

Continue cooking on medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Cook until the halwa starts to thicken again. Then add ghee and stir until the halwa fully absorbs the ghee, and cook for 5 minutes. Add cardamom powder, lemon juice, edible camphor and the fried cashew. Cook for 2 more minutes. Turn off the heat while the halwa is still a little runny. It will thicken when it cools down. Serve it as a dessert and enjoy!

title: Chicken Dalcha
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the dal for 20 minutes. To a pressure cooker, add the dal, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, asafoetida, ghee, salt and water. Pressure cook the dal for 7 whistles and take it off the flame. Keep it aside and let the steam reduce gradually.
Heat a kadai, add oil. Add the whole spices and let it crackle.

Add the chopped onions and saute till it turns golden brown. Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a minute. Add the tomatoes and masala powders and cook till the tomatoes become soft and oil oozes out from the sides.
Add chicken and mix it for 10 minutes on a medium flame. Add a little water.
Add the boiled dal and  mix well and partially mash it too. Bring the gravy to a boil. Cover and cook it for 10 minutes on a low flame. Open the pot, give it a stir and take it off the flame.
Prepare a tempering with hot oil, ginger juliennes and sliced green chillies and add it to  the chicken mixture. Garnish it with chopped coriander leaves. Serve it hot with rice/biryani.

title: Chinna Vengaya Kaara Kuzhambu
cooking_instructions: Soak the tamarind in hot water. Heat Oil in a pan. Add the mustard, fenugreek, curry leaves, dry red chilli, asafoetida and let it crackle. Add the shallots and saute till it turns translucent. Add garlic and cook it for a minute.
Add the tomato. Add the masala powders and cook until the tomatoes are mashed. Add water, mix it well and bring it to a boil.

Add the tamarind soaked water, mix it well and let it boil till the gravy starts to become thick. Season it with salt and jaggery. Mix it till the jaggery dissolves. Transfer it to a bowl. Garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot with rice.

title: Thai Basil Fried Rice
cooking_instructions: Start by soaking the tamarind in hot water for at least 5-10 minutes, to extract the tamarind paste. In a pan, toast the dry chillies on low heat until the colour starts to darken on some spots. Remove it from the pan and set aside.

Add oil and add the garlic and shallots. Saute until it starts to turn golden brown. Mix the chillies also along with these, and allow it to cool down. Blend it into a slightly coarse paste along with roasted peanuts, jaggery/sugar and salt. Add the tamarind paste and blend again. Heat oil in the pan again and add the prepared paste. Cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes, or until the raw taste is gone. Set it aside to cool. You can also store this in the refrigerator for upto 3 weeks.
Prepare the thai basil leaves by removing them from the stems. Mix the boneless chicken pieces along with soy sauce.
Heat oil in a pan and add the chicken along with onions and garlic. Saute on high heat for 2-3 minutes.

Add the chilli paste, soy sauce, oyster sauce and Thai basil leaves. Mix to combine evenly. Add the cooked rice and toss on high heat for 2-3 more minutes. Adjust salt if needed. Add a handful of Thai basil leaves, toss for a few more seconds and turn off the heat.

title: Creamy Coconut Chicken
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add cumin, fennel, curry leaves, green chilli and let it crackle. Add onion and saute till it turns soft and translucent. Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a minute.
Add the chicken, turmeric powder and saute for 2-3 minutes. Add water, mix well. Cover and cook it for 10 minutes on a medium flame.

Add coconut milk and salt, turn the flame to low and mix well. Add salt, black pepper, fresh cream and coriander leaves and mix well till the ingredients combine evenly. Simmer it for 2-3 more minutes. Let the gravy start to thicken.

For the tempering:
In a small pan, add oil, add ginger and curry, fry for a second and then add it to the curry. Take it off the flame, serve it hot with steamed rice or any tiffin item

title: Pineapple Pudding
cooking_instructions: In a kadai add the milk and condensed milk and let it heat up
Once hot add the gelatin and mix until it melts. Strain the liquid to filter out unwanted lumps formed by the gelatin.
Add it back to the kadai and heat it up. Turn off the flame and add food colour, the pineapple crush and chunks.
Mix until thoroughly combined and add it to the mould of your choice and let it sit overnight. Serve chilled.

title: Chettinad Paal Paniyaram
cooking_instructions: Soak the raw rice and urad dal together for at least 3 hours.

Add the grated coconut, green cardamom and water to a mixer jar. Blend it for a few seconds to extract the coconut milk. Strain it into a bowl. Add the remains again to a mixer jar along with water. Blend it again, and repeat the same process of straining. Add sugar and mix until the sugar is completely dissolved.

Grind it into a very smooth batter along with salt. Heat oil for deep-frying. Once it is hot, reduce the heat to low and add the batter in small batches at a time. Remove it from the oil before it changes colour, but when it’s crisp enough. Soak it in the coconut milk for at least 10 minutes. Then serve garnished with chopped nuts.

title: Creamy Tomato Mushroom pasta
cooking_instructions: Add water to a pan, add salt to it. Bring it to a boil. Add the pasta and boil it according to the time mentioned on the pack. Strain the pasta, reserve some of the water, grease it with oil and keep it aside.
Heat a pan,add olive oil. Add chopped garlic and saute till it starts to turn light brown. Add the mushrooms and saute for 2-3 minutes. Add the tomato puree and cook it for 5 minutes.
Add the reserved pasta water and let it simmer for 5 minutes. Ada oregano and butter, mix well.
Add the fresh cream and mix till it combines evenly. Add the boiled pasta and mix and toss till it is coated well with the sauce. Garnish it with coriander and serve it hot.

title: Holi Thandai Pudding
cooking_instructions: In a pan dry roast all the ingredients and blend into a fine powder.
In a pan pour milk, cream and sugar, warm it up.

Add gelatin to the milk mixture and mix thoroughly until completely dissolved. Add the ground powder to the milk and mix until completely dissolved. Strain the mixture to make sure it’s silky smooth. Pour it into matkas and refrigerate overnight.

title: Afghani Paneer Gravy
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl add the cubed paneer and add the ingredients for the marinade. Mix gently making sure you don’t break the paneer and set it aside.

In a pan add garlic, coriander leaves, ginger, onion and cashew nuts, and saute for 2-3 minutes or until the onions turn translucent. Let it cool completely before blending it into a fine paste along with the curd

In the same add back the gravy along with some coriander powder, garam masala and turmeric. Cook on a medium heat until the raw flavour disappears. Add cream and kasoori methi cook for another minutes and turn off the flame.
In a pan add the paneer fry until they turn golden and add it to the gravy. Garnish with some cream and coriander leaves.

title: Hyderbadi Chicken Fry
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl add the chicken along with the ground masalas, curd, ginger garlic paste and fried onions. Mix until the chicken is thoroughly coated and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
In a kadhai pour oil and add whole garam masalas. Once hot add the marinated chicken and cook on a medium-low flame for 10 minutes. Once cooked through add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Mongolian Lamb
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl add the lamb strips and add baking soda, soy sauce, cornstarch, salt and pepper. Mix it thoroughly and let it rest for 20 minutes(this tenderises the meat).
Once the meat is rested add some more corn starch and mix it thoroughly and deep fry on a medium flame until golden brown.
In a kadhai or wok pour in oil and add the fine chopped spring onion whites, garlic and ginger, saute until aromatic.
Add the Onion and Bell Peppers and Saute for 30 Seconds on a high flame. Add all the above mentioned sauces and saute on a high flame for 30 seconds and pour in the water and bring it to a boil.
Add the cornstarch slurry and cook until thickened. Add the fried lamb and spring onion greens and toss until well coated in the sauce. Serve Hot!

title: Pudukottai Muttai Mass
cooking_instructions: Peel and cut the boiled eggs into 8 pieces.
Heat oil in a tawa/pan and add green chilli, curry leaves and onion. Saute for a minute or until the onion softens.
Add the tomato, salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and garam masala powder. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the cut boiled eggs. Mix to coat the masala, and continue to fry on high heat for a minute.
Pour the salna over the eggs and cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle black pepper powder and curry leaves.. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve along with parotta, idli or dosa.

title: Kerala Style Mutton Roast
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl add the mutton, ginger garlic paste, coriander powder, garam masala, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, lemon juice, green chillies, coconut oil and curry leaves. Mix it thoroughly and let it set for 30 minutes.
Add the marinated mutton to a pressure cooker along with salt and cook for 15 minutes on a medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.
In a pan pour coconut oil, add coconut slivers and toast until it turns golden brown. Then add thinly sliced onions and saute for 2 minutes, next the pounded shallots.

Saute on high heat until they turn golden brown add the mutton to the pan. Cook on high heat, add black pepper powder, garam masala powder and coriander powder. Cook until the water evaporates. Serve hot.

title: Berry Loaf Cake
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 180-degree celsius. In a mixing bowl add all the ingredients and mix until homogeneous.
Bake in a loaf tin lined with parchment paper and bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely and serve.

title: Dhaba Style Aloo Palak
cooking_instructions: In a kadhai pour oil and add cumin seeds, once it splutters add the onion, dry red chilli, green chilli, ginger and garlic.

Saute for 30 seconds and add the potato and salt. Cook the potato for 2 minutes on medium flame. Add turmeric and tomato, cook covered until the potato cooks through, then add capsicum, spinach leaves, kasoori methi and garam masala.
Cook for 3 minutes so that the spinach wilts and the raw flavour disappears. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Prawn Pepper Fry (OT)
cooking_instructions: In a kadhai pour oil and add fennel seeds and curry leaves, saute until they turn aromatic. Add the Cookd Onion Tomato Masala and cook for 10 seconds.
Add washed and deveined prawns and salt to the gravy. Cook for 3-4 minutes on a moderate flame. Add pepper powder and garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves and serve.

title: Egg Drop Curry (OT)
cooking_instructions:
In a kadai, pour oil and add curry leaves and fennel powder. Saute for 10 seconds and add the Cookd Onion Tomato Masala. 
Give it a good mix. Pour water and bring it to a boil. Once it reaches a boil, reduce the flame to simmer. Break the eggs making sure the yolk doesn’t break. Cover and cook for 1-2 minutes on a low flame, or according to your desired egg doneness. Garnish with sliced green chillies and coriander leaves, and serve.

title: Tawa Pulao (OT)
cooking_instructions: In a pan add butter and the Cookd Onion Tomato Masala and saute for 10 seconds. Add diced bell peppers and saute for 30 seconds or until aromatic. Then add all the blanched vegetables and paneer and saute for 30 seconds, making sure the vegetables don’t mash
Add pav bhaji masala and Kashmiri red chilli powder and give it a good mix
Add the boiled basmati rice and 1 tbsp butter and mix gently making sure the rice doesn’t break. Garnish with coriander leaves and fine chopped onion and serve hot.

title: Dal Tadka (OT)
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the dal for 20 minutes. Add it to a pressure cooker with water, salt, turmeric and cook it 4 whistles (approx.5-7 minutes). Let the pressure reduce gradually
Head a kadai add oil. Add cumin seeds dry red chillies and let it crackle. Add the cookd onion tomato masala and saute for 2 minutes.

Add the boiled dal to the mixture and mix till they combine evenly. Season the mixture and mix well and adjust its consistency with water. Add salt,lemon juice and mix well. Bring the gravy to a , garnish with coriander leaves and rogan and serve it hot.

title: Mutton Curry (OT)
cooking_instructions: Heat a pressure cooker, Add the cookd all purpose gravy and saute for a minute. Add the washed mutton pieces and mix it with the masala for 2 minutes. Add water, mix well. Add salt, mix well and bring the mixture to a boil

Cover and pressure cook the mutton on a medium flame for 15 minutes. Let the pressure reduce gradually. Open the cooker, check if the mutton is cooked. Garnish it with coriander leaves and serve it hot.

title: Veg Kuruma (OT)
cooking_instructions: For the coconut paste, add a splash of water and grind everything into a fine paste.
Heat the Cookd Onion Tomato Masala in a pan. Add the vegetables, mint leaves and coconut paste. Saute for 2 minutes. Add salt, fennel powder and water.
Bring it to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes. Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and coriander leaves. Serve hot with chapathi, appam, parotta or idiyappam.

title: Chicken Biryani (OT)
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes.

Heat a pressure cooker, add cinnamon, cardamom and cloves. Let them crackle. Add green chillies, chopped coriander and mint and saute for a few seconds. Add kashmiri red chilli powder and mix till the mixture turns red.
Add the chicken pieces, mix it well with the masala for 2 minutes. Add the cookd onion tomato masala and saute for 2 minutes. Add water, salt and mix well. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Add the soaked and strained rice and mix it gently. Cover and pressure cook for 2 whistle and turn off the flame. Let the steam reduce gradually. Serve it hot with raita.

title: Mushroom Dum Biryani (OT)
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes. In a deep pot, bring water to a boil. Add salt and ghee. Add the rice and boil it for exactly 4 minutes. Strain the rice and keep it aside.

Heat a pan, add oil/ghee and add the whole garam masala and let it crackle. Add the mushrooms and saute on a high flame for 5 minutes. Add the cookd onion tomato masala and saute with the mushroom for 2 minutes. At this point the mushroom will leave out water.Bring it to a boil
Season the mixture and mix well. Take half of the mushroom mixture and keep it in a bowl.

Start layering the biryani. Mushroom mixture, Rice, coriander and mint leaves, fried onions, and second half of the mushroom mixture. Repeat the process and finally top it with ghee, saffron milk, and kewra water. Cover the pot, keep it on a preheated tawa and keep it on dum for 5 minutes on a high flame and 5 minutes on a low flame. Open the pot, fluff the rice and serve it hot with raita.

title: Rajma Masala (OT)
cooking_instructions: Soak the Rajma for at least 6 to 8 hours. Add it to a pressure cooker along with bay leaf, salt and water. Pressure cook for 1 whistle on high flame. Then reduce the heat to low and cook for 20 minutes. Once the pressure releases, open the cooker and check if the rajma is fully cooked.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds and green chilli. Mix briefly and then add Cookd Onion Tomato Masala and Rajma masala. Heat it for 2-3 minutes.
Add the boiled rajma and bring it to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5-6 minutes. Add the cream, butter and chopped coriander leaves. Mix and turn off the heat. Serve with rice/roti.

title: Chettinad Avial
cooking_instructions: Soak the tamarind in hot water. To prepare the masala paste, dry roast the spices first and keep them aside. Dry roast the coconut till it isn't moist and add it to the roasted spices. Transfer it to a blender and blend it to a fine paste and keep it aside.
Heat a kadai, add groundnut oil. Add the curry leaves and green chillies and let it crackle. Add the onions and saute till it turns translucent.
Add the tomatoes and saute till it turns mushy. Add turmeric powder and the diced potato and brinjal. Saute for 2 minutes.

Add the ground masala paste, tamarind extract, salt and water. Mix well, bring it to a boil and reduce the flame to low. Cover and cook the gravy for 15 minutes, till the potato and brinjal are cooked. Garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot with idli or dosa.

title: Karupatti Paal Kozhukattai
