To a pan/pot, add oil, followed by the garlic and green chillis. Fry the garlic until lightly golden before adding the onions and curry leaves. 
Add salt and saute for 8 - 10 minutes, or until the onions turn golden brown. 
Add the ginger garlic paste along with red chili powder, turmeric powder, and half of the masala powder.
Cook for 2 minutes, or until the raw smell of the chilli powder goes. 
Add the chicken and mix to combine well. 
The chicken should be nicely coated in the onion mixture. 
Cook on a medium high heat for 8 - 10 minutes, while mixing every now and then. This allows the chicken to get lightly crispy. 
Add the rest of the masala powder along with curry leaves and mix to combine well. 
Saute for an additional 30 seconds before turning the flame off. 
Serve hot with some rice!

title: Choco Chunk Cookies
cooking_instructions:
Melt the butter. 


In a bowl, combine butter and sugars. Add the vanilla essence and milk and whisk for 2 mins. 


Sift in the flour and baking soda, and fold gently using some more milk. 
Finally,  add chopped chocolate chunks and crushed walnuts/ chopped nuts. Fold gently. 
Chill the mixture for 30 mins.


Portion equally using a measuring spoon or weighing scale. Place them on a plate or tray lined with parchment paper. 
In a preheated oven, bake for 15-18 mins at 180C or to bake in a kadhai - add salt in a heavy bottom kadhai with a lid, preheat for 10 mins on high, place a stand, and keep the cookies on a plate or idli plate. Bake for 18-20 mins on medium.

title: Mutton Chutney
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl add all the dals, and wash them thoroughly. 
In a pressure cooker, pour ghee, add the mutton and sear until golden brown. (around 2 minutes)
Add the whole spices and cook until aromatic. (around 30 seconds)
Add the washed dal to the cooker, add red chilli powder, salt and saffron.
Add the ginger garlic paste and coriander leaves and green chillies and saute it until aromatic (around 30 seconds).
Pour water and bring it to a boil. 
Cover and pressure cook on a simmer for 20 minutes. 
Let the pressure subside, and mash the mixture until fully smooth. 
Cook it on a low flame for 2 minutes, garnish with coriander and serve hot with rotis, chapatis.

title: Sweet Sichuan Noodles
cooking_instructions:
Add the jaggery and water to a pot and bring to a boil. 
Once all the jaggery is dissolved, add the whole spices, spring onion whites, ginger and garlic. 
Simmer for 10 minutes, or until fragrant. 
Add the soy sauce and simmer for 5 minutes. The mixture should have slightly thickened. 
While the mixture is simmering, add the cornstarch slurry and start mixing. The mixture should start to significantly thicken. 
Turn the flame off  after 2 minutes and strain the mixture, to remove the solids. 
In a separate pot, bring water to a boil. 
Add the noodles and cook according to the package directions.
Once cooked, strain the noodles. 
To plate, add 1 full ladle of the sauce into a bowl, followed by the strained noodles. 
Top with the spring onion greens, sesame seeds, green chilli, garlic, chilli oil and roasted cumin powder. 
Mix well to combine before eating!

title: Parangikai pulikari
cooking_instructions:
In a bowl add tamarind , water and let it soak for 15 minutes and extract tamarind puree.
In a kadai add oil, urad dal, fenugreek seeds and let it fry for a few seconds.
Now add the onion, tomato and saute it for 5 minutes or until it turns golden brown.
Now remove half the mixture from the kadai and add it to the mixer jar
Now blend the ingredients in the mixer jar along with the grated coconut. Blend into a fine paste.
In the same kadai add the pumpkin and saute it for 2 minutes.
Add red chili powder, salt and mix it well.
Add water, cover and cook it for 7 - 8 minutes on a medium flame.
Now open the kadai, add the coconut paste and simmer it for 2 minutes.
Now add the tamarind puree and simmer it for 5 minutes.

title: Banana Ice Cream
cooking_instructions: Peel and slice 8 bananas (you can use 10 bananas if they are small in size). Store in an airtight plastic container and freeze for 5 hours.
In a saucepan, add milk and sugar and bring to a boil. In a small bowl, mix together the cornstarch and 2 tbsp of milk. Add this mixture to the milk and mix well to combine without any lumps.
Once the milk has started to thicken, add the condensed milk and stir.
Turn off the heat and pour it into a bowl. Cover with cling wrap and poke a few holes in the wrap to allow the steam to escape. And Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
In a blender, add the frozen bananas and chilled milk mixture. Blend until smooth.
Pour into an airtight plastic container and freeze for 6 hours.

title: Mexican Corn Soup
cooking_instructions: In a pan, heat oil and add the chopped garlic, onion, and jalapeno. Saute until the onion turns translucent
Add the cumin powder, red chili powder, salt, and sweet corn kernels. Saute for 1 minute. Add 1 cup of vegetable stock and simmer, covered, for 5 minutes.
Blend into a smooth puree
Heat a pan, add some oil and saute the corn kernels for 2 minutes, or until cooked.

For the topping, we are going to make a fresh Salsa, also known as Pico de Gallo. In a small bowl, combine the chopped onion, chopped tomato, coriander, lemon juice, cumin powder and salt. Set this aside.
Add the puree back into the pan and add 1 ½ Cups of vegetable stock to the corn puree. Bring to a boil. Add the cream and turn off the heat.
Top the soup with some of the sauteed corn and some Pico de Gallo (fresh salsa). Arrange some jalapeño slices on top, and sprinkle a pinch of paprika on top. Mexican Corn Soup is ready to serve!

title: Chicken Vengaya Pakoda
cooking_instructions:
In a pan, pour water, add 1 tsp salt, and bring it to a boil. 
Then add the chicken breast. Cover and cook on a low medium flame for 10 minutes. 
Once cooked, take the chicken and shred it into thin strips. 
Add the sliced onion, garlic, ginger, green chillies and curry leaves to a mixing bowl. 
Add the shredded chicken, and all the flour salt butter and mix gently until thoroughly combined. 
Deep fry the pakkoda until golden brown. 
Serve hot with the beverage of your choice.

title: Chicken Shawarma Gravy
cooking_instructions:
To make the hot sauce, boil together the ingredients until the garlic is soft and mashable, a minimum of 20 mins.
Strain and blend with the remaining water as needed, until smooth. Strain the sauce, if needed.
To make the garlic mayonnaise, blend all ingredients together until it is smooth except the oil and lemon, add them and pulse blend till thick and smooth.
Add all the spices under marination in a mixer jar and blend to a fine powder. 
Add the other ingredients under marination and blend to a fine paste.
Add 2 tbsp of this marination to the chicken, and mix well. 
On a hot pan, add oil and cook until charred outside/ you can also grill it directly on an open flame. 
Remove from heat
Scrape off the excess burnt bits from the pan. 
In the same pan, add the gravy, bring it to a boil while mixing continuously, and add the milk, again while stirring continuously.
cut into long strips
Add the chicken and mix well. Cover and simmer for 15 mins until cooked.
To assemble the shawarma gravy, squeeze the hot sauce and garlic mayonnaise on top. Serve with a side of salad/ veggies and pita/ chapati.

title: Muttaikose Varuval Dosa
cooking_instructions:
In a pan add oil, urad dal and saute for 10 seconds.
Add onion, garlic and saute for a minute.
Add cabbage and saute for 5 minutes, on a medium heat.
Add red chili powder, salt and saute for 5 minutes.
Now add water, cover and cook it for 15 minutes.
In a mixer jar add coconut, fennel seeds and coarsely blend it.
Now open the lid and add the coconut mixture and saute it for 5 minutes.
Now prepare a dosa, add butter and keep the prepared cabbage on it and roll it.

title: Brownie Halwa
cooking_instructions:
To a pan, add ghee, followed by the walnuts. 
Toast the walnut for 1 - 2 minutes or until lightly golden. 
Remove the walnuts from the pan.
In the remaining ghee, add the atta and stir continuously for 6 - 7 minutes on a medium low heat. The atta should start to darken and the raw smell should go. 
Once the atta has darkened, add the cocoa powder and stir for another minute.
Add the water and keep mixing for 2 minutes, the mixture should significantly thicken. 
Add the jaggery powder in 3 batches, making sure the add the next batch once the previous batch is fully incorporated.
The halwa should slightly loosen now, keep mixing and cooking for an additional 5 minutes. 
Add back the walnuts and the dark chocolate and mix once. 
Remove from the heat and serve hot!

title: Marundhu Kozhambu
cooking_instructions:
In a pan add all the ingredients for the powder, and dry roast on a low medium flame for 3 minutes or until aromatic. 
Blend the prepared ingredients into a fine powder and set aside. 
In a kadhai, pour oil add the mustard, and fenugreek seeds and saute until the mustard seeds splutter. 
Add curry leaves, garlic and shallots, and saute until the shallots turn translucent (around 3 minutes)
Pour the tamarind water, salt and turmeric powder and bring it to a boil. 
Add the prepared powder to the kozhambu and cook until it thoroughly thickens. 
Finish the gravy with asafoetida and curry leaves and serve hot.

title: Chappati Upma
cooking_instructions:
Tear the chappatis and pulse blend into a powder-like consistency. 
Heat ghee in the pan and splutter mustard seeds, followed by urad dal and cashew.
As soon as the colour starts to change, add hing, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves, and onion. Saute for a minute.  
Add the chapati powder, sprinkle some water, cover and cook for 2-3 minutes on a simmer, stirring in between - this will ensure it gets steamed and is not too dry.  
Serve garnished with freshly chopped coriander leaves and grated coconut.

title: Seeralam
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl ad all the ingredients for the idli, wash and let it soak for at least an hour. 
Strain the ingredients, and blend it into a coarse batter. 
Add salt, turmeric powder and baking soda and mix thoroughly. 
Pour water and loosen the batter slightly, add the prepared batter into greased idli moulds and steam them for 10-15 minutes. 
Once cooked, let it cool down and cut it into cubes and set aside. 
In a kadhai, pour oil and add the urad dal and mustard seeds, once they splutter add the onions and green chillies and saute on a medium flame for 3 minutes or until the onion turns translucent. 
Add the curry leaves and asafoetida, and cook for 30 seconds. 
Pour in water and bring it to a boil. 
Add in the cubed idlies into the pan and cook until the idli absorbs all the water and becomes soft (around 3- 5 minutes)
Garnish it with grated coconut and serve hot!

title: Mochai Kathirika Karuvadu Kolambu
cooking_instructions:
Soak the mochai overnight (around 8 - 10 hours) Pressure cook the mochai in 1 Cup water, for 5 whistles, on a medium heat. 
Add water to the karuvaadu and soak for 15 minutes. Soak the tamarind for 15 minutes by adding ½ cup of water. Once soaked, squeeze the pulp out and strain
In a kadai add coconut oil and groundnut oil Once hot, add channa dal, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and urad dal.
After popping, add the shallots. Saute for 2 minutes. 
Add the tomato and mix well.
Add the raw banana, chilli and brinjal. Saute for 5 minutes.
Add turmeric powder, salt, red chilli powder, along with some water. Bring it to a boil and then simmer covered for 6 - 7 minutes. 
Now add the pressure cooked mochai and the soaked karuvaadu (dry fish) cover and cook it for 5 minutes on a medium flame.
Add the coconut to a blender with some water and make a paste. 
Add the paste to the pan and mix to combine well.
Add the tamarind water and bring to a boil.
Cook for 5 minutes before turning off the heat.

title: Maggi Goreng
cooking_instructions:
In a pan pour water and bring it to a boil. 
Add the Maggi noodles and cook for 2-3 minutes or until done. 
Strain the noodles, pour oil and mix thoroughly. 
In wok/ kadhai pour oil and add the chopped vegetables. 
Saute for 10 seconds on high flame and add the sausages. 
Cook together for 30 more seconds on a high flame and add the prawns. 
Saute for 10 seconds and add in the cooked noodles. 
Add all the sauces and toss thoroughly. 
Garnish with spring onion and set aside. 
In a pan pour oil and break in an egg. 
Cook the eggs on a medium flame to make a sunny side up. 
Serve hot.

title: Peri Peri Paste
cooking_instructions: For the sauce: Blend all the ingredients into a fine paste and set aside.

To cook, heat oil in a pan and add the sauce and water. 
Cook until the raw flavor goes, it must be thick and oil must be released from the sides. About 10-15 mins. Cover and simmer, stirring often.

Finish with dried parsley. 
To consume: Mix with steamed rice, eat as is, or add veggies/ eggs/ protein of choice, and stir fry with rice.

title: Neer Urundai
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the raw rice for at least 3 hours. You can also soak it overnight.
Adding ½ cup of the soaking water and ½ tsp of salt, grind the rice into a coarse paste. Make sure the paste is not too fine, the texture should be coarse.

In a pan, heat up coconut oil and add the mustard seeds. When it starts to splutter, add the split urad dal and chana dal. When the color of the dals starts to change, add the curry leaves and dry red chilies. Add the grated coconut and saute.
Add the coarse rice paste and cook on medium heat, stirring continuously until the mixture has thickened into a dough consistency. Turn off the heat.
When the mixture has cooled down enough to be able to handle, but still warm, roll the dough into 2-inch sized balls. If it is sticky, use some oil to grease your hands.
Set up a steamer and arrange the rolled-out pieces on the steamer tray. Steam for 10 minutes. Serve warm with chutney.

title: Andhra Chilli Chicken
cooking_instructions:
Add all the ingredients required for the chicken marinade and mix well to combine. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes and up to overnight.
Blend all the ingredients required for the green chilli paste. It should be a smooth paste. 
To a pan/pot, add oil, followed by the curry leaves, cumin seeds and garlic. 
Saute until the garlic starts to turn lightly golden brown, around 2 minutes. 
Add the marinated chicken and mix to combine well. 
Once the chicken starts to stick to the bottom of the pan, after around 5 minutes, add the soy sauce and mix.

title: Mediterranean Upma
cooking_instructions: In a kadhai, roast the rava and set it aside.

In the same kadhai pour olive oil and add the onion and garlic. 
Saute until the onion turns translucent. 
Add the chopped veggies to the kadhai and cook on a medium flame for 30 seconds. 
Add back the roasted rava and mix thoroughly.
While this happens, heat 2 cups of water along with the chilli flakes, oregano and salt and bring it to a boil.

Add the boiling water to the rava batch by batch and mix thoroughly. 
Let the upma rest for 5 minutes covered before fluffing it up and serving hot. 
Garnish the Upma with some Feta Cheese, Cherry Tomatoes, Olives and Pomegranate.

title: Mixie Channa Masala
cooking_instructions: Soak 1 cup of dried channa in 3 cups of water, overnight or a minimum of 6 hours
For the masala paste, blend all the ingredients into a smooth paste

In a pressure cooker, heat ghee and add the whole spices. Fry for a minute. 
Add the masala paste and cook while stirring constantly, until it is thick and oil releases from the masala - about 7 or 8 mins. 
Add the soaked channa and pour about 2 ½ cups of water, stir, and bring to a boil.

Cover and pressure cook 1 whistle on a high flame and 6 whistles on a low flame. 
Allow the pressure to release naturally. 
Open the cooker and mash some of the channa and adjust the consistency with more water, if needed. 
Bring to a boil again and finish with chopped coriander leaves.

title: Kongunadu Vellai Mutton Biryani
cooking_instructions: For the paste add all the ingredients into a blender and blend it into a smooth paste.
Add the prepared paste to the mutton along with curd and mix thoroughly and let it sit for 30 minutes.

In a deep pan add the peanut oil and ghee, add the whole garam masalas, and once aromatic add the sliced onion and green chillis and saute for 30 seconds, then add tomatoes, coriander leaves and mint leaves. Saute until the leaves wilt.
Add the marinated mutton and cook until the raw flavour goes away, then add tomatoes, coriander leaves and mint leaves. Saute until the leaves wilt.

Add coconut milk, salt, and water, and bring it to a boil. 
Cover and cook the mutton on a low medium flame for 45-50 minutes depending on the quality of the mutton. 
Add soaked jeera samba rice and mix gently making sure the mutton doesn’t break. 
Bring it to a boil, simmer the flame, and cook on low heat for 12-14 minutes.
Rest the biryani for at least 15 minutes, fluff up the rice and serve.

title: Kavuni arisi - Inippu
cooking_instructions: Wash the rice and soak it 8 - 10 hours or overnight. Strain the water and set aside.
In a cooker, add the soaked rice and rice soaked water, and pressure cook for 7 - 8 whistles on a medium flame.

Once pressure naturally releases, open the lid and mash it lightly.
Now add the sugar and mix it well.
Add the grated coconut, ghee and mix it well.
Garnish with grated coconut and serve it hot.

title: Dosa Jalebi
cooking_instructions:
To make the simple syrup, add the sugar, water, lemon juice and cardamom to a pot and bring to a simmer. Cook for around 12 - 15 mins until thickened. 
Allow the syrup to cool before adding the food colouring
To make the jalebi batter, add all the required ingredients and mix to combine well.
Cut a small corner from the milk packet and transfer the batter into the milk packet.
Pipe the batter into the jalebi shape into hot oil and cook for 3 - 4 minutes or until crispy.
Drain the oil from the jalebi and add to the simple syrup and allow to soak for 10 - 15 minutes. 
Serve hot!

title: Chicken Mousse Curd Rice
cooking_instructions:
In a pan pour water, add the salt and ginger garlic paste and bring it to a boil. 
Add the cubed chicken to it, cover and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Strain out the chicken and add it to a blender along with the ice cubes, green chilli and cumin powder. 
Blend it into a super fine paste while adding the cream. 
In a mixing bowl add thick curd and mix the prepared chicken mousseline.
In a tadka pan pour oil, add mustard seeds, split urad dal, dry red chillies and curry leaves and saute until aromatic and golden brown. 
Add the prepared tadka to the curd mousseline. 
Mix in cooked rice to the curd, and serve cold with pickle of your choice.

title: Gongura Prawn Biryani
cooking_instructions:
To a pan/pot, add oil. Once hot, add the garlic along with the green chillis.
Cook until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the gongura leaves followed by the coriander leaves and cook until wilted, around 5 minutes on a medium heat. 
Transfer the mixture to a plate and let it cool. Once cooled, blend into a smooth paste, adding a little water if necessary.
To a pot, add ghee, followed by the whole spices. Toast for 3 minutes on a medium heat or until aromatic. 
Add the green chillis and the onions and saute for 8 - 10 minutes, on a medium heat, until deeply golden. 
Add the ginger garlic paste and spice powders and mix to combine well.
Add the gongura paste and the prawns and cook for 3 - 4 minutes. 
Once the paste starts sticking to the bottom of the pan, add the water and stir to mix well. 
Bring the mixture to a boil before adding the soaked and strained rice. 
Stir gently for 2 minutes, until the rice and the water level are the same. 
Close tightly with a lid and cook for 12 - 14 minutes on a low heat.
Once the time has passed, turn the flame off and let the biryani rest for 15 minutes before opening the lid.
Open the lid and add some ghee and fluff the rice.
Enjoy with some lemon, green chilli and onions.

title: Fish Cutlet
cooking_instructions: Cut the potatoes in half and cook with enough water to cover them and ½ tsp of salt in a pressure cooker for 2 whistles. Once done, peel and mash the potatoes. Set them aside.
In a pan, bring water to a boil and add ½ tsp salt and turmeric powder. Add the boneless fish chunks and boil them for 5 minutes. Remove the fish from the water and shred them with a fork.
Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a pan. Add finely chopped onion, green chilli, garlic, ginger and curry leaves. Cook for 1 minute. Add 1 tsp salt and black pepper powder.
Add the mashed potato and shredded fish to the pan. Mix and cook for 1 minute.Cool the mixture completely.
Once the mixture has cooled down, form them into 3-inch wide cutlets.
In a wide-mouthed bowl, crack open an egg and beat it. In another plate, add the breadcrumbs. Dip each cutlet in the egg mixture and then in the breadcrumbs, and then place them on another plate.
Heat up oil, and shallow fry them until they turn golden brown.

title: Gym Bro Tumbler Brownie
cooking_instructions:
In a mixer jar add the dates, sugar and eggs. Blend it into a very smooth paste.
In a mixing bowl, mix the prepared mixture and thick curd thoroughly. 
Sieve in the cocoa powder and flour and gently mix, ensuring not to over-mix
Add the dark chocolate and fold it in gently. 
Add the prepared batter to a floured and greased mould/ tiffin box
Add it to a deep pan, cover and cook on a medium flame for 10 minutes or until the middle of the brownie is almost set. 
Demould and let it sit for 5 minutes and serve hot.

title: Nagercoil Godhumai Mutton Biryani
cooking_instructions:
To a pan, add oil. Add the cashews and saute until lightly golden, around 2 minutes. Then add the raisins and saute until puffed, around 30 seconds. Remove from the pan. 
In the remaining oil, add the sliced onions and fry them until deeply golden brown. 
To a pressure cooker, add the mutton and cover with water. Pressure cook for 7 whistles, on a medium heat, around 30 minutes. 
Strain the mutton and liquid, reserving the liquid, 
In a pot, add ghee. Add the whole spices and saute for a minute or until fragrant. 
Add the onions and the green chillis and cook for 5 - 6 minutes. 
Add the ginger garlic paste and tomatoes. Mix to combine well. 
Add the coriander leaves and mint leaves. 
After the leaves have wilted, add the spice powders and cook until the raw smell is gone. 
Add the pressure cooked mutton and mix to coat well. 
Add the mutton stock, followed by the coconut milk. 
Once boiling, add the broken wheat and mix well. 
Cover and cook on a low heat for 15 minutes. 
Garnish with fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves, fried cashews, fried raisins and pineapple.

title: Attlappam
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl, add the rice flour, rava, sugar, salt, spice powders, and baking soda.

Pour ghee into a pan and roast the channa dal, cashews, raisins and coconut chunks until light golden and thoroughly roasted. 
Add it to the prepared mixture.
Pour water and whisk it into a thick dough (thicker than dosa batter)
Take a tin, grease it thoroughly with 3 tbsp ghee and pour the prepared batter.
Whisk two eggs and pour it on top of the batter, top it off with coconut slivers
Cover and cook in a preheated kadhai for 25 minutes or until thoroughly cooked, flip and cook again

title: Boli and Palada Payasam
cooking_instructions:
For payasam- Soak the rice ada in a bowl of boiled water and keep it aside.
Add the milk, sugar and salt to the pressure cooker and boil it.
After it is done, close the lid and simmer the milk for 1 hour under low-medium flame. 
Strain the ada.
Add the ada and stir it until you get the required consistency.
For boli- Make a dough with flour, salt and turmeric powder. Fold it with gingelly oil and keep it aside.
Boil the channa dal and don’t make it mashy.
Melt the jaggery 
Heat a pan and add cardamom powder, nutmeg powder, melted jaggery and channa dal.
Grind it all together.
Make it into balls and cover it up with the dough.
Flatten the dough and cook it like chapathi.

title: Simple Mutton Fry
cooking_instructions:
To a cooker, add oil, cinnamon and saute for a few seconds.
Now add onion, garlic and saute for 3 minutes.
Add mutton, red chilli powder, salt and saute for 5 minutes on a medium flame.
Add water, pressure cook it for 20 minutes on a medium flame.
In a mixer jar, add coconut, fennel seeds, water and grind it to a fine paste.
Once pressure gets down, open the cooker and add the coconut paste.
Mix it and roast it well.

title: Dal Fries
cooking_instructions:
Combine the rice and the dal, along with the ghee. 
Shape into rectangular flat logs and chill in the fridge for 20 minutes. 
To make the dredge, combine maida with water and whisk until smooth and thick. 
In another bowl, add maida and salt. 
To make the tempering, heat ghee in a pan. 
Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal, garlic, curry leaves and hing.
Add half of the tempering to the dry maida mixture and mix to combine well. 
Once set, cut the logs into bite size pieces.
To coat the dal rice mixture, first drop it into the dry maida mix. Tap off the excess maida and then drop it onto the wet maida mix. Remove it and add it back to the dry maida mix.
Once all the dal fries are coated, deep fry until golden brown, around 3 - 4 minutes. 
Drain on a paper towel before seasoning with a little salt. 
Serve hot with avakaya and appalam

title: Mutton Ennai chukka
cooking_instructions:
Pulse grind the shallots in a mixer grinder
Grind the black pepper corns and cumin seeds together into a powder

Add Ground nut oil in an iron Kadai and heat
Add the shallots and saute until light brown
Add the mutton pieces and saute for 2 mins

Add turmeric powder, chilli powder coriander powder and rock salt
Close the kadai and Cook for 45 mins stirring occasionally and preventing it from getting stuck to the bottom of the pan.
After 45 mins, add the ground powder and stir for 3-5 mins and remove from the heat

title: Guava Chutney
cooking_instructions:
In a kadhai pour oil, add the channa dal and saute until it turns golden brown. 
Add the dry red chillies and saute for 10 seconds on a medium-low flame.
Add the sliced onions, ginger and garlic and saute on a medium flame for 1 minute or until it turns translucent.
Add in the curry leaves, guava and tamarind and saute for 1 minute on a medium flame or until the guava turns soft and mushy. 
Add asafoetida, give it a mix and take it out of the flame and let it cool. 
Blend the chutney into a coarse paste and set aside. 
For the tempering, pour oil add mustard and urad dal, once they start to splutter add the curry leaves and pour them on the chutney, mix thoroughly and serve.

title: Fish Moilee
cooking_instructions: Marinate the fish with ½ tsp of salt, turmeric powder, and pepper powder.
Shallow fry them in coconut oil. This is mainly for the crust, you do not have to cook it completely at this point. Set them aside.
In a pan, heat up some coconut oil. Fry the cashew nuts until lightly golden and set them aside.
In the same pan, add cardamom, peppercorns, onion, green chili, and ginger. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add curry leaves, ½ tsp of salt, and a pinch of turmeric powder. Mix them well. Then add the thin coconut milk and let it come to a boil.
Add the fried fish and simmer for 3 minutes.

Turn the heat to low, and add the thick coconut milk. Simmer for 10 seconds and turn off the heat. Cut the tomatoes into slices and add them on top. It will soften a little with the heat from the Fish Moilee. Garnish with the fried cashew nuts. Serve with bread or Appam.

title: Banana Idiyappam
cooking_instructions:
Mash/ blend the bananas into a fine puree.
In a pot, boil the water with the salt, coconut oil, turmeric, and cardamom powder. 
Switch off the flame and add the rice flour and banana puree. Roughly mix. 
Cover and let it sit for 10 mins.
Bring together the dough and divide it into portions.
Bring together the dough and divide it into portions. 
Grease an idiyappam squeezer with coconut oil and fill the dough. 
Squeeze this onto a greased idli plate or greased plate. 
Steam for 5-6 mins. 
Serve with milk/ coconut milk and jaggery.

title: Nellore Karam Dosa
cooking_instructions:
Add the dry red chillies, onion, garlic, tomato, salt and cumin seeds to a blender and blend into a smooth paste. 
Add the oil to a pan and add the mustard seeds and curry leaves. Once they splutter, add the blended paste and cook on a medium heat for 15 - 20 minutes, until the raw taste is gone and the paste starts to thicken.
Remove the paste from the heat, and add a little water to thin it down if necessary.
Add a ladle of dosa batter to a tawa and spread into an even circle. 
Add ghee and let the dosa cook for 2 - 3 minutes. 
Spread a spoonful of the karam chutney into an even layer and let it cook for an additional 1 minute.
Remove the dosa gently and serve hot!

title: Kappa and Meen curry
cooking_instructions: Boil the tapioca in the pressure cooker with salt and turmeric powder.
In a blender, prepare a mix of grated coconut, turmeric powder, salt, green chilli, cumin powder and garlic.
Mix this into the pot.
Use curry leaves, mustard seeds and dry chilli for tempering.

Saute the fenugreek and mustard seeds.
Add the ginger, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves and shallots.
Then add the chilli powder, turmeric powder and coriander powder.

Once the raw smell subsides add water, malabar tamarind with required salt and let it boil.
Add the fish and close the lid.

title: Tumbler Bread
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl add the maida, water, sugar and yeast. 
Start kneading the dough, once a sticky and shaggy dough forms, add the salt and mix thoroughly. 
Add the butter and mix it into the dough, if the dough is too sticky sprinkle in some maida, make sure not to add too much. (We need a very soft dough)
The dough is done when nothing sticks to your hand and the dough is soft and supple (knead for 8-10 mins)
Shape it into a ball, cover it with a damp towel and let it rest for 1 hour or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough, knead for 1-2 minutes, shape it into a loaf and let it rest for 30-45 minutes on a well-floured plate or 1 ½ in size. 
Add the plate to a pre-heated pan lined with salt.
Cover and let it cook for 20-25 minutes or until the bread is brown and sounds hollow when tapped. 
Let the bread rest for 15-20 minutes before cutting into it.

title: Appalam Vatha kulambu
cooking_instructions:
Soak the tamarind for an hour in 1 litre of water
Break each appalam into 4 pieces, deep fry in hot oil and set aside.
In a kadai, add gingelly oil and once it's hot add the tempering ingredients - mustard seeds, fenugreek, chana dal, curry leaves and whole red chilli.
Add turmeric powder and asafoetida once the mustard starts to crackle.
Add the sambar powder and mix it with the oil
Filter out the tamarind and add the tamarind water to the kadai.
Once the contents come to a rolling boil, add the appalams.
Simmer it for 10 more minutes until the kulambu becomes slightly thick and remove from heat.

title: Magilampoo Puttu
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the moong dal for 2 hours.
In a blender add the moong dal, salt, water and blent it to a batter consistency

Take an Idly pan and pour the batter.
Steam it for 15 minutes
Now melt the jaggery into a thin consistency
In a small kadai, add the ghee, cashewnut, coconut and saute it until it has a nice aroma
Rest it for 10 minutes and blend it into small pisces
our it over the puttu, now add this ghee mixture into the puttu and mix it

title: Al Faham Chicken
cooking_instructions:
Roast the spices for the Garam Masala.
Blend it and keep it aside.
Make a marinade with all the measured ingredients
Add the chicken and marinate well. Rest it for half an hour
In a blender add eggs, sugar, salt, vinegar, milk, garlic and half the amount of oil.
Add the oil gradually until the correct consistency
Thinly slice the red cabbage.
Add mayonnaise, milk maid, sugar, white pepper, black pepper and salt.
Mix it well and top it off with chopped pineapple.
Add salt to the base of your cooker/pot and create an elevation. 
Preheat the pot for 15 minutes
Now place the chicken inside the pot and cook it for 15 minutes both sides.
Serve it hot with a bread

title: Moru Moru Prawn Fry
cooking_instructions: Marinate the prawn with all the ingredients listed under marination. Refrigerate for 30 mins, if possible.
For the batter - whisk the ingredients until smooth.
Thaw/ de-frost the spring roll/ samosa sheets and cut them into thin strips like noodles.
Dip the prawn in the batter and coat it with the spring roll sheets, it should be wrapped not very tightly.

Deep fry in medium hot oil until crispy and golden brown. 
Serve hot with ketchup/ sweet chilli sauce/ mayo.

title: Kerala Banana Chips
cooking_instructions: Make 2 thin slits along the length of the Nendran banana. Make sure that the bananas are raw. Using the edge of the knife, peel the banana carefully from the slits.
In a large bowl or basin, add the water, salt, and turmeric powder. Mix to combine. Soak the peeled bananas in the salted water for at least 15 minutes.

Heat coconut oil in a Kadai on high flame. Using a mandolin or a slicer, slice the bananas directly into the oil. Fry them until the bubbling has subsided. Remove the chips onto a bowl lined with kitchen paper. Store them in an airtight container for up to 1 month.

title: Cookd Donne Veg Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of seeraga samba rice rice for 20-30 mins.In a pressure cooker, add the donne biryani paste and saute it on a low flame for a minute.
Add the vegetables and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add the paneer and mix gently.
Add 375 ml water and bring it to a boil.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the cooker.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook it on medium flame for 2 whistles and turn off the flame
Let the steam reduce gradually and allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Open the cooker, pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice gently. 
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Donne Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of seeraga samba rice rice for 20-30 mins.
In a pressure cooker, add the donne biryani paste and saute it on a low flame for a minute.
Add the chicken and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 375 ml water and bring it to a boil.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the cooker.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook it on medium flame for 2 whistles and turn off the flame.
Let the steam reduce gradually and allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Open the cooker, pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice gently. 
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Malabar Veg Biryani
cooking_instructions:
In another pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
Wash and soak 250g of kaima rice for 20-30 mins.
In a biryani pot, add the malabar biryani paste and saute for a minute.
Add the vegetables and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 1 cup (250 ml) of water and cook for 8-10 mins on a medium flame, until the consistency is thick again.
Add the paneer and mix to combine. 
Strain the cooked rice and add directly on top of the biryani masala and add 1/4 cup of the boiled rice water.
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves and fried cashews as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Malabar Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions:
In another pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done
Wash and soak 250g of kaima rice for 20-30 mins.
In a biryani pot, add the malabar biryani paste and saute for a minute.
Add the chicken and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 1 cup (250 ml) of water and cook for 8-10 mins on a medium flame, until the consistency is thick again.
Strain the cooked rice and add directly on top of the biryani masala and add 1/4 cup of the boiled rice water.
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves, fried cashews and fried raisins as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

In a biryani pot, add the hyderabadi biryani paste and saute for a minute.

Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

cooking_instructions:

Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
In a biryani pot, add the hyderabadi biryani paste and saute for a minute.

Add 1 cup (250 ml) of water and cook for 8-10 mins on a medium flame, until the consistency is thick again.

title: Cookd Donne Mushroom Biryani (pressure cooker)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of seeraga samba rice rice for 20-30 mins.
In a pressure cooker, add the donne biryani paste and saute it on a low flame for a minute.
Add the mushrooms and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 375 ml water and bring it to a boil.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the cooker.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook it on medium flame for 2 whistles and turn off the flame.
Let the steam reduce gradually and allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Open the cooker, pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice gently. 
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani (pressure cooker)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of Basumati rice for 20-30 mins.
In another pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
In a pressure cooker, add the Hyderabadi biryani paste and saute for a minute.
Add the mutton and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 1 cup (250 ml) of water and cook for 15 mins on a medium flame until the mutton is tender.
Open the cooker and cook until the consistency is thick again.Strain the cooked rice and add directly on top of the biryani masala and add 1/4 cup of the boiled rice water.
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves, fried cashews and fried raisins as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Minestrone Soup
cooking_instructions: Roast the tomatoes over a flame, peel them, and cut them into dice. Set aside.
In a pot, heat oil and add the onions, garlic, and celery. Saute until the onions go translucent.
Add the tomato puree and cook until the raw flavor goes for about 5 mins. Add the carrot, beans, and zucchini, Saute for 3 mins.
Add the diced tomatoes, salt, oregano, and black pepper powder. Pour in the water, add the pasta and simmer for 10 mins. Until the vegetables are tender and pasta is cooked. Finish with basil.

title: Cookd Malabar Mutton Biryani (pressure cooker)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of kaima rice for 20-30 mins.
In another pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
Add the mutton and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 1 cup (250 ml) of water and cook for 15 mins on a medium flame until the mutton is tender.
Open the cooker and cook until the consistency is thick again.
Strain the cooked rice and add directly on top of the biryani masala and add 1/4 cup of the boiled rice water.
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves, fried cashews and fried raisins as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Donne Mutton Biryani (pressure cooker)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes
To a pressure cooker add the Cookd Donne biryani paste and saute for a minutes
Add the mutton and mix to combine well
Add 1 Cup of water and bring to a boil. 
Cover and pressure cook for 15 minutes, on a medium low heat. 
Once the pressure has naturally released, open the cooker and bring the mixture to a boil.
Cook and reduce for 6 - 7 minutes mins on a medium flame, until the consistency is thick again.
Add the soaked and strained rice, give it a gentle mix
Cover the cooker and pressure cook it for 2 whistles on a medium flame.
Cover the cooker and pressure cook it for 2 whistles on a medium flame.
Turn off the flame after 2 whistles and let the steam reduce gradually for about 10 minutes.
Open the cooker, fluff the rice and serve it hot with raita.

title: Cookd Malabar Mutton Biryani (open pot)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the kaima rice for 20 minutes.
In a pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Add the soaked and strained rice and give it a mix.
Boil for 5 - 6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
Strain and reserve the cooking water
In a biryani pot, add the malabar biryani paste and saute for a minute.
Add the mutton and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 2 ½  cups of water and cook for 45 - 60 minutes on a medium flame, or until the mutton is tender. Add more water if neded.
Stir and reduce until the consistency is thick again.
Layer the rice on top of the biryani paste
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves and fried cashews as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani (open pot)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the basmati rice for 20 minutes.
In a pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Add the soaked and strained rice and give it a mix.
Boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
Strain and reserve the cooking water
In a biryani pot, add the hyderabadi biryani paste and saute for a minute.
Add the mutton and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 2 ½  cups of water and cook for 45 - 60 minutes on a medium flame, or until the mutton is tender. Add more water if neded.
Stir and reduce until the consistency is thick again, around 6 - 7 minutes.
Layer the rice on top of the biryani paste
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves and fried cashews as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Ajantha Chicken Pulao
cooking_instructions:
For the rice, add some oil and ghee to a pot. Once hot, add the whole spices and cook for 1 - 2 minutes on a medium heat or until fragrant.
Add the onions, salt and the green chillis. 
Cook for 7 - 8 minutes, or until the onions start to turn golden brown. 
Add the curry leaves, and ginger garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes. 
Add the turmeric powder followed by the coriander leaves and mint leaves. Cook for 30 seconds, or until they start to will. 
Add water and bring to a boil. 
Add the rice and stir gently. 
Cover tightly and cook on a low heat for 12 minutes.
To make the chicken, add oil to a kadai. Once hot, add the whole spices and cook for 1 - 2 minutes, or until fragrant. 
Add the onions, salt, curry leaves and green chillis and saute for 6 - 8 minutes on a medium heat, or until softened and starting to turn golden.
Add the ginger garlic paste, followed by the tomatoes and mix to combine well. 
Cook for an additional 4 - 5 minutes, or until the tomatoes have softened and have become like a paste. 
Add the spice powders and mix to combine well. 
Add the chicken followed by water and bring to a boil. 
Let the chicken simmer for 15 minutes and then reduce until a thick gravy is achieved. 
To assemble, add some ghee to a frying pan. Add cashews and fry until lightly golden.
Add curry leaves, some of the gravy and a chicken piece to the pan and saute it.
Once done, let the rice rest for 15 minutes before uncovering.
Fluff the rice.
Once the chicken starts to get crispy remove it from the pan and plate along with the rice.

title: Sri Lankan Cheese Kothu
cooking_instructions:
In a pan pour ghee and grill the parottas until golden brown and crispy. 
Tear the parottas into small pieces and set aside.
In a mixing bowl add the chicken, salt, black pepper, garam masala and cumin powder, mix and set aside.
In a wok/deep pan add butter and saute the chicken on a high flame until golden brown and cooked through. 
Take the chicken out add in the spring onion whites, and saute for 10 seconds, add in the ginger garlic paste and cook until the raw flavour disappears (around 10 seconds) 
Add in the green chillies and toss. Add in the tomato, cabbage, carrot and capsicum juliennes and toss until thoroughly combined. 
Add in the eggs and scramble them. 
Pour in milk and bring it to a boil. Add the chilli flakes and garam masala, curd and the grated cheese. 
Add in the parotta and toss. The desired consistency is a kothu parotta consistency. 
Garnish with curry leaves and coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Easy Paneer Shawarma
cooking_instructions:
To make the hot sauce, boil together the ingredients until the garlic is soft and mashable, a minimum of 20 mins.
Strain and blend with the remaining water as needed, until smooth. Strain the sauce, if needed.
To make the garlic mayonnaise, blend all ingredients until it is smooth except the oil and lemon, add them and pulse blend till thick and smooth.  
Add all the spices under marination in a mixer jar and blend to a fine powder.
Mix curd, blended spice powder and grated onion and garlic.
Add 2 tbsp of this marination to the paneer, and mix well. 
On a hot pan, add oil and cook until charred outside/ you can also grill it directly on an open flame. 
Remove from heat and cut into long strips.
To assemble the shawarma, place the pita bread, add the sliced paneer, sliced onion and tomato, and squeeze the hot sauce and garlic mayonnaise on top.
Roll the shawarma with parchment paper and serve.

title: Chocolate Biscuit Roll
cooking_instructions:
Crush the biscuits into large chunks. 
Melt butter on a low flame and turn off the flame. 
Add chocolate and melt until completely smooth. 
Add coffee (optional), cocoa powder,  milk, and vanilla extract, and mix until combined.
Add crushed cookies, and nuts and mix until combined.
 Spread half the mixture onto plastic wrap and shape it into a log. Roll the plastic wrap and twist the ends to seal. Roll back and forth few times to make the log evenly round. Repeat with the remaining mixture. 
Refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours until firm. 
Remove the plastic wrap, and dust with powdered sugar from all sides (or roll in powdered sugar). 
Brush off excess sugar and cut into discs. 
Store refrigerated for up to a week.

title: Cheese Stuffed Mushrooms
cooking_instructions: For the cheese mixture, combine the ingredients as listed and mix until well combined.
To make the batter: combine the flour, corn starch, salt, and pepper with water to make a thick batter.
Fill the de-stemmed mushroom cavities with the cheese stuffing.
Dip the stuffed mushrooms in the batter, coat in bread crumbs. And repeat the process to double coat the mushrooms. Refrigerate for 20 mins.
Heat oil in a pot. Fry in a medium flame until golden brown and crispy, about 2 minutes

title: Poori and Naatukodi Pulusu
cooking_instructions:
Dry roast all the ingredients required for the masala powder and blend into a powder. It shouldn’t be too fine. 
In a large pot, add oil. Once hot, add the whole spices and fry for 1 - 2 minutes on a medium heat, or until fragrant.
Add the onions, green chilli, salt and curry leaves, and saute for 6 - 7 minutes on a medium heat or until starting to turn golden, Add the ginger garlic paste followed by the turmeric powder and coriander powder. 
Mix to combine well and saute for a minute, or until the raw smell of the ginger garlic paste goes. 
Add the country chicken and mix well. Add the red chilli powder and half of the prepared masala powder. MIx well. 
Once the chicken starts to stick to the bottom of the pot, add water and bring the a boil. 
Cover and cook for 20 minutes. 
Once the chicken is 70 percent cooked, add the tomatoes and curry leaves. 
Bring to a simmer and cook for an additional 20 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked. 
Add the remaining half of the prepared masala powder along with coriander leaves
To make the puris, roll out the balls of dough into evenly sized circles, that are around 3-4 mm thick. Fry the puris in hot oil, until they puff up and are golden, around 30 seconds. 
Serve the hot puri with the hot naatu kodi pulusu and enjoy.

title: Vattayappam
cooking_instructions:
Take a pan and make a mixture of 3 tsp of rice powder and water
In a mixer jar, mix all the measured ingredients with the mixture.
Add the mixture gradually to get a dosa/idly batter consistency.
Rest the batter for at least 3-4 hours for fermentation. 
Brush the pans with butter.
Pour the batter into the pans leaving space for the batter to rise. 
Make sure the steamer is hot before placing the pans. 
Steam it for 20 minutes on a medium flame.
Cool down the dish before serving.

title: Chinna Vengaya Chutney
cooking_instructions:
In a pan, add oil, dry red chilli and saute until it becomes slightly black.
In a mixer jar, add the roasted dry red chilli, rock salt, tamarind and blend it into a fine paste.
In a pan, add gingelly oil, mustard seeds, urad dal and fry until it pops.
Now add the shallots and saute for 2 minutes.
Now add the red chilli paste and let it cook for 5 minutes.

title: Pumpkin and Carrot Pasta
cooking_instructions:
To cook the pasta, bring water to a boil. 
Once boiling, add salt.
Add the pasta and cook according the package instructions.
Strain once the pasta is cooked.
In a pressure cooker, add the ghee. Once hot, add the pumpkin and carrot and saute for 2 - 3 minutes or until starting to soften.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Close and pressure cook on a medium heat for 12 minutes.
Once the pressure has released, open the pressure cooker and transfer the contents to a blender.
Once the contents have cooled sufficiently, blend into a smooth paste.
Add the blended sauce to a pan, along with strained pasta and toss to combine well.
Add the pasta seasoning and mix to combine.
Optional add some grated cheese on top.

title: Chilli Omelette
cooking_instructions:
In a bowl break in the eggs and whisk until totally mixed. 
In a non-stick pan pour oil and add in the whisked eggs, cook the eggs until well done and take them out.
Cut the eggs into cubes and set aside. 
Add all the ingredients for the batter in another mixing bowl and whisk it until thoroughly combined and lump-free. 
Add the eggs to the batter coat them thoroughly.
Deep fry them on a moderate flame for 2-3 minutes or until golden brown and crispy. 
In a wok, pour oil and add in ginger and garlic. Saute on a high flame until golden brown and fragrant. 
Add in the chopped onions, green chillies and spring onion whites. 
Saute until the onion turns soft and fragrant. 
Pour in the sauces and cook on a high flame until the sauce reduces. 
Add in the fried eggs and toss until thoroughly coated.
Garnish with spring onion greens and serve hot.

title: Bellam Pulusu
cooking_instructions:
To a pan, add oil. Once hot, add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal and curry leaves. 
Once the mustard seeds splatter, add the green chillis followed by the onions and salt.
Saute for 6 - 7 minutes or until the onions are starting to turn golden. 
Add the brinjal and ladyfingers and saute for 2 minutes. 
Add the bottle gourd and sweet potato.
Add the water and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes, or until the vegetables have started softened. 
Add the tamarind pulp and the jaggery and simmer for 5 more minutes. 
Garnish with curry leaves and coriander leaves. 
Serve hot with rice and appalam.

title: Nei Kucchi Mittai
cooking_instructions:
Dry roast the cashew nuts on a low flame, until light brown and cool completely. 
Pulse blend into a powder and add in a bowl.
Grease a steel plate and set aside
In a pan, heat the sugar, ghee, and water until it reaches a golden brown colour (to test, when added to water it must become hard and crisp). You must work very fast, the caramel changes colour very quickly. 
Switch off the flame and add it into the cashew powder
On a greased plate, spread this evenly into a rectangle shape. 
And make slits with a knife, in stick shapes. 
Cool completely and wrap individually in butter paper.

title: Meen Polichathu
cooking_instructions:
Make a curry paste of garlic, ginger, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, black pepper powder and salt.
Use ¼ of the curry paste and marinate the fish.
Shallow fry this fish on both sides and keep it aside.
In the same pan, saute the shallots, onion, ginger, green chilli and tomato.
Add the remaining paste.
Now pour the coconut milk with chopped tamarind.
Add the fish and let it simmer.
Place a sprig of curry leaves and fish onto a banana leaf and tie it together.
Shallow fry it on a pan.

title: Gym Bro Mixture
cooking_instructions:
Add all the ingredients one by one until golden brown, well-roasted and crispy in a heavy bottom kadhai, and set aside.
Each ingredient takes 5-6 minutes each. 
Add all the ingredients to the pan, add the powdered spices, and toss until thoroughly combined, with this stove switched off. 
Let the mixture cool down completely before serving.

title: Paneer Pasanda
cooking_instructions: Combine the mint and coriander in a mixer grinder until it is ground, with 2 tbsp of water.
Combine this paste with the grated khoya, cashew nuts, raisins, chopped green chilies. Season with salt, cumin powder, and chaat masala.
Cut the paneer into thick slices and stuff the khoya mixture in the middle.
For the besan batter: Combine the besan, salt, chili powder, and turmeric powder with ¼ cup of water, or a little more as needed to make a thick batter.
Dip this stuffed paneer in the besan batter carefully and deep fry until golden in hot oil. Cut this paneer into triangles and set aside.
For the gravy, add cardamom in hot oil, saute for a minute and then brown the onions and add the ginger garlic paste and saute until the raw flavour goes, about 2 mins.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cashew nuts. Saute until soft, about 5 mins. Add the chilli powder and garam masala, season with salt and sugar.
Pour 1.5 cups of water and let it simmer for 10 mins.
Cool the mixture and blend in a mixer grinder and strain the gravy.
Heat a tbsp of ghee and add cumin seeds, once aromatic, add ¼ tsp of chilli powder and then add the gravy. Add ½ cup of water, mix well and simmer for 5 mins.
Finish with Kasuri methi and fresh cream. Serve the gravy in a utensil, place the fried paneer and garnish with cream and chopped coriander leaves.

title: Crispy Fried Oyster Mushroom
cooking_instructions:
Tear the mushrooms into large pieces. 
In a bowl, add all the ingredients for the marination and mix. Add the mushroom and mix well to coat evenly. Marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, if possible. 
In another bowl/plate, season the cornstarch with salt and pepper. 
Add the pieces of mushroom to the cornstarch and coat them individually. Squeeze them lightly to make compact pieces and remove the excess starch. 
Deep-fry them on medium-low heat just until they start to turn golden brown. Remove them from the oil and set aside on a cooling tray/rack for 3-4 minutes.
Heat the oil again over high heat. Add the mushroom back into the oil (in batches) and cook until crispy and golden brown. This will take around 1 minute. Serve with mayonnaise and lemon wedges.

title: Instant Sambar Mix
cooking_instructions:
In a thick-bottomed pan, add the copra or desiccated coconut and roast until lightly golden, make sure not to roast the coconut over and set aside. 
Add all the other ingredients one by one and roast on a very low flame until all the moisture is evaporated and nicely roasted. 
Add the toor dal and roast it for 1-2 minutes on a very low flame, we do not want any colour on the toor dal.
Let the mixture cool down completely before blending it into a fine powder.
Add 4 tbsp of the prepared instant sambar powder and saute for 10 seconds. 
Pour water and bring it to a boil.
Cover and cook for 6-7 minutes or until all the vegetables are mushy and the sambar is thick. 
Finish the sambar with coriander leaves and a simple mustard red chilli and curry leaf tempering.

title: Ayira Meen Kulambu
cooking_instructions: Make a paste of shallots, grated coconut, cumin seeds and bengal gram

Add gingelly oil in a pot and add shallots, garlic and chopped tomato. 
Saute it well and pour the coconut paste into the pot. 
Next, add coriander powder and red chilli powder.

Mix it thoroughly until it’s not raw and you can add tamarind water and salt.
When the oil is separated you can add water and keep it boiling.
Lastly, finish it off by adding fish and take it out of the stove. Let it cook within the pot

title: Kettle Picha Potha Chicken Varuval
cooking_instructions:
Add water to the kettle and bring to a boil.
Once boiling, add the chicken breast to the kettle and let it cook for 10 minutes.
Once cooked, remove from the kettle and discard the water.
Shred the chicken into bite sized pieces. 
To the kettle, add oil, onion and garlic. 
Turn it on and shake to prevent burning, add a little water if needed. 
Once the onions are soft, add the chicken, followed by salt, red chilli powder, black pepper powder  and turmeric powder.
Mix or shake well and turn the kettle on.
Add the eggs and mix to combine.

title: Kaluththupudi kari
cooking_instructions:
To a cooker, add oil, fennel seeds, cinnamon and saute for a few seconds.
Now add onion, garlic and saute for 3 minutes.
Add tomato and Saute for 3 minutes.
Now add red chilli powder, Turmeric Powder, Coriander Powder, salt and saute for 5 minutes on a medium flame.
Now add the mutton pieces and give it a mix.
Add water, pressure cook it for 20 minutes on a medium flame.
In a mixer jar, add coconut, fennel seeds, water and grind it to a fine paste.
Once pressure gets down, open the cooker and set asid.
In an iron dosa tawa, add coconut oil and the cooked mutton pisces.
Now squeeze the coconut paste on top of the mutton pisces and roast it well.
Take out from the tawa, serve it hot with some diced onions on top of it.

title: Tumbler Butter Biscuit
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl add the butter and sugar and whisk until thoroughly combined and the butter turns light (around 5-6 minutes)
Add in the flour and mix it very gently until combined, the texture should be like wet sand. 
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and shape it into a log. 
Freeze the dough for 20-30 minutes or until firm. 
Cut the log into discs, arrange it on a plate and place it in a deep container lined with salt, cover and let it bake for 17-20 minutes or until the edges turn light brown. 
Let the biscuit rest for 10-15 minutes before consuming.

title: Eggless Muttaimittai
cooking_instructions:
Make breadcrumbs from fresh crust-less bread and set aside
Soak the almonds for a couple of hours and peel them. 
Blend the almonds with water to make a smooth paste. 
In a pan, mix the milk, sugar, cardamom powder, custard powder, bread crumbs and almond paste. 
Simmer and bring to a boil. Add the ghee
Cook until it is thick, about 2-3 mins. 
Transfer this mixture to a greased baking tray and top with chopped almonds and a sprinkle of sugar. 
Bake in a preheated oven at 180 C for about 20-30 minutes until golden brown on top. 
Cool completely, slice, and serve.

title: Squid Roast
cooking_instructions:
In a pan, add mustard seeds, fennel seeds, dry red chilli and curry leaves. 
Add julienne of green chilli, garlic and ginger and saute it for a few minutes.
After it is cooked, add onion and shallots. Saute it well.
Add coriander powder, kashmiri red chilli powder, turmeric powder and black pepper powder. Cook it well.
Blend tomatoes into a paste and pour it into the pot. 
Pour some water with salt and let it boil.
Add the squid with lemon juice and cook it for 3-4 minutes.
Open the lid and roast it till it’s thick.

title: Kootu Curry
cooking_instructions: Wash the chana dal and soak for 1 hour.
Pressure cook the soaked chana dal with ½ tsp of salt, ¼ tsp of turmeric, and 1 cup of water, for 1 whistle

Cook the yam in 1 cup of water, with ¼ tsp of turmeric powder and ½ tsp of salt for 4 minutes, or until it is half done. Add the raw banana and cook for a further 3 minutes, or until both the vegetables are cooked.
Heat coconut oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and when they splutter, add shallots and curry leaves. Saute until the shallots begin to brown.
Add the red chili powder and saute. Add the grated coconut. Saute for 1 minute on medium heat.
Add the cooked chana dal without the excess water. Add the cooked yam and raw banana. Mix well and cook for 1 more minute.

title: Uppukandam Sambar
cooking_instructions:
Marinate the mutton with turmeric powder and salt. 
Tie the mutton pieces in a thread and dry under the sun for 3 days.
The mutton pieces will shrink into half the original weight. (if it's 750g, it'll shrink into 300g)
In a pressure cooker, add all the ingredients mentioned above.
Cover and cook it for 15 minutes on a medium flame. (4 to 5 wistles)
In a kadai , add oil, mustard seeds, urad dal, cumin seeds, and curry leaves. Saute it well.
Now add shallots, tomato, veggies and saute for 5 minutes.
Add spice powders, water and simmer it for 5 minutes.
Now, add the ingredients inside the cooker to this kadai and give it a mix.
Add some salt with coriander leaves and let it simmer.

title: Aatukaal Cake
cooking_instructions: In a mixer, add the sugar and cardamom powder and blend into powder.
In a bowl,add an egg , sugar powder and mix it well.

Now add the rest of all the ingredients and mix it well to a tight dough consistency.
Cover and rest it for 15 minutes.
Now take a small ball from the dough and deep fry it on a low flame.

title: Guntur Fried Rice
cooking_instructions:
To a wok or pot, add some oil. Once hot, add the garlic and let it fry for 2 minutes, or until golden. 
Add the cumin seeds, mustard seeds, peanuts, curry leaves and dry red chilli and cook for 1 more minute. 
Add the chicken and salt and mix to combine.
Cook the chicken on a medium high heat for 3 - 4 minutes, until some colour is achieved. Ensure to mix every now and then, to prevent burning.
Add the carrots, beans and cabbage and mix to combine well. 
Add the avakaya and mix well. 
Add the rice along with more avakaya and salt, and mix to combine well. 
Add the soy sauce and toss 
Garnish with coriander leaves, lemon wedges, papadom, fried egg and more avakaya.

title: Appalam Chutney
cooking_instructions:
In a kadai, heat 1 cup of oil. 
One by one fry the ingredients - appalams and red chillies. 
Add the shallots first, then tamarind, and finally curry leaves. 
Drain all on tissue paper and allow it to cool.
Add the ingredients to a blender and pulse blend until coarse. 
Transfer to a bowl and then add coconut oil and salt - mix well. 
Serve with hot rice.

title: Gym Bro Noodles
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl, break in 3 eggs, add salt and black pepper and whisk thoroughly. 
In a non-stick pan, pour 1 tsp oil and pour in the eggs. 
Cook it on a medium flame until cooked through and tender. Make sure you don’t over cook the eggs. 
When the omelette is warm, roll and cut the eggs into thin noodle-like strips and set aside.
For the stir fry, pour oil and add the chicken strips, cook on a high flame for 30 seconds, tossing continuously. 
Add in all the cut veggies and saute on a high flame for 20 seconds. 
Make a well in the middle and add the ginger garlic paste and all the sauces. 
Give it a good mix and add in the omelette strips. 
Toss on a high flame for 10 seconds and serve hot.

title: Tharid (Bread and Mutton Stew)
cooking_instructions:
Saute the spices inside the cooker with some ghee.
Add onion and ginger garlic paste. Saute it well for 5 minutes. 
Now, add cumins seeds, turmeric powder, coriander powder and garam masala. Fry it well. 
Add the mutton nalli and boneless pieces. Mix it in with some sliced tomatoes and close the lid. Pressure cook it for 5 whistles on low flame.
Open the lid, add the vegetables and pressure cook it for 2 more whistles on high flame. 
Garnish it with coriander leaves.
Steam the bread using a steamer until it’s soggy and soft.

title: Pavakkai Varuval
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the split urad dal, cumin seeds and curry leaves. Saute until brown. Add the garlic and shallots and saute until golden brown.
Add the bitter gourd, powdered spices, salt, and jaggery. Continue to saute stirring constantly, on a high flame until it turns dry and crispy.
Finally, add the crushed peanuts, chopped curry leaves, and mix.

title: Seppankizhangu roast
cooking_instructions:
Boil the colocasia in hot water for 20 minutes.
Once it is cooked remove from the water, peel off the skin and cut it into round pieces.
Now add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt to the colocasia and mix it well.
In a pan, add oil and add the colocasia.
Roast it for 10 minutes.

title: Fufu and Mutton Curry
cooking_instructions:
Wash the tapioca root thoroughly and peel. 
Cut the tapioca into cubes and add to water to prevent discolouration.
Add the cubed tapioca along with water and blend into a very smooth paste. 
Add the paste to a pot along with salt and cook on a medium heat while stirring continuously.
The paste will significantly thicken and smoothen after 10 minutes.
Let the fufu cool before removing and shaping. 
Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds and whole black pepper to a mortar and pestle and crush to a coarse powder.
To make the mutton curry, add oil to a pressure cooker. Once hot, add the cinnamon, star anise, cloves and cardamom. 
Saute for 1 minute or until fragrant.
Add the onions, green chilli and curry leaves. Cook for 7 - 8 minutes or until deeply golden brown.
Add half of the powder now, to toast in the oil. 
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, or until the raw smell goes. 
Add the tomatoes and mix to combine well. 
Cook for an additional 5 minutes, or until the tomatoes become soft and paste like.
Add the mutton and mix to combine well. 
Add water and bring to a boil. 
Add salt to season. 
Pressure cook for 20 minutes.
Let the pressure naturally release. 
Add the coriander leaves and the remaining coarse powder and mix well to combine. 
Serve hot with the fufu.

title: Easy Paneer Puff Roll
cooking_instructions:
For the easy puff dough - 
In a mixing bowl, add maida, salt, sugar and water. Mix well. 
Add water, melted butter 2 tbsp and mix to bring together a rough dough. 
Cover and rest for 10 mins. 
Knead the dough until smooth and rest again for 10 minutes. Apply 1 tbsp of butter. 
Portion into 6-8 pcs. Dip in melted butter and rest.
For the filling - 
Heat oil in a pan. Add the onions and cook until translucent. Add the ginger garlic paste and green chillies, and cook until the flavour is no longer raw.
Add the capsicum and cook until tender.
Add the powdered spices and salt and mix well to combine.
Add the paneer and mix well. Finish with chopped coriander leaves. Keep aside to cool. 
Roll out each roundel as thin and large as possible. Stretch gently. Drizzle some butter. 
Place some filling closer to one side. 
Drizzle 1 tbsp of melted butter, apply and fold in itself. Drizzle more butter after each fold. 
Roll like how a spring roll is made (sides in and then rolled gently). 
Place this on a baking sheet. Repeat with all rolls and the remaining filling. 
Bake in a preheated oven at 180C for 25-30 mins until golden brown. Cool slightly and serve!

title: Vethalai Kulfi
cooking_instructions:
Heat a heavy-bottomed Kadai and bring the milk to a boil and continue to simmer on medium heat. Keep stirring at intervals to prevent milk from sticking to the bottom of the pan. Simmer until the volume of the milk is reduced by half. Should take around 30 minutes.
Add sugar, and continue to simmer for 5 more minutes.
Remove from heat and allow it to cool.
Add betel leaf, camphor, and the cooled down reduced milk in a Mixer jar and blend into a coarse paste.

Strain the betel leaf mixture into the milk, gulkand and mix it well.
Once it reaches room temperature, transfer to kulfi molds and freeze for at least 10 hours. After 3 hours, if necessary, insert a wooden stick to use as a handle.
Unmould the kulfi, sprinkle the chopped nuts, rose petals and serve.

title: Chapati Sandwich
cooking_instructions:
Add the ingredients mentioned to the mince and mix it thoroughly. 
To make the cucumber raita, grate the cucumber.
Add the grated cucumber to curd, along with lemon juice and salt.
Mix to combine well and use as a dipping sauce. 
Make a straight slit from the center of the chapati to the edge. 
Place the cheese and mince on the left side of the chapati and flatten it out into a triangle.
Fold the chapati over itself to form a little triangle pocket.
To a pan on low flame, add oil and place the chapati sandwich.. Cook for 7 - 8 minutes or until deeply golden on one side.
Flip the sandwich and follow the same process on the other side.
Once deeply golden on both sides, sear the exposed meat side until golden and crispy 
Once done, remove and let it cool slightly.

title: Oats Ela Ada
cooking_instructions:
Roast the oats and blend it into fine powder.
Mix oats powder, rice flour and salt into a wet dough.
Melt the jaggery with some water and keep it aside.
Add ghee into a pan and add grated coconut. Saute it well.
Now, add the melted jaggery, cardamom powder and diced bananas.
Apply ghee onto the banana leaf and spread the wet dough on top. 
Make sure it has the same thickness all over. 
Add the filling on one side and fold into half. 
Steam it for 15 minutes.

title: Pepper BBQ Marinade
cooking_instructions:
Roast all the whole spices for 1 - 2 minutes, or until fragrant. 
Let them cool.
Add the roasted spices along with the powder to a blender and blend into a powder.

To cook the protein of your choice, take 2 tbsp of the marinade, splash water and make it into a paste.  
Add 200g of chicken or paneer and mix thoroughly. 
Let it marinate for 30 minutes.
Grill the protein of choice on a medium-high heat and serve hot
Assemble with your favorite foods

title: Steamed Eggs
cooking_instructions:
Add all the ingredients required for the eggs to a bowl and beat with a fork, just until the egg whites and yellows are well mixed. 
Add the eggs to a heatsafe bowl and tap on the table gently to remove any air bubbles.

Place the eggs into a steamer and steam on a low heat for 10 - 12 minutes, or until the eggs are set. To test this, put a spoon on the surface of the eggs, if it stays on the surface, the eggs have set.

To make the tempering, heat some oil. 
Add the garlic, followed by the urad dal. 
Once fragrant and golden, add the rest of the ingredients and fry.

Cut the eggs and add a spoon of soy sauce.
Add the hot tempering on top of the eggs and enjoy hot with rice.

title: Mutton Paya Soup
cooking_instructions: Grind all the ingredients under to grind into a smooth paste.
In a pressure cooker, cook the mutton legs with Gingelly Oil, turmeric and 6 cups or 1.5 litres of water for 7 whistles.
Add this paste, coriander leaves, salt to the pressure cooker and cook for a further 5 whistles in medium heat. Let the pressure cool down on its own.
Add pepper powder and adjust salt if necessary. Finally, garnish with more coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Kurukku Kalan
cooking_instructions: Grind the grated coconut, green chilies, and cumin seeds. Grind into a thick paste, adding water as needed. Add the curd and grind again to a fine paste.
Cut the Nendran banana in four lengthwise and remove the seeds. Cut into cubes.
Boil the bananas with turmeric powder, chili powder, salt, and water for 10 minutes.
Add the coconut paste to the pot and mix well. When it starts to boil, remove it from the heat.

In another pan, heat the coconut oil and add mustard seeds. When it starts to splutter, add the fenugreek seeds and allow them to splutter. Add dry red chilies and curry leaves. Add this tempering to the Kalan. Serve with rice.

title: Tumbler- Bakery Honey Cake
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl combine all the wet ingredients together along with the sugar and whisk until thoroughly mixed.
Add in the maida, baking powder, soda and gently mix.

Grease and flour a baking tray and add in the batter. 
In a deep pan, pour in salt and let it pre heat on a low medium flame for 10 minutes. 
Add in the tray into the pre heated pan, cover and let it cook on a low medium flame for 35-40 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean. 
Let the cake rest for 10 minutes.
In the meantime, add in the sugar, water and honey for the soak, once the sugar dissolves, romove it from the heat and spon it on top of the cake.
While the cake soaks, add in the jam and loosen it up with some water.
Top the cake with the jam and sprinkle some desiccated coconut on top and serve.

title: Pistachio Kunafa Kesari
cooking_instructions:
Heat ghee in a pan, fry the nuts until golden, and remove them. 
In the same pan, fry the fine vermicelli until golden brown, and remove it. 
 Add a tbsp of ghee and add the rava, roast for 5 mins on a medium flame.

Add the water to the rava. 
Mix until the water is absorbed. About 4-5 mins. Mixing continuously. 
Add the sugar on a low flame and mix until the sugar has dissolved.
Keep simmering on a low flame while stirring constantly until the Kesari has thickened.
Finish with ghee, the fried nuts, and rose water.
add the pistachios to a blender with some sugar, blitz into a powder. Add some neutral oil and blend into a fine paste. (any nut butter of choice will work for this recipe
Mix the vermicelli and 2-3 tbsp of the pistachio butter together

For the topping - melt dark chocolate on a double boiler/ in a microwave. 
For assembling - in a bowl, add some kesari, top with the pistachio kunafa filling and finally a thin layer of dark chocolate on top. 
Set in the fridge for 10-15 minutes until the chocolate sets.

title: Thari Kanji
cooking_instructions:
Pour some ghee in a pan and fry the rava until it’s roasted.
To completely cook the rava, add water.
Now add the milk and mix it thoroughly. Make sure there’s no lumps.
Add sugar, salt and cardamom powder. Mix it well. 
Switch off the stove and add coconut milk. 
For tempering, saute some raisins, shallots and cashews in ghee. 
Pour this over the kanji and mix it well.

title: Mersal Chicken
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl add all the ingredients except oil into a mixing bowl and mix everything thoroughly, or directly add everything into a pot and mix thoroughly
Saute the chicken on a high flame for 2 minutes.

Pour water and let it cook on a medium flame for 10 minutes or until the chicken is thoroughly cooked and the gravy is fully reduced. 
Garnish with coriander leaves are serve hot with chapatis, dosas, idlies or rice.

title: Cheesy Mushroom Bread roll
cooking_instructions:
For the filling, heat the butter in a pan and saute the garlic and onions until translucent. 
Add the chopped mushrooms, salt and sugar and cook until dry again. Add the oregano and chilli flakes.
Sprinkle the maida and mix well. 
Pour the milk and make a thick mixture. Finish with cheese, after switching off the flame. 
Cool this mixture on a plate.
For the batter, mix together maida, salt and water to form a slightly runny batter. Keep the breadcrumbs on a separate plate.
To stuff, cut the edges of the bread and wet lightly with water/ milk. Press two slices together. 
Place the stuffing in the middle and roll it tightly, pinching the edges and ends to seal it.
Dip the rolls first in the batter and then in the breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry in oil until it is golden brown on all sides. Turn it occasionally so that the colour is even. 
Serve it with tomato ketchup or a dip of your choice.

title: Devil chutney
cooking_instructions:
In a mixer jar, add the onions and blend into fine paste. 
Remove the onion paste and set aside
Now add all the other ingredients to the mixer jar and blend into a fine paste.
Add the onion paste to this mixture and blend it for a few seconds.

title: Elaneer Rasam
cooking_instructions: In a mixer jar add all the ingredients and blend into a coarse paste and set aside.
In a bowl, add the tamarind, pour water and let it soak for 10-15 minutes

In a deep pan or a kadhai, pour ghee and add the mustard seeds, dried red chilli, urad dal and curry leaves. 
Once they splutter, add in the garlic, tomato and saute.

Once aromatic, add the prepared paste and cook on a medium flame for 2-3 minutes or until the raw flavour disappears. 
Pour the prepared tamarind water and bring it to a boil. 
Cover and let it boil for 5-6 minutes.
Pour in the tender coconut water, garnish it with coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: No Oven Cupcake
cooking_instructions:
Add all the ingredients required for the cupcake to a blender and blend until combined well. 
Oil your intended baking vessel and dust with cocoa powder. Remember to dust off any excess powder. 
Pour the mixture, to fill ¾ of the vessel.
In a deep pan, pour in salt to cover the base, and let it preheat on a medium flame for 10 minutes. Add something to provide some height so the baking vessel isn't directly touching the salt.
Place the baking vessel into the pre heated pan, cover and let it cook on a low medium flame for 15 - 20 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean. 
Let it rest for 10 minutes. 
Using a knife or a spoon, gently go around the edges to release the cupcake from the vessel. It should come out smoothly. 
Serve and enjoy warm!

title: Brain Fry
cooking_instructions:
In a kadai add oil, mustard seeds, urad dal, cinnamon and saute it. 
Now add onion, tomato and saute for 5 minutes.
Now add the spice powders, salt and cook for a few minutes. 
Now add the mutton brain with some water. Cover and cook on medium low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the grated coconut and  pepper, saute for a minute and serve it hot!

title: Cookd Marina Fish Fry Kit- Whole fish
cooking_instructions:
Add 1 pouch (75 g) masala to a bowl with 7 tbsp (100 ml) water, add juice from 1 lemon and mix to form a thick paste.
Apply the marinade on the fish and spread it evenly. Let it marinate for 30 minutes for better results.
Heat a pan, add oil and sear the fish on a medium flame for 4 minutes on each side.
