title: Navapalam Chutney
cooking_instructions:
In a bowl of water, add salt and wash the jamun, strain and take it out.
De seed the jamun and transfer the pulp into a mixer jar.
Now add coconut, green chilli, garlic, ginger, salt, Asafoetida and blend into a paste.
Serve it along with idly, dosa or chapati.

title: Veg Paaya
cooking_instructions:
Wash and peel the mudavattukal kilangu. Chop some into tiny cubes, retain some as larger pieces. 
In a pan, heat oil and add the fennel seeds, cumin seeds, peppercorns, chillies, cashew nuts and curry leaves. Sauté for 2 mins. 
Add this to a mixer grindger with the shallots, tomato, the small vegetable chunks, coconut and coriander leaves. 
Make a thick paste without adding extra water.
In a pressure cooker, heat oil. Add fennel seeds, curry leaves and shallots. Sauté well and add the paste. Cook for 5 mins on a medium flame. 
Add salt and coriander powder. 
Add water and bring to a boil, then add the garam masala powder. Add the chunks of the vegetable. 
Pressure cook for 4 whistles. Allow the pressure to release naturally. 
Finish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with idlis.

title: Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar - Masala
cooking_instructions: Wash the toor dal until the water runs clean.
Add the washed toor door and water into a pressure cooker and pressure cook on a low to medium flame for 4 whistles (around 7-8 minutes) and set aside.

Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a kadhai.
⁠Add 15–20 peeled shallots (50 g) and 1 chopped tomato (70 g). Optionally, you can add any vegetable fo choice- 1 Cup (100 g)
Add 1 pouch of Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar Masala, mix and add the cooked dal and 1½ cups of water.
Close the lid and cook on a low- medium heat for 10 minutes. Finish with 1 tsp ghee and fresh coriander leaves.

⁠In another pan, heat 2 tsp oil, add ¼ tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter, add 1 dried red chilli and some curry leaves.
Add the tempering to the sambar and serve hot

title: Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar - Kit
cooking_instructions:
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a kadhai.
⁠Add 15–20 peeled shallots (100 g) and 1 chopped tomato (70 g), sauté on a medium flame for 2 minutes or until the shallots turn translucent. Optionally, you can add any vegetable of choice- 1 Cup (100g)
Add 1 pouch of Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar Masala, mix and add 1 pouch cooked dal 
Add 1½ cups of water.
Close the lid and cook on a low- medium heat for 10 minutes. Finish with 1 tsp ghee and fresh coriander leaves.
⁠In another pan, heat 2 tsp oil, add ¼ tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter, add 1 dried red chilli and some curry leaves.
Add the tempering to the sambar and serve hot.

title: Methi Malai Chicken
cooking_instructions: Marinate chicken with salt, ½ tsp each of cumin, coriander powder and ¼ tsp of garam masala.
Pressure cook the onion, cashew nuts and cardamom in water for 4 whistles.
Cool, blend and strain the mixture in a bowl.
To prepare the gravy, heat ghee in a pan and add ginger garlic paste, saute for 2 mins. Add the gravy base and simmer for 5 mins.
Add the powdered spices, salt and sugar.
Add the milk and chicken, cover and simmer for 10 mins.
Add the methi and grated khoya and mix well until thick and creamy.

title: Muringa Ela Pesto Pasta
cooking_instructions:
Boil penne pasta with salt for 11 minutes, run it over water.
Saute muringa leaves for like 30 seconds with some oil and take it out. 
Blend the above ingredients with olive oil and muring leaves until the required consistency
In a pan, mix the pasta with the sauce and toss it nicely.
Garnish it with grated cheese.

title: Ulli Vada
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add onions with salt and sweat the onions until the water is out.

Add green chillies, ginger, curry leaves (all finely chopped) with red chilli powder, besan flour and maida. 
Mix it nicely and add water only if necessary. (since onion have moisture)
Combine them well and check for seasoning.
Heat up oil in a kadai. Make roundels of onion mixture in your hand and fry it until golden brown in color.

title: Corn Cheese Balls
cooking_instructions:
Combine the leftover rice, rice flour, maggi masala, garlic, coriander leaves, tomato ketchup and salt. Mash and mix well.
For the filling, combine the mozzarella cheese, sweet corn and salt.
Take some rice mixture and press it to form a cup. Add the filling and cover it using more rice mixture. Shape it into balls.
Heat the oil and fry the balls till golden brown.
Serve it.

title: Lemon Pepper Eggs
cooking_instructions:
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with salt and pepper powder. 
Heat a non-stick pan and pour the egg mixture, flip in 2 mins and cook through. 
Cut the omelette into cubes. 
In the same pan, heat butter and add garlic and green chillies. Cook for a minute. 
Add soy sauce, mix well and add a cornstarch slurry made by mixing the water and cornstarch.
mixing the water and cornstarch. 
Cook for 2 mins, till it thickens. 
Season with salt, pepper and MSG. 
Switch off the heat and finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves. 
Add the eggs and mix well; serve with hot rice.

title: Cookd Mutton Ularthiyathu
cooking_instructions: Add 500 g sliced red meat to a pressure cooker with half a packet (20 g) of masala and 2 tbsp of thick curd. It can be slow-cooked without water or with some water (½ Cup), around 15 mins on a medium flame (5-6 whistles) or until the meat is tender.

Heat 4 tbsp of coconut oil in a kadhai. 
Add 20g ( ¼ cup) of coconut chunks. Fry till golden. 
Add 3 sliced onions (180g) and a spring of curry leaves. 
Once the onions and fry until they turn golden brown.

Add the cooked meat. Add the remaining ½ pouch (20g) of masala. 
Cook until the masala is dry and coats the meat.
Finish with a fresh sprig of curry leaves and dry red chilli bits (2-3 nos).

title: Cookd Chicken Ularthiyathu
cooking_instructions:
Heat 4 tbsp of coconut oil in a kadhai. Add 20g ( ¼ cup) of coconut chunks. Fry till golden. 
Add 3 sliced onions (180g) and a spring of curry leaves. 
Once the onions and fry until they turn golden brown. 
Add 500g chic, 2 tbsp of thick curd and ¼ cup of water. Add the ½ pouch (20-25g) of masala.
Cook until the meat is cooked and the masala is dry and coating the meat. 
Finish with a fresh sprig of curry leaves and dry red chilli bits (2-3 nos).

title: Cookd Soya Ularthiyathu
cooking_instructions:
Soak the soya in hot water and 1 tsp of salt (optional)
Squeeze out the water completely after 15-20 minutes and keep it aside. 
Heat 4 tbsp of coconut oil in a pan. Add 20g ( ¼ cup) of coconut chunks. Fry till golden. 
Add 3 sliced onions (180g) and a sprig of curry leaves. 
Once the onions and fry until they turn golden brown. 
Add the soya, 2 tbsp of thick curd and ¼ cup of water. Add the ½ pouch (20-25g) of masala. 
Cook until the masala is dry and coating the meat. 
Finish with a fresh sprig of curry leaves and dry red chilli bits (2-3 nos).

title: Railway Tomato Soup
cooking_instructions:
In a pressure cooker oil, bay leaf, cardamom, garlic, ginger and saute for a minute.
Add green chilli, garlic cloves, finely chopped onion and saute for a minute.
Add 5 roughly chopped tomatoes, 2 cup of water, Spice powders, salt and pressure cook for 3 whistles.
Open the pan, remove bay leaf, cardamom and using a hand blender or mixer grinder, blend this into a smooth puree. Strain this using a strainer.

In another saucepan add the strained mixture, 2 cups of water and bring it to boil. 
Add sugar, tomato ketchup, butter, chat masala and simmer for 2 more minutes.
To make the Croutons, cut the bread into 1-inch cubes, brush with oil and shallow fry in a Tawa or bake in an oven for 10-15 mins at 200 C.

title: Cookd Mushroom Roast
cooking_instructions:
Heat 4 tbsp of coconut oil in a pan. 
Add 3 sliced onions (180g) and a spring of curry leaves. 
Once the onions sweat and turn light brown, add 1 sliced tomato and cook well.
Add the mushrooms and 1 pouch (25g) of masala with ½ cup of water. Cook it well. 
Roast it nicely until it’s cooked through.
Finish with a fresh sprig of curry leaves.

title: Cookd Egg Roast
cooking_instructions:
Boil the eggs for 6 to 7 mins on medium flame.
Once it get cools down ,peal it and keep it aside.

Heat 4 tbsp of coconut oil in a pan. 
Add 3 sliced onions (180g) and a spring of curry leaves. 
Once the onions sweat and turn light brown, add 1 sliced tomato and cook well.
Add the 1 pouch (25g) of masala and ½ cup of water. Cook it well.

Add the boiled eggs and fold it well with the masala. 
Finish with a fresh sprig of curry leaves.

title: Kara Murukku
cooking_instructions: Add all the ingredients except water and butter and mix together. Combine all the butter with the mixture to get a crumble texture.
Knead a smooth but firm dough, add water in additions.
Grease the murukku mold and fill with the mixture.
Make the required shape and size on a greaseproof paper.
Carefully put into hot oil and fry until golden brown on a medium flame.

title: Cookd Donne Paneer Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of seeraga samba rice rice for 20-30 mins.
In a pressure cooker, add the donne biryani paste and saute it on a low flame for a minute.
Add the paneer and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 375 ml water and bring it to a boil.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the cooker.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook it on medium flame for 2 whistles and turn off the flame.
Let the steam reduce gradually and allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Open the cooker, pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice gently. 
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Hyderabadi Paneer Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of basmati rice for 20-30 mins.In another pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
In a biryani pot, add the hyderabadi biryani paste and saute for a minute.
Add the paneer and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add ¼ cup of water and cook for 4 - 5 mins on a medium flame, until the consistency is thick again.
Strain the cooked rice and add directly on top of the biryani masala and add 1/4 cup of the boiled rice water.
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves and fried cashews as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Shawarma for babies
cooking_instructions:
Combine the whole wheat flour, salt, carrot puree and make a soft dough. Finish by rubbing ghee onto the dough.
Combine hung curd, garlic, salt, pepper and coriander leaves in a bowl and mix well.
Take water in two separate bowls. Add equal quantities of lemon juice, salt, sugar and water in two bowls.
Add the finely chopped juliennes of beetroot and cucumber in separate bowls.
In a bowl, combine chicken kheema,ginger garlic paste, salt, cumin powder, turmeric powder, garam masala and red chili powder.
Heat ghee in a pan and add the kheema mixture. Saute till the kheema is cooked.
Top it off with chopped coriander leaves.
Make small sized chapatis using the dough.
Take a spoonful of hung curd and apply it on the chapati.
Put kheema filling and pickled veggies.
Roll it and wrap it using wrapping paper.
Plate it and serve.

title: Cookd Chicken Roast
cooking_instructions:
Heat 4 tbsp of coconut oil in a kadai.
Add 3 sliced onions (180g) and a spring of curry leaves.
Once the onions sweat and turn light brown, add 1 sliced tomato and cook well.
Add 500g chicken and ½ cup of water. Add the 1 pouch (25g) of masala.

Cook until the meat is cooked and the masala is dry and coats the meat. 
Finish with a fresh sprig of curry leaves.

title: Cookd Mutton Roast
cooking_instructions: Add 500 g sliced red meat to a pressure cooker with half a packet (12-13g) of masala. It can be slow-cooked without water or with ½ Cup of water, around 15 mins on a medium flame (5-6 whistles) or until the meat is tender.

Heat 4 tbsp of coconut oil in a kadhai. 
Add 3 sliced onions (180g) and a spring of curry leaves.
Once the onions sweat and turn light brown, add 1 sliced tomato and cook well.
Add the cooked meat. Add the remaining masala (12-13g).

Cook until the masala is dry and coats the meat. 
Finish with a fresh sprig of curry leaves.

title: Thecha Curd Rice
cooking_instructions:
Boil rice until mushy. (1 part rice to 4 parts water)
Mash it well with curd, milk, and salt until it’s a creamy consistency.

In a pan, heat oil and saute the cumin, green chillies, peanuts, and garlic cloves. 
Add the coriander leaves and salt.
Transfer this to a mortar and pestle and make it into a coarse paste.
Mix this techa chutney into the curd rice and serve cold with vadaam

title: Sharkara Varatti
cooking_instructions:
Cut raw bananas into quarters and soak them in turmeric water.
In a pot, heat oil and deep fry them until they are cooked and crispy. Keep it aside.
Blend sugar, rice, ginger powder and cardamom together into a powder form and keep it aside. 
In a big kadai, (big enough to mix the fried raw bananas) melt some jaggery with little water and make it into a thick consistency. 
Add the fried raw bananas and stir continuously until it coats well. 
Add the blended powder portion wise to get the chips separately.
Finish it off when every single fried chip is separate.

title: Honeymoon Chutney
cooking_instructions: In a pan, add oil and dry red chilli and saute until it turns light brown. Remove from the pan and set aside.

In the same pan, add mustard seeds, urad dal, cashew nuts, and peeled almonds and roast them for a few minutes (3 to 4 minutes)
Now add grated coconut to it and saute for a few more minutes  (4 to 5 minutes)
Add the sauteed dry red chilli, salt and tamarind into a blender and blend until coarse.
Now add all the other roasted ingredients into the blender and blend into a coarse chutney

title: Katti Parippu (Kerala style)
cooking_instructions: Wash the dal
Pressure cook it with turmeric powder until it’s fully cooked.
Blend grated coconut, cumin seeds and green chilli with some water into a very fine and runny mixture.

Pour the mixture into the cooked dal and add sufficient salt and water. 
Make it into a runny consistency
Finish it off with curry leaves and ghee.

title: Poha Chivda
cooking_instructions: Roast the flattened rice evenly in a pan until crispy, mixing constantly. Cool completely.
Heat the oil and add the cumin seeds and garlic. Saute for a minute. Add the peanuts and coconut and fry until golden brown.
Add the curry leaves and mix well. Switch off the flame and add the raisins, salt, sugar and red chilli powder.
Quickly toss the toasted poha in this masala and cool. Store airtight.

title: Ada Pradhaman
cooking_instructions:
Combine rice flour, ghee, salt and water to make a runny batter. 
Boil or steam the banana leaves and just spread the batter or sprinkle the batter on top
Roll and tie the leaves nicely. Boil for 8-10 minutes until it’s cooked. (you can see a change in color on banana leaves) 
Take it out and slowly peel off the ada from the leaves. You can also add those leaves into cold water to get the Ada, much faster.
Melt the jaggery in an open pot. Make sure there are no lumps. 
Add the ada and mix it well. 
Pour the 3rd coconut milk and boil until it regains the thick consistency.
Add the 2nd coconut milk, cardamom powder and dry ginger powder. Boil it nicely. 
Switch off the stove and add the 1st coconut milk (thicker one) and ghee
Switch off the stove and add the 1st coconut milk (thicker one) and ghee. 
Mix it well and add the fried coconut slices, raisins and cashew nuts.

title: Creamy Chicken Pasta
cooking_instructions:
For the pasta, add water in a stockpot. Bring it to a boil, add salt and oil, followed by pasta. Cook till done.
Strain the pasta and toss it in oil.
Marinate the chicken breast with red chili powder, onion powder, dried parsley, salt, black pepper powder and garlic.
In a pan, heat butter and pan sear the chicken till cooked and keep aside.
For the sauce, heat butter in a pan. Add the onion and garlic and saute for a minute.
Add the maida and saute for 1 minute.
Add the milk and mix, avoiding lumps.
Season with salt, oregano and chili flakes.
Grate cheese into the sauce.
Add the pasta and mix.
Plate it and place the chicken on top

title: Tea kadai Uppu biscut
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar, oil, ghee, and salt until well combined.
Add the cumin powder. Gradually add the wheat flour, a little at a time, mixing until a crumbly dough forms.
Divide the dough into portions
Roll each portion flat with a rolling pin and cut into small biscuit-sized pieces

Heat a pan over low flame, adding a pinch of salt, and let it warm for 15 minutes.


Place the dough pieces on a plate, then transfer them to the heated pan. Bake on low heat for 25–35 minutes or until fully cooked.


Remove from the pan and let cool completely. Serve with tea

title: Kozhukattai Pasta
cooking_instructions:
In a kadhai, dry roast the rice flour on a low flame for 2–3 minutes until aromatic. The flour should remain white. Remove and set aside.
In the same kadhai, bring water to a boil. Add salt and ghee.
Gradually add the roasted rice flour, stirring continuously until it comes together into a smooth dough.
Transfer the dough to a flat surface and knead until soft and pliable. Shape into your desired pasta shapes.
Drop the shaped dough into boiling water and cook for about 5 minutes, then strain and set aside.
Heat gingelly oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds, black pepper, urad dal, and toor dal. Toast until golden.
Add dried red chilli, garlic, and a pinch of asafoetida. Sauté on low–medium flame until aromatic.
Stir in the grated coconut and cook for 30–40 seconds.
Transfer everything to a mixer jar, add water, and grind into a thick paste
In a pan, heat thick coconut milk. Stir in the prepared paste and simmer until it thickens and reduces.
Add the freshly boiled pasta, toss well, and serve hot.

title: Moist Veggie Chocolate Cake
cooking_instructions: Grate the zucchini and set aside.

Mix all the dry ingredients in a bowl. 
Add the wet ingredients and gently combine, but not fully.
Add the grated zucchini and mix well.

Transfer to a greased/ lined baking dish. Even out the top. 
Bake at 180 °C for 40-45 mins.
Cool and serve, but can also be served hot

title: Banana Brulee
cooking_instructions:
Roughly chop the bananas and cook it till mushy
Add milk to it and blend it
Strain the mixture
Add cream to this and cook over low flame
In a bowl combine the egg yolk and sugar
Add the egg mixture to the banana mixture slowly while whisking
Add the cornstarch
Finish off with butter and vanilla extract
Pour into banana peel moulds and set it in refrigerator for 45 mins
Add sugar and scorch it using a hot spoon

title: Stuffed Chicken Noodles
cooking_instructions: Roughly knead the dough with flour, salt, oil, and water.
For the filling: combine all the ingredients and mix well.
Apply oil and rest for 10 mins.
Add all the ingredients for chilli oil in a bowl
Roll out the dough into flat discs using cornstarch to prevent sticking.
Place some of the mixture in each and seal using water in a long shape.

Stretch them out into noodles and then boil in hot water for 2-3 mins. 
Drain, apply oil and set aside.

pour over the hot oil. 
Add the boiled chicken noodles and mix well.

title: Netholi Popcorn
cooking_instructions:
Marinated the fish with salt, pepper and ginger garlic paste. Let it rest under room temperature for half an hour to remove moisture content. 
Make a runny batter with the above ingredients. Incorporate the (chilled) soda water slowly into the mixture. 
Dust the fish with maida, dip it in batter and deep fry.
Make sure the oil is hot and take it out when it’s golden in color.
Serve it with fries and tartar sauce.

title: Tomato Ketchup
cooking_instructions:
In a saucepan, add tomatoes, onion, garlic, beetroot and let it cook.
Add in bayleaf and clove. Cook till the tomatoes are mushy.
Cool it and blend it.
Transfer it to a saucepan and add cumin powder, kashmiri red chili powder and salt.
Cook till the ketchup thickens.
Add sugar and vinegar.
To check if the ketchup is cooked, add some of the ketchup to a plate. The water should not run separately. If you make a line using your finger, the shape should remain. 
Allow it to cool and then store it in the refrigerator in a glass bottle or container. It can be stored for up to a month.

title: Cookd Hyderabadi Prawn Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of basmati rice for 20-30 mins.
In another pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
Add the prawn and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add ¼ cup of water and cook for 4 - 5 mins on a medium flame, until the consistency is thick again.
Strain the cooked rice and add directly on top of the biryani masala and add 1/4 cup of the boiled rice water.
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves and fried cashews as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Appam
cooking_instructions: Wash the rice and soak for 3 hours.
Add ½ cup of water and grind it into a fine paste.
Remove ¼ cup of the paste and cook it in a pan along with 1 cup of water until it turns into a thick paste.
Add this back into the mixer jar. Add the grated coconut and ½ cup of water. Grind it again.
Cover it and leave it to rest at room temperature for 8-10 hours.
Add baking soda, salt and sugar. Mix well to combine.

Heat an Appam pan over medium heat. Grease lightly with oil. Pour a ladle of Appam batter into the pan. Swirl the pan around to spread the batter. The batter should be thin around the sides and thick in the center.
Cover and cook for 45-60 seconds or until the sides have started to turn golden brown. Remove from the pan and serve hot with stew, coconut milk or any gravy of your choice.

title: Cookd Malabar Chicken Biryani (Pressure Cooker)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of seeraga samba rice for 20 mins.
In a pressure cooker, add the Malabar biryani paste and saute it on a low flame for a minute.
Add the chicken and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 375 ml water and bring it to a boil.
Add the soaked rice and add it to the cooker.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook it on medium flame for 2 whistles and turn off the flame.
Let the steam reduce gradually and allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Open the cooker, pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice gently. 
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani (Pressure Cooker)
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of basmati rice for 20 mins.
In a pressure cooker, add the Hyderabadi biryani paste and saute it on a low flame for a minute.
Add the chicken and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 375 ml water and bring it to a boil.
Add the soaked rice and add it to the cooker.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook it on medium flame for 2 whistles and turn off the flame.
Let the steam reduce gradually and allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Open the cooker, pour over the seasoning oil and the required garnishes. Fluff the biryani rice gently. 
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Saiva Eeral Masal
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the green grams for 4 hours.
Drain them, blend into a smooth batter, and steam on an idli tawa.
Once cooled, cut into small cubes and set aside.

In a kadai, add oil, bay leaf, and fennel seeds; sauté for a few seconds.
Add onion, garlic, ginger-garlic paste, and tomato; cook for 5 minutes.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder; sauté for 5 minutes.
Now add the green gram cubes and sauté for 2 minutes.

title: Instant Stuffed Peda
cooking_instructions: For the stuffing, pulse blend the cashew nuts, coconut, milk powder, and sugar into a powder. Optionally, you can add saffron and rose water to flavour it.

Add 1-2 tbsp of milk and make this into a pliable dough. Adding food colour is optional. 
Roll this into small portions and set aside.
For the mixture, blend together the coconut, milk powder, sugar, and cardamom powder to get a smooth and uniform powder.
Add 2-3 tbsp of milk and bring together a pliable dough.

To shape the sweet, take a portion of the mixture and flatten it out. Place a small piece of the stuffing inside and enclose the stuffing with the mixture and roll well, till there are no cracks. 
Flatten slightly and garnish with chopped pistachios/ almonds or silver leaf. 
Store refrigerated, for up to 2 weeks.

title: Cookd Donne Prawn Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of seeraga samba rice rice for 20-30 mins.
In a pressure cooker, add the donne biryani paste and saute it on a low flame for a minute.
Add the prawn and mix with the paste for a minute.
Add 375 ml water and bring it to a boil.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the cooker.
Cover the pressure cooker and cook it on medium flame for 2 whistles and turn off the flame.
Let the steam reduce gradually and allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Open the cooker, pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice gently. 
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Cookd Malabar Prawn Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 250g of kaima rice for 20-30 mins.
In another pot, bring 2L water to a boil with 1 tbsp (12g) of salt.
Strain the soaked rice and add it to the pot of water, boil for 5-6 mins, until the rice is 75% done.
In a biryani pot, add the malabar biryani paste and saute for a minute.
Add the prawn and mix with the paste for a minute.
Cook for 2 - 3 minutes.
Strain the cooked rice and add directly on top of the biryani masala and add 1/4 cup of the boiled rice water.
Add fried onions, coriander leaves, mint leaves, fried cashews and fried raisins as garnish.
Cover tightly and cook on dum for 12-15 mins then allow it to rest for 10-15 mins.
Pour over the seasoning oil and fluff the biryani rice and masala gently
Drizzle ghee (optional) and serve hot!

title: Chatti Pathiri
cooking_instructions:
Boil the chicken with salt and turmeric powder.
Cool it down and shred the chicken.
Make a batter with maida, salt, sugar, eggs and water. 
Whisk it thoroughly and keep it aside
In a pan add chopped onion and ginger garlic paste. Saute it nicely. 
Saute it until it’s done and chopped green chillies and curry leaves. 
Add the masalas and roast it well.
Add the shredded chicken with tomato ketchup and mix it nicely.
Make an egg mix with salt, pepper powder and some milk. 
Heat up a non-stick pan and make dosa with the batter. 
Make sure the pan is not too hot so that the batter doesn’t stick to the pan.
In a pot, brush it with ghee/oil
Dip the dosa in egg mix, place one dosa on the bottom of the pan and keep the filling on top. Dip another one again and place another dosa and do this until you get at least 6,7 layers.
Pour the egg mix into the side at the end so that it binds together. 
Close the pot with a lid and keep the pot on another pan and heat it up for 15 minutes. 
After 15 minutes, flip it and sear it for another 5 minutes.

title: Masala Pasta- Leftover series
cooking_instructions:
Add water in a stockpot and let it boil. Add salt.
Once the water is boiling, cut the dough into pasta shape using a scissor and toss it into the boiling water. Reserve some pasta water to add in the masala.
Let the pasta cook for 10 mins. Strain it and toss it with oil.
For the masala, splutter cumin seeds in oil.
Add garlic and saute for 30 secs then add onion and saute till brown.
Add the tomatoes and saute for 2 mins. 
Add garam masala,  red chili powder, turmeric powder, salt and mix well.Pour in some pasta water.
Add capsicum and saute for a minute. Add in the ketchup.
Add the boiled pasta and toss.
Garnish with coriander leaves and grated cheese.

title: Tumbler Pasta
cooking_instructions:
In a pressure cooker, add the butter and let it melt.
Add in the pizza seasoning, chilli flakes and black pepper powder and saute for 5 seconds. 
Add the chopped onion and garlic and saute on a medium flame for 2 minutes or until the onions turn translucent.
Add the chopped carrots and golden corn and saute for 2-3 more minutes or until the carrot softens. 
Add the maida and cook on a low flame for 2-3 minutes or until the raw flavour disappears. 
Pour in the water and milk and bring it to a boil. Add in the mustard sauce and salt. 
Add 1 tumbler of pasta, cover, and pressure cook on a medium flame for 1 whistle. 
Immediately run it over running water to release the pressure.
Open and let it cook for 2 more minutes or until the sauce thickens. 
Finish the pasta with grated cheese and chopped capsicum. 
Serve hot

title: High Protein Japan Chicken
cooking_instructions:
In a mixer jar, add the ingredients for the sauce and blend into a very smooth paste 
In a mixing bowl, add the chicken cubes, cornstarch, salt, and black pepper powder, and mix thoroughly until the chicken is evenly coated. 
In a pan, pour oil and cook the chicken until light golden brown and set aside. 
In the same pan, pour the prepared sauce and cook until the raw flavour disappears and the sauce thickens. 
Add the cooked chicken back to the sauce and toss till coated. 
Finish the chicken with kasoori methi and coriander leaves.

title: Kerala Chicken Fry
cooking_instructions: Blend the shallots, green chillies, ginger, garlic, curry leaves and coconut oil into a paste.
Add the chicken along with salt, black pepper powder, Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder and fennel powder. Mix well using your hands. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.

Add rice flour and mix well. Deep fry in oil on high heat for 2 minutes. Reduce the flame to medium and cook for 6 more minutes. Add curry leaves a few seconds before taking the chicken out of the oil. Serve hot. Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Unnakaya
cooking_instructions: Steam the bananas for 10 minutes.
Mash the bananas and make it into a dough. If you feel the dough is watery, add rice four accordingly.

In a pan, add ghee and saute grated coconut, chopped cashews and raisins until it’s fully toasted. 
Add sugar and cardamom powder to the filling.
Make balls from the dough and spread it in your hand. Add the filling inside and shape it into cylinder shapes.
Deep fry until golden brown in hot oil.

title: Poondu Kara Chutney
cooking_instructions:
Heat oil in a pan. Add urad dal and fry for a few seconds until light golden.
Add dry red chillies, tamarind, garlic, and curry leaves. Sauté on medium flame for about 5 minutes until aromatic.
Add salt and red chilli powder. Fry for another 1 minute and switch off the flame.
Let it cool completely, then grind to a smooth paste in a mixer jar (adding little water if needed).
In a kadai, heat oil for tempering. Add mustard seeds, urad dal, and garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes until golden.
Add the blended paste and cook on medium flame until the oil separates.
Serve with rice, dosa, or idli.

title: Boost Lava Cake
cooking_instructions: In a separate bowl, combine boost and hot water. Make sure there are no lumps.

Sift the maida and baking powder together.
Add castor sugar, eggs and mix.
Add the boost mixture to the batter and whisk well.

Grease the ramekins by first applying butter and then put cocoa powder and shake to remove excess.
Add equal amounts of batter in each ramekin. Fill it till it is ¾ th full.

Bake at 180 C for 15 mins, if using a cooker, keep it on medium flame for 15 mins.
Demould the cake once done.
Serve hot.

title: Coconut Rava Fry
cooking_instructions: Mix all the ingredients for the marination together. Add water as needed to form a smooth and thick paste.

Coat the tender coconut in the marination. 
Coat the marinated coconut in the rava.
Shallow fry in oil until cooked and crisp on both sides, a total of 2-3 minutes depending on the size of the pieces.

title: Kalyana vazhakkai varuval
cooking_instructions: Cut the raw banana into diamond-shaped pieces. Add salt and red chili powder, and mix well in a bowl.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil for 2 minutes, strain, and keep aside.

In a kadai, add oil, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, and dried red chili, and sauté for a minute.
Now add onion, garlic, tomato, coconut chunks, salt, and red chili powder, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Once it cools down, transfer to a mixer jar and coarsely blend.
In another pan, add oil, urad dal, curry leaves, onion, tomato, ginger-garlic paste, salt, red chili powder, and the blended coconut mixture.

Sauté for 5 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Now add the fried raw banana pieces and sauté for 5 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

title: Tumbler Poori Channa
cooking_instructions:
For the Channa Masala, Soak One Tumbler of Kabuli Channa overnight. 
For the Poori Dough, add all the ingredients and knead for 8-10 minutes or until a smooth and supple dough forms. 
Cover with a wet cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes
Pressure cook the soaked channa on a medium heat for 4-5 whistles or until cooked through and soft (5 minutes)
In a kadhai/wok, pour the ghee and add the whole spices, letting them splutter. 
Add in the finely chopped onions and saute until light golden brown. 
Add in the ginger garlic paste and tomato, and saute on a medium flame for 3-4 minutes or until mushy (Pour in some water if required). 
Add in all the powder spices and cook on a medium flame until fragrant and the raw flavour disappears. 
Pour in water and bring to a boil. Let it cook for 8-10 minutes or until the gravy thickens. 
Add the cooked and drained channa to the gravy and let it cook for 3 minutes on a medium flame. 
Finish the gravy with the finely chopped capsicum and coriander leaves. 
For the poori, separate it into small pedas (to your desired size) and roll into small chapathis, making sure not to roll it too thin and not too thick. 
Deep fry on a medium flame until puffed up and cooked through. 
Serve hot.

title: Coconut Jaggery Puffed Rice Bar
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl, add the puffed rice and all the other ingredients.
Melt the jaggery in a pan on a medium-low flame. 
Once the jaggery has melted, take it to the hardball stage.  
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix quickly.
Once well combined, spread it on a baking tray and shape into bars.
Once cooled down, cut into bars using a serrated knife and serve

title: Hot & Sour Soup
cooking_instructions: In a pot, heat oil and add in the garlic, ginger, green chillies and spring onion whites. Saute and then add in the cabbage, carrot, beans and mushroom. Saute on high heat for 1 minute.
Pour in the water/vegetable stock. When it comes to a boil, add in the soy sauce, red chilli sauce, white pepper powder, sugar, vinegar salt. Allow it to simmer for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare a slurry by mixing the cornstarch with water. Add this to the boiling soup and mix immediately.
When it comes to a boil and starts to thicken, add the spring onion greens and turn off the heat.
In a small pan, heat 3 tbsp of oil. When it is very hot, pour it into a small bowl with the chilli flakes. Allow it to rest and infuse for 2-3 minutes. Then mix it and pour it over the soup.

title: Savoury Puffed Rice Bar
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl, add the puffed rice and all the spice powders. 
Melt the jaggery in a pan on a medium-low flame
Once the jaggery has melted, take it to the hardball stage.  
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix quickly.
Once well combined, spread it on a baking tray and shape into bars.
Once cooled down, cut into bars using a serrated knife and serve

title: Creamy Eggs on Toast
cooking_instructions:
Heat a pan, add oil.
Add onion and saute till it turns translucent.
Add garlic and saute for few seconds.

Add the sweet corn and cook for a minute.
Add maida and saute. Add milk and make a sauce, avoiding lumps.
Add the spinach and mix till it shrinks and is cooked.
Add salt and black pepper powder, mix till combined.
Crack the eggs on it and let it cook for 5 mins.
Heat a tawa, keep it on a low flame.
Add butter and place a slice of bread on it.Toast it.
Place the eggs on toast. Garnish with coriander leaves.

title: Kothavarangai Kondai Varuval
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the channa dal for 8 hours.
Now pressure cook the channa dal for 3 whistles on a medium flame.
Add coconut and fennel seeds to a mixer and blend into a paste.
In a kadai, heat oil and add cinnamon, onion, and garlic. Sauté for a minute.
Now add tomato, cluster beans, red chili powder, and salt. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add water, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Open the pot, add the soaked and cooked channa dal along with the coconut paste.
Add some water and simmer until everything combines well.
Finally, add curry leaves and serve hot with your meal.

title: Tumbler-shaped tea cake
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine all the dry ingredients and set aside.
In a bigger mixing bowl, combine all the wet ingredients and sift in the dry ingredients.
Gently fold the batter until smooth
transfer it into a greased and floured tumbler.

In a preheated pot lined with salt, place the tumbler in an elevation, cover and bake on a medium flame for 30-35 minutes or until golden brown and completely cooked. 
Let it cool slightly and demould it.

title: Sweet Banana Chips
cooking_instructions: Make a salt mixture in a bowl and keep it aside.

Peel off the banana and keep it in a water bowl. 
Heat oil in a pot and directly slice the banana with a mandolin slicer to prevent it from sticking.

When it is half done, add the salt mixture and stir them well. 
You can take it out when it’s golden in color. You’ll see the oil start sizzling down.

title: Mushroom Chop Masala
cooking_instructions:
Heat butter in a pan. 
Add finely chopped garlic, green chilli and coriander leaves. Sauté for 2 mins until light brown. 
Add the chopped onion and saute until lightly browned. 
Next, add the chopped tomatoes, powdered masalas, salt and tomato ketchup. 
Cook until the masala is dry, about 3-4 mins. 
Add the chopped mushrooms and mix well. Cook until it starts to boil, the mushrooms will release water and add the milk. Cook until it is thick.
Switch off the flame, grate 1 cheese cube on top and finish with fresh coriander leaves. 
This can be served with toast, chappatis/ paratha.

title: Sandhavai
cooking_instructions:
Soak the idli rice for at least 1 hour.
Grind it in a mixer, with salt and water. The batter should be fine textured and of thick consistency.
Grease the idli molds with oil.
Pour the batter into idli molds and steam it for 20 mins or till done. Check the doneness by inserting a knife, it should come out clean.
Scoop out the idlis and cool it down.
Using a sandhagai maker, press the idlis.
Serve the sandhagai with sweetened coconut milk/ ghee and jaggery or prepare any other dish of choice.

title: High Protein Paneer Butter Masala
cooking_instructions:
Add all the ingredients to a pressure cooker. Cover and pressure-cook on medium heat for 5 whistles (around 15 minutes). 
Allow it to cool down, then grind it into a smooth paste. 
Optionally, you can strain the gravy for a smoother texture. Add it into a pan and heat it up. 
Add milk, mix and bring it to a boil. Cover with a lid, turn the flame to low and cook for 10 minutes. Stir occasionally.  
Add the paneer cubes, Kasuri methi, garam masala powder and honey. Cook for just 2 minutes and turn off the heat. Serve it hot with pulao/naan/roti.

title: Cookd Persian Wedding Biryani
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak 500g of basmati biryani rice for 20 mins. 
Strain and set aside for 5 mins
In a pot, add ghee, and fry the rice for 2 minutes. 
Add water and bring it to a boil. Add the salt, turmeric powder, and saffron. 
Don’t mix too much. 
Once the water and rice and in the same level, close and keep on dum for 15 mins on a low flame. Keep a tava under the vessel to prevent it from burning. Allow it to rest for 15 mins. 
Heat 2 packets of curry paste in a kadhai and add 1 kg of chicken biryani cut. 
Do not add any extra water, cook for 18-20 mins until the chicken is done. Cook on a medium flame, stirring occasionally.
Open the dum and top with the seasoning oil from the Cookd wedding bhai biryani paste. Mix gently. 
In a large platter, add a layer of rice and top it with the meat masala in the center. Garnish it generously with the fried cashew nuts, raisins, pomegranate, mint leaves, coriander leaves, and some dried rose petal

title: Karunai Kilangu Masiyal
cooking_instructions:
Wash the yam thoroughly once or twice.


In a pressure cooker, add the yam and water, then pressure cook for about 15 minutes (6 to 7 whistles).


Once it cools down, peel off the skin.
In a bowel add tamarind and water soak it and squeeze to extract tamarind water.
Add tamarind water, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt, and coarsely mash.
In a kadai, heat oil and add mustard seeds, urad dal, fennel seeds, onion, garlic, and green chili. Sauté for about 5 minutes.

Now add the mashed yam mixture and sauté for 15 minutes on medium flame.
Serve hot with rasam rice or sambar rice.

title: Oats Idli
cooking_instructions: Grind the oats into a fine powder.
Make tempering by heating oil and splutter the mustard seeds, add the dals and slightly brown them. Add the curry leaves, chillies, ginger and asafoetida.
Add the rava and oats flour and roast for a few minutes. Cool this mixture.
Add the carrot and chopped coriander. Add the curd and water and make a thick but smooth batter.
Grease the idli molds and heat water in the steamer.
Add the eno/ fruit salt and mix thoroughly. Pour the batter in the molds and steam for 12 mins.

title: Fish Pickle- Kerala Style
cooking_instructions: Marinate the fish with salt, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, black pepper powder and curry leaves. Rest it for 10-15 minutes.
Fry it until hard and brown.

In a pan, heat 2 cups of leftover gingelly oil and add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. Let it splutter. 
Add curry leaves, chopped green chilli, ginger and whole garlic. Let it cook for 5 minutes.

Add the masalas and roast it in the oil. 
Next, add vinegar and asafoetida powder. Let it boil.
Add the fish and mix it gently.

title: Chinna Veedu Chicken Roast
cooking_instructions:
Heat oil in a pan and add curry leaves, fennel seeds and dry red chillies. 
Add the onions and saute until golden in color. 
Followed by crushed ginger, garlic and green chillies. Saute for 2-3 minutes. 
Add the Masala powder and roast it in oil. 
Add the chicken and saute for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the curd, cashew paste and rose water. Add salt and let it boil under low flame. 
Finish it off with dried rose petals, garam masala and ghee.

title: Peanut Butter
cooking_instructions:
Roast the peanuts on low flame for 10-15 mins, until the skin starts separating and you get the roasted aroma.
Transfer it to a plate and let the peanuts cool down.
Separate the skin using a cloth.
Transfer the peanuts to a mixer grinder and pulse it.
Add oil, jaggery and salt and make a smooth paste.
Allow the mixer jar to cool in between if it heats up while grinding
For crunchy peanuts, add some chopped peanuts and mix. For high protein peanut butter, mix the protein powder in peanut butter.
Serve it over toast/oatmeal/ milkshake.
Store at room temperature

title: Guntur Muttai Thokku
cooking_instructions:
Heat oil in a pan/ wok. Splutter the mustard seeds. 
Add the onions and saute until translucent, about 3-4 mins. Add the curry leaves. 
Add the tomatoes and saute until soft, about 3-4 mins. 
Add the guntur masala and ¼ cup of water. 
Cook until thick again. 
Whisk the eggs in a bowl, and pour them over the masala. Cover and cookd for 2-3 mins. 
Flip and cook for a further 2 mins. Finish with fresh coriander leaves. 
Serve hot with plain, soft bread for a quick and easy breakfast.

title: Muttai Raita
cooking_instructions:
In a pot, pour water and bring it to a boil. 
Add the eggs gently, cover and let it cook for 12 minutes. 
Transfer it to an ice bath and peel the shells, and set aside.
In a mixing bowl, add all the vegetables for the raita and mix thoroughly
Add in the curd, cream and honey. Mix thoroughly.
Once the eggs have completely cooled, chop them and add them to the mixture.
For the tempering, melt the ghee and brown the garlic. Finish it off with the powdered spices
Add it immediately to the raita.

title: Kidney Beans Butter Beans Pulao & Brinjal Fry
cooking_instructions:
Heat oil and ghee in a pressure cooker.
Add cumin seeds, cinnamon, and bay leaf. Sauté for a few seconds until aromatic.
Add onion, green chili, and ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for about 5 minutes until the onions turn golden.
Add the soybeans, butter beans, soaked rice, water, and milk. Mix well.
Cover and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Once the pressure releases naturally, open the cooker and gently fluff the rice.
Heat oil in a kadai (pan).
Add urad dal and fennel seeds; let them splutter for a few seconds.
Add onion and tomato. Sauté for 2 minutes until soft.
Add chopped brinjal and sauté for another 2 minutes.
Add red chili powder, turmeric, salt, and coriander powder. Mix and sauté well.
Pour a little water, cover, and cook for 5 minutes until the brinjal becomes tender.
Open the lid, add curd, and sauté for 1 minute.

title: Nellikai Chutney
cooking_instructions: Wash and cut the gooseberries.
In a kadai, add oil and dry red chilies. Sauté until they turn dark in color, and keep it aside

In the same kadai, add mustard seeds, urad dal, and channa dal. Let them splutter.
Now add asafoetida and grated coconut. Sauté for a minute until it turns aromatic.

Transfer this mixture to the same mixer jar and coarsely blend it.
Serve it with idli.

title: Sponge cake- 3 ways
cooking_instructions:
Preheat the oven at 180 C for 15 mins. If using a cooker, add salt in the bottom of the cooker, place the stand, close the lid and let it heat on medium flame for 15 mins.
Sift maida and baking powder together in a bowl.
In a separate bowl, add baking soda to curd and whisk. Keep it aside.
Combine oil and sugar. Add curd mixture to this and mix well.
Fold in the sifted maida to make a smooth batter.
Add vanilla essence to the batter and mix.
Divide the batter into 3 portions- 1st portion will be for vanilla sponge cake. Pour it into baking tin,
Take the 2nd portion, add cocoa powder and instant coffee powder mixed with warm water to this. Fold it gently, pour it into a baking tin
Take the 3rd portion and mix cocoa powder and red food colour in this.
Bake at 180 C for 40 mins in the oven. If using a cooker, bake it for 30 mins, or when a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Let the cakes cool. Demould it.
Once completely cooled, cling wrap it and store it in the fridge for up to 2 weeks or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: No-fry Spinach Pakoda
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine the dosa batter, besan flour, carrom seeds, salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and asafoetida. Adjust the consistency with water. The batter must be smooth and runny.

Use any large leaf spinach like Palak/ Pasalakeerai. Wash and pluck the leaves. 
Heat a dosa tawa and brush some oil. 
Dip the leaves in the batter and cook both sides on the dosa tava until golden brown.

title: Filter coffee- for babies
cooking_instructions:
Soak ragi in water for at least 2 hours.
Soak the almonds for at least 1 hour.
Strain and transfer it to a mixer. Add water and grind it.
Spread a cheesecloth on a strainer and pour the mixture on it.
Squeeze out the milk using cheese cloth and keep it aside. Add more water and thin down the milk.
For the decoction, melt jaggery in water. Add cocoa powder to it and make a decoction. Check the consistency, it should not be too thick.
In a glass, pour the decoction and then pour hot ragi milk onto it. Froth it.
Serve it.

title: Egg Omelette Curry
cooking_instructions: Grind Coconut, Cumin seeds, Fennel seeds, coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder and garam masala powder in a blender with some water and grind to a paste
To make omelette whisk all ingredients under omelette and mix well.

Heat oil in a non-stick pan, when hot pour the omelette mixture. Once cooked on one side, turn the omelette over with a spatula and cook the other side. Remove from the pan, once cooled, cut the omelette into half and then cut crossways into strips. Roll up the strips and keep aside.
To prepare the gravy, heat oil in a frying pan, fry the sliced onion over medium heat and cook until onions are golden brown. Add the spice paste and fry for a further 4 minutes.
Add green chillies and tomatoes and saute for 5 minutes. Add lemon juice, 400 ml of water and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add coriander leaves and omelette strips. Cook for a further 3 minutes over low heat and serve with Chapati/Roti.

title: Rava Laddoo
cooking_instructions: Pulse blend the rava in a mixer grinder to make it fine.
Lightly roast the cashew nuts and raisins in a tbsp of ghee and remove.
In the same pan, Lightly roast the rava, until aromatic but colour should not change.
Add the semolina and cashews along with the other ingredients except the ghee in a bowl.
Heat the remaining ghee and pour over the mixture.Mix thoroughly.
Press gently and form into lemon-sized laddoos while the mixture is still warm.

title: Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala (Pouch)
cooking_instructions:
Wash the toor dal until the water runs clean. 
Add the washed toor dal and water into a pressure cooker and pressure cook on a low to medium flame for 4 whistles (around 7-8 minutes) and set aside. 
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a kadhai.
⁠Add 10–15 peeled shallots (50 g) and 1 chopped tomato (40 g). 
Add the diced Drumsticks, pour 2 cups of water and let it cook for 5-6 minutes on a low to medium flame. 
Instead of Drumsticks, you can add any vegetable of your choice- 1 Cup (100g)
Add 1 pouch of Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala, mix and add the cooked dal and mix thoroughly. 
Close the lid and cook on a low- medium heat for 10 minutes. Finish with 1 tsp ghee and fresh coriander leaves.
In another pan, heat 2 tsp oil, add ¼ tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter, add 1 dried red chilli and some curry leaves and add the tempering to the sambar.

recipe_ingredients.ingredient_name: Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala Pouch

Wash the toor dal until the water runs clean. 
Add the washed toor dal and water into a pressure cooker and pressure cook on a low to medium flame for 4 whistles (around 7-8 minutes) and set aside. 
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a kadhai.
⁠Add 10–15 peeled shallots (50 g) and 1 chopped tomato (40 g). 
Add the diced Drumsticks, pour 2 cups of water and let it cook for 5-6 minutes on a low to medium flame. 
Instead of Drumsticks, you can add any vegetable of your choice- 1 Cup (100g)
Add 1 pouch of Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala, mix and add the cooked dal and mix thoroughly. 
Close the lid and cook on a low- medium heat for 10 minutes. Finish with 1 tsp ghee and fresh coriander leaves.

recipe_ingredients.ingredient_name: Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala

title: Cookd High Protein Wedding Bhai Biryani (veg)
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak basmati Rice for 20 mins

In a pressure cooker, add the Cookd Wedding Biryani Paste and add the soya chunks, tofu and boiled channa
Pour the water and bring it to a boil.

Add the soaked and strained rice and pressure cook on a medium flame for 2 whistles 
Let the steam reduce gradually for 10 minutes
Open the cooker, add the seasoning oil and the capsicum, fluff up the biryani and serve it hot with raita and salad.

title: Coconut Prawn Fry
cooking_instructions: Clean and wash the prawns, then set them aside.
In a mixer jar, add all the ingredients and coarsely blend them.

Transfer this mixture to the bowl of prawns and mix well.
Let it rest for at least 10 minutes.

In a kadai, heat some oil and add urad dal; let it splutter.
Add the prawn mixture to the pan , cover and cook it for 5 minutes on a medium flame
sauté until it is roasted well

title: Peanut Maggi
cooking_instructions:
Boil the maggi without the seasoning. Drain the water and keep the maggi aside.
Boil the egg and keep aside.
In a bowl, combine spring onion, garlic, red chili flakes, sesame seeds,  and soy sauce, and maggi seasoning.
Pour hot oil on this and mix.
Now add maggi to this sauce and toss.
Garnish with spring onion and serve with boiled egg.

title: High Protein Chilli Chicken
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine all the ingredients for the chicken. Coat and let it sit for 5 minutes.
In a non-stick pan, add 1 tsp oil, add the marinated chicken and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side or until golden brown.

In a kadhai/wok, add 1 tsp oil, add in the garlic and ginger and let it turn golden brown. 
Add the capsicum and onion petals and saute for 10 seconds. 
Add all the sauces, salt, pepper and toss.
Mix the corn starch with water and add it to the wok. Cook on a high flame for 1 minute.

Add in the chicken and cook for a couple more minutes until thoroughly coated. 
Finish with spring onion greens and serve hot.

title: Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar (pouch)
cooking_instructions:
Wash the toor dal until the water runs clean. 
Add the washed toor dal and water into a pressure cooker and pressure cook on a low to medium flame for 4 whistles (around 7-8 minutes) and set aside. 
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a kadhai.
⁠Add 10–15 peeled shallots (50 g) and 1 chopped tomato (40 g). 
Add the diced Drumsticks, pour 2 cups of water and let it cook for 5-6 minutes on a low to medium flame. 
Instead of Drumsticks, you can add any vegetable of your choice- 1 Cup (100g)
Add 1 pouch of Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala, mix and add the cooked dal and mix thoroughly. 
Close the lid and cook on a low- medium heat for 10 minutes. Finish with 1 tsp ghee and fresh coriander leaves.
⁠In another pan, heat 2 tsp oil, add ¼ tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter, add 1 dried red chilli and some curry leaves and add the tempering to the sambar.

recipe_ingredients.ingredient_name: Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar Masala Pouch

title: Red Thecha Potato Fry
cooking_instructions:
In a pan, heat oil and fry the ingredients for the thecha - cumin seeds, red chilies, peanuts, and garlic until golden brown.
Switch off the flame and add the coriander leaves. 
Coarsely crush this mixture/ pulse blend in a mixer grinder and set aside. Add salt. 
In a pan, heat oil, splutter the mustard seeds, then add the split urad dal, curry leaves, and asafoetida. 
Add the potato batons, fry until lightly browned and cooked through. Sprinkle water and steam for 2-3 mins. About 5-7 mins total.
Add the prepared thecha and mix well. Cook further for 2-3 mins. 
Serve hot with curd rice.

title: Iffa Chicken
cooking_instructions:
Marinate the chicken with the above ingredients and rest it for 15-30 minutes.
Take a blender and mix boiled egg whites and the given ingredients until thick consistency. 
Loosen it up with oil, if necessary.
In a hot pan, pour oil and place the chicken. 
Sear it under low flame and cook the chicken with a cover.
When the chicken is almost cooked, pour the white sauce on top and cook it until it combines well.

title: Bun Dosa With Sambar
cooking_instructions:
In a bowl, add rava, curd, salt, rice flour, and water. Blend it to a smooth batter.
 • In a kadai, heat oil and add mustard seeds, urad dal, and channa dal. Let it splutter.
 • Add onion and green chilli, and sauté for a minute.
Add this mixture to the prepared batter and mix well.
Heat a pan, add a little oil, pour the batter, and cook for two minutes on both sides.
In a pressure cooker, add the moong dal, water, onion, and tomato. Cover and pressure-cook for 2 whistles.
Once the pressure releases, add 1 pouch of Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar Masala and let it simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish with 1 tsp ghee and fresh coriander leaves.
In another pan, heat 2 tsp oil. Add ¼ tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add 1 dried red chilli and a few curry leaves.
Add this tempering to the sambar and serve hot.

recipe_ingredients.ingredient_name: Cookd Madras Tiffin Sambar Masala Pouch

title: Moong Dal Kachori
cooking_instructions: Rub together the ghee with the flour and salt until it resembles crumbs. Add water and knead a semi-soft dough. Rest the dough for 30 mins, covered.
For the stuffing: soak the moong dal for 30 mins in plain water.
Strain the moong dal and pulse blend in a mixer grinder until coarse.
Pound the spices.

Heat ghee in a pan and add the powdered spices and besan, on a low flame. Add the moong dal and mix well, add half a cup of water and constantly stir for 4-5 mins. Cool down the mixture completely. The consistency should resemble a dough.
Divide the dough into roundels. Flatten them and add the stuffing in the center of each, bring the ends together to seal it and flatten them to ½ inch thickness.
Deep fry in a low flame for about 15 mins until golden brown and crispy.

title: Healthy base gravy
cooking_instructions: In a saucepan, add oil, add the vegetables, along with garlic and roast for 15 mins
Cool it down and grind it into a smooth puree

In a pan, add oil.
Add jeera, let it splutter. Then add chopped garlic and green chillies. Saute for few seconds.
Pour the vegetable puree.

Add the kashmiri chili powder, garam masala and mix.
Roast it for a while till the raw taste goes away. Season with salt.
Finish off with butter
Any protein or vegetable of choice can be added to this base gravy to make different preparations, eg, butter paneer masala, butter chicken, kadai paneer, etc.

title: Coconut Milk Rasam
cooking_instructions:
Soak a lemon-sized portion of tamarind in 1 cup of water. 
Strain the tamarind water in a cooking vessel. Add the chopped tomatoes and smash them well.
Coarsely crush the peppercorns and cumin seeds to the tamarind water
Crush the garlic, ginger, shallots & green chillies and add to the tamarind water
Add salt, turmeric powder, 1 sprig of curry leaves and some coriander leaves. Pour 2 cups of water.

Place this on the stove and bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 mins. 
Switch off the stove and add ½ cup of thick coconut milk.
Make a tempering in a pan with ghee, mustard seeds, asafoetida, curry leaves and gundu chillies. Pour into the rasam and mix

title: Tumbler Fried Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 30 minutes

In a pressure cooker, pour oil and add the chopped garlic and saute until light golden brown. 
Add all the other vegetables immediately and saute for 10 seconds.
Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar and add all the seasonings.
Add the soaked and thoroughly drained basmati rice and saute on a high heat gently for 1-2 minutes or until the rice is slightly fried.

Add the chicken cubes to the rice, pour water and bring it to a boil. 
Cover and let it cook on a low-medium heat for 12-14 minutes.

Once the pressure fully releases, open the rice, add the chopped capsicum and spring onion greens and fluff up the rice. 
Serve hot.

title: Coconut Milk Maggi
cooking_instructions:
In a saucepan, add oil. Add carrot, beans and babycorn to this and saute for 3 mins, till the vegetables are cooked.
Add water, maggi cakes and maggi seasoning. Let it cook for a few mins.
Pour coconut milk and close the pan with a lid. Bring it to a boil and turn off the heat.
Transfer it into a bowl.
Garnish it with fried onion, fried garlic, spring onion, peanuts, boiled egg, lemon wedges or any other garnish of choice

title: Palak Chana Masala
cooking_instructions:
Pressure cook the soaked chana with water, salt, black cardamom and bay leaf for 6 whistles on a medium-low flame. 
Allow the pressure to release naturally; the chana should be soft when pressed. 
Remove some chana from this and mash it well. Keep aside, this will be used to thicken the gravy. 
For the palak puree, blanch palak spinach in boiling water for 1 min. Drain and place in cold water. Squeeze out the excess water. 
Transfer to a mixie jar with some water and blend to a fine puree
For the masala, heat ghee in a pan. Add the whole spices and cumin seeds. Fry briefly. 
Add onions and saute until they start developing a brown colour, add the chopped green chillies and ginger garlic paste. Cook till the raw smell goes.
Add the tomatoes, powdered spices and salt. Add a splash of water and cook until the tomatoes are soft and the oil starts to release.
Add the palak puree and mix well. Add the boiled chana. 
Cover and simmer for 5-7 mins. 
Open the lid, add the mashed chana and kasuri methi. Mix well and cook to the desired consistency. 
Finish with ghee and fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with chappatis or pooris

title: Mysore Pak Toast
cooking_instructions:
Take a mixing bowl and add besan, ghee and sugar to it. Whisk it to make a paste
Take 4 slices of bread and apply ghee on one side. Apply the paste on the other side.
Garnish with chopped almonds and cashew nuts
Preheat the oven or airfryer to 180 C for 10 mins.
Place the toast on the baking tray and bake for 5 mins or until lightly crispy

title: Cooker Sambar Sadham
cooking_instructions:
Wash the toor dal and rice until the water runs clean. 
In a pressure cooker, pour oil and add the mustard and fenugreek seeds
Once the mustard seeds splutter, add all the vegetables and saute for 2-3 minutes on a medium flame.

Add the Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar and mix thoroughly. 
Add the washed toor dal and rice, and water into a pressure cooker on a low to medium flame for 4 whistles (around 7-8 minutes) and set aside.
Finish with ghee and coriander leaves.

recipe_ingredients.ingredient_name: Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala

title: Two in one chicken
cooking_instructions:
In a pan, heat oil. Add  onions and saute.
Once the onions are translucent, add  tomato and saute for a few mins.
Add Chicken Masala  and mix. Now, add grated coconut and mix.
Cool the mixture and grind it into a smooth paste with some water.
In a pan, add oil,  add  onion, red chili, green chili  and saute till translucent. 
Add  tomato and cook for a few minutes until soft. 
Add the paste to this and Chicken Masala.
Add 1 kg of chicken to this, water as needed and let it simmer.
Adjust the salt if needed.
Add curry leaves, let it simmer
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
In a pan, add oil,curry leaves, green chili and onions.Saute till onions turn brown.
Add chicken masala and chicken pieces followed by pepper powder. Stir it well and garnish with chopped coriander leaves.

title: Coconut Ice -Cream
cooking_instructions:
Separate the coconut flesh from the shell.
In a mixer, add the coconut chunks along with some water and grind it into a paste.
Now strain this mixture to get fresh coconut milk.
Now in a mixer, add the coconut milk, banana, cashewnuts, jaggery powder and vanilla essence.
Grind it into a smooth batter like consistency.
Use the coconut shells as molds and pour this mixture into the shells.
Freeze it for 5 hours and serve.

title: Parsi Brown Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash the basmati rice and soak it for 20 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pot and add the whole spices. Cook it until they turn fragrant. Add the onions and saute them continuously until they start to brown.
Add the sugar and allow it to caramelize, stirring occasionally.
Add the water and bring it to a boil. Strain and add the soaked rice. Boil on high flame until the level of rice almost reaches the level of the water.
Cover with aluminum foil or with a tight-fitting lid. Cook on a low flame for 14 minutes.
Once cooked, stir it gently from the sides. Serve with any dish of your choice. This rice is a classic combination with Parsi Dhansak.

title: Pressure Cooker Millet Sambar Rice
cooking_instructions:
Wash the Toor Dal and Barnyard Millet until the water runs clean. 
In a pressure cooker, pour oil and add the mustard and fenugreek seeds
Once the mustard seeds splutter, add all the vegetables and saute for 2-3 minutes on a medium flame. 
Add the Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar and mix thoroughly. 
Add the washed toor dal and rice, and water into a pressure cooker on a low to medium flame for 4 whistles (around 7-8 minutes) and set aside.
Finish with ghee and coriander leaves.

recipe_ingredients.ingredient_name: Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala

title: Bombay Ice Halwa
cooking_instructions:
In a pan, combine the ghee, maida, sugar and milk. Mix well. 
Keep it on a low heat and keep cooking until it thickens. 
Add the cardamom powder and food colour, and if using saffron, soak it in some warm milk and add. 
Cook until it releases from the pan and is a stretchy dough.
Transfer this between 2 greased parchment papers, roll it out as thin as possible. 
Add the almond slivers and rose petals as garnish. 
Allow it to cool and dry for an hour. 
Cut into squares and serve.
If storing, place between sheets of parchment paper.

title: Street Style Masala Sundal
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the white peas for 5 to 6 hours.
Add the soaked peas to a cooker, pour in water, turmeric powder, and salt, and pressure-cook for 2 whistles on medium flame.
On the other side, add tomato, onion, green chilli, and ginger–garlic to the mixer jar and blend into a thick paste.
In a kadai, heat oil and add the onion-tomato paste along with all the spice powders. Sauté until the raw smell goes away.
Strain the peas and reserve the cooked water.
Separate some of the cooked peas, mash them, and keep aside.
Now add the cooked peas, reserved water, and the mashed peas. Add additional water if needed and let it simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with chopped onion, coriander leaves, cornflakes, and masala vadai of your choice

title: Aravana Payasam
cooking_instructions:
Melt the jaggery and keep it aside to cool down
Roast coconut slices and raisins with ghee in a pan and keep it aside.
Pour some water in a pot and let it boil.
Add washed matta rice and cook it till it’s 75% cooked.
Add melted jaggery, ghee, raisins, cardamom powder and dry ginger powder to the payasam and mix it well.
Stir continuously until it thickens up to required consistency. 
Add ghee to top it off.

title: Gym bro High Protein Parotta
cooking_instructions:
In a mixing bowl, add all the ingredients and knead them into a smooth and soft dough. 
Cover and let it rest for 15-20 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, add all the ingredients and knead them into a smooth and soft dough. 
Cover and let it rest for 15-20 minutes.
Divide the dough into balls and let it rest for 10-15 minutes.
Roll the dough until very thin (dusting with flour and oil and shape into an accordion. 
Fold and roll into a parotta, set aside. 
And cook on a tawa on a high flame until cooked through. 
Stack the cooked parottas on top of each other and smash to flake them up and serve hot with any curry of your choice

title: Tumbler Christmas Fruit Cake
cooking_instructions: Add the dried fruits to a pan along with orange juice, brandy/rum, and orange zest. Mix well and cook on a low-medium flame for 3–4 minutes, until the fruits absorb the liquid. Set aside and allow to cool completely.

In a mixing bowl, add the brown sugar and melted butter. Whisk until evenly combined.
Add the eggs one at a time, whisking well after each addition.

Sift in the maida, spice powder, and baking powder. Mix gently until just combined.
Add the cooled, soaked fruits and fold gently to form a thick batter.

Line a baking tin with parchment paper and pour in the prepared batter.
In a deep pan, spread a layer of salt at the bottom and place a stand or elevation inside. Place the cake tin on the stand, cover, and cook on a medium flame for 50–60 minutes, or until the cake is cooked through and moist.
Remove the cake and pour 2–3 tablespoons of orange juice or brandy over the top. Let it rest for 2–3 hours.
Once completely cooled, slice and serve.

title: Thakkali Chutney
cooking_instructions:
Boil the tomato, mash it partially, and set it aside.
In a kadai, add oil, mustard seeds, and urad dal, and let it splutter.
Now add the onion and sauté for 2 minutes.
Next, add the mashed tomato, red chilli powder, and salt, and simmer for 5 minutes
In a bowl, take 2 tablespoons of idli batter and dilute it with water.
Add the diluted idli batter to the pan and simmer again for 5 minutes.
Finish with coriander leaves and curry leaves

title: Thavala Vadai
cooking_instructions:
In a bowl, add the dal and rice, take out 1 tbsp of moong dal and set aside. 
Wash the dals and rice until the water runs completely clear. 
Add the dried red chilli and let it soak for 1 hour. 
Strain the dal into a mixer jar. 
Blend into a coarse, very thick batter, add it to a mixing bowl and set aside. 
In a pan, pour groundnut oil, add the urad dal, curry leaves and saute until golden brown. 
Add the grated coconut, asafoetida and saute on a medium flame for 1 minute, making sure the coconut doesn’t change colour and add it to the prepared dal. 
Add salt and the moong dal and mix thoroughly.
Shape into vadais and deep from on a medium flame for 4-5 minutes on a low medium flame. 
Serve hot.

title: Easy Mutton Roast
cooking_instructions: Add mutton, salt, ginger garlic paste and turmeric in a pressure cooker for 6 whistles on a medium flame with water.
Drain the mutton, retain the stock.
Heat oil and add the curry leaves. Add the green chillies and onions. Saute until light brown.
Add the boiled mutton and stir for 2 mins on high heat.
Add red chilli powder and stir. Add the strained stock. Boil until nearly dry again.
Add the coriander, fennel, black pepper powder and garam masala powder and cook until dry and the masala coats the meat.

title: Biryani Cheesecake
cooking_instructions:
Add the digestive biscuits and fried onions to a bag and break them into a coarse powder.
Add the powder to a mixing bowl and add all the other ingredients to the powder, and mix thoroughly. Add it to a spring-form cake tin and press into a tight layer- making sure it’s not too thick or thin.
In another mixing bowl, add the cream cheese, mix the corn flour thoroughly into the hung curd, and add it to the cream cheese. 
Add all the other ingredients for the cream cheese filling and mix thoroughly, making sure everything is evenly combined.
Pour the prepared filling into the tin and bake in a water bath for 60 minutes at 160 degrees Celsius. 
Let it cool completely (for at least 1 hour) and keep it refrigerated for 3-4 hours, or until completely set. 
Slice into your preferred thickness and garnish with fried onions, saffron, coriander, mint leaves, and raita, then serve.

title: One bowl Instant Bread
cooking_instructions:
In a bowl, add the maida, salt, baking powder, and mixed seeds. 
Add the Greek yogurt, water, and olive oil. 
Using a spatula, bring together a rough dough.
 Tip it onto a floured surface and form a rough ball. It doesn’t have to be kneaded. 
Transfer the dough to a baking tray, on parchment paper dusted with flour. 
Bake in a preheated oven at 180 °C for 20-25 mins until the crust is golden. 
Allow it to cool for a while, slice and serve. Store in an airtight container, outside for 3 days or in the fridge for 5-7 days.

title: Tumbler Banana Bread
cooking_instructions:
Mash the overripe bananas in a mixing bowl and add sugar, milk and oil.
Mix thoroughly until thoroughly combined. 
Sift in the dry ingredients- maida, baking soda, salt, cinnamon powder and baking powder
Add the chopped walnuts and fold gently, making sure not to overmix them. 
Transfer the batter into a greased loaf tin. 
Place it in a deep pan lined with salt, cover and bake on a medium flame for 30 minutes. 
Let it cool for 30 minutes, cut into slices and serve.

title: Podi Muttai Chutney
cooking_instructions:
Boil the eggs for 12 mins (hard boil).
Peel and grate the eggs, keep it aside.
In a bowl add idli podi and salt.
In a tadka pan, add oil, once the oil heats up, add cumin and mustard seeds, let it splutter.
Add curry leaves and crushed garlic cloves to it.
Pour this tempering over idli podi.
Add grated eggs to this mixture and mix well.
Serve it with crispy dosas.

title: Beetroot Chips
cooking_instructions:
Peel off the skin and cut the beetroot into thin strips.
Wash it thoroughly. 
Mix them with salt, red chilly powder, besan flour and corn starch. Combine them well.
Heat oil in a pot for deep frying. 
Fry it until it’s crispy and cooked.

title: Kathirikai Chutney
cooking_instructions:
In a kadai, heat some oil and add garlic and ginger. Sauté for about 4 minutes until they turn golden brown.
Now add the chillies and curry leaves, and sauté for a few seconds.
Next, add the onion and brinjal, and cook for about 10 minutes until the raw smell goes away.
Add the remaining ingredients and sauté for a minute.
Let it cool, then transfer it to a mixer jar and coarsely blend it into a chutney.
Finish with a tempering and serve.

title: Koova Podi Payasam
cooking_instructions:
Wash Koova podi with water and let it settle for 15 minutes. Throw away the water and do this twice.
Mix water with arrow root powder and mix it well without lumps.
Add Ghee into a pot and saute coconut slices. Take it out when it’s golden in color. 
Add the arrowroot/water mixture with jaggery and cook it until it’s thick and lumpy.
Add the roasted coconut slices with cardamom powder and mix it well. 
Serve it hot!

title: Thiruvathirai kali
cooking_instructions: In a kadai, dry roast the rice and moong dal, then blend it coarsely (like rava).
In the same pan, melt the jaggery and strain it.
In a thick-bottomed vessel, add the melted jaggery and all the other ingredients and mix well.

Now add the blended rice flour to the jaggery mixture and mix well without any lumps.
Add the ghee at the end for flavor.

title: Ulundu Adai & Coconut Chutney
cooking_instructions:
Wash and soak the dal for 6 to 7 hours.
 In a mixer jar, add the soaked urad dal and coarsely blend it.
Transfer it to a bowl and add all the other ingredients, then mix well.
Cook it on a dosa pan with some oil.
Blend the coconut, roasted chickpeas, dry red chilli, and salt into a chutney.
 In another pan, heat oil and add mustard seeds, urad dal, and curry leaves for tempering.
 Add the tempering to the chutney and serve it along with the dosa.

title: Masala Macaroni
cooking_instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add salt and pasta. Boil for 7-8 minutes until it has softened but not mushy.
Reserve some of the water for later use. Strain the pasta, coat with oil and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds, garlic, ginger and green chilli. Add the onions and saute until it has softened.
Add the turmeric powder, red chilli powder and coriander powder. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato along with green peas. Once the tomato has slightly softened, add the tomato ketchup, chilli sauce (red/green), salt, pepper powder, capsicum and corn. Saute for 1 minute on high heat.
Add the reserved pasta water and cook for a minute.
Add the cooked pasta. Add coriander leaves, kasuri methi,  butter and cheese. Stir well and turn off the flame. Serve hot.

title: Instant Curd Rice
cooking_instructions: Soak the poha for 2 mins or until soft.
Add it in a bowl and mix it well with curd, milk, and salt until it’s of creamy consistency.

For making the tempering, heat the oil. Add jeera, mustard seeds, let it splutter.
Add dry red chillies, curry leaves.
Now add ginger, green chillies, peanuts and add this tempering over curd rice and mix.
Garnish with coriander leaves.

title: Oorga Muttai
cooking_instructions:
Heat a pan, then add the pickle oil. You can use the oil from any pickle (mango, lemon, mixed veg, fish pickle).
Crack the eggs onto it, let it cook for few seconds.
Add onion, tomato and salt.
Garnish with coriander.
Take it out while the yolk is still runny and serve it with toasted bread.

title: Thiruvathirai kootu
cooking_instructions:
Wash the rice and moong dal, and pressure-cook them for 3 whistles.
Wash and cut the veggies in same size
In a kadai, add water, all the vegetables, onion, tomato, red chilli powder, salt and turmeric powder. Cover and cook for 15–20 minutes on medium flame.
Once the vegetables are cooked, add the cooked dal, coconut and coriander leaves. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Prepare a tempering with oil, mustard seeds, urad dal and curry leaves, and pour it on top.

title: Chilli Garlic Mutton
cooking_instructions:
Add halved shallots and saute
Fry for a minute
Mix it well 
Place the whole garlic pods inside 
Don’t add any water, pressure cook on a low flame for 25 mins 
Once the pressure settles, open the cooker
Squeeze the garlic pulp from the pods 
Mix gently so that the mutton doesn’t break
Simmer to the desired consistency
Finish it with coriander leaves

title: Sugiyan
cooking_instructions: Pressure cook green gram with water and salt for 5 whistles. Don’t overcook.
Make the batter with maida, salt, sugar, turmeric powder, rice flour and water. Mix it well and keep it aside.

Mix grated jaggery, grated coconut, cumin powder and cardamom powder with boiled green gram and combine them well. 
Make the filling into balls and keep it aside.

In a pot, heat oil for deep frying.
Dip the balls into the batter and fry it when oil is hot. When it’s golden in color, you can take it out. 
Serve it with hot tea!

title: Sambar Fried Rice
cooking_instructions:
In a wok, heat oil and add mustard seeds. Let it splutter.
Saute curry leaves and dry red chillies followed by chopped garlic.
Next, add the veggies and let it cook for 5-10 minutes until soft.
Add the rice, soy sauce and Cookd Lunch Sambar Masala. Toss it nicely until well combined.

Add a bit of sugar and MSG. Salt, if needed. 
Finish it off with chopped coriander leaves.

recipe_ingredients.ingredient_name: Cookd Tamil Nadu Lunch Sambar Masala

title: High Protein Idly
cooking_instructions: In two separate bowls, add idly rice in one and all the lentils in the other. Wash well and soak for 4–5 hours.

Drain the water. Grind the rice with cold/ice water into a very smooth batter. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Grind the lentils into a slightly coarse batter and add them to the rice batter.
Mix both batters well. The consistency should be slightly thick, like regular idly batter.
Cover and ferment for 8 hours or overnight.
Once fermented, add water, salt, soy chunk powder, and hung curd. Mix into a loose, watery batter.

Pour into idly moulds and steam for 7–8 minutes.
Demould and serve hot.

title: Athalakkai Kulambu
cooking_instructions:
In a kadai, add oil, mustard seeds, urad dal, and curry leaves, and let them splutter.
Now add the shallots and garlic, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato and sauté for 3 minu
Now add the athalakkai and kulambu chilli powder, and sauté for a minute.
Add water, mix well, cover, and cook for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a mixer jar, add coconut, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, and water, and blend into a paste.
Add the coconut paste to the pan and simmer for 2 minutes.

title: Stuffed Kovakkai
cooking_instructions:
