To make motichoor laddoos, add half this mixture to a mixer grinder with a tbsp of warm milk and pluse blend 2-3 times until the boondis are broken down.
Clump them together to form laddoos. Garnish with silver leaf or halved cashew nuts

title: Chicken Pickle
cooking_instructions: Mix the chicken pieces with salt and turmeric powder.
In a non-stick pan, cook the chicken pieces without any oil until the moisture evaporates.
Heat oil in a pan and add the chicken and curry leaves. Fry on medium heat until crisp and golden brown. Remove the chicken pieces from the pan.
To the same oil, add ginger garlic paste and cook until the raw aroma goes away.
Add the fried chicken pieces back into the pan. Add red chilli powder, salt, coriander powder and methi powder.
Mix well and cook until the oil floats on top. Allow it to cool completely. Once it has cooled completely, add the lemon juice and mix well.
Allow it to rest for 1 day for the flavours to meld together, then consume the pickle. Store in a clean, dry airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 months.

title: Rara Gosht
cooking_instructions: In a cooker, heat the ghee and fry the whole spices until aromatic. Add the sliced ginger and the garlic paste and saute for 2 mins.
Add the halved red chillies and mutton. Saute for 2 mins. Add the water and salt and simmer covered for 20 mins after the first whistle comes on a high flame.
In a pot, add ghee and oil and add the onions and fry until golden brown.
Add the powdered spices, salt and tomatoes. Cook until soft and mushy.
Add the minced mutton meat and mix constantly to prevent the meat from clumping up.
Add ½ Cup of water and bring to a boil.
Simmer the gravy and add the curd, stirring constantly. Simmer covered for 10 mins. Add the pressure cooked meat to the mince.
Cook on a low flame for 10-15 mins until the oil separates.
Finish with coriander powder, ginger julienne and chopped fresh coriander leaves.

title: Spring Roll
cooking_instructions: For the sheets, in a bowl take the maida, salt and oil and mix to combine well.
Add water and knead a medium soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest the dough for 20 mins.
Knead the dough until smooth and divide into small roundels.
Dust with dry flour and roll the sheets thin.
To roll them completely thin. Apply oil on two of the sheets and dust with maida.
Layer them one on top of the other, three pieces in total and roll them out until very thin dusted with some maida as needed.
Cook them on a tava placed on a low heat. Cook both sides but without developing any colour. The sides must slightly dry out.
Take them off the tava and gently peel the layers. The sheets are ready.
In a wok, heat oil and add the chopped ginger, garlic and green chillies, saute until aromatic.
Add the remaining cut vegetables except the spring onion greens and saute until tender on a high flame.
Add the salt, pepper, vinegar, red chilli sauce, soya sauce, spring onion and ketchup. Mix well to combine.When the mixture is dry, transfer to a plate and allow the mixture to cool completely.
Prepare a thick mixture of maida and water to stick the spring roll ends.
To make the spring rolls, place some mixture on one end of the sheet and tuck the ends in, gently but tightly try to roll them, seal with the maida paste.
Deep fry them in a low flame for a minute or two and then in medium hot oil until golden brown and crispy, about 4 mins.

title: Onion Pakoda
cooking_instructions: Cut the onions into thin slices. Chop the curry leaves and green chillies. Take onion slices, curry leaves, green chillies in a mixing bowl
Add cumin seeds, asafoetida, chilli powder and salt to taste.
Add besan flour little by little and mix it with the onions. Ensure that too much besan flour is not added. Add rice flour to this mixture.
Mix everything together by sprinkling water such that the masala coats in each of the onion pieces. Ensure the masala is not too watery to get crispy pakoda

Heat enough oil to deep fry this. Add small batches of the mix and deep fry until the onions and batter turn crispy. Remove from oil, drain into a paper towel to remove excess oil. Serve hot as an evening snack.

title: Masala Tea
cooking_instructions: Crush the cloves, cinnamon stick, cardamom, star anise and ginger in a pestle and mortar.
Bring 500 ml of water to boil, add the crushed spices, tea powder and ginger. Let this boil for 2 minutes
Add sugar and milk to this. Keep simmering, stirring at intervals until the quantity reduced by 30%.
Filter and serve hot.

title: Naan
cooking_instructions: In a kneading bowl, add maida, salt, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, curd and water. Knead until everything combines.
Add oil and continue kneading the dough for 3 mins.Rest the dough for 60 mins.
Split the dough into equal-sized balls. Roll the dough into roti shaped circles.
Hold the rolled dough in between both your palms and flip your palms on both sided to extend one side of the dough.
Place the dough on a rolling board, apply oil or butter on the facing side. Apply little water on the other side of the rolled and extended dough.
Heat an Iron or Stainless Steel Tawa, place the water applied side on the Tawa.
Cook the dough for a few seconds. Lift the Tawa and show the other side of the dough to direct flame to cook the other side and also to get a chared look that we get in a tandoor naan.
To make Garlic Naan, add the finely chopped garlic on the facing side(the side where butter is applied before cooking) and cook it the same way. The garlic side has to be cooked on direct flame.
Apply butter once the naan is removed from the Tawa on the charred side.

title: Old-Delhi Mutton Korma
cooking_instructions: Fry sliced onions in hot oil until golden brown and allow them to cool and turn crispy.
Transfer to a mixer grinder and pulse blend until fine.
Heat the oil and ghee in a cooker and add the whole spices, saute until aromatic. Add the mutton and sear the meat on all sides in the hot oil. Continue cooking on a high flame for 10 mins.

Add the ginger garlic paste after it releases moisture, cook until the raw flavour goes. Add the powdered spices- turmeric, coriander and red chilli powders, salt and saute until oil begins separating.
Add the water, cover and simmer for 20 mins.
Once the pressure releases, open and add the whisked curd. Simmer for 10 mins.
Add the crushed fried onions. Finish with the chopped coriander leaves, kewra water,garam masala, nutmeg powder and mace.
Serve it with any Indian bread, rice or pulao.

title: Spiced Hot Chocolate
cooking_instructions: In a saucepan, heat milk and add the chopped chocolate. Stir to melt the chocolate.
Add the sugar, cocoa powder, vanilla essence and red chilli powder.
Add the cinnamon stick and mix until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is well combined.
Switch off the flame, cover, and steep the cinnamon for 10 minutes.
Return to heat and gently whisk the cream and simmer for a minute.
Remove from heat and serve warm with a pinch of red chilli powder.

title: Baked Oats
cooking_instructions: Add the oats, banana, honey, egg, salt, cinnamon powder and baking powder in a mixer grinder and blend to a smooth batter.
Grease an oven-safe mould with butter. Fill up the batter halfway through.
Add the chocolate chips and walnut bits on top and lightly press them.
Bake at 180°C for 20 mins in a preheated oven.
Serve it with a drizzle of honey.

title: Paneer 65
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the curd, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, garam masala, coriander powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, pepper powder, cornflour, maida, and rice flour.
Sprinkle water as needed to form a paste. Mix this well. Add lemon juice and mix again.
Add paneer cubes and mix gently to coat thoroughly.
Add oil in a deep frying pan, heat the oil and deep fry the marinated paneer in batches for 3-4 mins. Serve hot with lemon slices and onion rings.

title: Filipino Quail Eggs
cooking_instructions: Add all the ingredients into a saucepan. Mix well and simmer for 3 minutes or until the sauce thickens.
Bring water to a boil and drop the quail eggs in it. Boil for 3 minutes.
Cool them down and peel the shells.
Dredge the peeled eggs in cornstarch.
For the batter, combine all the ingredients except water and mix. Add the water gradually until you get a thick batter.
Dip the eggs in the batter. Using a skewer and a fork, pick them up and drop them directly into hot oil.
Fry for 3 minutes or until crispy and golden brown in colour. Serve with the dipping sauce.
Arrange the fried eggs on a skewer and serve them with the dipping sauce.

title: Japanese Chicken Katsu
cooking_instructions: If the chicken breast is too large, slice it to make two thin slices. Place the chicken breast between two sheets of plastic/cling wrap. Use a meat hammer or a heavy pan to pound the chicken breast until it is even in thickness (around ½-inch thick).
Keep breadcrumbs, maida and egg beaten with water in separate plates/flat bowls.
Salt the chicken with salt and pepper. Dredge the chicken breast in maida, and shake off the excess flour. Add it to the beaten eggs and then into the panko breadcrumbs and coat completely.
Add it into a pan of hot oil and fry until golden brown and crisp, turning it halfway through. The frying should take around 4-5 minutes.
For the sauce, combine all the ingredients together in a bowl.
Serve with rice or with a shredded cabbage salad.

title: Basbousa
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine the fine semolina, sugar, baking powder, desiccated coconut, egg, melted butter and vanilla essence. Add the curd and whisk until evenly combined.
Grease an ovenproof pan with butter. Pour the batter into the pan. Tap on the counter a few times to flatten the surface. Refrigerate for an hour.
Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Add the almonds and boil for 1 minute or until they start to puff up. Remove the almonds from the water and remove the skin.
Remove the skin from the almonds.
In a saucepan, add the water and sugar and bring to a boil. Add the lemon juice. If there is any foam or impurities floating on the surface, remove and discard them. Let it simmer for 10 minutes.
Once the batter has been refrigerated and has firmed up a little, cut them into squares. Place a blanched almond on each piece.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180 degrees Celsius for 35 minutes or until it turns golden brown.
Remove from the oven. Pour the sugar syrup over the baked Basbousa.
Bake again for another 10 minutes. Cool it before cutting it into pieces. This can be served warm or chilled.

title: Adai Dosa
cooking_instructions: Wash the rice and all the lentils together. Soak it along with the dry red chillies for at least 2-3 hours.

Strain and reserve the water from the dal and rice. Add the rice and dal to a mixer jar along with the dry red chillies, chopped onion, curry leaves, coriander leaves and salt. Grind it into a paste. Add 1 cup of the reserved soaking water.
Heat up a Tawa and grease with a bit of oil or ghee. Pour one ladle of the prepared batter and spread lightly using the back of the ladle. Cover with a lid and cook for 45 seconds to a minute.
Add a teaspoon of ghee and cook it for a further 15 seconds to let it crisp up a little.
Remove from the pan. Serve with chutney or Avial.

title: Modak
cooking_instructions: Bring the water to a boil with salt and ghee. Add the rice flour and mix immediately to form a rough dough.
Switch off the flame, cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Grease the bowl with ghee. Knead into a smooth dough, cover with a moist cloth and set aside.
For the sweet filling: Toast 1 cup of coconut for 2 minutes and add the jaggery. Mix well and add the cardamom powder. And set aside.
Divide the dough.
Roll the dough into discs, cut using a cutter for uniform shape.
Place the stuffing in the center and close the ends of the dough to make a half-moon shape, make indents at the end with your finger.
Steam the modaks for 10 minutes.

title: Pina Colada Mocktail
cooking_instructions: In a blender, combine the frozen pineapple, ice cubes, coconut milk, pineapple juice, fresh cream and brown sugar. Blend until smooth.
Pour into a glass and garnish with pineapple slices and cherries.

title: Pasta Salad
cooking_instructions: Boil the pasta until tender but not overboiled in salted water with oil.
Drain the pasta and coat with oil to prevent sticking.
To make the dressing, combine the mayonnaise, tomato ketchup, salt and pepper.
Combine the dressing, pasta and cut vegetables along with some parsley and mix well.
Finish the salad with some chopped parsley, cherry tomatoes and diced cheese.

title: Korean Fried Chicken
cooking_instructions: To the chicken wings, add the salt, pepper, baking powder, garlic powder and dry ginger powder. Mix until evenly combined.
Coat each piece in the cornstarch, pressing gently to make sure that it is properly coated.
Fry it on medium-low heat just until the chicken turns a light golden brown, around 6-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the oil and rest for a few minutes.
Increase the heat to high. Once the oil gets heated up, add the chicken back into the oil and fry for 2-3 minutes or until crispy and golden brown.
De-seed the chillies and soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Grind it along with garlic to a fine paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add the chilli paste. Cook for 3-4 minutes or until the oil floats around the sides.
Add the ketchup, soy sauce, honey, vinegar and sugar. Bring it to a simmer and then turn off the heat.
Add the fried chicken and toss. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and spring onion.

title: Wheat Halwa
cooking_instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pan, melt the ghee. Roast the cashews until they turn golden brown. Remove the cashews from the ghee and set aside.
In the same ghee, add the whole wheat flour. Stir and cook continuously on medium heat for 12-15 minutes. It should reach a deep golden colour similar to caramel.
Add the cardamom powder and sugar. Stir and cook for 2 minutes.

Add around ½ cup of the boiling water to the wheat mixture and stir well until it is combined. When the water is combined, add another ½ cup of the water. Keep repeating this step until you have eventually added all the water.
Cook for another 5 minutes while stirring constantly. Remove from the pan after cooking.
Transfer it in a flat dish. And let it for cool for two hours.
After it has cooled completely, turn it over onto a cutting board and cut it into cubes. Garnish with the fried cashew nuts.

title: Easy Dinner Rolls
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine the milk, sugar, yeast, butter and egg.
Mix the salt with the flour in a large bowl. Make a well in the centre.
Add in the wet mixture. Mix it using a wooden spoon until it forms a shaggy dough, then turn it onto a floured surface.
Knead until smooth. Cover with a moist cloth and rest for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into individual portions. Cover again and rest for 20 minutes.
Brush the dough balls gently with egg wash. Bake at 180 c in a preheated oven for 20 minutes.

title: Nutty Coffee Fudge
cooking_instructions: Heat the condensed milk in a pan until it starts to boil and turn off the stove.
Add the roasted nuts into the pan. Add the butter and vanilla essence. Mix well to combine, add the coffee as well.
Sift and add the cocoa powder in 3 additions and mix well in between additions. Once all the cocoa powder has been added, it will be firm and pliable.
Transfer to a parchment lined and oiled tray. Level the top and cover with a cling wrap/ plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 3 hours.

Dust a surface with cocoa powder and transfer the chilled fudge block and dust on top with cocoa powder. Cut them into small squares and further shape by hand into any desired shapes. Optionally can be dusted with cocoa powder to finish.

title: Thinai Payasam
cooking_instructions: Dry roast Thinai and Moong dal on low flame until it is fragrant. Set this aside.
Add Jaggery and water in a pan and heat it till the Jaggery melts completely. Use a filter to remove the impurities and extract Jaggery syrup. Keep aside
In a small pan add Ghee, Cashews and Raisins. Roast until golden brown and till the raisins puff. Keep aside.
Cook Thinai and Moong dhal with 2 cups of water in a pressure cooker for 3 whistles.
In a pan add milk, cooked Thinai and Moong Dhal and jaggery syrup.
Add Cardamom powder and keep stirring continuously.
Add Ghee, Roasted Cashews and Raisins. Remove from the heat. Serve warm or chilled.

title: Palak Paneer
cooking_instructions: In a pot simmer chopped onion, cashew and green chilli for 15 minutes.
Blend this into a smooth paste once it cools.
Wash and chop the Palak leaves, add this to boiling water for 2-3 minutes.
Drain this and transfer it to a container with cold water to stop the leaves from cooking further and to retain the green colour. Blend the leaves in a mixer grinder to make a puree. Keep this aside.
In a pan, heat oil and butter. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and saute for 2 minutes. Add onion-cashew paste and cook for a further 5 mins.
Add spinach puree and 1 cup of water to the pan and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add garam masala, salt, sugar and Kasuri methi and cook for a further 3 minutes.
Add paneer cubes and cook for a further 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh cream and serve hot with Rice/Roti/Phulka.

title: Egg Curry
cooking_instructions: Hard Boil the eggs and deshell them.
In a pan, heat 2 tbsp oil, add turmeric, chilli powder, salt and fry the hard-boiled eggs in it and keep it aside.
Puree the tomatoes in a mixer grinder.
In a pan heat oil, add Cinnamon, Cloves, Cardamom, Bay leaf, Cumin Seeds and saute it. Add finely chopped onions to the same pan and saute onions until onions are golden brown.
Add tomato puree to the onion followed by the ginger garlic paste and saute it well till the raw smell goes off
Add Kashmiri Red Chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, salt and little water and continue to cook for 10 mins with the lid on.
Add one boiled egg yolk to thicken the gravy. Add Kasuri methi and black pepper powder to the gravy.
Once thickened add the boiled egg and continue cooking for 5 mins.
Garnish it with chopped coriander and serve hot.

title: Madurai Mutton Sukka
cooking_instructions: Dry Roast the ingredients mentioned under Dry Roast and Grind, until it turns aromatic.
Grind it and keep it aside.
Pressure cook mutton pieces with 1 tsp Gingelly oil, ¼ tsp turmeric powder, 1tsp ginger garlic paste, salt and 1 Cup of Water for 10-12 whistles. Keep Aside.
In another pan heat Oil and add Red chilli, Cinnamon, Bay Leaf, Fennel Seeds and let the spices splutter for 30 seconds. Add shallots, ginger garlic paste and cook for a few minutes.
Add Chilli Powder, Coriander Powder, ¼ tsp of Turmeric powder and salt. Add the mutton stock water(Water in the pressure cooker) to the pan and let the spices cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked mutton pieces and continue cooking until the liquid starts turning thick.
When most of the water is evaporated, add the ground spice powder and roast the mutton till it is dry. Add curry leaves and lemon juice.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with Rice.

title: Madras Meen Kulambu
cooking_instructions: Marinate the fish with lemon Juice, vinegar and a little salt for 30 minutes.
In a mixer grinder, grind all the ingredients under ‘To Grind’. Keep aside.
Pound in a pestle and mortar or grind coarsely the fenugreek and cumin seeds together and keep aside.
Soak tamarind in 200 ml of water, extract tamarind juice, strain and keep aside.
Heat the oil in a broad pan and add mustard seeds. Once they splutter add onions and fry until golden brown. Add curry leaves to this.
Add Coriander powder, Chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Stir fry this for a minute.
Add coconut paste and saute this for 5 minutes.
Add tamarind water and 3 cups of water. Bring the curry to boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Slowly add the fish pieces and reduce the heat and cook for 3 minutes. Sprinkle the powder of fenugreek and cumin and remove from the heat.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with steamed rice.

title: Bakery Butter Bun
cooking_instructions: Combine the yeast and milk and allow the yeast to bloom for a few minutes.
In a large bowl, add the maida, salt, sugar and melted butter and then the milk mixture.
Knead a smooth and soft dough, apply butter on top and rest the dough for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Knock back the dough, knead until smooth and divide into medium sized roundels, flatten them. Rest the portioned dough for 10 mins
Heat oil in a kadai in medium heat, reduce the heat to low and deep fry the dough for 8 minutes until golden brown and fluffy, cooked through.
For the cream, whisk the sugar and butter together until light and fluffy.
Add the milk and vanilla essence and combine well. Whisk to hold stiff peaks.
Once the bun has cooled, cut the bun in half and apply the butter mixture in the center.

title: Chicken Shami Kebab
cooking_instructions: Soak the Chana Dal for 30 mins.
In a pan, add 1 tbsp ghee, onion and fry for 2 mins. Add bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, coriander seeds, chopped garlic and chopped ginger. Mix well.
Add the minced chicken, soaked chana dal, salt and red chilli powder. Add 2 cups of water and cook the chicken until the water evaporates.
Remove the cinnamon, bay leaf, cloves and cardamom.
Transfer the cooked mixture to a mixer grinder jar. Add green chilli, coriander leaves, mint leaves, egg, garam masala, cumin powder to the mixer grinder jar.
Make round flat patties with the grounded chicken.
In a Tawa, add ghee and fry them on both sides. Serve hot with mint chutney.

title: Kesar Pista Kulfi
cooking_instructions: Chop the Almonds and Pistas.
Heat a heavy-bottomed Kadai and bring the milk to a boil and continue to simmer on medium heat. Simmer until the volume of the milk is reduced by half. Should take around 30 minutes.
Add Sugar and saffron, continue to simmer for 5 more minutes.
Add the cardamom powder, chopped almonds and chopped Pista. Mix well.
Remove from heat and allow it to cool.
Once it reached room temperature, transfer to kulfi moulds and freeze for at least 10 hours. After 3 hours, if necessary insert wooden stick to use as a handle.
Unmould the kulfi and serve cold.

title: Tamarind Rice
cooking_instructions: Soak Tamarind in warm water for 10 mins and extract tamarind Juice.
In a pan dry roast the ingredients under spice powder and grind it into a fine powder.
Heat 3 tbsp of oil in a pan, add split urad dal, Bengal gram, peanuts and red chilli. Fry until the dal and peanuts turn golden brown. Add tamarind juice and salt. Let this cook for 10 mins.

Add the spice powder to the cooking tamarind juice. Reduce the flame to low and Keep stirring the pan to incorporate the spices in the tamarind juice. Once the paste thickens, remove the pan from heat.
In another pan, heat oil and add the tempering ingredients. Once the tempering splutters, add the tempering to the puliodharai mix. Once the mix is cooled, we can store this in an airtight container.
To assemble the puliyodharai, take 2 cups of cooked rice, add sesame oil, a little salt and some puliyodharai mix. Mix well, rest for 15 mins and serve.

title: Peas Pulao
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 20 mins.
Heat the pressure cooker and add oil and butter. Add the whole spices and saute for a minute. Add the sliced onions and green chillies and saute till onions turn golden brown.
Chop the garlic cloves and add it. Add the peas and saute for 2 mins. Add coconut milk and salt. Let it boil.
Add the basmati rice and mix all the ingredients together. Add 1/2 cups of water and pressure cook for 1 whistle.
Serve hot with onion raita.

title: Ellu Curry
cooking_instructions: Soak the tamarind in ½ cup of hot water for 15 mins.
Toast the sesame seeds and grind them into a fine powder.

Dry roast the dry red chillies and urad dal. When the urad dal starts to change its colour, add the grated coconut and continue cooking until the coconut has browned. Add water as needed and grind to a fine paste.

Cut the yam pieces a little smaller than the potato and the raw banana. This ensures that they cook adequately and evenly. Pressure cook the diced yam, raw banana and potato along with turmeric powder, salt and 1 cup of water, for 1 whistle on a high flame.
Add the tamarind pulp and the ground coconut paste. Allow it to cook for 5 minutes.
Add the jaggery to the curry and season with salt.
Meanwhile, we can prepare the tempering. In another pan, heat coconut oil and add mustard seeds. When the mustard seeds start to splutter, add the curry leaves and remove from the heat.
Add the tempering to the pan. Add the toasted sesame powder and turn off the heat.

title: Chicken Adobo
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken with soy sauce, peppercorns, bay leaves and 2 tbsp of garlic.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat the oil and add the chopped onion and 1 tbsp of garlic.
When the onion turns translucent, add the marinated chicken pieces and cook for 30 seconds on each side, on high flame. Then add in the excess marinade into the pan. Add in ½ cup of water.
When it comes to a boil, cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add in the vinegar and sugar.
Cook on high flame until the sauce reduces and becomes thick enough to coat the chicken. Serve hot with rice.

title: Ghee Mysore Pak
cooking_instructions: Melt 2 cups of ghee in a pan. It does not have to be heated much, just until it melts.
Grease a tray with ghee and line with parchment paper and set aside.
Sieve the gram flour to remove any lumps. In a bowl, combine the besan and ½ cup of ghee into a smooth and lump-free mixture.
Add the sugar and water to a pan and heat it to form the sugar syrup. Continue cooking until it reaches a 1-string consistency.
On a low flame, add the gram flour mixture into the sugar syrup. Mix well.
Once it is combined, add the remaining ghee ¼ cup at a time. Add more ghee only after the previously poured ghee has been completely incorporated with the mixture.

Continue this step and keep stirring continuously. Keep cooking until the mixture starts to leave the side of the pan and the mixture gets cooked. You can check if it is cooked by taking a small piece of the mixture between your fingers and rolling it. If it forms into a ball without sticking, then it is done.
At this stage, bring the flame to high and mix vigorously for around 30 seconds.
Turn off the flame and immediately pour the mixture into the greased pan. Allow it to cool for 3 hours. De-mould it and cut it into pieces.

title: Badushah
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the maida,baking powder and salt, mix well. Add ghee and crumble until the texture resembles crumbs.
Add water and clump together a soft dough. Cover and rest for 30 mins.
Boil the sugar with water and add the cardamom powder and saffron soaked in 2 tbsp of hot water to the syrup and mix well, bring to one string consistency. Cover and retain the heat of the syrup.
Portion into small roundels and make a hole with your finger in the center of each.
Fry the badushah in a low heat until crispy and golden brown, about 18-20 mins. Turn them gently mid way through.
Dip the fried Badushah in the warm sugar syrup for 5-10 mins and strain them. Cool and serve.

title: Kaju Katli
cooking_instructions: Grind the cashew nuts in a mixer jar. Grind for 3-5 seconds, mix using a spoon and then grind again. Repeat this process around 4 times or until the cashew is completely powdered.
In a pan, heat the sugar and water together on medium heat until it thickens. It should have a two string consistency.

Turn the flame to low and add the cashew powder. Mix continuously until the mixture becomes even and thickens. Roll a small piece of the mixture between your fingers. If it does not stick, then it is ready.
Turn off the heat and allow it to cool slightly, until you can touch it with your hands.

Transfer the mixture onto a sheet of parchment/butter paper. Flatten it using your hands greased with ghee and place another piece of parchment paper on top. Roll it into 1-cm thick using a rolling pin.
Place the silver leaf on top. Allow it to cool for 30 minutes. Cut it using a sharp knife.

title: Cocktail Samosa
cooking_instructions: Place the maida, salt and ajwain in a bowl and rub in with the oil to make a crumble consistency.
Add water and knead a semi-hard dough and rest it for 20 mins.
For the mixture, coarsely grind the sev with all the spices and seasonings.
Heat oil in a pan and add the mixture, saute until aromatic and the oil is absorbed well. Set aside the mixture to cool.
Portion the dough into roundels. Roll out into circles and cut into semi-circles.
Make a cone with the semi-circle and place the stuffing, enclose the samosas securely.
Deep fry in medium hot oil until golden brown. Cool completely and store airtight.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, whisk the curd along with all the ingredients for the marination except mustard oil and red chilli powder.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan until it reaches its smoking point. Turn off the heat and add red chilli powder. Immediately mix it gently and add it to the curd marination.
Add in the chicken. Mix well and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan. Fry the marinated chicken pieces in a pan, leaving space between each piece. Fry for 4 minutes on each side. Remove from the pan.
In the same pan, add butter and add onions. Saute until the onion turns golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder and coriander powder, and saute.
Add tomato puree, salt and sugar. Cook until the oil floats on top (5 to 7 minutes) and the mixture has thickened slightly. The raw taste of the tomato should have disappeared by this stage.
Add in cream, garam masala powder, kasuri methi, the cooked chicken and coriander leaves. Mix well and bring it to a simmer. Serve hot with naan/rice.

title: Red Velvet Cookies
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine the maida, baking powder, salt and cocoa powder together. Set aside.
In a bowl, cream the butter and sugar together until fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time. Add the vanilla essence and lemon juice and mix until just combined.
Add red food colour as needed and mix. Fold in the white chocolate chips.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Scoop out each portion of the mixture into a bowl of icing sugar. Coat and place on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Leave plenty of space around each cookie as it will spread out.
Bake at 180 c for 15 minutes. Allow cookies to cool completely before consuming or storing in an airtight container.

title: Coleslaw
cooking_instructions: In a large bowl, add the shredded cabbage and salt. Set the bowl aside for 10 minutes. This is to soften the cabbage.
In another bowl, mix the mayonnaise, white pepper powder and lemon juice.
Mix this dressing with the cabbage, along with the carrot and onion.
Mix well to combine. Serve cold or at room temperature.

title: Chapli Kebab
cooking_instructions: In a pan, add all the ingredients for the kebab masala and toast on low heat until they turn aromatic, around 2-3 minutes.
In a bowl, combine the mutton mince, onion, green chilli, tomato, ginger garlic paste, coriander leaves and salt. Add the previously prepared masala as well. Add the egg and gram flour and mix well.
Rest it in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Divide the mixture and roll them. Using a plate that is greased with oil or lined with butter paper, flatten the meat into thin kebabs.
Heat oil in a pan and fry until cooked through.

title: Aval Payasam
cooking_instructions: In a blender, powder 2 tbsp aval with 8 cashew nuts and set aside.
For the jaggery syrup, melt the jaggery with water and strain it. Allow the syrup to cool completely and become sticky.
For the preparation, heat ghee and add the cashews and raisins, fry them until golden and set them aside.
In the same pan add and saute the aval until aromatic, add the powdered aval and cashew nuts as well. Saute for a minute more.
Add the milk and gently bring to a boil while stirring to thicken the milk and cook the aval until tender. Add the cardamom powder.
Turn off the stove and add the fried cashew and raisins.
Finally, add the cooled syrup and mix well. This payasam can be served hot or cold.

title: Wheat Dosa
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the wheat flour, rice flour, salt, semolina, mix them. Add the remaining ingredients and mix well.
Add the curd and water, Whisk until lump-free and smooth.
Rest the batter for 20 mins.
Heat a tava on high flame and pour the batter on the tava in a thin layer, add ghee on top as needed. Mix the batter well before preparing each dosa.
Allow the dosa to become crispy on a low-medium flame and flip it, if desired. About 2 mins.Fold it as needed. Serve hot with chutney.

title: Aloo Paneer Tikki
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the ginger garlic paste and green chillies, cook until the flavour is no longer raw.
Add the onions and cook until translucent. Add the capsicum and cook until tender.
Add the powdered spices, salt, desiccated coconut and powdered peanuts. Mix well to combine.
Add the paneer and mix well.
Soak bread in water and squeeze out the water thoroughly. Add it to the potatoes and add salt. Mash until smooth.
Use cornstarch to bind the dough well.
Stuff roundels of the potato mixture with the paneer mixture and flatten into tikkis.
Deep fry in medium hot oil until golden brown and serve warm with ketchup.

title: Tiffin Sambar
cooking_instructions: Soak tamarind in ½ Cup of water and extract tamarind juice.
Wash the Dal until the water is clear.
Pressure cook the Toor dal and pumpkin with turmeric powder, 2 Cups of water for 8 whistles and mash the dal and pumpkin. Keep aside.
Dry roast and grind all the ingredients under Sambar powder into a powder.
Heat oil in a Kadai, add mustard seeds, urad dal, dried red chilli and asafoetida. Add the chopped shallots, tomato and saute for a minute.
Add the salt, sambar powder and cook for 2 mins. Add the tamarind juice to the Kadai and let it simmer for 3 mins.
Add ghee. Add the mashed dal and pumpkin mixture, 1 Cup water and Jaggery to the Kadai and let it simmer for 5 mins.
Add the curry leaves and coriander leaves. Remove from heat and serve hot with Dosa/Idly/Pongal.

title: Paruppu Poli
cooking_instructions: Soak the Chana dal in water for 60 mins.
In a bowl, add flour, a pinch of salt, 2 tbsp of oil and water and knead into a smooth, loose dough.
Add 2 tbsp of oil to cover the kneaded dough and rest the dough for 2 hours.

Cook the soaked chana dal with 2 Cup of water in a pressure cooker on a medium flame for 5 whistles. Remove the pressure cooker from heat and let the pressure settle down. Drain out the water from the Chana.
Heat a pan, add 1 tsp of ghee and 2 tbsp of grated coconut. Saute this till coconut turns golden brown.
Transfer the cooked chana dal to a mixer grinder jar. Grind the chana dal with cardamom powder and jaggery.
Transfer the ground mixture to a pan and saute for 5 mins to remove moisture.
Set this aside to cool. Make lemon sized balls out of this cooled mixture.
In a banana leaf, apply oil, take a small portion of the dough and flatten it using the fingers. Place a ball of stuffing and cover it with the dough by pinching in the top.
Place a ball of stuffing and cover it with the dough by pinching in the top.
Apply oil to your hands and flatten the dough with the stuffing to form a circle.
Cook this on a Tawa on medium heat. Apply oil on both sides and cook.
Set aside to cool and serve.

title: Bisi Bele Bath
cooking_instructions: Dry roast all the ingredients under Bisi Bele Bath masala until aromatic and grind it into a powder using a mixer grinder.
Soak tamarind in warm water and extract tamarind juice.
Cook the washed Toor Dal and Rice in a pressure cooker for 4 whistles with 6 cups of water.
In a Kadai, heat 2 tsp of oil, add the shallots and saute until they are translucent. Add the chopped vegetables to the same Kadai and stir fry for 2 minutes.
Add 1 Cup of Water and cook the vegetables for 7 mins.
Add tamarind juice to the cooked vegetables and continue to cook for another 2 mins. Add turmeric powder, salt and 4 tbsp of prepared bisi bele bath masala, jaggery. Mix well and remove from heat.
In another pan, add 3 tbsp of ghee and add the tempering ingredients. Roast until the cashews are golden brown.
Mash the dal and Rice mixture and add the cooked vegetable mixture. Add jaggery and cook for 5 mins till the water is absorbed and Bisebelabath reaches the desired consistency.
Add the tempering to the cooked bisi bele bath and mix well. Serve the Bisebelabath hot with Potato Chips or Vadagam.

title: Punjabi Rajma Masala
cooking_instructions: Add Rajma and water in a bowl and soak the Rajma for 8 hours to overnight.

Drain the soaked rajma and wash it once more with fresh water. Pressure cook the washed rajma with 5 cups of water, bay leaf, cinnamon stick and salt for 10 whistles. Once the pressure settles, keep the cooked rajma with the water in which it had been cooking aside.
Blend onions in a mixer grinder to make onion paste.
Blend the tomatoes in a mixer grinder to make tomato puree.
Heat 3 tbsp of ghee in a pan, add dried red chilli, cloves, cardamom, cumin seeds and black peppercorns and saute for a minute. Add onion paste and saute until they turn into light brown colour.
Add chopped green chillies. Add the ginger-garlic paste and saute for a couple of minutes.
Add coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder and salt and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato puree and continue cooking for 5 mins or until the oil separates from the masala.
Add cooked Rajma with the water in which it has been cooking. Add garam masala powder, Kasuri methi and coriander leaves and cook for 10 mins or until the gravy reaches the desired consistency.
Remove from the heat, and serve hot with steamed rice or chapati.

title: Squid Fry
cooking_instructions: Dry Roast, Coriander Seeds, Dry Red Chilli, Black Peppercorns and Cumin Seeds in a pan until aromatic.
In a mixer grinder, grind the dry roasted spices along with Onion, Garam masala powder, turmeric powder, lemon juice, ginger, garlic, salt and water into a smooth paste.
Marinate the squid with the ground masala paste.
In a pan, heat oil, add marinated squid and roast on high flame, stirring at intervals.
Add curry leaves and continue to roast the squid. Add ¼ tsp of Black Pepper Powder. The total cooking time will be around 6-7 mins. Remove the pan from heat. Serve the squid hot as an appetizer.

title: Crab Masala
cooking_instructions: Heat a pan, add oil and add all the ingredients under roast and grind except fennel seeds and grated coconut. Saute until the spices emit aroma.
Add fennel seeds and grated coconut to the hot ingredients and mix well.
Once cool, add the mixture to a mixer grinder and grind into a fine paste with ¼ Cup of water.
Heat a pan, add oil and then add the bay leaf. Add chopped onion, curry leaves and saute well till it starts to turn golden brown.
Add chopped tomato, add turmeric powder and chilli powder. Saute till the tomatoes turn mushy.
Add water, salt and crab to the masala mixture and cook covered for 7 minutes.
Add the spice masala paste to it, mix well and cook for 5 minutes.
Add coriander leaves and serve it hot.

title: Baked Yogurt
cooking_instructions: Preheat an oven to 180 C
Whisk together the cream, curd, and condensed milk. Add the vanilla essence.
Divide equally among 3 oven-proof bowls. Place the bowl in an oven-proof tray and pour a cup of water into the tray.
Bake in the oven for 20 mins.
Refrigerate for 2 hours, minimum. Garnish with fresh mango fruit.

title: Kumbakonam Kadappa
cooking_instructions: Dry roast the dal and transfer it to a pressure cooker.
Pressure cook it with garlic and turmeric with 2 cups of water for 2 whistles and let it cook on low flame for 5 mins.
Heat coconut oil in a pan, add the cloves, broken cashews and fry till golden in colour.
Add shallots, green chillies, tomatoes, salt and cook well.
Add the pressure cooked dal. Add a cup of water and curry leaves. Let it simmer for 3 mins.

Add asafoetida and mix, then the coconut milk and coriander leaves. Don’t let it boil after adding coconut milk. Switch off the flame as soon as the small bubbles appear. Serve hot with idlis, idiyappam, and appam.

title: Palada Payasam
cooking_instructions: Boil 2 cups of water in a saucepan. Turn off the heat and add the Ada. Cover with a lid and let it sit for 30 minutes.
In a pressure cooker, add the milk, sugar and ghee. Pressure cook on high flame for 1 whistle. Immediately after the first whistle, reduce the flame to low and cook for a further 20 minutes.
Strain the Ada and wash it until it is not sticky anymore.
Add the Ada to a pan along with the reduced milk. Cook for a further 15 minutes on medium flame, or until the mixture has reduced significantly.
Add the condensed milk and bring to a boil.
Turn off the flame. Serve either warm or chilled.

title: Gobi Paratha
cooking_instructions: Knead a smooth and semi-firm dough using the flour, salt and water. Rest for 10 mins.
Combine the grated cauliflower with the other ingredients and mix well.
Stuff the dough with the gobi mixture, by dividing the dough into roundels. Dust in flour and flatten a little. Place the mixture in the center.
Sprinkle some wheat flour and seal the edges by pinching together and dust in flour again and rest for 5 minutes.
Roll the roundels flat, gently.
Alternatively, flatten two roundels and place some cauliflower mixture in the center of one.
Use the other to place on top and seal the edges. Rest for 5 minutes and roll the paratha to required thickness, gently.
Cook on a preheated tava on medium heat, applying ghee and till golden brown on both sides. Serve with white butter/ Makkan.

title: Shakkarpare
cooking_instructions: In a bowl whisk together the water, ghee, sugar and cardamom powder to dissolve the sugar.
In another bowl, mix together the flour, sesame seeds and baking powder.
Add the liquid into the flour. Knead a smooth dough and semi-soft dough. Rest the dough for 30 mins.
Roll the dough out thinly and cut then into strips, further cut into square shape.
Deep fry until golden brown.

title: Bombay Karachi Halwa
cooking_instructions: Combine the cornstarch and water together in a bowl.
In a pan, combine the sugar and 2 ½ cups of water. Heat it until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cornstarch mixture to the sugar syrup and mix well on a medium-low flame.
Once it starts to thicken and become glossy, add in 2 tbsp of ghee and mix well. Repeat this step until all the ghee is used up. A total of ¾ cup of ghee will be used for this recipe.
After around 30 minutes, the mixture will start to leave the sides of the pan. Add the cardamom powder, chopped nuts and orange food colour. Mix well until evenly combined.
Pour into a mould greased with ghee. Allow it to set for 2 hour until it has cooled down and solidified.
Cut into pieces and serve.

title: Bread Ravioli
cooking_instructions: Add butter to a pan and add the onions and garlic, cook until the onions turn translucent.
Add the chopped vegetables and corn. Season with salt, sugar and add the dried herbs. Saute until the vegetables turn tender.
Add the tomato puree and cook until no longer raw in aroma and the mixture turns dry again.
Finish with fresh cream to make a thick but creamy mixture.
Keep the filling and cheese ready. Make a thick mixture out of maida and water.
Roll out the bread pieces to flatten them and cut out the required shapes.
Place the mixture and cheese on a piece of bread and place another piece of bread on top. Seal the edges using a thick mixture of 3 tbsp water and 2 tbsp of maida.
Pan fry the ravioli until golden brown and crispy.

title: Phuket Fish
cooking_instructions: Add the salt and egg to the fish fillets and mix well.
Coat the fish thoroughly in the cornstarch mixture.
Fry the fish in medium hot oil until golden brown and crispy, about 7 mins. Drain the fish and set aside.
In a pan, add oil and add the ginger, garlic, green chillies. Add the onions and spring onion and saute for 2 mins on a high flame.
Add the chilli paste, soya sauce, salt, pepper powder and MSG.
Mix well and add the water. Finish with the spring onion greens.
Add the fish in the prepared sauce and coat well.
Garnish with spring onion greens and serve!

title: Roast Chicken
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine the softened butter along with rosemary, garlic and thyme. Mix it until evenly combined.
Make a mixture of olive oil, paprika, salt and black pepper powder. Apply it all over the chicken.
Gently separate the skin of the chicken near the breast using your fingers or a rubber spatula. Spread the butter mixture in the gap between the skin and the meat.
Pierce a lemon a few times. Place the lemon in the chicken cavity. Make slits on the thickest parts of the chicken legs and thighs.
Tie the chicken legs using a string/twine and then tie it near the breast, crossing the wings. Make slits on the thickest parts of the chicken legs and thighs.
Make slits on the thickest parts of the chicken legs and thighs. Apply the paprika mixture all over the chicken.
In a roasting tray, place the halved onion and garlic. Place the chicken over the vegetables.
Preheat an oven to 220c and roast for 1 hour, checking occasionally after 40 minutes to ensure that the chicken does not burn. Allow the chicken to rest for 20 minutes after roasting.
Meanwhile, mash all the remaining vegetables in the pan along with the juice.
Add flour and mix evenly to ensure that there are no lumps. Add the water and bring to a boil and season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 3 minutes and turn off the heat.
Strain the sauce. This is the sauce for the chicken.
Carve the roast chicken into pieces and serve with the roasting gravy/jus.

title: Honey-Glazed Chicken Wings
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken wings in ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, salt, black pepper powder and red chilli powder. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
In a bowl, combine all the ingredients for the coating.
Add the chicken wings and coat completely.
Deep-fry on medium-high heat for 10 minutes or until it turns golden brown.
For the glaze, combine all the ingredients in a bowl.
Heat a pan and add the glaze. Bring it to a simmer. Add the fried chicken and toss well.
Serve garnished with toasted sesame seeds and spring onions.

title: Paal Pongal
cooking_instructions: Rinse and soak the rice for 20 mins.
Dry roast the moong dal until aromatic and wash it well.
Add the soaked rice and moong dal to a cooker with salt and water and pressure cook for 3 whistles, allow the steam to escape naturally.
Lightly mash the rice and dal mixture.
In a separate pan, fry cashew nuts in ghee until golden brown.
Place the mixture back on a low flame and add the milk in additions, mixing well in between.
Once all the milk has been blended in, switch off the flame.
Add the fried cashew nuts and the leftover ghee into the paal pongal, serve warm.

title: Mangalore Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins.
Dry roast the spices until aromatic.
Add to a mixer grinder and blend to a fine powder. Reserve 1 tsp separately.
Grind the coconut to a fine paste with the ginger, green chillies and garlic with ¾ cup of water. Add the cashew nuts and grind fine. Add the coriander and mint and blend to a smooth paste.
To the chicken, add this paste, salt and the powdered spices. Marinate the chicken for a minimum of 30 mins.

Cook the rice with 6 Cups of water, salt,1 tbsp ghee, bay leaves and the coconut milk until 80% done by dum method- boil the rice until the level of rice and liquid are equal. Cover and cook for 10 mins. Fluff up the rice.
For the gravy, heat oil in a pot and add the onions. Saute until golden brown.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add the marinated chicken and cook for 15 mins, covered and simmering. Remove some of the chicken pieces for layering.
Add half the rice, the chicken pieces and the remaining rice. Top with cashew nuts, reserved masala powder, chopped mint and coriander.
Sprinkle ¼ Cup of water on top.
Cover and keep on a high flame for 2 mins and simmer for 12 mins.

title: Home-Made French Fries
cooking_instructions: Wash and peel the large potatoes. Cut them into french fry baton shapes and soak them in cold water for 10 mins.
Place them in water with baking soda and salt. Bring it to a boil, for a minute or two.
Strain and dry the batons completely.
Fry them in medium hot oil for 2 mins and strain them, allow them to cool completely.
Fry them again, in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
Toss them with salt and serve.

title: Bun Butter Jam
alternate_titles: Bakery/ teashop style bun butter jam
cooking_instructions: In lukewarm milk, add the sugar and yeast and allow it to bloom for 10 mins.
Add the milk to the maida and mix well until it comes together.
Add the butter and bring together a rough dough.
Cover and rest the dough for 10 mins.
Pull and stretch the dough 15 times, fold up after each stretch. Try to ensure the stretching is even throughout the dough. Knead until the surface of the dough is smooth.
Roll the dough into a ball and place in a bowl, in a warm place, covered and oiled for an hour.
After resting, lightly press down the dough. Divide the dough into roundels.
Place on a baking tray, cover and rest for 20 mins.
Brush with milk and bake for 30 mins at 180C until golden brown and fluffy.
Brush with oil and allow the bread to cool down completely.
For the buttercream, whisk soft butter with sugar until light and fluffy. Add the vanilla essence and milk and mix well until combined.

To assemble the bread butter jam, slice the bun in half and add the butter on one side and jam on the other side. Close the sides to sandwich and cut into 2 or 4 pieces if needed, it can also be whole.

title: Kaara Chutney
cooking_instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and add the urad dal, chana dal and dry red chillies. When the dals start to change their colour, add the garlic and onion.
When the onion turns translucent, add the tomatoes and salt. Cook until the tomatoes have softened. Add the tamarind and turn off the stove.
Add the tamarind and turn off the stove. Allow it to cool.
After it cools, blend into a paste. Transfer it into a bowl.
In a small pan, heat oil and add mustard seeds and split urad dal. When the mustard seeds start to crackle, add the curry leaves. Remove from the heat after 10 seconds.
Add the tempering to the chutney and serve with dosa, idli or any other breakfast dish of your choice.

title: Pazham Pori
cooking_instructions: The banana used for this recipe should ideally be ripe, but not too soft. Cut the banana in half. Cut each half into three long slices.
For the batter, combine the maida, rice flour, turmeric powder, salt, sugar and water. Whisk it until there are no lumps.
Heat oil in a pan on high heat. Dip the banana slice in the batter and deep fry them until the edges are golden, around 2 minutes.

title: Basil Breaded Chicken
cooking_instructions: Add the pesto into the bowl of chicken strips and coat well, also add the salt, pepper, onion and garlic.
Add the egg and mix well. Marinate for 30 mins.
Cut the crusts from fresh white bread and pulse in a mixer grinder to make fresh bread crumbs.
Coat well with bread crumbs and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and shallow fry until golden brown and crispy.

title: Scotch Eggs
cooking_instructions: To the minced chicken, add in salt, black pepper powder, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli powder and a small grating of nutmeg. Mix well to combine.
Add flour and breadcrumbs and mix again.
Coat the eggs lightly in flour.

Take a portion of the mince and flatten it. Place the egg in the middle and fold the sides to encase the eggs completely. You can adjust and remove any excess chicken mince or add more if required. Repeat this step for each egg.
Coat them in flour, then in a beaten egg mixture, and finally in breadcrumbs. Freeze them for 15 minutes.
Deep fry them on a medium flame until the chicken is cooked completely, 7 to 8 minutes.

title: Butter Chicken
cooking_instructions:
In a pan, heat the mustard oil. Remove from the flame and add the kashmiri chilli powder. Allow it to cool
In the hung curd, add the powdered spices- cumin, coriander, kasuri methi, garam masala. Whisk well and add the chilli oil.
Dice 800gms of chicken thigh boneless and add the salt, ginger garlic paste and lemon juice.
Add this marination to the chicken and mix well. Refrigerate for 30 mins, minimum.
In a pressure cooker, add the tomatoes, cashew nuts , kashmiri red chillies, salt and water and pressure cook for 6 whistles on a medium-high flame. Allow the pressure to release naturally and cool the mixture.
Blend to a fine puree and pass through a strainer to get a fine and smooth gravy base.
To prepare the gravy, heat ghee in a heavy bottom pot. Add the ginger garlic paste and cook until no longer raw in aroma. Add the kashmiri red chilli powder and stir well.
Add the gravy base, salt, sugar and cardamom powder.
Add milk and gently bring up to a boil. Cover and simmer for 20 mins, stirring occasionally. To finish the gravy, add the cream, butter, kasuri methi, and garam masala.
Grill the chicken on a grill pan on high heat for 10 mins per batch, flipping occasionally until there are some char marks on the chicken pieces.
Transfer to a bowl, smoke using a piece of coal by adding some melted butter on the smouldering coal piece for 2 mins, covered. And finish the chicken with lemon juice, melted butter and chaat masala.
Add the chicken and any leftover juices/pan drippings into the gravy. Simmer the gravy for 2 mins further. Serve hot garnished with fresh cream and melted butter.

title: Twice Baked Potatoes
cooking_instructions: Coat the potato with olive oil and salt and prick with a fork. Bake for 40 mins.
Cut the top of the potato, skin on, and scoop out the soft flesh and transfer to a bowl.
In the same bowl combine all the ingredients of the stuffing, retain a little cheese for the topping.
Fill this mixture into the hollowed potatoes and top with cheese and red chilli flakes.
Bake further for 10 mins. Serve warm and enjoy!

title: Pineapple Smoothie Bowl
cooking_instructions: Place the pineapple and bananas in a freezer proof vessel and freeze them overnight.
Combine the frozen fruits, coconut milk and honey in a mixer grinder and blend until smooth.
Transfer to a bowl and garnish with coconut flakes, pumpkin seeds and chia seeds.

title: Bread Omelette
cooking_instructions: For the mint chutney, blend all the ingredients into a thick paste, adding water if necessary.
In a bowl, combine the eggs, onion, green chilli, salt, pepper powder and red chilli powder. Whisk well.
Apply butter on both sides of the bread. Toast lightly on both sides and set aside.
Add 1 tsp of butter to the pan. Add the egg mixture and spread it around the pan.
Place the toasted bread back into the pan and coat both sides with the egg mixture. Leave at least 1-inch between both slices of bread.
Place the slice of cheese on one piece of bread. Spread the mint chutney on the other piece of bread.
Fold the excess egg onto the bread. Fold in half, with the bread slice on top of the other.
Flip and allow to cook for 30 seconds until the cheese softens. Remove from the pan, cut in half and serve.

title: Masala Milk
cooking_instructions: Grind  cashew, almonds, pistachios and cloves into a fine powder using a mixer grinder.
Add 2 cups of milk to a saucepan and heat it. Add the ground powder, saffron strands, nutmeg, cinnamon powder, sugar, and mix well. Heat the milk until it comes to a boil.
Simmer for 3 minutes, while stirring to ensure that the milk does not boil over.
Serve the masala milk hot.

title: Tandoori Pineapple
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients for the marination. Whisk until it turns smooth.
Add the pineapple and capsicum dices to the marinade and mix gently. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Soak bamboo skewers in water for at least 20 minutes.
Skewer the pineapple and the capsicum dices on the bamboo skewers.
Heat a grill pan on high heat. Arrange the skewers on the pan and sear, turning regularly to get a brown colour on each side.
Remove from the heat and brush with butter and sprinkle chaat masala.

title: Spring Potato
cooking_instructions: Combine the maida, cornstarch, Kashmiri chilli powder, chaat masala, salt and water to form a batter.
In the meanwhile, you can prepare the topping mix. Mix chaat masala, black salt and red chilli powder together and set it aside.
Insert the skewer lengthwise into the centre of a potato. Cut the potato into a thin spiral carefully. Gently separate the potato slices from each other.
Using a ladle, pour the batter over the potato.
Fry it in oil over medium heat until it turns golden brown and crisp.
Immediately squeeze lemon juice over the fried potato. Sprinkle the previously prepared topping mix over the potato on all sides.
Top it with mayonnaise and chopped coriander leaves.

title: Mutton Rogan Josh
cooking_instructions: Make a spice pouch by tying up the ingredients in a cheesecloth/muslin cloth.
Heat the ghee in a pressure cooker. Add the mutton pieces to the cooker without crowding them together. Flip the mutton pieces and cook until they have browned on all sides, around 4 minutes.
Add the saffron, salt and water. Add the spice pouch. Cover and pressure cook on medium-low heat for 30 minutes.
In a bowl, add the curd, Kashmiri chilli, ginger powder, fennel powder and asafoetida powder. Whisk it into a smooth paste.

When the mutton is cooked, remove the lid and discard the spice pouch. You can either continue cooking in the pressure cooker or transfer it to another pan as per your convenience. Add the curd paste on a low flame. Mix well until it is completely combined.
When it comes to a boil, reduce the heat to low. Cover and cook for a further 15 minutes or until the oil floats on top.

title: Instant Kalakand
cooking_instructions: Add the grated paneer, cardamom powder, rose water and condensed milk in a heavy bottom kadai and cook until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan, approximately 10 mins on a medium-high flame.
Transfer to a greaseproof paper-lined container and spread to ¾ inch thickness. Sprinkle over the chopped nuts and rose petals. Pat gently.
Sprinkle over the chopped nuts and rose petals. Pat gently.
Set in the fridge for 2 hours and cut into the desired shape.

title: Mawa Peda
cooking_instructions: Cook the grated the khoya and sugar in a heavy bottom kadai for 10 mins on a medium-high flame.
Cool for 20 mins in a bowl.
Grease your palms and make small roundels and flatten slightly, place an almond in the centre and press slightly.

title: Akki Roti
cooking_instructions: Combine the rice flour, salt, onion, carrot and chopped coriander in a bowl and mix well.
Pour boiling water into this vessel and do not stop mixing until a dough has formed. Cover and rest for 20 mins.
Grease your hands and a banana leaf with oil and flatten some of the mixture to make a flat roti shape. Make some holes.
Heat a tava and add ghee, place the banana leaf upside down to place the akki roti on the tava, peel off the banana leaf.
Cook, flipping sides until golden and adding ghee as needed.

title: Thalassery Fish Biryani
cooking_instructions: Marinate the fish in salt and turmeric powder. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Wash the rice and soak for 20 minutes.
Make a paste of the ginger, garlic, green chilli and shallots, using water if needed.
In a pot, heat ghee and oil. Fry the cashew nuts until golden brown. Set them aside.
In the same oil, fry the raisins until they puff up. Remove from the oil and set aside.
Add the sliced onions and fry them until they are golden brown. Remove them onto a plate lined with paper towels.
Remove 3 tbsp of the oil from the pan. Set this aside to cook the rice.
Fry the marinated fish for 2 minutes on each side. It should not be completely cooked, only about 80% through.
To the same pot, add the onion and saute until it softens. Add the previously prepared paste (ginger, garlic, shallots, green chillies). Saute until the raw smell disappears.
Add the red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder and salt. Saute again till the raw smell of the spices disappears, around 5 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too dry.
Add the sliced tomatoes and cook until it has softened and the masalas are completely cooked, around 5 minutes.
Add the curd, mint leaves, coriander leaves and Biryani masala. Mix well and cook for 3 more minutes. The masala is ready.
To cook the rice, add in the oil and ghee mixture that was removed from the pot earlier.
Add cardamom, bay leaves, clove, cinnamon and mace. When it starts to release its aroma, add in the rice and saute on medium heat for 3 minutes or until it starts to turn opaque.
Add in the hot water and season with salt and sugar.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes on a low flame.
To layer the Biryani, remove half the masala into a bowl.
Add in half the rice. Add half of the fried onions.
Add in the remaining masala and then arrange the fried fish slices.
Add in the rest of the rice. Sprinkle the fried onions, cashew nuts and raisins on top. Cover tightly with a lid.
Place on a low heat for 8 minutes.

title: Fish Mappas
cooking_instructions: Marinate the fish slices in salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder and lemon juice.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the fish for 2 minutes on each side. Set them aside.
Heat 2 tbsp of coconut oil in a pan. Add the ginger, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves and onion. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the turmeric powder, coriander powder and salt. Saute until the raw smell goes away.
Add the sliced tomatoes along with the 2nd press coconut milk. Bring it to a boil.
Add the fried fish into the gravy. Drizzle the vinegar into the pan. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.

Reduce the flame to low and add in the 1st press coconut milk. Mix it by gently swirling the pan around. Avoid using a ladle/spoon to prevent the fish from breaking. Turn off the heat after 30 seconds.
Sprinkle curry leaves and coconut oil on top. Cover and let it sit for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Punjabi Mutton Masala
cooking_instructions: Pressure cook the mutton for 7 whistles with 2 Cups of water, 1 tsp of salt and ½ tsp of turmeric powder.
Roast the spices for the masala until aromatic and powder them in a mixer grinder.
Add ghee and oil to a kadhai and add the sliced onions. Brown them.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies. Cook until the raw aroma goes.
Add the powdered spices and salt and cook on a low flame for 3 mins. Add water and cook until dry again.
Add the tomatoes and cook until completely soft.
Add salt and the powdered prepared masala.
Add the mutton and the water. Simmer for 10 mins.
Finish with chopped coriander leaves, kasuri methi and lemon juice.

title: Chilli Egg
cooking_instructions: Combine the ingredients for the better and whisk a smooth, thick batter.
Dip the egg quarters and deep fry until golden brown.
Heat oil in a wok and add the chopped ginger, garlic and green chillies, saute until golden brown.
Add the diced capsicum and onions and saute for 2 mins.
Add the soya sauce, vinegar, ketchup and red chilli sauce and saute for a minute.
Add the water and bring to a boil. Mix 1 tbsp corn starch with 2 tbsp of water and pour to thicken the sauce.
Add salt and the eggs and toss to coat well in the sauce. Finish with chopped spring onion.

title: Paneer Butter Masala
cooking_instructions: Soak the cashews in water for 15 mins.
Blend the soaked cashews in a mixer grinder with the water in which it was soaking.
Roughly chop the tomatoes into cubes and grind into a smooth puree. Keep Aside.
In a pan on medium heat, add butter and bay leaf.
Add ginger-garlic paste and saute for a few seconds. And add the tomato puree and cook for 5 mins.
Add Kashmiri red chilli powder and continue cooking until most of the water from the tomato puree is evaporated.
Add the cashew paste and cook for a further 3 mins.
Add 1.5 Cup of water and simmer the gravy for 5 mins.
Add salt to taste and sugar to the gravy. And add the Garam Masala powder and crushed Kasuri Methi.
Once the gravy thickens to the desired consistency, add the paneer cubes. And finally the Fresh Cream to the gravy.
Mix well and switch off the flame.

title: Veg Tawa Pizza
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the water, yeast and sugar. Allow it to rest for 10 minutes. This allows the yeast to bloom. If it doesn’t rise, the yeast might be old or expired.
Measure 2 cups of Maida and put it into a large bowl. Add salt and mix, to make sure that the salt is distributed evenly.
Make a well in the centre of the Maida, using your fingers or a wooden spoon. Add the wet mixture in the middle.
Start adding a little bit of flour into the wet mixture. Continue doing this until all the flour is mixed in, and a shaggy dough is formed.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead well until a smooth dough forms.
Add 2 tbsp of oil to the dough. Knead well again until the oil is completely mixed in and the dough becomes smooth.
Cover with a damp cloth and allow it to rise for at least 45 minutes, up to 1 ½ hours.
Divide the dough into 3 portions.
Roll one portion into a 1 cm thick round base. Pierce all over with a fork.

Cover a skillet or a Tawa with a lid, and heat it until it gets very hot. Turn down the heat to low and then add the rolled Pizza dough. Cook, covered, for 2 minutes. Flip over to the other side. Cook for 30 seconds.
Remove the dough onto a flat plate or a work surface. Spread sauce on the pizza base, except for 1 inch around the edges.
Add the shredded Mozzarella cheese. Top with the onion and capsicum. Add the sweet corn kernels and sliced olives on top. Sprinkle chilli flakes and oregano on the pizza.
Place it back in the Tawa and cook, covered for 2 minutes, or until the cheese has completely melted and has slightly changed colour.
Remove from the pan. Cut into 6 pieces and serve hot.

title: Manchatti Meen Kulambu
cooking_instructions: Add a large lemon sized ball to 2 cups of hot water to extract the tamarind water.
Dry roast all the spices for the masala and blend to a fine powder and set aside.

Heat oil in a pot and add the mustard seeds. After they splutter, add the dried red chillies and fenugreek seeds. Followed by the curry leaves and green chillies. Add the garlic, ginger and shallots and saute until light brown in colour.
And the tomato puree.

Add the powdered spices, add the tamarind water and simmer until the oil releases from the gravy, about 20 minutes. Season with salt and add the fish and raw mango pieces. Add the previously prepared spice powder.

Simmer until the fish is tender. Add coriander leaves and mix gently before turning off the flame. This dish tastes great when covered and allowed to rest for at least 1 hour, or overnight for the best flavour. Serve with rice.

title: Kumbh Kaju Masala
cooking_instructions: Melt the butter in a kadai and fry the cashews until golden brown and set aside.
In the same kadai add the whole spices and fry until aromatic.
Add the onions and saute until golden brown in colour.
Add the ginger garlic paste and saute until the raw aroma goes.
Add the tomato puree, turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder and salt and mix well until the tomato puree is no longer raw. Add the garam masala and sugar.
Add water to the masala to make a gravy consistency.
Add the mushrooms and boil until the gravy is thick for about 7 mins.
Add the kasuri methi and cashew nuts and mix well. Finish with chopped coriander leaves and fresh cream.

title: Kheema Matar
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf, star anise and cumin seeds. Add the ginger, garlic, green chillies and saute.
Add the onion and cook until it turns golden brown.
Add all the spice powders and the tomato puree. Cook for 4 minutes.
Add the minced mutton. Cook for 2 minutes on high flame, stirring continuously. Add water.
Cover and cook for 8 minutes on medium-low heat.
Add the green peas and cook for 2 more minutes. Cook it reaches the desired consistency, if required. Add coriander leaves and mint leaves and stir. Serve hot with pav/rice/roti.

title: Pound Cake
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees C (350 degrees F) and place the oven rack in the centre of the oven. Butter or spray with a non-stick vegetable spray, 9*5*3 inch (23*13*8 cm) loaf pan. Line the bottom of the pan with parchment paper and butter or spray the paper.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs, along with the milk and vanilla extract.
In another bowl, add the flour, baking powder, salt, sugar and mix well.
Add the butter to the dry ingredients, along with half of the egg mixture. Mix on low speed until the dry ingredients are moistened.

Increase the mixer speed to medium and beat for a minute to develop the cake’s structure. Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl as needed. Add the remaining egg mixture, in two additions, beating well after each addition for 30 seconds to incorporate the egg and strengthen the cake’s structure.

Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with an offset spatula or the back of a spoon. Bake for about 60 minutes or until the cake is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the centre of the cake comes out clean. Rotate you loaf pan about halfway through baking.

title: Achari Baingan
cooking_instructions: Fry the slit brinjals in oil until golden and tender, remove from the pan.
Add the mustard oil to the pan. Add the whole spices and cook until aromatic.
Add the chopped garlic, ginger and saute until golden brown.
Add the chopped onions and cook until golden brown.
Add the powdered spices, salt and chopped tomatoes. Cook until soft and mushy.
Simmer the gravy and add the curd. Mix and cook well until the oil starts separating.
Finish with the pickle, brinjal and kasoori methi, add the water and simmer until thick in consistency. Garnish with chopped coriander leaves and serve.

title: Bread Gulab Jamun
cooking_instructions: To make the sugar syrup, heat the sugar and water on medium-low heat until it turns sticky - around 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally.1
Add lemon juice, cardamom powder and rose water. Turn off the heat and set aside.
For the Gulab Jamun, add the bread into a mixer and grind into a fine powder.
Add the milk, cream and mix into a smooth dough.
Shape and deep-fry the dough balls over medium heat until golden brown.
While still warm, soak it in the sugar syrup for at least 2 hours. Garnish with chopped pistachios.

title: Paneer Lasooni
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add the cumin seeds, cardamom, onion and garlic. Saute for 1 minute.
Add all the other ingredients except water. Saute on high heat for 2 minutes.
Add water, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Allow it to cool, then grind into a smooth paste adding water as required.
In a bowl, combine the ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder and salt with water.
Heat oil in a pan and add the garlic. Saute until it turns lightly golden brown.
Add the masala paste and saute until oil starts releasing from the sides.
Add the prepared paste and continue to simmer for 3-4 minutes until the oil floats from the sides.
Add water, cover and cook for 10 minutes stirring regularly.
Add sugar, garam masala powder and paneer cubes. Mix gently to coat the paneer with the gravy.
Add Kasuri methi powder, butter, coriander leaves and cream. Turn off the heat as soon as it comes to a simmer. Serve with naan/roti/rice

title: Home-Style Kuzhi Paniyaram
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add mustard, curry leaves, green chillies, black peppercorn and let it crackle.
Add onions and cook till it turns translucent.
Add asafoetida and mix it well.
Add the grated carrots and cook it till it turns soft.Add asafoetida. Mix it well and keep it aside.
Add 4 cups of dosa/idli batter to a bowl. Add the onion carrot mixture and mix it till it all evenly combines.
Add Salt, mix it well.
Heat a paniyaram pan. Add oil into every cavity.Then gently spoon the batter into every cavity.
Cook it for 4 minutes on a low flame till it turns golden brown. Use a skewer to slowly turn over the paniyaram and cook it for another 4 minutes.
Take the paniyaram off the pan. Arrange it on a plate. Serve it hot with coconut or tomato chutney.

title: Instant Bhatura
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine the flour, semolina, salt. Add ½ tsp baking powder and a pinch of baking soda, mix well.
Add the ghee, curd and crumble.
Add the water and knead a soft and pliable dough.
In this method, the dough needs to be rested for 15 mins to develop flavour. Apply ghee on the surface and cover the dough.
Divide dough into roundels and roll out thinly on a floured surface.
Fry the bhaturas in medium hot oil until golden and crispy on both sides. Serve hot with pindi choley/choley masala.

title: Chicken Tikka
cooking_instructions: Add all the ingredients for the first marination with the chicken. Rest for 30 minutes.
Add all the spice powders for the 2nd marination into the hung curd.

To prepare the chilli oil, heat the oil in a small pan until it reaches its smoking point. Turn off the heat and immediately add the red chilli powder. Add this to the marinade immediately. Do not leave the chilli powder in the hot oil for too long, as it will burn.
Add all the remaining ingredients to the marination. Remove the excess moisture from the chicken and add it to the marination.
Remove the excess moisture from the chicken and add it to the marination. De-seed the tomatoes and dice them. Dice the capsicum and onion. Add them to the marinade and mix well.
Place a metal bowl in between the chicken pieces. Place hot charcoal and pour ghee on top. Cover immediately and let it rest for 3 minutes. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Skewer the chicken pieces, alternating with the onion, tomato, and capsicum dice.
Heat and grease a grill pan or a Tawa. Grill the skewers on high heat for 30 seconds on each side or until it is lightly charred all over.
Reduce the flame to medium and cook for a further 12-14 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Remove them from the pan. Brush them with melted butter and sprinkle with chaat masala. Serve with mint chutney.

title: Shahi Tukda
cooking_instructions: Heat up milk in a saucepan. Once it comes to a boil, add sugar, saffron and cardamom. Reduce the flame and let it simmer.
Cook it for 15 minutes on a medium-low flame, stirring regularly, until the volume of milk has reduced a little.
Add the condensed milk to the saucepan and cook for 3-5 more minutes. This mixture should be thick enough to lightly coat the back of a spoon. Pour this into a bowl and refrigerate.
Cut off the edges of the bread slices and cut the slice diagonally.
Fry the bread slices in oil or ghee until they are golden brown.
Fry the chopped cashew nuts until they are golden brown.
Arrange the slices on the serving dish and pour the cooled milk mixture on top.  Garnish with fried cashew nuts, chopped pistachios, and almonds.

title: Grape Wine
cooking_instructions: Boil water and allow it to cool completely.
Remove the stems from the grapes. Make sure there are no spoilt grapes. Wash and dry them completely.
Tie the whole wheat in a pouch.
Add in half the grapes in a completely dry glass or ceramic jar. Add in half the sugar.
Add in the remaining grapes and sugar. Add the spices and the whole wheat on top. Pour in the cooled water into the jar.
Cover with a cotton cloth and tie tightly. Allow it to rest for 21 days in a dark place. Stir every day for 1 week, and then stir every alternate day for the next 2 weeks.
Strain the wine. Avoid touching it directly using your hands.
Bottle the wine in a cool, dark place. It is now ready for consumption.

title: Prawn 65
cooking_instructions: Clean the prawn. In a bowl, add the prawn, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, garam masala, coriander powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, cornflour, rice flour, green chilli, curry leaves and egg. Mix this well.
Marinate the prawn in this mixture for 30 mins
Add oil to a deep frying pan, heat the oil, and deep fry the marinated prawn in batches for 3-4 mins on medium-high heat. Serve hot with lemon slices and onion rings.

title: Moongphali Paneer
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the ginger-garlic paste and green chillies, cook until the flavour is no longer raw.
Add the onions and cook until translucent.
Add the capsicum and cook until tender.
Add the powdered spices, salt, desiccated coconut, and powdered peanuts. Mix well to combine.
Add the paneer and mix well, finish with chopped coriander leaves.

title: Bombay Grill Sandwich
cooking_instructions: For the chutney, combine all the ingredients and blend in a mixer grinder until coarse in texture.
For the masala, dry roast the whole spices and blend finely with the powdered spices.
Pressure cook the beetroot until tender, for 3 whistles.
To assemble the sandwich, apply the green chutney and butter on all the slices, apply butter on the outside of 2 slices for the top and bottom.
Add the sliced vegetables and sprinkle with the special sandwich masala after each layer of vegetable. Close the sandwich and press gently.
Place in a hot toaster and grill until golden brown. Cut into 6 pieces, apply some butter and green chutney on top. Sprinkle fine sev.

title: Golden Fried Coconut Prawns
cooking_instructions: Marinate the prawns with lemon juice, onion and garlic powders, salt and paprika.
Make a batter of maida, cornstarch and water.
Combine the panko and the desiccated coconut and set aside.
Season the prawns with salt. Dip the prawns in the batter and coat with the breadcrumbs. Repeat the process to double coat the prawns.
Deep fry until golden brown and serve with sweet chilli sauce and lemon.

title: Hyderabad Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions: In a bowl take thinly sliced onions. Add 1 tsp of Salt and Rest for 5 mins. Remove the excess water after the sliced onions have rested for 5 mins.

Heat oil in a deep frying pan and deep fry the onions for 5 mins on medium heat. The onions should turn brown. Ensure that the onions don’t get burnt. Keep the fried onions aside for 15 mins to become crispy.
Wash and soak the Basmati rice for 20 mins.
Heat ½ Cup of water in a saucepan, bring it to a boil. Add it to the saffron, mix well to prepare the Saffron Water.

In a biryani pot, take the cleaned and washed chicken.Add Kashmiri Chilli Powder, Cumin Powder, Garam Masala Powder, Salt, Cinnamon, Cardamom, Black Cardamom and Bay Leaf. Mix the chicken well with all the spices and spice powders.
Add the slit green chilli, ginger garlic paste, ginger, mint leaves, whisked curd. Mix well.
Add half of the fried onions to this and also add 1 tbsp of ghee. Mix well and marinate the chicken for 1 hour.
In a pan bring 5 cups of water to a boil and add the cardamom, black cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf, cumin seeds, salt and coriander leaves.
Add the soaked rice to the boiling water, add 2 tsp of oil, cover and cook for 5-7 mins or until the rice is ¾ done.
Using a strainer or a muslin cloth, strain the rice and spread it over a wide plate or pan.
Take the biryani pot in which the chicken is marinating, add 75% of cooked rice on top of the marinating chicken.
Add the 50 % remaining fried onion, 50% of the saffron water, 1 tbsp of ghee on top of the rice.
