Add the balance rice on top of this. Add the remaining saffron water, 1 tbsp of mint leaves, 1 tbsp of coriander leaves, balance fried onion and 1 tbsp of ghee.

Place the pot on a stovetop, and cook on high heat for 5 minutes. Remove the pot from the stove. Line the sides of the pot with chapati dough or cover the pot with aluminum foil to prevent steam from escaping the pot. Close it with a lid to dum cook the biryani.
Now Place a Tawa on the stove, and place the biryani pot on top of the Tawa, and dum cook for 35 minutes on medium heat.
Fluff the rice gently and serve the biryani hot with Onion Raita and Mirchi ka salan.

title: Chicken Kurma (South-Indian Style)
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the cinnamon, cardamom, fennel seeds and green chilli. Add the cashew and poppy seeds. Saute until light golden brown.
Add the coconut and saute for 1 minute.
Allow it to cool and then grind into a fine paste.
In a pan, heat oil and add cinnamon, kalpasi, fennel seeds and curry leaves. Add the onion and saute until translucent.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, and all the spice powders. Saute for 3-4 minutes.
Add the chicken and saute on high heat for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring it to a boil. Cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the prepared masala paste. Mix well and simmer for 5 minutes.

title: French Omelette
cooking_instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl. Add salt and pepper. Whisk well until thoroughly combined.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Melt the butter. Add in the egg mixture and stir constantly so that a few lumps form.

Once most of the egg starts to solidify, add the cheese and start folding the egg from one side. Bring it to one side of the pan, so that it forms an oblong/crescent shape. Turn it onto a plate. Garnish with chives/spring onion.

title: Stuffed Sweet Puri
cooking_instructions: Crumble the maida with the salt and ghee until it resembles sand. Add water and knead a smooth dough.
Grind the coconut without water to a thick paste.
Lightly roast the cashew nuts and rava in a tbsp of ghee.
Prepare a syrup with the sugar and water, boiling for 5 mins.
Add the cashew nuts, rava . Cook until the mixture thickens.
Add the ghee and coconut pasteand mix thoroughly. Add the cardamom powder and mix well. Set aside to cool completely.
Stuff the dough roundels with the mixture, similar to stuffing parathas and flatten slightly.
Deep fry until golden brown in low-medium heat oil for about 10-12 mins.

title: Dal Khichdi
cooking_instructions: Wash the rice, moong dal with some water. Remove the water and set them aside.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker. Saute the bay leaf and cumin seeds on a low flame.
Add ginger-garlic paste, green chilli, onion, and fry until fragrant. Sprinkle asafoetida.
Add tomato, carrot, beans, potato, salt, turmeric powder and saute for 2 minutes.
Add drained rice, moong dal and mix well.
Add 6 cups of water and mix well.
Pressure cook for 6 to 7 whistles on a medium flame. Let the pressure settle on its own.
Add 1 ½ cups of water and mix well on high flame for 2 mins.
Garnish with coriander leaves, more ghee, and serve it hot for lunch.

title: Honey Mustard Dip
cooking_instructions: Combine all the given ingredients in a bowl, whisk until smooth and well combined. Store refrigerated.

title: Paneer Pakoda
cooking_instructions: Marinate the paneer strips with lemon juice, salt, red chilli powder, garam masala, ginger garlic paste.
To make the batter, combine the besan and rice flour, add the turmeric, asafoetida, ajwain, baking soda and red chilli powder.
Add water and salt whisk a smooth and lump-free batter.
Dip the paneer in the batter and deep fry in medium hot oil until golden and crispy.
Sprinkle with chaat masala.

title: Andhra Pepper Chicken
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken with salt, turmeric powder, lemon juice and ginger garlic paste. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds and fennel seeds. When they splutter, add garlic, ginger, green chilli, onion, salt and curry leaves. Saute until the onion turns golden brown.
Add coriander powder, cumin powder and black pepper powder. Add the chicken and saute on high heat for 2 minutes.
Add water, cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent it from burning.
Add garam masala, coriander leaves, and some more crushed pepper and curry leaves. Mix well and serve.

title: Sheer Kurma
cooking_instructions: Soak the nuts in hot water for 10 mins. Soak the raisins and dates, too.

Strain the nuts and cut them into slices. Let the cuddappah almonds be whole. Cut the dates into strips. Heat 2 tbsp of ghee in a pan and fry the nuts and dry fruits on a low flame until aromatic but not browned or bitter. Add the raisins and dates at the end.
Strain the nuts and 1 tbsp of ghee to the pan, add and fry the fine semiyan until aromatic and light golden but not dark on a low flame.
In a pot, boil and then simmer the milk for about 10-15 mins.
Add the dry fruits and nuts, rose water, cardamom powder and continue simmer for a further 10-12 mins until the milk thickens further to ¾ th the initial level.
Add the fried semiyan with the ghee, saffron and cook until it turns tender and thick in consistency.
Finish with condensed milk, simmer for a further 5 mins until thick.

title: Easy Quail Egg Roast
cooking_instructions: Add the quail eggs to a pot of boiling water. Boil for 5 minutes.
Cool it down and peel the shells.
Heat oil in a pan. Add the shallots and curry leaves and saute until it starts to change colour.
Add all the spice powder, salt, and ginger-garlic paste. Saute for 2-3 minutes, or until the oil starts to separate from the sides.
Add the quail eggs to the pan. Mix well and roast for 3 more minutes.

title: Pindi Choley
cooking_instructions: Soak the chickpeas overnight with 3 tea bags and 2 black cardamom. Pressure cook after soaking for 5 whistles with the tea bags and salt.
Combine all the ingredients for the masala and dry roast for 4 minutes, until aromatic.
Blend in a mixer grinder to a fine powder.
For the gravy: heat oil in a kadai, add the onion paste, ginger-garlic paste, and asafoetida and saute until the raw flavour goes.
Add the tomato puree and saute for 3 minutes. Add the red chilli powder, salt, black salt and mix well. Add the ground masala. Cook until the masalas are cooked and the oil begins separating.
Add the boiled chickpeas. Simmer for 10 minutes. Add some sugar.
Add the dry mango powder, kasuri methi, ghee, and chopped coriander leaves. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally until semi-dry

title: Babycorn Jalfrezi
cooking_instructions: Blanch the baby corn in salted water for 2-3 minutes. Strain and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and saute the vegetables- onion, tomato, and capsicum on a high flame for 2 mins. Season with salt and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds, followed by ginger, garlic, and green chilies. Saute for 2 mins.
Add the onions and saute until turning golden brown.
Add the tomato puree. Cook the tomato until no longer raw in the aroma.
Add the powdered spices. Add the ketchup and vinegar.
Add some water, salt and cook the masalas, for a few minutes, until the oil starts releasing from the masala.
Add the sauteed vegetables and blanched baby corn. Add some water and cook until dry again.
Finish with chopped coriander leaves.

title: Sura Puttu
cooking_instructions: In a pot of water, add salt and turmeric powder and bring it to a boil. Add the fish, cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Remove it from the water. Mash it using a fork.
In a pan, heat oil and add the shallots, garlic, ginger, and green chilies.
When they start to brown, add the curry leaves, grated coconut, turmeric powder, and salt. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add the shredded fish and pepper powder, and saute for 2 more minutes. Add the coriander leaves and mix well.

title: Set Dosa
cooking_instructions: Wash the rice, urad dal and fenugreek seeds until the water runs clear and soak in fresh water for 4 hours.
In another bowl add 1 cup of poha, wash and soak it for an hour.
Blend the rice and dal mix into a smooth batter with 1 Cup of water in total, in batches.
Blend the poha with the last batch of the rice and dal mixture, it must be thick, smooth and of pouring consistency. Adjust the consistency with ½ Cup of water.
Adjust the consistency with water. Ferment the mixture for 8 hours, minimum.
Season with salt before preparing.
Add ghee and cook on a medium-hot tava, covered until the underside is golden and the dosa is cooked.

title: Soya Matar Keema Masala
cooking_instructions: Soak the soya chunks in hot water for 10 mins.
Squeeze and remove the water and pulse blend the soya chunks to make the keema.
Heat oil and ghee in a pan and add the whole spices, fry them for a minute.
Add the finely chopped onions and fry them until golden brown in color.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chopped green chillies and saute for a minute until the raw aroma goes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook them until soft and mushy and the oil begins to separate.
At this stage, add the powdered spices and salt and mix well.
Reduce the flame and add whisked curd into the masala. Mix well to combine and simmer further for 2 minutes.
Add the soya keema and green peas into the masala and mix to combine well.
Add water and cook until reduced and dry again.
Finish with a spoon of ghee, a squeeze of lemon and finely chopped fresh coriander leaves.

title: Poha
cooking_instructions: Put the Poha / flattened rice into a colander and rinse in water. Let it sit for 5 minutes. The Poha should be soft to the touch.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Add the peanuts and cook for 1 minute. Remove them from the oil and set aside.
Next, add the small dices of potato to the oil, fry them for 2 minutes and remove them from the oil.
Add an extra ½ tbsp to the same pan, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add the chopped onion, green chilli and saute for 1 minute.
Add turmeric powder and salt and mix well. Add the soaked Poha and mix well. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the previously cooked peanuts and potatoes and mix them. Taste and adjust the level of salt. Add the chopped coriander leaves and some freshly squeezed lemon juice. Turn off the stove.

title: Choco Nut Squares
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven. Whisk the eggs and sugar until light and foamy.
Add and mix the rest of the ingredients to form a thick batter.
Spread as a sheet onto a baking paper and bake at 180 C for 20 mins, until golden brown.
Cut into fingers/ squares while still warm
To make the icing, whisk the milk, icing sugar and honey until thick and spreadable in consistency.
Add the icing on top as needed. Cool completely prior to serving.

title: Cheesy Paneer Tikka Roll
cooking_instructions: For the marination, combine the oil with the chilli powder and then all the other spice powders. Mix well. Add in all the other ingredients and mix again. Add in the paneer cubes and mix to coat.
For the mint chutney, grind all the ingredients together.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the marinated paneer. Cook for 3 minutes, turning occasionally.
Add in the lemon juice and tomato ketchup. Mix and take off the flame.
Mix the onion and capsicum together with a pinch of salt.
To assemble, use roti/parotta. Place 2 slices of cheese and spread 1 tablespoon of the chutney. Place some of the mixtures in the center along with the vegetables. Sprinkle some chaat masala on top.
Heat oil in a pan. Heat the rolls, turning frequently until it is slightly crispy on all sides.

title: Kadala Curry
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the black chana for 8 hours or overnight.
In a pressure cooker, add the chana with 3 cups of water. Add 1 tsp of salt and bayleaf. Cook for 20 minutes.
Grind the coconut with little water to a smooth paste. Set it aside.
In a kadai, heat oil and crackle mustard seeds. Add chopped onion, curry leaves, chopped ginger and slit green chilli. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the coriander powder and fry for 1 minute on low heat. Then add the chilli powder, garam masala and turmeric powder. Cook until the masala is cooked, around 2 minutes. Add water if required.
Add the boiled Chana, and allow it to come to a boil. Then add the ground coconut paste. Cook for 3 minutes. Add salt. It is best served with puttu or appam.

title: Bombay Masala Toast
cooking_instructions: Mash the boiled potatoes.
Add the remaining ingredients for the filling. Mix to combine well.
For assembling the sandwich, apply the mint chutney and place some of the potato filling followed by grated processed cheese.
Top with another slice of bread and butter the outside of the sandwich.
Grill/ toast them until golden brown and crisp, cut them into triangles.
Dip the filling side down in fine sev to garnish and serve warm with ketchup and potato chips.

title: Parsi Mawa Cake
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C. Cream the butter and sugar until pale, light and fluffy.
Add the vanilla essence and eggs one at a time and whisk well.
Add the dry mix into the wet ingredients and whisk to combine well.
Finally, add the grated khoya and whisk well.
Pour the batter into a parchment-lined and greased mold and bake at 180C for 50 mins until the top is golden brown and a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Allow the cake to cool in the tin for 30 mins and de-mold it. Cut into slices and serve warm slices with vanilla ice cream.

title: Aloo Bhujia
cooking_instructions: Peel and grate the boiled potatoes using the small grater.
Add all the other ingredients to the potatoes. Mix well to form a smooth dough.Add water a few drops at a time, only if required.
Using an Idiyappam maker/murukku maker, fill the dough with the small hole attachment.
Heat oil in a kadai. Press the bhujia into hot oil. Fry until it turns golden brown, turning halfway through. Remove from the oil.
Once it has cooled down, crush the aloo bhujia.

title: Cheesy Chicken Sandwich
cooking_instructions: Make a marinade by mixing olive oil, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and red chilli powder. Coat the chicken in the marinade and rest for at least 15 minutes.
Heat a pan and add oil. Add the chicken breast on high heat along with whole cloves of garlic. Flip and cook until it is brown on both sides.
Add water and bring it to a boil. Cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pan. Reduce the remaining liquid until thickened. Mash the cooked garlic. Shred the chicken using a fork.
Add the chicken to a bowl along with onion, capsicum, mayonnaise, tomato ketchup, red chili sauce, oregano, coriander leaves, salt, pepper, and cheese. Mix well to combine evenly.
Spread evenly on a slice of bread. Sprinkle some more cheese on top. Cover with another slice of bread.
Apply butter to the bread. Toast the sandwich for 1 minute on each side, on medium heat.

title: Goan Chicken Cafreal
cooking_instructions: Make slits on the chicken pieces. Marinate it with turmeric powder and salt. Set aside.
For the paste, grind all the ingredients into a thick paste, adding water if needed.
Mix the paste along with the chicken pieces. Allow it to rest for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan. Add the chicken pieces and cook on medium-high heat for 2 minutes on each side. Remove the chicken pieces from the pan.

In the same pan, add the onions and saute until translucent. Add the remaining paste along with tomato ketchup and water. Bring the chicken pieces back into the pan. Cover and cook on medium heat for 20 minutes.
For the potato wedges, heat a flat pan and add the oil. Add the potato slices on medium heat and sprinkle salt over them.
Flip them after they have browned on one side, for around 2 minutes. Season with salt again. Cook for a further 2 minutes.
Serve the chicken with potato wedges and slices of lemon.

title: Mushroom Cutlet
cooking_instructions: In a saucepan, pour enough water to cover the potatoes. Boil it, covered, until a knife pierces through it smoothly.
Transfer the potato pieces to a bowl and mash. Set it aside.
Chop the mushrooms. Cut each mushroom into 6 to 8 pieces.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan. Add the onions and saute for 1 minute on medium heat. Add the chilli powder, coriander powder, jeera powder, black pepper powder, salt and the chopped tomato. Cook for 2 more minutes until the tomatoes have softened.
Add the mushrooms and cook until all the moisture has evaporated around 4-5 minutes.
Add this mixture to the bowl with the mashed potato. Add garam masala and the breadcrumbs. Mix to combine. Divide the mixture into 8 equal-sized balls. Flatten them to form patties.
Take the rice flour in a plate/ bowl and coat the patties in the rice flour.
Shallow fry them until they are golden brown and crisp on both sides.

title: Shrikhand
cooking_instructions: Whisk the curd until smooth with the powdered sugar and cardamom powder.
Add and mix the dried rose petals and pistachios.
Garnish with chopped pitachios. Serve chilled.

title: Adhirasam
cooking_instructions: Rinse and soak the rice for atleast an hour. After an hour, drain the water from rice and spread it in a clean towel to get it dried. It could take atleast 5 to 10 minutes but you should feel the dampness in your palm or fingers.
Grind the rice in the mixer to a fine powder and sieve it to get a lump-free rice flour.
For the syrup, add jaggery in a pan with 1/4 cup of water and when it dissolves, strain the jaggery water to remove dirt and sand.
Again boil the jaggery water and keep stirring it until the jaggery comes to a boil, frothy.
Now remove the jaggery from the flame and add to the wet rice powder and mix it well along with cardamom powder, dry ginger powder, and sesame seeds.
Mix well, so that no lumps are formed till you get a soft dough consistency. Keep this adhirasam mixture aside for at least one day, covered. Add oil on the surface.
Heat required oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Make a small ball of the adhirasam mixture and place it in a oil greased banana leaf or parchment paper. Flatten them gently.

Add them to the heated oil. When the adhirasam gets cooked, it will automatically rise up in the oil. Gently using a spatula turn the adhirasam to the other side and allow it to cook for another minute.
Then hold your spatula in one hand and take out the adhirasam from oil. Using another ladle, gently press the center of the fried adhirasam to squeeze out the excess oil.

title: Tomato Mint Chutney
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and splutter the mustard seeds.
Add the dried red chilies, asafoetida, garlic, and ginger. Lightly saute them and then add in the tomato, turmeric powder, salt, and sugar.
When the tomato softens and releases its moisture, add the mint leaves and coriander leaves. Cook for 1 more minute.
When it cools lightly, blend it into a slightly coarse chutney. This can be served as a dip with idli, vada, dosa, and also with roti and rice. It can also be used as a sandwich spread.

title: Veg Thai Green Curry
cooking_instructions: Combine all the ingredients for the green curry paste and blend in a mixer grinder to a smooth paste with ¼ cup water.
In a pan, heat oil and fry the curry paste for 10 minutes until the raw smell and flavour goes.
Add the vegetables and saute for 3 minutes.
Add 1 Cup of water and salt. Boil until the vegetables are tender.
Add the brown sugar and soya sauce.
Add the thick coconut milk, basil leaves, lemongrass and lime leaves, bring to one boil. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Sago Kheer
cooking_instructions: Wash the tapioca pearls well, strain it. and soak the tapioca pearls in warm milk.
Soak them for an hour in 300ml of milk.
Add the water first and bring the milk to a boil while stirring continuously.
Add the soaked tapioca pearls.
Cook on a medium-low flame, stirring until the milk reduces to 3/4th the original quantity and the pearls are completely cooked and soft.
Add the chopped nuts, soaked saffron, and condensed milk and cook for a further 7 mins.

title: Mutton Biryani
cooking_instructions: Marinate the mutton pieces in ginger garlic paste, salt and turmeric powder.
Wash the rice and soak in water for 20 minutes.
Grind the mint and green chilies into a fine paste.
In a heavy-bottomed utensil, pour the oil and ghee and heat together. Add the marinated mutton and saute lightly on all sides.
Add the mint paste, mix well and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the sliced onion and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato, red chili powder, salt, and biryani masala. Stir and then add the chopped mint and coriander leaves. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the beaten curd and mix well. Cover and cook on medium heat for 25 minutes, or until the oil starts floating on top and meat is cooked halfway through.
Add 3 cups of water and lemon juice. When it comes to a boil, add the soaked rice.
Boil until the level of rice almost reaches the level of the water. Cover with aluminum foil and place on a heated Tawa. Cook on a low flame for 25 minutes.

title: Cauliflower Steak
cooking_instructions: For the yogurt dip: whisk the ingredients listed until smooth and serve the cauliflower steaks with garlic yogurt dip.
Preheat an oven at 200 C. Clean the cauliflower head in salted water. Cut into large “steak” pieces/ thick slices lengthwise.
Combine the ingredients for the marinade in a bowl.
Place the cauliflower slices on a baking sheet and brush the marinade generously on both sides. Roast until golden brown, 20 minutes.

title: Pollachi Mutton Kulambu
cooking_instructions: Add the mutton to a pressure cooker, pour 4 cups of water. Add salt, pepper, and turmeric, mix it. Close the cooker and pressure cook it for 6 whistles, turn off the flame. Let the pressure reduce gradually.

Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, coriander seeds, ginger, garlic, dry red chilies, and let it crackle. Add the shallots, saute them for a few minutes. Add the grated coconut and cook it for a while.
Transfer the mixture to a blender, add water, and blend it to a fine paste.
In another pan, heat oil, add cumin seeds, curry leaves, dry red chilies, and let it crackle.
Add the shallots and cook it till it turns slightly brown.Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a few seconds..
Add the brinjal and drumstick and cook it for a while, until tender.
Add Chilli powder and Turmeric powder, mix it well Add a cup of water, mix it well. Cover and cook it for 10 minutes
Add the coconut paste to it and cook it till it starts boiling.
Add the boiled mutton along with the stock, mix it well. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes. Season it with salt and black pepper powder. Mix it well.
Transfer it to a bowl, garnish it with chopped coriander. Serve it hot.

title: Srilankan Fish Curry
cooking_instructions: Wash the fish slices. Marinate it with turmeric powder, salt, lemon juice and let it rest for 10 minutes. Heat a tawa, add oil and sear the marinated fish to a golden brown colour on both sides and set it aside.
In a pan, heat oil, add cinnamon, cumin, mustard, curry leaves, green chilies and. Let it crackle.
Add the chopped onions and saute it till it is golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook it for a few seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook it till it is mashed.
Add turmeric powder, add a little water, mix it.
Add the coconut milk. Mix it well.
Season the gravy with salt and pepper and let it simmer.
Add tamarind paste, sugar, fresh cream, and mix it well.
Add the fish to the gravy, cover the pan and let it simmer for a few more minutes.
Transfer it to a bowl. Garnish it with coriander sprigs and fried curry leaves. Serve it hot.

title: Smoked Paneer Tikka Pizza
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the water, yeast and sugar. Allow it to rest for 10 minutes. This allows the yeast to bloom. If it doesn’t rise, the yeast might be old or expired.

Measure 2 cups of Maida and put it into a large bowl. Add salt and mix, to make sure that the salt is distributed evenly. Make a well in the centre of the Maida, using your fingers or a wooden spoon, Add the wet mixture in the middle.
Start adding a little bit of flour into the wet mixture. Continue doing this until all the flour is mixed in, and a shaggy dough is formed
Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead well until a smooth dough forms
Add 2 tbsp of oil to the dough. Knead well again until the oil is completely mixed in and the dough becomes smooth.
Cover with a damp cloth and allow it to rise for at least 45 minutes, up to 1 ½ hours

For this recipe, we use a technique to give our pizza a smoky flavour. To a bowl of the pizza sauce, place a small metal bowl in the centre. Place an activated hot charcoal in the middle. Pour 1 tbsp of oil on top, and cover the whole bowl with aluminium foil. Let it sit for at least 3 minutes before opening.

For the Paneer Tikka marination. In a bowl, combine the curd, Kashmiri red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, chaat masala, ginger garlic paste and salt. Mix in the paneer, onion, capsicum and oil.
After the dough has risen, divide the dough into 3 portions.
Roll out the dough to your preferred thickness, and transfer to the baking tray. You can also divide the dough in 2, for a larger sized pizza, Pierce the dough using a fork.
Spread the smoked pizza sauce on the dough, except for 1 inch around the border, spread shredded cheese on the pizza. Place the marinated Paneer, onion and capsicum around the pizza.
Bake in an oven preheated to 230 degrees celsius for 12 minutes, or until the cheese starts to turn golden.
Take out of the oven and brush the crust with olive oil. Cut into 6 pieces and serve hot.

title: Street Style Chilli Mushroom
cooking_instructions: Cut Mushrooms into halves, add soy sauce, maida, corn flour and water and mix it till it coats evenly.
Heat oil in a Kadai, deep fry the mushrooms till it turns golden brown and crispy. Keep it aside.
In a wok, add oil. Let it heat up. Add chopped ginger and garlic, saute for a few seconds. Add the chopped green chilies and the dry red chilies and let them crackle.
Add the diced onions, cook it for a few seconds. Add bell peppers and toss them for a few seconds on a high flame.
Add water, soy sauce and tomato ketchup, stir it in. Add the cornstarch, mix it in.
Add the fried mushrooms, toss it on a high flame till the sauce coats evenly on them.
Transfer it to a bowl, Garnish it with chopped coriander leaves. Serve it hot.

title: Goli Baje
cooking_instructions: To a large bowl, add the Maida. Add curd and ½ cup of water and mix until there are no lumps.
Add the hing, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves, black peppercorn and cumin seeds. Beat for 4-5 minutes using your hands to make the batter fluffy and slightly stretchy.
Add salt, baking soda, and mix to combine. Mix well, and rest for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Using wet hands, take small portions (around 1-2 tbsp) of the batter and drop it into hot oil.
Deep fry until it turns golden brown and is floating in the oil. Remove from the oil and serve hot with coconut chutney.

title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
cooking_instructions: Place a sheet of cling wrap over the chicken breast. Flatten it using a heavy object such as a meat mallet, rolling pin or a flat pan.
Apply dijon mustard on the inner side of the flattened chicken breast. Season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Arrange a slice of ham and cheese, around ½ inch space on the sides.
Cover it tightly in cling wrap. Tie the edges and twist in opposite sides to tighten. Freeze for 15-20 minutes so that it forms up and holds its shape.
Season the maida with salt and pepper in a bowl. Keep the beaten egg and breadcrumbs ready in separate bowls.
Remove the cling wrap and coat the chicken in maida, then the eggs and finally in breadcrumbs. Make sure that it is completely coated.
Shallow fry on medium heat until golden brown on all sides, turning it occasionally to ensure even cooking.
Once it is completely golden brown on the outside, transfer to a baking dish and bake for 8-10 minutes at 180°c in a preheated oven.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice and serve.

title: Mushroom Bonda
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl, add besan flour, cornflour, rice flour, turmeric powder, red chili powder, salt, tomato sauce, water and mix everything together.
Add chopped mushroom, onion, green chili, curry leaves, coriander leaves and mix well until evenly combined.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan. Once the oil is hot, deep fry the mushrooms until crispy and golden brown.
Sprinkle chaat masala over the fried bondas and toss. Serve hot as snacks or as an appetizer with chutney/tomato ketchup.

title: Eggless Bread Pudding
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. In a pan of milk, add the sugar, vanilla essence, custard powder, and butter. Heat until it comes to a boil while whisking, it will thicken up.
In an oven-safe bowl, grease it with butter and add the bread pieces and arrange them evenly. Add the raisins also.
Pour the milk mixture on top of the bread.
Sprinkle sugar on top and bake at 180 C in the oven for 35 mins or until the top is golden brown.
Cut it and serve it hot. They can be garnished with fresh fruits and whipped cream as needed.

title: Chilli Garlic Noodles
cooking_instructions: To cook the noodles, bring a pot of water to a boil. Season generously with salt and add the noodles. Cook the noodles until it is 90% cooked or according to the cooking time on the package. Drain the noodles and run them under cold water. Apply oil and set aside.
For the chilli paste, remove the seeds from the chillies. Soak in hot water for 15 minutes.Grind it into a paste along with the garlic.
Heat oil in a pan and add chopped garlic. Saute until it starts to brown.
Add the chili garlic paste and saute for 2 minutes or until the oil separates from the sides.
Add the ginger, onion, cabbage, and capsicum. Saute on high heat for 1 minute.
Add the cooked noodles along with soy sauce, salt, sugar, black pepper powder, MSG, vinegar, and spring onion. Mix well and saute for 2 minutes.
Garnish with sliced spring onions and serve!

title: Holi Thandai
cooking_instructions: Dry roast the ingredients until aromatic, 5 mins on a simmer and allow them to cool down. Grind into a fine powder and sieve through a strainer.
Grind any leftover pieces and add them to the powder.
Mix 2 ½ tbsp with 1 glass of chilled milk and serve with some slivers of pistachio/almonds/rose petals/saffron.

title: Eggless Chocolate Mousse
cooking_instructions: Heat the cream gently on a low flame. When it is warm, turn off the heat and whisk in the cocoa powder and sugar.
In a bowl, mix the cornstarch and milk together. Mix well to ensure that there are no lumps.
Combine both the mixtures together. Pass it through a strainer into a pot.
Heat on a low flame, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Add the chocolate and allow it to melt completely. Turn off the heat.
Transfer it into a pan that is greased and lined with butter paper. Alternatively, you can also pour them into cups to serve as individual portions.
Once it has cooled slightly, cover with cling wrap and refrigerate for 5-6 hours.
Dust with cocoa powder and serve.

title: Chha Gosht
cooking_instructions: To cook the mutton, heat ghee in a pressure cooker and add all the whole spices. When they turn aromatic, add the mutton along with salt and water. Cover and pressure cook for 25 minutes.

To make the masala paste, heat the mustard oil until it reaches its smoking point. Allow the oil to cool down, then add the Kashmiri chili, cumin seeds, asafoetida, and all the powdered spices. Saute lightly on a low flame. Add the ginger, garlic, and onion. Saute until it turns translucent. Allow it to cool, then grind into a paste.
Make buttermilk by whisking the curd and then adding water gradually.
Dry roast the besan in a pan on low heat until it turns aromatic. Add the buttermilk gradually and mix constantly to ensure that there are no lumps.
Add the masala paste and the water from the cooked mutton. Mix well.
Add the mutton pieces and simmer for 5 minutes or until it reaches the desired consistency.
Serve it hot and garnish it with a sprig of coriander

title: Nalli Nihari
cooking_instructions: Grind all the ingredients for the masala into a fine powder. Mix with the rest of the powdered spices and salt.
Heat ghee in a pot and add bay leaf and onion. Saute until the onion turns golden brown. Remove ⅓ of the onions and set aside.
Add the mutton shanks and saute for 4 minutes.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and the Nihari masala. Add 2 cups of water. Saute for 5 minutes, then add the hot water.

Once it comes to a boil, reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour until the meat is completely cooked. Turn off the heat and allow it to rest for 10 minutes or until the fat floats on top. Remove the excess fat and set it aside for garnishing later.

Mix the wheat flour and water to form a thin mixture. Add it gradually into the pot until it thickens. Add the brown onions that had been removed earlier. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until it reaches the desired consistency, and remove from the heat.
Serve hot, with the toppings.

title: Chicken Nuggets
cooking_instructions: To the chicken, add garlic, salt, white pepper powder, soy sauce and cornstarch. Mix well until it forms a smooth mixture. You could also use a mixer or food processor for this step, to produce a smooth mixture. Chill in the refrigerator for 20 minutes. This helps to make the mixture firm and easier to shape
Keep a bowl with flour ready. In another bowl, beat an egg. In another bowl, add the breadcrumbs, chilli powder, black pepper powder and salt and mix to combine
Shape the chicken mixture into small portions and shape them into nuggets, Dip each piece in flour, then egg and then in the seasoned breadcrumbs
Deep fry them until they are golden brown. Deep fry for 1 minute on high flame and then reduce the flame to low and cook for 4 minutes

title: Vegetable Au Gratin
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Boil water in a pot and add salt, add the vegetables and cook until tender but still crunchy, about 7-8 mins. Strain the vegetables and set them aside.
In a pan, heat and melt some butter and add garlic and onions and saute until translucent.
Add and saute the capsicum dice.
Add maida and cook on a low flame for 2 mins.
Add the milk while whisking constantly, in 3 additions.
Season with salt, black pepper powder, and dried mixed herbs. Add the cheese and mix it well
Add the vegetables to the sauce and finish with some fresh cream.
Transfer to an ovenproof dish and top with grated cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20 mins at 200C.

title: Pizza McPuff
cooking_instructions: Mix baking powder and salt into the maida. Add the oil and mix using your fingers until the oil is spread evenly. The maida should become crumbly.
Add water gradually and knead into stiff dough. Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 30 minutes.
For the filling, heat oil in a pan and saute onion and garlic until translucent.
Add all the vegetables and saute for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato ketchup, pizza sauce, salt, pepper, chilli flakes and oregano. Mix well and remove from the heat. Allow it to cool completely.
Take a portion of the dough and roll it out thin. Trim the edges to get a square/rectangle.
Cut rectangle portions of equal size.
Once the filling is completely cooled, add cheese and mix.
Place some of the filling on the centre of the dough. Use a fork to seal the edges. Trim again with a knife, if needed.
Deep-fry on medium-low heat until golden brown and puffed.
Serve Hot with ketchup on the side

title: Vegan Mango Smoothie
cooking_instructions: Add the mango, coconut milk, chia seeds, ice cubes, and sugar into a blender jar.
Blend it just until it turns smooth.
Transfer it to a glass with ice cubes, garnish it with mango dice. Serve it cold

title: Rava Dosa
cooking_instructions: Combine the rava, rice flour, maida, and salt in a bowl.
Add the chopped onion, green chili, ginger, coconut bits, coriander leaves, curry leaves cumin seeds, and peppercorns. Mix all of them together.
Add the curd and mix well. Add water and make a thin batter of pouring consistency.
Rest the batter for 20 mins.
Pour some water to readjust the consistency, a total of 5 Cups.

Heat a flat tava and pour the batter with a round ladle. Mix the batter well in between the preparation of each dosa. Add some ghee and allow it to cook until golden brown, release the sides and fold in half. Serve it hot.

title: Chicken Kothu Parotta
cooking_instructions: Cut the cooked Parotta into small pieces.
In a Tawa/Pan, heat oil and add the finely chopped onions, green chili, and curry leaves.
Once the onions are translucent add the finely chopped tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes are mushy.
Add the chopped Parotta and mix well.
Add the Eggs and Salt to the Pan/Tawa. Mix well and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the Chicken Salna, Shredded Chicken, mix well until combined, and continue to cook by mixing it for 4 minutes.
Use the iron/steel ladle shred the parota into small bits
Add the Black Pepper Powder, Coriander leaves, mix well and remove from the heat.
Serve it hot.

title: Christams Fruit Cake
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 deegrees.Soak the dry fruits ovedrnight in rum and strain it.
Cream the butter, brown sugar, and Cookd Christmas spice mix.
Add the eggs one at a time and mix well in between each addition. Add the vanilla essence.
Add the soaked fruits and nuts and combine the mixture well.
Finally, add the flour and baking powder and fold to mix well.
Finally, add and mix in the oil.
Pour in a lined mold, top it off with de-skinned almonds and bake at 180C for 40-45 mins
Cool completely prior to consumption. cut it and serve

title: Egg Satay
cooking_instructions: Grind all the ingredients for the marination paste together.
Cut the egg white cubes into thick strips. Coat them in cornstarch.
Marinate the egg whites with half of the marination paste. Skewer the eggs with satay sticks.
Grease a grill pan with oil and grill the satay for 4 minutes on each side.
For the sauce, heat oil in a pan and add the remaining marination paste. Cook for 1 minute. Add the peanut butter and sugar.
Add the coconut milk and bring it to a simmer. Turn off the heat and add lemon juice.
Serve, it hot with the sauce on the side.

title: Puttu
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak rice in water for 4 hours.
Strain the rice, lay on a cloth, and dry for 30 minutes.
Grind it into a powder. Sieve it and grind any leftover rice again. Add it to the ground rice.
Mix salt and coconut to the rice flour.
Take the puttu flour in a wide bowl. Add salt and ½ cup of the grated coconut and mix.
Sprinkle the water a little at a time, and mix gently with your fingers until the moisture is spread evenly.
In the puttu cylinder (puttu kutti), put in 1 tbsp of coconut. Add the puttu mixture halfway through. Add 1 tbsp more of the grated coconut. Repeat the same one more time until it is filled.
In a puttu steamer, add water in the bottom vessel and bring to a boil.
Place the lid on top and steam for 10 minutes.

To cook the puttu without the puttu steamer, in a bowl add grated coconut and then the puttu mixture and pack it tightly. Demould it onto an oiled plate. and keep it in a makeshift steamer and let it steam for 10. minutes.
Take it out of the steamer and serve it hot with sugar or stew.

title: Pan-Fried Potatoes
cooking_instructions: Slice the baby potatoes thick and rinse them in cold water.
Dry them completely.
Heat oil and butter in a pan and pan-fry the potatoes until golden brown.
Retain 1 tbsp of the same oil and saute the onions until golden and caramelized. Add the smashed garlic while cooking the onions.
Finish with salt, paprika, dried herbs, and chopped coriander leaves. Add the pan-fried potatoes and toss well. Serve it hot.

title: Sour Cream
cooking_instructions: Combine the ingredients mentioned and whisk until thick and smooth.
Chill and serve.

title: Malabar Fish Roast
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, take the boneless fish cubes. Add red chilli powder, coriander powder and salt. Mix well.
In a pan, add coconut oil and Tawa fry the fish cubes for 4 mins.
Soak tamarind in water and extract the tamarind juice.
In a mixer grinder, add the grated coconut and water. Grind to extract coconut milk. Filter the coconut milk and set aside.
Heat another pan to make the masala. Add coconut oil. Once the oil is hot, add finely chopped onions and saute until translucent.

Add the slit green chilli and ginger garlic paste. Cook until the raw smell of the ginger-garlic paste leaves. Add the tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes are soft and mushy.Add the red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, salt and continue to cook for 2 mins.
Add the tamarind extract and cook for a minute.Add the Tawa fried fish cubes and curry leaves.
Add the extracted coconut milk and cook until the sauce thickens and coats on all the fish pieces. Continue to roast on high heat for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Serve hot with Appam, Idiyappam, Idli or Dosa.

title: Eggless Chocolate Cake
cooking_instructions: Sieve the maida, cocoa powder and baking soda together. Add the powdered sugar and salt.
Make a hole in the center and add oil, vinegar, vanilla essence and warm water. Mix until there are no lumps.
Transfer it to a greased pan. Bake in a preheated oven at 180 c for 20 minutes.
For the frosting, add the chocolate and cream to a bowl. Place the bowl over a pot of boiling water and mix it until it melts.
Take off the heat and allow it to refrigerate for 1 hour or until it thickens.
Apply it over the cake.
Additionally, you can also decorate it with strawberries or chocolate decorations.

title: Kerala Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash, rinse and soak the rice for 15 minutes. Grind the shallots and green chilli into a fine paste.
Heat oil and ghee in a pan. Add the onion and saute until translucent.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, shallot green chili paste, turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Cook until the oil starts getting released from the sides, around 10 minutes.
Add the mint leaves, coriander leaves, and curd. Mix well.
Add the chicken pieces and stir. Cover and cook for 10 minutes on medium heat.
Add the sliced tomatoes and biryani masala. Cover and cook for 10 more minutes. Take off the heat.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add all the whole spices except bay leaf and saute until aromatic.
Add the water and bring it to a boil. Season with salt and sugar and add the bay leaf. Add the soaked rice and cook until the rice almost reaches the level of the water.
Cover tightly and cook for 10 minutes.
Spread the chicken in the bottom of a heavy-bottomed vessel. Add half of the fried onion and coriander leaves.
Add the rice on top. Top with fried onion, cashews and raisins, coriander leaves and ghee. Cover tightly with aluminum foil and a lid.
Heat a tawa and place the vessel on top. Cook on a low flame for 10 minutes. Serve it hot.

title: Fish Nirvana
cooking_instructions: Mix all the ingredients for the marination into a paste. Apply it on the fish.
Heat coconut oil in a pan and shallow fry the fish for 2 minutes on each side.
In an earthen pot, place a banana leaf. Pour in coconut oil and heat.
Add curry leaves and fried fish.
Add the coconut milk, ginger, green chili, and pepper powder. Allow it to simmer for 4 minutes.
Drizzle coconut oil over the top and turn off the heat. Garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot.

title: Coconut Laddoo
cooking_instructions: Heat Ghee in a tawa. Roast the coconut in ghee for 2 minutes.Add Cardamom Powder and mix well.
Add the condensed milk and cook until the mixture leaves the side of the pan and the ghee separates slightly from the sides.Transfer the mixture to a bowl and let it cool slightly.
Form the mixture into roundels and coat with desiccated coconut and serve.

title: Eggless Lemon Cake
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. In a bowl, take the maida and grate the zest of 1 lemon. Add the baking powder, baking soda and mix well.
In another bowl, combine the oil and sugar and mix well. Add the curd,  lemon juice and vanilla essence. and combine well.
Combine the wet and dry ingredients to make a smooth batter. Finally att the milk and mix it well.
Pour in a greased and lined baking pan and bake for 45 mins at 180C.
To make the buttercream: whisk the room temperature butter with the sugar until light and fluffy. Add the vanilla, milk and lemon juice and mix well.
Apply the buttercream on the cake only after completely cooling.

title: Keerai Vadai
cooking_instructions: Wash the urad dal and chana dal, and soak for 2 hours. Strain the water out and grind it into a coarse mixture without adding any water. Do not blend it completely.
To this mixture, add in the cumin seeds, green chillies, ginger, salt, hing, curry leaves and spinach. Mix well until thoroughly mixed.
Using a greased piece of banana leaf/butter paper/plastic sheet, flatten some of the mixture. Make a hole in the centre using your finger.
Deep fry it on medium-low flame for 10 minutes or until golden brown on both sides. Serve it hot witha chutney on the side.

title: Murg Mughlai Paratha
cooking_instructions: Add salt to the maida and rub in the oil into the flour until it is well mixed in.
Knead a soft dough with the water.
Apply oil, cover and rest for 20 mins.
For the chicken masala, heat oil in a kadai and add the ginger garlic paste. Cook until the raw flavour goes and add the onions.
Cook the onions until soft and translucent.
Add the powdered spices and salt and mix well, add the chicken mince and cook while continuously mixing and breaking up the mince.
Cook on a low flame for 8 mins.
Cooldown the mixture.
For the egg mixture, add 3 eggs with salt, green chillies and add the sliced onions and chopped coriander leaves and set aside.
Divide the dough into 6 roundels and apply a little oil on both sides.
Roll out the roundels thin and large.
Place some of the mince stuffing and pour some of the egg mixture carefully over the mince.
Fold the ends like an envelope, gently pressing down the sides.
Shallow fry the parathas, fold side down in medium hot oil, basting with oil to ensure faster and even cooking
Flip them halfway through and fry until golden brown on both sides, about 8 minutes in total.
Cut it into half, serve it hot.

title: Apple Crumble
cooking_instructions: Preheat an oven at 180C.
Peel, core and dice the apples. Combine the apples with the remaining ingredients for the filling and mix well.
For the topping: crumble the butter with the flour and oats until coarse in texture.
Add the brown sugar, walnuts, cinnamon powder and mix well.
Add the filling in an oven proof bowl, add some topping in the middle.
Loosely add the mixture on top of the apples without compacting it.
Bake for 40 mins until the top is golden brown and crunchy.
Serve warm with Vanilla Ice cream

title: Potato Shots
cooking_instructions: Pressure cook the potatoes for 4 whistles with water and 1 tsp of salt.
Peel and grate the potato.
In the bowl of grated potato, add the dried mixed herbs, onion, salt, chilli flakes, the cornflour and maida.
Mix well to form a firm mixture.
Form into the potato shots with greased hands, place on a plate lined with greaseproof paper.
Fry them in hot oil until golden brown and crispy, about 4 minutes. Take it off the oil. Serve it hot with ketchup on the side

title: Tehri
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice in water for 20 minutes.
In a pan, heat ghee and add the whole spices. Saute for a minute until aromatic.
Add the sliced onions and saute until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes and the mixed vegetables.
Add the powdered spices and saute for 2 minutes. Add the water and bring to a boil. Add the rice and salt. Cook it until the level of water and rice equals. About 5 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and kewra essence. Add the chopped mint and coriander.
Cover and reduce to the lowest flame and cook for 15minutes.
Open, fluff the rice with a fork and serve it hot.

title: Veg Dum Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 to 30 mins.
For the masala: Heat oil and ghee and add the whole spices, fry until aromatic. Add the sliced onions and fry until golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, green chillies and saute for 2 mins.
Add the tomatoes and powdered spices. Cook well and add the curd. Mix well.
Add the cut vegetables and 1 Cup of water. Simmer for 2 mins, then add the mint and coriander leaves. Set aside.
Boil the rice in water with 1 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp oil until 70% done and strain it.

Place the pot on a pre-heated tawa and remove half of the masala. Layer half of the masala and rice alternatively, pour ¼ Cup of water. Garnish with the remaining chopped mint and coriander leaves, kewra and rose water, saffron strands, ghee and a pinch of garam masala.
Cover well and cook on a high flame for 3 mins and a slow flame for 12 mins.
Open the dum and serve hot with raita.

title: Kothu Parotta
cooking_instructions: Knead the flour, salt, sugar, egg and water together. Add more water if required to form a smooth and soft dough. Knead for 10 minutes continuously.
Apply oil and rest for 1 hour. Divide and roll the dough into even spheres and apply oil on them.
Roll out a portion of dough into a very thin sheet. Apply oil over the rolled dough.
Fold the sheet of dough to form layers. Gather it into a spiral.
Flatten the dough spirals using your hands. Cook on a heated Tawa on medium flame until completely cooked.
Shred 4 Parottas into small pieces and set aside.
In an iron pan, heat oil and add the onion, green chilli, curry leaves and tomato.
Add in the shredded Parotta and mix well. Add the egg, pepper and salt.
Add in the empty Salna. Mix well and cook for 1 minute, while breaking up any large bits of Parotta. Transfer it to a plate and serve it hot.

title: No-Bake Bournvita Biscuit Cake
cooking_instructions: Mix the water and coffee powder and set aside.
Heat milk in a saucepan over medium heat with cocoa powder and sugar.
After it boils, Switch off the heat.
Add the chopped chocolate and mix well until glossy.
To assemble: Line a mold with Silver Foil.  Dip the biscuit in the coffee and place a layer in the mold. Pour over some of the chocolate mixture. Repeat until the biscuits and chocolate are used up.
Cover and place in the freezer overnight.
Carefully de-mold, dust cocoa powder and cut into slices and Serve

title: Salted Caramel Popcorn
cooking_instructions: Fry the dried corn in oil for 2 minutes until the colour gets lighter.
Cover with a lid and let the corn pop on a medium flame.
Remove the lid and let the steam escape.
Caramelize sugar in a pot until golden brown.
Add 1 tbsp of butter, ¼ tsp of salt and a pinch of baking soda.
Add the popcorn and mix well for a minute until well combined.
Cool completely on a large plate and consume.

title: Homemade Peanut Butter
cooking_instructions: Add ½ cup of peanut to a mixer grinder, pulse for a few times to get coarse peanuts. Keep it aside.
Add 1 ½ cups of peanut to a mixer grinder and grind it to smooth paste.
Add Groundnut oil, honey, salt and grind it again to get creamy consistency.
In a mixing bowl, add the ground paste, coarse ground peanut and mix well.
Store it in an airtight container and use whenever needed.

title: Goan Fish Curry
cooking_instructions: Soak the chillies for 15 minutes in 1 Cup of water.
Soak ½ tsp of tamarind in ¼ cup of water for 10 mins.
Wash and clean the fish pieces with salt, turmeric powder and lemon juice.
Grind the tomato to extract the tomato puree.
In a mixer grinder jar, add coconut, coriander seeds, chopped onion, cumin seeds, turmeric powder, garlic, tamarind, soaked red chilli with the water.
Grind this into a very smooth paste. Should take around 5 minutes in the mixture grinder.
Heat oil in a Kadai, add thinly sliced onions and saute until the onions are translucent.
Add the spice paste and saute for 7 minutes.
When the spice paste is cooked, add 3 cups of water.
Once the curry comes to a boil, add the salt, tomato puree, green chilli and simmer the curry for 6 minutes.
Add the tamarind water.
Add the fish and cook for 3 mins.
Add coriander leaves, mix and remove from the heat. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Kerala Sambar
cooking_instructions: Soak the tamarind in 1 Cup of water for 20 mins.
Wash and drain the toor dal.
In a pressure cooker, add the washed toor dal, turmeric powder, water and pressure cook for 7 whistles.
Heat 2 tsp of coconut oil in a pan, add the fenugreek seeds, and saute until aromatic.
Add the coriander seeds, dried red chili, curry leaves, and saute for 2 mins.
Add asafoetida, grated coconut and saute for a minute.
Once cool, add the sauted mixture to a mixer grinder along with ½ Cup of water and grind it into a smooth paste.
Extract the tamarind juice from the soaked tamarind.
Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a Kadai, add the mustard seeds, and let it splutter. Add the shallots, curry leaves, and saute till it gets translucent.
Add the tomato and saute till the tomatoes are soft.
Add the drumstick, white pumpkin, brinjal, turmeric powder, salt, 4 cups of water, mix well, cover and cook for 20 mins.
Add the cooked toor dal, ground masala paste extracted tamarind juice, and simmer for 5 mins.
Remove from the heat and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Paneer Tikka
cooking_instructions: Place a muslin cloth/cheesecloth in a strainer. Pour the curd into the cloth and cover. Place in a refrigerator for 3-4 hours. This is to remove the excess moisture and get hung curd, for our marination.
Add all the ingredients for the marination, into the hung curd.

To prepare the chilli oil, heat the oil in a small pan until it reaches its smoking point. Turn off the heat and immediately add the red chilli powder. Add this to the marinade immediately. Do not leave the chilli powder in the hot oil for too long, as it will burn.

Cut the paneer into large cubes, 2-inches wide and 1 inch thick. De-seed the tomatoes and dice them. Dice the capsicum and onion. Add them to the marinade and mix well. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. You can also cook this immediately.
Soak the bamboo sticks in water for 20 minutes. Skewer the paneer pieces, alternating with the onion, tomato and capsicum dices.
Heat and grease a grill pan or a Tawa. Grill the skewers on medium heat. Cook each side until all the sides are charred.
Remove them from the pan. Brush them with melted butter and sprinkle with chaat masala, Serve with mint chutney.

title: Coconut Stuffed Pancakes
cooking_instructions: Break the egg into a bowl and whisk it. Then add in 1 cup of water, salt, and sugar.
Then add in the flour and mix well. When there are no lumps, add the remaining water to form a thin dough.
For the filling, combine the grated coconut, sugar, and cardamom powder in a bowl.
To cook the pancakes, heat up a nonstick pan. On medium flame, pour the batter and swirl the pan to spread it around. Cover and cook for 3 minutes.
Transfer it to a plate, place the filling in the center. Tuck in from the sides and roll it into a tube shape and serve.

title: Mangalore Fish Curry
cooking_instructions: Wash, drain and score the sides of the fish. Soak the tamarind in ½ cup of water for at least 20 minutes.

Broil the dry red chilies and set them aside. In the same pan, broil the black peppercorns, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and fenugreek seeds. Add all the broiled ingredients into a mixer jar with all the other ingredients for the masala paste, and grind into a smooth paste.

In a pan, add the ground masala paste without any oil and add water. Add the sliced onions and green chilies. Add salt and 1 ½ cups of water. Cover and cook till the raw taste disappears, around 10 minutes.
Add the fish, salt, and tamarind pulp.
Once it comes to a boil again, turn the heat to low and simmer covered until the fish is cooked, around 10-15 minutes depending on the size of the fish.
Add coconut oil on top and turn off the heat. Serve it hot.

title: Jam Swiss Roll
cooking_instructions: Preheat an oven to 180C. For the batter, mix together the salt, maida and baking powder and set it aside.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, vanilla and sugar until thick and foamy.
Incorporate the oil and finally the flour mixture.
Line a tray with parchment paper. Apply oil and dust with maida.

Pour the batter into the lined mold, spread it out evenly. Add a few drops of food color and make a swirl pattern using a toothpick as needed and bake for 15 mins until firm and light golden in color.
On a large clean cloth/ parchment paper dust generously with icing sugar and tip over the cake onto it and dust with icing sugar in top as well. Gently roll it up into a log and allow it to cool.
Whisk the whipping cream until soft peaks form and set it aside.
For the filling, whisk the jam and water until it’s smooth in consistency.

Once it has cooled, roll out the cake and apply a thin layer of jam followed by a layer of whipped cream. Sprinkle the diced strawberries on the cream and roll it back gently into a log. Allow it to cool for an hour. Cut it into slices and serve.

title: Crispy Egg Fingers
cooking_instructions: In a bowl beat 5 eggs, add the salt, red chilli powder, black pepper powder. To the egg mixture add finely chopped onion and jalapeno, and mix.
Pour the egg mixture into a greased pan and steam until firm, for 12 minutes.
De-mold the eggs and cut into fingers/ large batons.
In a bowl combine 1 egg and milk. In two separate bowls, place flour and breadcrumbs.
For crumbing: dust the egg fingers in flour and then place in the egg mixture, drain the excess and then coat with breadcrumbs evenly. Repeat for all the egg fingers.
Deep fry until golden brown and crispy.

title: Chicken Dum Parotta
cooking_instructions: In a pan, heat oil and add fennel seeds and Kalpasi. Add the onion and curry leaves and cook until the onion turns translucent.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, salt and all the spice powders (except the black pepper powder) on low heat. Saute and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken, black pepper powder, and ½ Cup of water. Cover and cook for 15 minutes. Add the coconut milk and turn off the heat when it comes to a boil.
In an earthen pot, apply a tablespoon of ghee on the bottom. Place 2 Parottas and apply gravy on both sides.
Add an adequate amount of chicken masala. Sprinkle half of the fried onions and cashew nuts and 1 tbsp each of coriander leaves and mint leaves.
Place 2 Parottas on top and add some gravy, boiled eggs, and the same quantities of fried onions, cashew nuts, mint, and coriander leaves.
Place 2 more Parottas on top and add more of the chicken gravy on top. Repeat the toppings again. Pour 1 tbsp of ghee on top.
Heat a banana leaf lightly over a direct flame. Cover the earthen pot with the banana leaf and tie it around the edges of the pot to seal it.
Place on a low flame and cook for 5 minutes.

title: Oats and Banana Cookie
cooking_instructions: Preheat an oven at 200 C.Pulse the oats until coarse.
Mash the bananas well, add the oats, walnuts, and choco chips. Mix until combined.
Shape into roundels and flatten them with wet hands and bake for 20 mins, on a tray lined with parchment paper.
Cool completely before consumption.

title: Maggi Spring Rolls
cooking_instructions: Prepare a smooth and lump-free batter with the given ingredients.
Pour on a greased non-stick pan on a low heat and spread to get a thin sheet, when the sides release, flip for a few seconds and remove the sheet.
To make the mixture, heat oil in a pan and add the minced garlic. Saute for a minute.
Add the sliced onions, cabbage and spring onions. Saute for 2 mins until soft. Add soy sauce.
Add the Maggi, masala, and slightly lesser water as per packet instruction and cook until dry but not mushy. Cool the mixture completely.
Mix maida and water to make a paste to stick the spring roll sheets.
Take each sheet and trim to make a square shape, place some stuffing in the middle roll, and seal using the maida paste.
Shallow fry until golden brown on all sides.

title: Aloo Gobi
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a Kadai, add cumin seeds, fennel seeds, and let it splutter.
Add onion, garlic, green chili, and saute till it turns golden brown.
Add tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, salt, saute till the tomatoes are mushy and the masalas are cooked.
Add potato, cauliflower florets and mix well.
Add 1 ¾ Cup of water cover and cook for 10 mins.
Open the lid, add garam masala powder, mix well and simmer for 2 mins.
Add the coriander leaves, mix and remove from the heat. Serve hot with Chapati/roti.

title: Raw Mango Fish Curry
cooking_instructions: Using a pestle and mortar powder the fenugreek. Set this aside for tempering.
Grind all the ingredients mentioned under Masala paste and set them aside.
Grind the grated coconut and water to form the coconut paste. Set this aside.
In a Kadai or Pot, add the thinly sliced onions, green chilies, curry leaves, ground masala paste, salt, and water.
Place this pot or Kadai on a stove and bring it to a boil. Add the raw mangoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Once the mangoes are cooked, add the coconut paste and simmer for 5 minutes.
Once the curry reaches desired consistency, add the sardine fish pieces. Cook this for 3 minutes and remove the pot from the heat.

In a tempering pan, heat oil, add the mustard seeds. When the mustard seeds start to splutter, add red chilli, shallots and curry leaves. Sprinkle the fenugreek powder and pour the tempering to the prepared curry.Mix gently and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Bun Parotta
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine Egg, Milk, Water, Salt and Sugar. Mix well until all the ingredients are incorporated together.
In another kneading bowl, take the maida and add the wet mixture prepared above and mix to form a dough.
Continue to knead the dough for 15 mins until the dough is very soft and stretchy.
Add 1 tbsp oil on top of the dough to prevent it from drying and cover the bowl with a cloth. Rest the dough for a minimum of 2 hours and a maximum of 5 hours.
Make individual 2-inch dough balls.
Add 2 tbsp of oil on the dough balls and rest for another 30 minutes.
Take a dough ball and flatten thin by using a rolling pin. Apply oil on the spread dough.

Using both your hands, spin the dough in a circular motion to make it thin. Fold the dough vertically and roll it sidewise. Turn the dough sideways to make it a spiralled dough about 3 inches in height.
Gently flatten the dough using your palms into a 4 inch circle.
Take a dough ball and flatten thin by using a rolling pin. Apply oil on the spread dough.

Flatten it further as thin as possible using a rolling pin, by rolling it into a large circle. Apply some oil again and fold the dough vertically and roll it sidewise. Turn the dough sideways to make it a spiralled dough about 3 inches in height.
Gently flatten the dough using your palms into a 4 inch circle.
Add some oil on the tawa, place the gently flattened parotta and cook on a medium high heat for 2 minutes and flip. Continue cooking on the other side for another 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and tap on the side of the parotta to fluff it up and to resemble a bun.

title: Maggi Ramen Bowl
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the mushrooms. Saute on high heat for 2 minutes. Remove the mushrooms from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add more oil. Add ginger, garlic and spring onion whites. Saute for 30 seconds or until fragrant. Add the soy sauce.
Add water and maggi seasoning. Once it comes to a boil, add the maggi noodles. Boil for 2 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook for 30 seconds more.
To make a soft boiled egg, heat water in a pan. The level of water should be around 1 inch. Add the egg, cover and cook for 6 minutes.
Remove the egg from the pot and put it into ice cold water. Once it is cool enough to handle, peel the egg and cut in half. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the noodles and broth into a bowl. Top with sriracha sauce, the soft-boiled egg, mushroom, spring onion and sesame seeds.

title: Coconut Prawn Pulao
cooking_instructions: Wash the basmati rice in water and soak it in water for at least 20 minutes. Soak the cashews in water.
In a pot, heat the ghee and add cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, and cardamom. Add the onions and green chilies. Cook until the onion turns translucent.
Add the ginger-garlic paste. Saute for 1 minute.
To this, add the peeled shrimp and chopped tomato.
Add the coconut milk and 3 cups of water. Add the salt and sugar.
Once it comes to a boil, add the lemon juice and the soaked rice.
Cover with a lid and cook on low flame for 20 minutes. After 20 minutes, add the soaked cashew nuts and gently mix the rice.

title: Veg Galouti Kebab
cooking_instructions: Boil the yam and ridge gourd in a pressure cooker for 3 whistles with 1 tsp of salt.
Strain and mash it well.
Add the powdered spices and salt. Mix well. Add the roasted gram flour and combine well.
In a bowl, place a smoking piece of coal and add 1 tsp of ghee. Smoke for 1 minute, covered.
Remove the coal and mix again. Form small-sized round and flat kebabs.
Shallow fry in ghee until golden brown on either side, 2 minutes each. Sprinkle chaat masala and serve.

title: Gulab Jamun
cooking_instructions: Take sugar and water in a pan and bring it to boil. Add saffron strands and cardamom powder once the syrup comes to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes, syrup consistency shouldn’t be too thick.
In a mixing bowl, combine the Khova, maida, baking powder and cardamom powder.
Start mixing it together to form a dough by adding sprinkles of water.
Once the mixture becomes a firm dough ball, make smooth crack free balls of dough using your palm. Refrigerate for 10 minutes.

Heat the oil to a medium-low temperature in a deep frying pan. Add the dough balls in the oil and fry for 6-7 minutes on medium-low heat. The outside should turn golden brown and the inside should also be cooked. Frying on high heat will prevent from being cooked inside.
Cool the fried Jamuns for 5 mins and add them to the warm sugar syrup. After 3-4 hours of soaking inside the syrup at room temperature, the jamuns are ready to be served.

title: Bread Pizza Cups
cooking_instructions: Cut the crusts off the bread slices and apply melted butter on both sides.
Keep all the toppings, sauce and cheese ready. Carefully fit the slices into greased cupcake molds.
Add a tbsp of sauce at the bottom followed by slices of vegetables and top with cheese.
Bake for 8 mins at 180C until golden brown.

title: Safed Maas
cooking_instructions: Soak the nuts and seeds in hot water for a few minutes.
Marinate the mutton for 1 hour with the salt, white pepper powder, curd and ginger garlic paste.
Make a thick paste of the nuts and seeds with some water.
Heat ghee in a cooker and add the whole spices. Add the marinated mutton and water.
Pressure cook for 20 mins on a simmer after the first whistle on high flame.
In a kadai, add the oil and the whole spices. Add the sliced onions and allow it to develop a light golden colour.
Add the green chillies, salt and add the nut paste and mutton.
Cover and continue to cook for 5-10 mins, then serve!

title: Carrot Chutney
cooking_instructions: Add ¼ cup of gingelly oil to a pan. When the oil heats up, add dried red chilies, onion, and garlic.
Add the grated carrots and tomato. Add salt and saute it for 10 mins on high flame.
Once it cools down, add them to a mixer grinder, ½ cup of water and coarse grind it. Add the ground chutney to a serving dish.
Heat a pan, add 2 tbsp of gingelly oil. Add the mustard seeds. Once it splutters, add the urad dal. When it turns golden brown, add the curry leaves. Add this tempering to the Chutney.
Add finely chopped coriander leaves and mix.

title: Kozhi Poriyal
cooking_instructions: Cut the chicken into large pieces. Add salt, turmeric powder and water and pressure cook for 15 mins on a low flame after the first whistle on a high flame.
Allow the pressure to release naturally and shred the chicken pieces and discard the bones.
In a kadai, heat oil and add the mustard seeds and let them splutter, add the red chillies and curry leaves. Add the shallots and saute until brown.
Add the ginger garlic paste and tomatoes and cook until mushy.
Add red chili powder, salt and the chicken and cook for 5 to 7 mins on a medium flame.
Finish with the finely chopped curry leaves and grated coconut.

title: Coconut Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 10 mins.
Add 2 ½ Cups of water, soaked rice in a Pressure Cooker and cook for 10 mins. Open the pressure cooker once the pressure settles on its own. Keep the cooked rice aside.
Heat coconut oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, and let the mustard seeds splutter. Add cashew nuts and fry till it turns golden brown.
Add green chili, dried red chili, curry leaves, ginger, and saute for a minute.
Add the grated coconut, asafoetida, ¾ tsp of salt and mix well.
Add the cooked rice and saute it for a minute on high flame. Remove from the heat and serve hot.

title: Palak Chicken
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken using all the ingredients for the marination. Allow it to marinate for 15 minutes at least. You can prepare the gravy in the meantime.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the sugar and vinegar. Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes. Remove the spinach into a bowl of ice cold water.
Grind it into a smooth paste without adding any water.
Heat oil in a pan. Add the whole spices followed by the garlic. Saute lightly and then add the onion and green chilli. Saute until light golden brown.
Add half of the Palak paste and saute on high heat until the excess moisture evaporates.
Add the marinated chicken and mix. Cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining Palak paste and salt. Cover and cook for 5 more minutes.
Add garam masala powder, kasuri methi powder, ghee, grated nutmeg and cream. Mix well and turn off the heat as soon as it comes to a simmer. Serve hot with rice/roti/naan.

title: Noodle Soup
cooking_instructions: Heat a Wok or a Kadai until it is very hot. Then add in oil, and add in the finely chopped ginger, garlic and green chillies. Saute until they start to change colour.
Add in the finely chopped cabbage, beans, coriander stems and the carrot. Add 1 tsp of salt. Cook for 2 minutes or until the vegetables have softened.
Add soy sauce, chilli sauce and White Pepper powder. Mix well and add in the vegetable stock, vinegar and sugar. Taste and add salt, if needed.
Add the noodles and cook until tender.
Make a paste of 1 tbsp of cornflour with some water. Add it to the soup and continue cooking it till it thickens to the desired consistency. (if needed)
Add the spring onion, fresh basil leaves and turn off the heat. Serve in a bowl and garnish with spring onions.

title: Mint Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 10 mins.
In a mixer grinder, add mint leaves, coriander leaves, garlic, ginger, green chilli, water and grind it into a thick paste.
In a pressure cooker, add 2 ½ cups of water, soaked rice and pressure cook it for 10 mins.
Heat oil in a kadai, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds and let it splutter. Add urad dal, cashew, dried red chilli, curry leaves and saute till the cashews turn golden brown.
Add the onion and saute till it gets translucent. Add the ground paste, salt and saute for 4 mins.
Add the cooked rice, mix well and remove from heat. Serve hot with potato fry/onion raita.

title: Masala Pav
cooking_instructions: Using a mortar & pestle or a mixer, make a coarse paste out of the chilli, ginger and garlic.
Heat butter in a pan and add the cumin seeds. Add the onion and the prepared paste. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the capsicum and saute for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, salt, red chilli powder and Pav bhaji masala. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add water and mix well. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mash lightly if the mixture is very lumpy. Reduce it until it turns thick. Remove the mixture into a bowl.
Cut a pav in half almost all the way through, but not completely. In the same pan, melt butter and toast the pav lightly.
Spoon the prepared masala onto the Pav.
Serve garnished with cheese, onion, coriander and lemon wedges.

title: Rasgulla Makhni
cooking_instructions: Bring the milk to a simmer and switch off the flame. Add the diluted vinegar a little at a time and stir constantly until the milk splits.
Add cold water to bring down the temperature. Drain using a cheesecloth and wash with cold water. Squeeze out some of the excess liquid and allow it to sit for 10-15 mins.
Transfer to a plate and knead the chenna until smooth in texture. Portion into small roundels.
Cook them in boiling water for 3 mins on high and 10 mins on a medium flame.
Allow them to sit covered for another 10-15 mins and then transfer to cold water.
To make the gravy, pressure cook the onion, tomato, ginger, garlic, cashew, dry kashmiri red chillies with some water for 4-5 whistles.
Allow it to cool down and blend to a fine paste. Strain the mixture.
To prepare the gravy, heat ghee, add the cardamom and add the red chilli powder followed by the strained gravy. Add the salt, sugar and garam masala. Allow the gravy to come to a boil.
Add the milk. Cover and simmer for 5-10 mins.
Finish the gravy with fresh cream, butter and kasuri methi.
Add the cooked rasgullas into the gravy and simmer further for 5 mins.

title: Tomato Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 10 mins.
In a Pressure Cooker, add water, soaked rice, and pressure cook it for 10 mins.
Heat ghee in a Kadai, add mustard seeds and let it splutter.
Add split urad dal, chana dal, and saute for a minute.
Add fennel seeds, green chili, curry leaves, ginger-garlic paste, onion, and saute till it turns translucent.
Add tomato and saute for 2 mins.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, kashmiri red chilli powder, asafoetida, salt, and saute till the masalas get cooked.
Add the cooked rice and mix well without breaking the rice.
Add coriander leaves, mix and remove from the heat. Serve hot with onion raita/appalam.

title: Onion Rings
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, combine the maida, cornstarch, baking soda, chilli powder, salt and ginger-garlic paste together. Add a little soda water at a time, and keep whisking until a thick batter is formed. Make sure there are no lumps.
Dip the onion rings in the batter and then coat them in the breadcrumbs individually.
Deep fry in oil until they turn golden brown and crisp.

title: Mor Kuzhambu
cooking_instructions: Soak the toor dal, raw rice, cumin seeds, coriander seeds in 6 tbsp of water for 15 mins.
Beat the curd into a smooth texture without any lumps.
In a mixer grinder, add the soaked ingredients along with the water, grated coconut, Green Chilli and grind it into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a kadai, add lady finger, curry leaves, and saute for 3 mins.
Add turmeric powder, water, ground paste, curd, salt, and simmer for 5 mins.
Heat oil in another pan, add mustard seeds, and let it splutter.
Add dried red chili, curry leaves, a pinch of asafoetida, and add this tempering to the curry.
Serve it hot with steamed rice.

title: Onion Sambar
cooking_instructions: Soak the tamarind by adding 1 Cup of water for 15 mins.
Wash the Toor dal.
In a pressure cooker, add the washed Toor dal, tomato, green chili, turmeric powder, salt, 3 cups of water, and pressure cook it for 7 whistles.
Heat a pan, add coriander seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal, chana dal, Fenugreek seeds, dried red chili, and dry roast them.
Once cool, add them to the mixer grinder and grind it into a fine powder.
Extract juice from the soaked tamarind. Keep aside.
In a Kadai, add ghee, mustard seeds, curry leaves, dried red chili, and let it splutter.
Add shallots and saute till it gets translucent.
Add the ground masala powder, extracted tamarind juice, asafoetida, and simmer for 2 mins.
Add the cooked Toor dal, 1 Cup of water, ¼ tsp of salt, and cook for 12 mins.
Add jaggery, coriander leaves, and mix well.
Onion Sambar is ready to be served with steamed rice.

title: Chicken Badami Shorba
cooking_instructions: Heat a saucepan, bring 1 cup of water to a boil.
Add the almonds and cook them for 1 minute. Remove from the heat.
Drain the almonds immediately and rinse them with cold water.
Peel the almond skin. Grind the Almonds with ¼ cup of water into a smooth paste.

In a pan, add the chicken, 2 ½ cups of water, ¾ tsp of salt, cover, and cook it for 3 mins. Remove the foam from the chicken stock to remove the impurities. Remove from the heat and transfer it to a bowl along with the chicken stock water.
Heat butter in a pan, add garlic, and saute for a minute.
Add maida and mix well without any lumps for a few seconds.
Add the ground almond paste and saute till the water is absorbed.
Add the cooked chicken along with the stock, cover, and simmer this for 6 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and simmer for 2 more minutes. Add black pepper powder, coriander leaves and mix well.
Remove from the heat and serve.

title: Spicy Masala Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 mins. Cook the basmati rice until 90% done and set aside to cool on a plate.
Saute the vegetables in white butter/ ghee and salt until tender. Set aside.
For the masala, in the same pan saute the given ingredients and blend to a masala.
Prepare the tempering in ghee, by adding the given ingredients in a sequence.
Add the rice to the tempering, followed by the vegetables, the masala, and salt. Mix to combine well.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and chopped coriander leaves.

title: Milagu Kashayam
cooking_instructions: Add the black peppercorns in a pan and dry roast it till it sputters. Using a mortar and pestle broke the roasted the black peppercorns into small pieces.
In a saucepan, add 2 cups of water. Add the broken black peppercorns, tulsi, Palm sugar and mix well. Simmer for 15 mins on medium flame.
Strain the kashayam using a strainer. Kashayam is ready and it is useful in treating indigestion, cough and common cold.

title: Vegetarian Omelette
cooking_instructions: Combine the gram flour, salt, pepper, baking powder and maida into a thin batter with water. The batter should be thin and runny.
Add the onions, green chilies, and chopped coriander leaves.
Heat a non-stick pan and grease it with butter. Pour a ladle full of the batter and swirl it around the pan, add some chopped tomatoes and grated cheese as well.
Allow it to cook covered for a minute on a simmer and fold in half.
Serve the soft and fluffy eggless omelets plain or with ketchup.

title: Kori Gassi
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and roast the chilies on low flame until they turn crisp. Remove it onto a plate.
Add coriander seeds, fennel seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds and clove to the pan. Roast until it turns aromatic. Remove it from the pan.
Pour more oil into the pan. Add onion and garlic, saute until translucent. Add the coconut and saute until it turns golden brown.
Grind all the roasted ingredients into a smooth paste, adding water as required.
Heat ghee in a pot and add curry leaves and onions. Saute until golden brown.
Add the tomatoes and saute until mushy. Add the chicken along with salt and turmeric powder. Saute on high heat for 2 minutes.
Add hot water and bring it to a boil. Cover and cook for 10 minutes on medium-low heat.
Add the prepared spice paste and cook for 10 minutes or until the chicken is completely cooked.
Add the tamarind water and stir. Add the coconut milk. Turn off the heat as soon as it comes to a simmer.

title: Sweet Samosa
