cooking_instructions: Crumble the maida with the salt and ghee until it resembles fine crumbs. Add water and knead a smooth dough.
Fry the cashew nuts a tbsp of ghee, add the poppy seeds and desiccated coconut. Roast until lightly browned and aromatic.
For the mixture, roast the soaked Bengal gram until lightly brown.
Combine the roasted ingredients and pulse blend until powdered. Add the sugar and cardamom powder and mix well.
Shape into roundels and roll out into discs. Cut these discs into semicircles and roll into cones and seal them.
Stuff the dough with the mixture and seal well.
Deep fry until golden brown in low-medium heat oil for about 8-10 mins

title: Instant Rava Idly
cooking_instructions: Heat oil and splutter the mustard seeds. Add the asafoetida, chana dal and urad dal and allow them to roast well.
Add the cashew to the pan. Add the curry leaves, chopped ginger, and green chilli and saute well.
Add the rava and roast the mixture on a low flame for 5 mins. Allow the mixture to cool down.
Add the salt, curd, water and baking soda and chopped coriander leaves. Whisk to combine well. Rest the batter for 15-20 mins.
Adjust the consistency with a little over ¼ Cup of water to make a thick but flowing batter.
Grease an idly mold and add the batter.
Steam the idlis for 10-12 mins.
Cool for a minute or two, De-mold with a spoon, and serve hot.

title: Meen Pollichathu
cooking_instructions: Mix all the ingredients for the marination into a smooth paste.
Make slits on the fish. Apply the spice paste generously over the fish.

Heat coconut oil and fry the fish on medium-high heat until it turns slightly crisp on the outside. It does not have to be fully cooked at this stage. The time would vary depending on the size of the fish. Set aside the fish.
Heat oil in another pan. Add the shallots, ginger, garlic, curry leaves, and green chili. Saute until the shallots turn translucent.
Add all the spice powders and salt. Add the tomatoes and saute until it turns mushy.
Add the coconut milk and vinegar. Saute just until it turns into a thick paste. Set aside.
Heat the banana leaf over a direct flame to make it flexible and to prevent tearing.

Add some finely chopped garlic and curry leaves to the banana leaf. Spoon some of the prepared masalas onto the center of the banana leaf. Place the fish on it and then cover it again with more masala. Fold in the sides of the leaf and tie it tightly using a banana fiber/kitchen twine.
Heat oil in a pan/tawa and cook the fish, covered, on low heat for 4-5 minutes on each side.

title: Chicken Popcorn
cooking_instructions: Cut the boneless chicken into bite-size chunks.
In a bowl, whisk the curd and then add 1 tsp of salt and ½ tsp of pepper.
Add chicken to this curd mixture and marinate for 60 mins.
In another bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, pepper powder, red chilli powder, onion powder, garlic powder, oregano.
Take a piece of marinated chicken, coat it with flour mixture and deep fry it in hot oil for 3-5 mins. And serve it hot

title: Bhuna Gosht
cooking_instructions: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker and add all the whole spices. Add the sliced onions and saute until golden brown.
Add the mutton pieces and saute for 4 minutes on high heat, or until all the pieces get decent brown color.
Add ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, Kashmiri chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, salt, and water. Cover and pressure cook for 20 minutes.
Once done, transfer the mutton to a wider pan/kadai. Stir continuously until it starts to thicken.
Add garam masala powder, curd, and green chili. Saute until the excess liquid is completely evaporated.
Sprinkle coriander leaves, mix well and serve!

title: Paneer Tikka Masala
cooking_instructions: Mix the mustard oil and red chilli powder together first to enhance the colour. Add all the other ingredients for the marination. Add the paneer and the vegetables and mix gently.
Place the hot charcoal (in a metal bowl) in the bowl of paneer. Add oil, cover and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Arrange the paneer on wooden skewers, alternating with onion, capsicum and tomato.
Cook the paneer skewers by searing them directly over the flame, until they are slightly charred on all sides. Brush with melted butter and set aside.
In a pan, heat oil and add the onion. Saute until the onion turns golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder and coriander powder, and saute.
Add tomato puree, salt and sugar. Cook until the oil floats on top (5 to 7 minutes) and the mixture has thickened slightly. The raw taste of the tomato should have disappeared by this stage.
Add water and bring it to a simmer. Add in cream, garam masala powder and kasuri methi. Mix well and bring it to a simmer.
Finish with coriander leaves and cold butter to give the gravy a velvety finish. Serve along with the paneer tikka. You could also mix the paneer and gravy together while adding the cream.

title: Prawn & Coconut Patties
cooking_instructions: Grind the prawns, coconut, shallots, ginger, garlic, green chilli, fennel seeds, salt and curry leaves into a coarse paste.
Add it into a bowl and mix with turmeric powder, black pepper powder and garam masala.
Shape it into patties. Shallow fry in oil for around 3 minutes, or until golden brown on both sides.

title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Tart
cooking_instructions: Mix the maida and the powdered sugar together. Add the cold butter cubes into the flour and blend it in using a fork to break down the butter pieces.
Add the cold water a few drops at a time and mix them gently to form a rough dough. Take care not to knead too much as this will make the tart shell chewy.
Cover and refrigerate the dough for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out and line it onto the tart pan evenly. Trim off the edges.
Prick with a fork and refrigerate again for 15 minutes.

In the meantime, prepare the fillings. Add the chocolate and cream into a heatproof bowl. Place the bowl over a pot of lightly simmering water. Keep mixing until the chocolate melts. You can also do this by microwaving it for 45 seconds instead, adding more time if needed.
Melt the peanut butter using the same method used for melting the chocolate ganache.
Lay a sheet of aluminium foil on the tart base. Add rice or any type of dried beans such as rajma to add weight on top. Bake at 180°c for 20 minutes.
Remove the beans and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown.
Pour the chocolate ganache into the tart shell. Freeze for a few minutes to slightly it.
Once it has set slightly, add the melted peanut butter on top.
Arrange the roasted peanuts on top.
Melt the chocolate and pour it onto a sheet of butter paper or good quality flexible plastic such as an OHP sheet.
Once it starts to set, cut it out into a circle that is the size of the tart pan. Place this over the peanuts on the tart.

Melt it using a hair dryer or a heat gun. Alternatively, you can place this in the oven for a couple of minutes just until the chocolate melts slightly. Refrigerate and serve chilled. Slice into portions using a knife dipped in warm water. This gives clean cuts.

title: Prawn Thoran
cooking_instructions: Add all the ingredients for the coconut mixture in a mixer jar. Pulse it briefly to lightly crush the coconut mix.
Heat oil in a pan and crackle the mustard seeds. Add the dried red chillies, curry leaves and shallots. Saute until the shallots turn translucent.
Add the prawns and salt, and mix. Add the coconut mixture on top. Without stirring, cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Open the lid and stir for a further 2 minutes. Prawn thoran is ready to serve! It is best eaten with rice.

title: Poricha Parotta
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl, add maida, salt, sugar and water. Combine the flour and mix it to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 15 minutes by continuously folding the dough.
Add 1 tbsp of oil on dough and rest for 60 minutes.
Make individual 2-inch dough balls.
Add 2 tbsp of oil on the dough balls and rest for 30 minutes.
Method 1: Take a dough ball and flatten as thin as possible by swirling it in a circular motion and forming a large circle. Apply oil on the spread dough.
Gather rolled dough in one corner and make a spiral. Repeat for all the dough balls.
Method 2: Flatten the dough ball using a rolling pin as thin as you can.
Apply oil on the dough and gather the rolled dough in one corner and make a spiral
Roll the spiralled dough using a pin or flatten it into a 3-4 inch circle using hands.
Heat a Tawa, place the flattened parotta on the Tawa. Cook on a medium flame until the parotta is half cooked on both sides.
In another shallow pan, add oil for half an inch height. Once the oil is hot, add the half cooked parotta and cook until golden brown and crispy. Flip inbetween. Repeat this for all the Parotta.
Tap the sides of the parotta to fluff them up when serving.

title: Chilli Parotta
cooking_instructions: Heat oil and fry the parotta until it starts to get crisp. Remove it from the pan.
In the same pan, add oil and then ginger, garlic, green chilli and curry leaves. Add the onion and saute until it turns translucent.
Add the Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, salt and tomatoes. Saute for 1 minute or until the raw smell of the spices disappears.
Add the diced onion and capsicum. Toss on high flame for 1 minute. Add the tomato ketchup and red chilli sauce. Mix well.
Add the fried parotta and saute for 1 minute.
Finish with fennel powder and coriander leaves. Serve hot!

title: Chicken Quesadilla
cooking_instructions: To make the tortilla, combine the flour, salt and baking powder together. Add the butter and mix it into the flour.
Add the warm water a little at a time. Knead it for approximately 5-10 minutes or until you get a smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Cut the chicken into half to make two thinner pieces. Add lemon juice and olive oil to them.
Combine all the ingredients for the spice mix together. Add the spice mix and coat the chicken completely.
Add oil to a pan and cook the chicken over medium heat for 8-10 minutes or until completely cooked.
Remove the chicken from the pan and add onion, garlic and capsicum. Season with salt and saute on high heat for 3 minutes.
Cut the cooked chicken into cubes and set aside.
After the dough is rested, knead again for 1 minute. Divide the dough into 4 portions. Roll out each portion into a very thin disc.
Cook over medium heat until golden spots begin to appear on both sides. Keep the tortillas covered in a cloth.
To assemble the quesadillas, spread cheese on the tortilla. Spread some of the onion mixture and the chicken on one half. Fold the tortilla in half.
In a pan, heat the oil and pan fry the quesadillas on medium heat until they turn crisp and the cheese has melted.

title: Achappam
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the raw rice for at least 4 hours. You can also soak it overnight. Strain the rice and spread it on a thick cloth. Allow it to dry for 30 minutes.
Grind it into a fine powder.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl. Add coconut milk, sugar and salt.
Add maida and beat until there are no lumps.
Add the rice flour a little at a time until completely mixed in. Add the black sesame seeds.
Heat oil in a Kadai along with the metal mould. The mould should be heated properly.

Dip the heated mould in the batter almost all the way through. It should not be dipped completely. Place the mould in the oil and shake it quickly to release the batter. Deep fry until it turns golden brown. Store it in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks.

title: Rava Pongal
cooking_instructions: Add the Moong Dal to a cooker with water and cook for 4 whistles.
Allow the steam to release and mash the dal and set aside.
In a kadai, heat ghee and add the cumin seeds. Saute until aromatic and add the cashew nuts. Allow them to turn golden brown.
Add the curry leaves,ginger, peppercorns and hing. Mix well and add the water. Allow the water to come to a boil. Season with salt.
Add the rava in portions and mix well in between each addition to prevent lumps.
Once all the rava has been mixed in, add the mashed dal and mix well.
Once it thickens, take off the heat and serve warm.

title: Flourless Peanut Butter Cookies
cooking_instructions: Preheat an oven to 200 C.
Mix together all the ingredients until smooth. Refrigerate the cookie dough for 20 mins.
Place spoon fulls of cookie dough on a tray lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 20 mins or until the edges are golden.
Cool completely before serving.

title: Avocado Strawberry Smoothie
cooking_instructions: Combine the ingredients in a mixer grinder and blend until smooth and thick.
Garnish the beverage with strawberries and mint sprigs.

title: Besan Ladoo
cooking_instructions: Heat a kadai, add the besan flour and dry roast it on a low flame till it loses the raw flavour.
Add the ghee and keep mixing till it becomes a paste-like consistency. Mix it for a little longer till it becomes thick. Make sure the besan flour loses its raw flavour by now.
Add the powdered sugar and keep mixing it till it mixed evenly and the mixture becomes almost crumbly but a little moist.
Add the cardamom powder and mix it till it combines evenly.
Let the mixture cool down completely. Divide the mixture and shape it into spheres. Garnish it with a piece of fried cashew nut and serve.

title: Jeera Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 15 mins.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, add bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cumin seeds, green chilli and saute well.
Add 1 ½ cups of water and salt.
Add the soaked basmati rice and mix well.
Pressure cook for a whistle. Let the pressure settle on its own and open the pressure cooker. Serve it hot.

title: Egg Soya Curry
cooking_instructions: Soak the soya chunks in hot water for 10 mins.
Heat oil in another pan, add mustard seeds, and let it splutter.
Add green chili, curry leaves, tomato, and saute for 2 mins. Add grated coconut and saute for a minute.
Once cool, add the above to a mixer grinder and grind it into a smooth paste by adding ¼ cup of water.
Drain the soya chunks using a strainer and squeeze out all the water from the soya chunks.
In a mixing bowl, add the drained soya chunks, turmeric powder, red chili powder, salt, besan flour, and mix well.
Heat oil in a pan, add the spice mixed soya chunks, and shallow fry for 6 mins. Remove from the pan and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a Kadai, add cumin seeds, onion, and saute till it gets translucent.
Add the ground masala paste and cook for 2 mins.
Add the eggs in the center of the gravy and mix till the eggs get crumbled.
Add a pinch of turmeric powder, ½ tsp of salt, and mix well.
Add fried soya chunks, 2 cups of water, cover, and simmer for 5 mins.
Add black pepper powder, coriander leaves, and mix. Serve hot with chapati/roti/rice.

title: Thenkuzhal Murukku
cooking_instructions: In a pan, dry roast urad dal. Blend it to a fine powder.
Add it to a bowl with rice flour.
Add ajwain, Cumin seeds, salt and butter and mix it with your hands till it forms a coarse texture. (when you hold the mixture tightly, it should bind together.)
Add water and mix it well till it forms a dough-like consistency.
Grease the murukku maker with oil, add the dough into it. Press it on parchment paper gently.
Heat oil in a kadai, gently drop the murukku into the oil and fry till it becomes crispy.
Take it off the kadai, drain the oil and serve.

title: Spicy Chicken Fry
cooking_instructions: Add the Cashews in a mixer grinder and grind it into a fine powder.
Add all the ingredients under “To grind” in a mixer grinder and grind it into a smooth paste.
In a mixing bowl, add chicken, ghee, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala powder, salt, lemon juice, coriander leaves, ground paste, mix well, and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add curry leaves, green chili, and saute for a minute.
Add the marinated chicken to the pan. Saute for a minute, mix well. Cover and cook this on a medium flame until the chicken is cooked. It would take around 5 to 6 mins.
Turn on high flame, continue to cook the chicken for 5 mins.
Add black pepper powder, ground cashew nut powder, mix well and roast the chicken for 5 mins on high flame. Add coriander leaves and remove them from the heat.

title: Honey Lemon Chicken
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken with a mixture of salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika powder.
Coat each piece of chicken in Maida.
Heat oil in a pan and sear the chicken on high heat until golden brown on both sides. Remove the chicken from the pan.
Add water into the same pan and bring it to a simmer. Add grated garlic, soy sauce, and honey. Mix well to combine.
Add butter and lemon juice. Turn off the heat and stir to combine.
Place the chicken in a pan or an oven safe tray and add the sauce on top of the chicken. Arrange the lemon slices on the chicken pieces.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°c for 20 minutes or until the sauce has thickened slightly. Spoon the sauce over the chicken pieces. Serve with herb garlic rice.

title: Iruttu-Kadai Tirunelveli Halwa
cooking_instructions: Wash the whole wheat and soak for 8 hours/overnight.
Add it to a mixer jar with plenty of water. Grind it. Use a fine strainer to strain the wheat milk.
Repeat the extraction process 2 or 3 more times until the extract isn’t white anymore.
Leave it out at room temperature for 3 hours.
The milk will separate and there will be a thin liquid floating on top. Using a ladle, gently remove most of this liquid without disturbing the bottom thick layer.
Add 1 litre of water to the remaining mixture and mix well.
Add this to a heavy-bottom pot. Cook on medium heat until it starts to thicken, around 15 minutes. Keep stirring it continuously, or there might be lumps.
Add the sugar. Stir and turn the flame to low, while we prepare the caramel.

To prepare the caramel, add the sugar to a small pan. On medium-low heat, allow the sugar to melt while stirring regularly. Keep cooking until it changes to a rich golden colour. Immediately transfer it to the wheat mixture. Take care not to overcook it as it can leave a very unpleasant bitter taste.
Mix the caramel and the wheat mixture together immediately. Continue cooking until the mixture turns thick, but falls off the ladle smoothly.
Add the ghee in 5 stages gradually. Add part of the ghee first and mix it until the ghee is completely absorbed.
Repeat the step with the next batch of ghee, until all the ghee is used up. Turn off the heat.

To check the consistency, allow some of the Halwa to cool down slightly. If you touch it using your hand, the Halwa should not stick. Garnish it with fried cashew nuts. Serve it warm or at room temperature.

title: Dahi Bhindi
cooking_instructions: Whisk together the curd and gram flour until smooth and without any lumps, mix and combine the water.
Fry the cut bhindi until cooked and tender, drain, and set aside.
For the gravy, heat oil and add the ajwain followed by the onions. Saute them until golden and add the ginger garlic paste.
Once no longer raw in aroma, add the tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add the powdered spices, salt, and sugar and mix well.
Add water and mix, then the curd mixture and whisk continuously to prevent the formation of lumps. Allow the gravy the simmer for 5 mins and the raw flavor to go while stirring often.
Finish by adding the fried bhindi, garam masala, Kasuri methi, and ghee.

title: Maggi Bhel
cooking_instructions: Use your hand to crush the maggi into small pieces.
Dry roast the coarsely crushed maggi on a medium flame for 2 minutes. And let them cool completely.
In a bowl, add maggi masala powder and tomato ketchup. Mix it well.
Add onion, tomato, green chilli, roasted peanut, roasted maggi, salt and red chilli powder. Mix it well.
Add lemon juice, coriander leaves and mix well. And serve the maggi bhel with coffee/tea, garnishing it with more coriander leaves.

title: Makai Gosht
cooking_instructions: Blend the onion, ginger, and garlic into a fine paste.
Heat ghee in a kadhai and add the whole spices, saute until aromatic. Add the mutton and cook until all the liquid has evaporated, stirring often.
Add the salt and garam masala. Add the onion paste and cook on a medium flame until no longer raw in the aroma.
Add the green chillies and the powdered spices. Saute until the oil starts to separate and the masalas are cooked.
Simmer the flame, add the corn kernels, the whisked curd, salt, cashew nut paste, and water just enough to cover the meat level. Mix well to combine.
Simmer covered until thickened slightly and the meat is tender for about 40 mins.
Finish with garam masala, ghee, fresh cream, chopped coriander, and ginger julienne.

title: Dosa Batter
cooking_instructions: Add the rice, urad dal, and fenugreek seeds to a bowl. Wash it thrice and soak for 4 hours.
Grind it into a slightly coarse batter using a mixer/stone grinder. Add a little water only if required.
Mix using your hands. Cover it and allow it to rise at room temperature for 8 hours or overnight.
Add the salt and mix gently. Add water if required to form a smooth, flowing batter. Dosa batter is ready!

title: Thattai
cooking_instructions: Combine the ingredients in a bowl and incorporate the butter to get a crumbly texture.
Add curry leaves and chana dal. Add water a little at a time to get a smooth and firm dough.
Spread a dry, clean cloth. Dive the dough into roundels and pat each roundel with greased hands to form a disc, not too thin.
Deep fry in medium hot oil until crispy and brown.

title: Kung Pao Paneer
cooking_instructions: Combine the ingredients for the marination and add the paneer in it. Set aside until the sauce is ready.
For the sauce: combine the brown sugar, soya sauce, water and vinegar in a bowl.
Heat oil and add the red chillies, chopped ginger and garlic and spring onion whites. Saute for a minute.
Add the prepared sauce mixture. Boil until reduced and add ½ Cup of water.
Once it has boiled add the paneer and reduce the sauce to a coating consistency and add the roasted peanuts and spring onion greens.

title: Black Pepper Chicken Leg
cooking_instructions: Slit the chicken drumstick pieces on the sides.
Add egg, cornflour and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken pieces.
Deep fry the chicken pieces in hot oil for 10 minutes or until cooked through. Set this aside.
In a mixer grinder, pulse grind the red chillies and black peppercorns into a coarse mixture.
In a hot wok/kadai, add oil and once the oil is hot add ginger, garlic and cook until the ginger and garlic turn golden brown.
Add finely chopped onion and cook until the onions turn golden brown.
Add soy sauce, vinegar and salt. Mix well and add some water.
Add the fried chicken drumstick pieces and the ground chilli and pepper mix.
Toss until the pepper sauce coats the chicken pieces. Add spring onions and remove from the heat. Transfer it to a plate, garnish it with chopped spring onions. Serve it hot.

title: Parsi Mutton Dhansak
cooking_instructions: Soak all the 3 dals in water for 3 hours or even overnight.
Add all the ingredients for the dal mixture in a pressure cooker. Cook on high flame for 1 whistle, then reduce the flame and cook for a further 4 whistles.
In a pan on low flame, saute all the spices until fragrant.
Turn off the flame and add green chili, coriander leaves, and water and grind to a fine paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add the sliced onions along with salt. Saute until the onions turn golden brown. Add the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the mutton pieces and cook for 5 minutes.
Add water, cover, and cook for 30 minutes on low heat until the mutton is completely cooked through. Cook for longer if necessary.
Add the cooked dal and the previously prepared Dhansak masala to the mutton.
Adjust the consistency with ¾ cup of water or up to the desired consistency. Allow it to cook for 5 minutes. Serve with Parsi brown rice.

title: Pesarattu Upma
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the dal for 3 hours.
Grind to a fine thick batter with ginger, coriander leaves, and green chilies adding water a little at a time, about 100 ml.
Transfer to a bowl and add the onions.
Add oil and splutter the mustard seeds, add the urad dal, curry leaves, asafoetida, green chilies, and ginger and saute for 2 minutes. Add the onions and cook until translucent.
Add the rava, salt and water. Cook until it leaves the sides of the pan. About 5-7 minutes. Finish with a tsp of ghee.
To make the pesarattu, heat a skillet over medium flame, spread the pesarattu batter thin like a dosa, allow it to cook on both sides.
Spread the upma and allow it to cook for 3 minutes or until brown and crispy. Fold in half and serve.

title: Ribbon Pakoda
cooking_instructions: In a mixie, blend the roasted gram to a fine powder along with the powdered spices, garlic and salt until it gets completely combined.
Sieve and add the dry ingredients in a bowl and combine well. Add and mix the sesame seeds.
Add hot oil into the dry flour and combine followed by water.
Combine and mix the dough well to get a soft dough. Rest the dough for 10 mins, covered.
Grease the mold and fill with the dough to 3/4th the height.
Heat oil in a kadhai and squeeze into the hot oil on a high flame and fry until crispy.
Cool down completely and break into pieces. Store airtight for 7-10 days.

title: Paal Khova
cooking_instructions: Bring the milk to a boil, switch off the flame and split the milk using diluted vinegar, a little at a time. The moment it splits, stop the process.
Filter the solids and wash it. Set it aside.
In a pan, combine the milk solids, fresh cream on a medium flame. Add ghee and mix to combine. Add cardamom powder to flavour the dish. Cook for 5 mins.
Add the sugar and mix well to melt and then add the condensed milk.
Cover the pan and cook on low flame for 10 mins, open occasionally and stir to prevent it from burning. Once the mixture is thick, keep the pan open and cook until thick.
Finish with ghee and mix well. Transfer to a bowl and allow it to cool. Garnish with chopped nuts, as needed. Can be stored refrigerated for upto a week.

title: Raw Mango Rice
cooking_instructions: Soak the rice for 15 minutes and cook in a pressure cooker with 2 ½ cups of water and ½ tsp salt, for 1 whistle. Allow the rice to cool after cooking

In a pan, add the dried red chillies, fenugreek seeds and peanuts. Toast them on low heat for 2 minutes. Add white sesame seeds, cumin seeds and asafoetida to the pan and toast on low heat for 1 minute. Add the grated coconut and toast until the coconut turns golden brown. Allow the mixture to cool and grind into a coarse powder.
Grate the raw mango with the skin on

Heat oil in a pan and crackle mustard seeds. Add the urad dal, chana dal and curry leaves. Add the chopped green chillies, ¾ tsp salt and the grated raw mango. Let it cook for 5 minutes until the mango has softened

Add the previously prepared powder and mix it. Cook it for a further 3 minutes until the raw taste has completely disappeared. Add ½ cup of water and mix well. Cook for 2 more minutes. Add the jaggery, mix and turn off the heat
Add the rice and mix well to combine. Taste and adjust salt as per taste

title: Pori Urundai
cooking_instructions: Dry roast the puffed rice for 2-3 mins and cool down completely.
Combine the jaggery and water in a pan. Allow it to melt and then it will start frothing, with the perfect colour and consistency. The ladle will leave trace marks in the pan. Reduce the flame.
Add the powdered spices and salt at this stage and mix well to combine. Add the puffed rice and combine well. Finish with ghee.
Dust your hands with rice flour/ maida and roll into roundels without applying too much pressure, roll only when warm.
Cool down completely and store airtight to maintain the crispness, upto 10 days.

title: Butter Murukku
cooking_instructions: In a pan, dry roast urad dal. Blend it to a fine powder.
Add it to a bowl with rice flour. Add ajwain, cumin seeds, salt and butter and mix it with your hands till it forms a coarse texture. (when you hold the mixture tightly, it should bind together.)
Add water and mix it well till it forms a dough-like consistency.
Grease the murukku maker with oil, add the dough into it.
Heat oil in a kadai, gently drop the murukku into the oil and fry till it becomes crispy.
Take it off the kadai, drain the oil and serve.

title: Rabdi
cooking_instructions: Bring the milk to a boil. Add the chopped nuts.

On medium heat, stir the milk regularly until it reduces to half of its original quantity, around 30-40 minutes. You can increase the flame to high if you are comfortable with stirring it vigorously. Keep scraping the sides at regular intervals, and adding them back into the milk.
Once the milk has reduced, add sugar, saffron and cardamom powder. Boil further until the mixture thickens, 5-10 minutes.
Once it has cooled slightly, transfer it into another dish. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or until chilled.
Once chilled, serve with a portion of the creamy top layer (malai). Optionally, garnish with more chopped nuts.

title: Kesar Doodh Peda
cooking_instructions: Add milk to a non-stick pan, keep stirring it on a medium flame and bring it to a boil.
Keep stirring the milk and scraping the residue of the sides of the pan once every few seconds till it becomes thick like rabdi.
Once it is thick like rabdi, keep stirring it continuously till it becomes thick like khoya. Add Saffron.
Add the sugar, keep sitting it till the sugar is completely dissolved. At this point the mixture will get a little loose. Keep stirring it continuously till it becomes thick again and holds shape.
At this point add the milk powder and mix it till it combines evenly and keep mixing it till its raw flavour is gone and the mixture holds shape.
Add the ghee and cardamom powder and mix it till it combines evenly

Transfer the mixture to a plate and let it cool down till it is hot enough to handle. And then apply a little ghee/oil on your palms, divide and roll the pedas into equal sized spheres and shape it in the mould. De-mould it, keep it on a plate. Garnish it with chopped pistachios and almonds and serve.

title: Somas
cooking_instructions: In the maida, add the rava, salt and hot ghee. Mix until crumbly in texture.
Add water and knead a firm dough, it will take 10 mins of kneading. Rest the dough for 15-20 mins, covered.
Dry roast the coconut until dry and set aside.
For the filling, heat ghee in a kadai and add chopped nuts and raisins. Fry until golden. Add and roast the rava in the same pan until aromatic. Add the roasted gram and cardamom, as well.
Switch off the flame and add sugar. Mix thoroughly.
Portion the dough into roundels and roll out thinly. Cut using a cutter to get perfect circles.
Place some mixture in the center and moisten the edges with water. Close and seal the dough well by pressing and then creating an impression with a fork.

Heat oil in a kadai and then reduce the flame, add them 1 at a time and flip and fry for 4-5 mins after which you can increase the flame to medium and fry until golden and crispy. Fry until the frying sizzling and bubbling subsides to ensure maximum texture.
Strain from the oil, cool completely and store air tight for upto a week.

title: Dry Gulab jamun
cooking_instructions: Add sugar, water and cardamom. Bring it to a boil and let it thicken a little.
In a bowl, grate khoya and paneer, add a tablespoon of milk. Knead it all together till it binds evenly. Add the 2nd spoon of milk if it does not bind evenly.
Divide and roll them into spheres.
Heat oil in a kadai, deep fry the kohya spheres in it till it turns golden brown. Keep it aside.
Transfer the fried jamun to the sugar syrup and let it soak for 25-30 minutes.
Take the jamun off the sugar syrup and drain it well.
Coarsely grind sugar and spread it on a plate.Roll the soaked jamun evenly on the sugar and serve.

title: Soya Chunk Pepper Fry
cooking_instructions: In a saucepan bring water to a boil, add salt, soya chunks and cook for 6 mins.
Drain the water using a strainer, squeeze the soya chunks using a spatula and keep the soya chunks aside.
In a pan, dry roast the spices mentioned under dry roast and grind. Using a mixer grinder, grind the dry roasted spices into a powder.
Heat oil in Kadai, add onion, and saute until the onions are translucent.
Add the green chili, ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell leaves.
Add curry leaves to the pan. Mix well.
Add the cooked and drained soya chunks. Mix well.
Add the ground spice powder to the pan. Mix well until the spice powder coats all the pieces of the soya chunks. Add salt and saute for 5 mins
Add lemon juice, chopped coriander leaves, mix well and remove from heat. Serve hot as an appetizer or as a side dish w10ith Rasam Rice.

title: Japanese Chicken Karaage
cooking_instructions: Cut the chicken thighs into approximately 2-inch pieces.
In a bowl, add all the ingredients for the marination and mix. Add the chicken and mix well to coat evenly. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
In another bowl/plate, season the cornstarch with salt and pepper.
Add the pieces of chicken into the cornstarch and coat them individually. Squeeze them lightly to make compact pieces and remove the excess starch.
Deep-fry them on medium-low heat just until they start to turn golden brown. Remove them from the oil and set them aside on a cooling tray/rack for 3-4 minutes.
Heat the oil again over high heat. Add the chicken back into the oil (in batches) and cook until crispy and golden brown. This will take around 1 minute. Serve with mayonnaise and lemon wedges.

title: Maharani Chicken
cooking_instructions: Grind the Green Chilli and Garlic into a coarse paste.
Mix the prepared Green Chilli and Garlic paste with the washed and cleaned Boneless Chicken Cubes.
To the Chicken mixture, add Salt, Cumin Powder, Chilli Powder, and Garam Masala.
Add the Egg, Corn Flour, and Maida to form a batter with the chicken cubes in it.
Heat Oil in a deep frying pan and deep fry the Chicken until the chicken is cooked, for about 5 mins. Set this aside.
In a pan, add Oil, Sliced Onions, Dried Red Chilli, and Curry Leaves, saute until the onions are translucent.

Add the deep-fried chicken cubes to the pan, mix well. Add Salt, Chicken Masala, Chilli Powder, Cumin Powder, Black Pepper Powder and toss until the spice powders are coated well on the chicken and the onions. Remove from the heat and serve as an appetizer.

title: Paneer Shawarma
cooking_instructions: Salt and powdered spices together make shawarma masala. To make the marinade for the paneer, mix the hung curd, lemon juice, garlic and onion paste, and shawarma masala. Add the paneer pieces and mix well. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Add the ingredinets for the mayonnaise and pulse blend until thick.
To make the hot sauce, boil together with the ingredients until the garlic is soft and mashable, minimum 20 mins.
Strain and blend with the remaining water as needed, until smooth. Strain the sauce, if needed.
Cook/ Reheat the pita bread and remove from heat and cover with a cloth.
Cook the paneer on a heated and greased grill pan or a Tawa/ roast over an open fire. Flip and cook until the paneer is cooked through and a bit charred.
Remove from heat and cut into long strips.
To assemble the shawarma, spread garlic mayonnaise on the Khubz/Pita. Place some of the paneers, along with the sliced onion, tomato, and hot sauce. Form into a roll, and serve hot!

title: Curry Leaf Rice
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds and coriander seeds followed by the dal.
Add the chillies and coconut and saute until golden. Add the curry leaves and saute until crisp.
Blend to a powder in a mixer grinder.
For the preparation: heat oil and add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add the curry leaves, thing, and peanuts.
Add the rice, curry leaf masala and salt. Mix well.

title: Tomato Pickle
cooking_instructions: In a pan add 2 tbsp oil, finely chopped tomatoes and saute it for 5 minutes. Add tamarind, turmeric powder and salt and cook for a further 5 minutes. Cool the mixture and grind it to a smooth paste.

In another pan, add 3 tbsp oil, mustard seeds, asafoetida, chopped garlic, chili powder, and the ground paste, water, and cook for a further 10 minutes adding 4 tbsp of oil. Adjust salt to taste at this point.
Add fenugreek powder and complete the cooking process. Store it in a ceramic or glass bowl and consume it whenever needed.

title: Maa Laddu
cooking_instructions: Blend the sugar along with the cardamom into a fine powder. Set aside.
Blend the fried gram into a fine powder. Add this to the powdered sugar. Sieve this mixture to remove any lumps.
Heat the ghee in a pan. Fry the cashew in ghee until it starts to change its colour. Add the hot ghee to the fried gram and sugar mixture.
Mix evenly with a spoon. Then mix using your hands. If you feel the mixture is too dry or not holding shape, add 1 tbsp of ghee and mix again.
Shape them into balls, approximately 1 inch in diameter. Serve immediately or store in an airtight container.

title: Palak Paratha
cooking_instructions: Add Spinach (Palak), green chili, garlic, ginger, water to a mixer grinder and grind it into a smooth paste.
In a mixing bowl, add wheat flour, salt and mix. Add the ground Spinach (Palak) paste and mix well. Add 1 tsp of water and knead it well till it becomes a soft dough.
Apply oil all over the dough, cover and rest it for 20 mins.
Make individual small dough balls. Take a dough ball, flatten it into a medium-thick circle.
Heat a Tawa, add some butter, place the flattened paratha on the Tawa. Cook on a medium flame for 2 mins and flip. Cook the other side for 2 mins.

title: Soya Dindigul Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins. Soak the soya chunks in water for 20 mins, squeeze and strain.
Combine the whole spices in a pan and dry roast them until aromatic, 3 minutes.
Transfer to a mixer grinder and make a powder. Add the ingredients for the masala to the same blender and blend without water until smooth.
Heat ghee in a pot, add the bay leaf and ginger garlic paste. Add the masala and saute well until aromatic and the raw smell goes, for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and the powdered spices. Saute for 2 mins until soft.
Add the curd and mix well. Drain, squeeze and add the soya chunks and potato and mix well.
Add lemon juice, 2.5 cups of water and salt to season. Bring it up to a boil.
Add the rice and cook until the level of rice and water are equal.
Turn down the heat, cover with foil and cook for 14 mins.
Open carefully and fluff up the rice with a fork.

title: Vegetable Raita
cooking_instructions: Toast the cumin seeds and crush them using a mortar and pestle.
In a bowl, add the curd, salt, toasted cumin powder and sugar. Whisk until it turns smooth.
Add all the other ingredients into the whisked curd. Mix until well combined.

title: Herb Rice
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins
In a pot, add plenty of water and bring it to a boil. Boil the rice until 90% done. Strain and set aside.
In a pan, heat butter and add the garlic. Saute until light brown. Add the bell pepper, red chilli flakes and dried mixed herbs.
Add the rice and salt and mix well.

title: Garlic Rasam
cooking_instructions: Combine the ingredients for the masala in a mixer grinder, pulse until coarse.
Heat ghee in a pot, add the mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add the urad dal, curry leaves, crushed garlic and hing. Saute for 2 mins.
Add the tomatoes and turmeric powder and cook until soft.
Add the salt, tamarind pulp made from 1 tbsp of tamarind and ½ cup of water and 2.5 cups of water and simmer for 6 mins
Finish with chopped coriander leaves.

title: No Oven Eggless Tutti Fruity Cake
cooking_instructions: Boil the milk and reduce it by 30% by boiling for approximately 12 mins, stirring constantly.
Add the sugar and cool the milk for 10 mins.
Add the custard powder, maida, tutti frutti, baking powder, vanilla essence and oil. Whisk to get a smooth and lump-free batter.
Pour the batter in a greased mold dusted with maida. Top with some more tutti-frutti.
Heat salt on high flame in a closed kadai.
Place the mold inside the kadai and cook covered for 45 mins on a low flame or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
De-mold, cool and cut into slices.

title: Masala Buttermilk
cooking_instructions: In a mixer grinder, add ginger, mint leaves, coriander leaves, green chilli, cumin seeds and grind it.
Add curd, salt, water, ice cubes and grind it without any lumps.
Filter the buttermilk using a strainer. Masala Buttermilk is ready to be served.

title: Vermicelli Veg Biryani
cooking_instructions: Dry roast the ingredients under “for biryani masala” for 2 mins.
Once cool, add them to a mixer grinder and grind it into a fine powder.
Heat 2 tbsp of ghee in a Kadai, add the bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon, cardamom, onion, green chilli and saute till it turns golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and saute well.
Add carrot, beans, potato, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, ground biryani masala powder, coriander powder, salt and saute till the masalas are cooked.
Add 1 Cup of water, mix, cover and cook for 10 mins on medium flame.
Add the mint leaves, coriander leaves, 2 tsp of ghee and mix well. Add 2 Cups of water and let it come to a boil.
Add the roasted vermicelli, mix Cover and cook for 8 mins on medium flame.
Serve the vermicelli veg biryani hot with onion raita.

title: Lemon Rice
cooking_instructions: In a pan, heat up gingelly oil and roast the peanuts on a medium flame for 1 minute. Remove them from the oil and set aside.

Add mustard seeds to the same pan. When the mustard seeds start to splutter, add the split urad dal, chana dal, dry red chilli and green chilli. Saute until the chana dal starts to turn golden brown. Add in the curry leaves, asafoetida, salt, and turmeric powder.
Add the cooked rice, lemon juice and sugar. Mix well. Taste and adjust the salt. Add the roasted peanuts and coriander leaves. Mix well and turn off the heat.

title: Mango Phirni
cooking_instructions: Wash and Soak basmati rice for 30 mins. Drain the rice using a strainer.
Add the soaked rice to a mixer grinder and grind it into a coarse consistency. The ground basmati rice should resemble Sooji(Rava).
In a mixer grinder add the mango and grind into smooth paste to extract the mango puree.
In a deep kadai, add milk and cook till it comes to a boil by stirring occasionally.
Add the ground rice mixture and cook till the milk is reduced into half and reaches the desired consistency.
Add sugar, saffron strands, cardamom powder, pista, mix well and simmer for 2 mins.
Add mango puree, mix well and remove from the heat.
Pour it in a serving bowl, once cool, refrigerate for an hour and serve.

title: Penne Alla Vodka
cooking_instructions: Bring a large pot of boiling water. Season with salt and add the pasta. Boil for 7-8 minutes or as per package instructions.
Reserve some of the water for use later in the sauce.
Strain the pasta, toss with oil, and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a pan. On medium heat, saute sliced garlic and red chili flakes until the garlic starts to brown slightly.
Add onion and saute until translucent. Add the vodka, stir well and allow it to evaporate.
Add the tomato puree, salt, sugar, paprika powder, and black pepper powder. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add the reserved pasta water and Italian herbs. Bring it to a simmer.
Add the fresh cream and stir. Add the pasta and the grated Mozzarella cheese. Stir well and serve!

title: Breakfast Tomato Kurma
cooking_instructions: In a mixer grinder, add grated coconut, ginger, garlic, green chilli, fennel seeds, mint leaves, water and grind it into a smooth paste. Keep aside.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cloves, cumin seeds, curry leaves, onion and saute until it turns translucent.
Add tomato, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, mix and cook until the tomatoes get mushy.
Add water, add the ground coconut paste and simmer for 10 mins.
Add coriander leaves and mix well. Remove from the heat and serve it with idli/dosa for breakfast.

title: Egg 65
cooking_instructions: Place the eggs on a saucepan, add 4 cups of water, bring the water to a boil, cover and cook the eggs for 9 minutes.
Once the eggs cool, remove the shells of the eggs and cut them into halves. Remove the egg yolks and fine chop the egg whites.
Add ginger garlic paste, curry leaves, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, black pepper powder, coriander powder, salt, besan flour, corn flour, lemon juice, egg white and mix well.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan, add small balls of the egg batter and fry until crispy. It would take around 4 mins. Remove from the heat.
Heat oil in a pan, add garlic, dried red chilli, curry leaves and saute for a minute. Add tomato sauce, a pinch of salt and mix well.
Add the deep fried egg balls, green chilli and toss on a high flame.
Add coriander leaves, mix well and remove from the heat. Serve hot as an appetizer.

title: Chettinad Fish Curry
cooking_instructions: Wash and Clean the fish pieces with lemon juice, salt and turmeric powder.
In a pan, heat Gingelly oil, add the Shallots and Garlic. Saute until the shallots turn translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until the tomatoes are mushy. Add the curry leaves. Add red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Cook for 2 mins.
Add the black peppercorns, cumin seeds and mix well. Add the grated coconut and continue to saute for 2 mins.
Add the tamarind and saute for a minute. Remove from heat and allow it to cool.
Transfer it to a mixer grinder jar. Add 1 Cup of water and grind it into a smooth paste.

In another Kadai, heat Gingelly oil. Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds and allow the spices to splutter. Add the curry leaves, dried red chilli, chopped shallots, sliced ginger and garlic cloves. Add ½ tsp of salt and saute until the onions turn golden brown.
Add the ground masala paste, 3 cups of water and simmer for 15 mins or until the oil separates from the curry.
Add the fish pieces and cook for 5 mins or until the fish is cooked.
Add chopped coriander leaves and remove them from the heat. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Andhra Mutton Fry
cooking_instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the mutton pieces, turmeric powder, salt, water, and pressure cook it for 15 mins.
In a mixer grinder add all the ingredients under “to grind” and grind it into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a Kadai, add curry leaves and fry until crispy. Add green chili, ground paste, cook for 5 mins.
Add red chili powder, Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala powder, salt, and saute for a minute.
Add the cooked mutton pieces along with the water, mix well and stir fry for 5 mins.
Add the lemon juice, coriander leaves and mix well. Remove from the heat and serve.

title: Egg Pepper Fry
cooking_instructions: To cook the eggs, cover the eggs with cold water in a saucepan and bring it to a boil. Cover and continue to cook for 9 minutes. Take the eggs out, wash in cold water and peel the skin. Cut the eggs into two and keep aside.
In a mixer grinder grind all the ingredients mentioned under grind into a smooth paste.
In another non-stick pan, heat groundnut oil and add the ground paste.
Continue to cook this for 3-5 minutes until the oil separates. Add curry leaves at this point.
Add the cut pieces of egg into this and continue roasting the eggs for 5 minutes. The masala should coat the egg.
Add coriander leaves and remove from the heat. Serve it as an appetizer or as a side dish with rice.

title: Plum Cake
cooking_instructions: Deseed and chop all the dry fruits and nuts. Grind the whole spices with a tablespoon of sugar.
Mix all the dry fruits, nuts, powdered spice, orange zest, and rum together and store it for 1 day to 20 days.
In a pan melt 2 tbsp of sugar, add a little water to it and add all the fruit mixture to it and cook it for 5 mins.
After cooking the mixture remove the pan off the flame and add 1 Cup of butter to it and let it cool until mixture reaches room temperature.
Powder 200-gram brown sugar in the mixer grinder. And in a separate bowl add eggs, powdered sugar and beat until fluffy, with the use of a hand mixer.
Add sieved flour, baking powder to the egg mixture and also the fruit mixture and mix well.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Add the mixture to the baking tray.
In the preheated oven, bake the cake for 40 mins at 170-degree celsius.

title: Prawn Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 30 mins.
Marinate the prawns using turmeric, chilli powder, salt, pepper powder and refrigerate it for 30 mins.
Heat a pan with oil, add the marinated prawns, saute it for 2 mins and remove it in a bowl.
In the same pan add all the whole spices followed by the sliced onions and saute it until dark golden brown.
Add sliced tomatoes, salt and whole green chillies to the pan and cook it until oil separates.
Add in all the dry masalas and ginger garlic paste, and continue to cook until the raw smell goes off. Add 3/4th of mint and coriander, followed by coconut milk.
Add the prawns and soaked rice. Pour in the water and adjust the seasoning at this point. Close the lid and let it cook for 15 mins.
Remove the lid add in the ghee, remaining mint and coriander and keep it for dum for 10 mins
Serve it hot with raita.

title: Madras Mutton Curry
cooking_instructions: Grind grated coconut with dry red chilli, ginger, garlic, black peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves, cumin seeds, poppy seeds and fennel seeds into a smooth paste, adding a little water.
Heat oil in a cooking pot, add the bay leaf, Chopped onions and fry until brown. Add the spice paste and fry for 15 mins over low heat, adding 2 tbsp of water in between.
Add the meat and saute for 5 mins over moderate heat.
Add Salt, Chilli powder and coriander powder.
Add tomatoes and saute for another 5 mins.
Add 4 Cups of water, cover and cook the curry for 45 mins, until the meat is well cooked and tender.
Add coconut milk, simmer for a few minutes. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice/roti/paratha.

title: Kashmiri Pulao
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins.
Soak the saffron in warm milk for 10 mins.
In a pot heat ghee and add the whole spices followed by the nuts and raisins. Fry until the nuts turn golden brown.
Add 2 cups of water and salt and sugar. Allow it to come to a boil.
Add the rice and let it come to a boil. Add the saffron milk. Once the level of water and rice is equal, cover and cook on a low flame for 12 mins.
Open, fluff the rice with a fork and add the pomegranate seeds and apple pieces.

title: Veg Kolhapuri
cooking_instructions: Cut the cauliflower into florets. Soak them in 1 cup of water along with ¼ of salt and ¼ tsp of turmeric powder. This is to clean the cauliflower properly. Let this sit for at least 10 minutes, and then discard the water.
For the masala paste, heat oil and add all the spices and the cashew nut. Cook on low flame for 3 minutes, or until the spices are aromatic.
Transfer to a blender jar and add two roughly cut tomatoes. Blend.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil and add carrot, beans and cauliflower. Saute for 4 minutes.
Add chopped capsicum and green peas, and saute for 2 more minutes.
Remove the vegetables from the oil.
In the same pan, add 2 tbsp more of oil. Then add whole red chillies and chopped onion and saute until golden brown.
Once the onion turns golden brown, add ginger garlic paste and all the spice powders. Cook for 1 minute. Add the masala paste and cook for 5 minutes on high flame, stirring continuously.
Add the cooked vegetables, add the water. Once it comes to a boil, turn the flame to low, cover with a lid and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with rice, roti or any Indian bread.

title: Dal Tadka
cooking_instructions: Wash the Masoor dal and the Moong dal twice. Soak them for at least 20 minutes. You can also soak them overnight.
In a pressure cooker, add the soaked lentils, salt, turmeric powder and water. Pressure cook for 3 whistles on a high flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

For the tadka, heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and dry Kashmiri red chillies. When the cumin starts to crackle, add the chopped ginger, garlic, onion and tomatoes. Cook them until the onions are translucent.
Add turmeric powder, chilli powder, coriander powder and Kasuri methi. Saute and cook for 1 minute.
Remove half the tadka into a bowl. This is for the tadka, that is to be added at the end.
Add the cooked dal to the pan. Mix well with the tadka. Allow the dal to simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped coriander leaves and lemon juice, mix and take off the stove.
Re-heat the reserved Tadka with the ghee, and pour it on top of the dal. Serve warm!

title: Chicken Thukpa
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and brown the chicken legs.
Add slit green chillies and chopped ginger, garlic and spring onion bulbs. Add the onion and carrot.
Season with salt and pepper. Add 650ml of water. Cover and boil for 5 mins.
Remove the chicken legs. Add soya sauce and honey. Add noodles to the broth, cover and simmer for 5 mins, until tender.
Finish with lemon juice, freshly chopped coriander and spring onion greens.
Shred the meat from the chicken legs.
Add the shredded chicken and noodles in a bowl while serving.

title: Malabar Prawn Curry
cooking_instructions: In a mixer grinder, grind the grated coconut and water. Pass it through a sieve to extract coconut milk.
In a bowl, soak the tamarind in ½ cup of warm water. Extract the tamarind juice from the tamarind.
In a Kadai, heat the coconut oil, add the mustard seeds and allow them to pop. Add the curry leaves. After a few seconds add the thinly sliced onions and saute for 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic, slit green chilli. Saute this for a couple of minutes.
Add the red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and dried red chilli. Add 2 tbsp of water and let the spices cook for a minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, salt and saute for a minute. Add 1 ½ cup of water and the extracted tamarind juice. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and stir.
Strain the curry using a strainer.
Heat a Kadai, add the strained curry, prawns, and cook this for 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.
In another tempering pan, heat 2 tsp of coconut oil and add the sliced shallots, once it turns golden brown, add curry leaves and let it splutter. Add this tempering over the prawn curry.
Serve the prawn curry with steamed rice.

title: Karaikudi Mushroom Fry
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add cornflour, maida, salt, pepper, and water to form a thick batter.
Add the mushrooms and coat each piece with the batter.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan. Fry the mushroom pieces until crispy. It would take around 2 mins. Remove and keep aside.
Grind the grated coconut, cashews with water to prepare the coconut paste. Set aside.
In a pan, add coconut oil, once the oil is hot, add the fennel seeds and saute for a few seconds.
Add the finely chopped onions and saute until translucent.
Add the green chilli and ginger garlic paste. Saute until the ginger garlic paste is cooked. Add the curry leaves and mix well.
Add the chopped tomatoes and saute until the tomatoes are mushy. Add Turmeric Powder, Fennel Powder, Coriander Powder, and salt. Saute for a minute.
Add the ground coconut paste, 3 tbsp of water, and cook for 2 mins.
Add the black pepper powder and mix well.
Add the deep-fried mushroom pieces and toss on a high flame. Ensure that the masala coats each mushroom piece.
Add coriander leaves, mix well and remove from the heat. And serve hot as an appetizer

title: Dhaba Style Paneer Curry
cooking_instructions: Heat up oil and add the whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, green cardamom and black cardamom). Add the sliced onions and cook until they are golden brown.
To the golden brown onions, add ginger garlic paste, slit green chillies, all the spice powders and salt. Saute for 20 seconds.
To this, add tomato puree. Cook for 5 minutes, covered.
Add water followed by the khoya to this and cover it with a lid. Cook it on low flame for 7-8 minutes.
Add chopped coriander leaves and kasuri methi leaves to the curry. Add the paneer pieces to this and mix for 2 minutes.

The oil should be floating on the top or around the edges. This is a sign that the masalas have been cooked. Taste and adjust the salt, if needed. Remove from the heat. Serve hot and top with melted ghee, ginger julienne and coriander springs.

title: Naatu Kozhi Chinthamani
cooking_instructions: Destalk, slit and deseed the dry red chillies
Heat Gingely Oil in a pan. Add the slit and deseeded Dried Red Chilli to the hot oil and saute for a minute.
Add the Shallots to the pan and continue to saute until the shallots turn translucent.
Add Ginger Garlic Paste and continue to cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the cleaned Country Chicken which is cut into small cubes and mix well.
Add Turmeric Powder, Red Chilli Powder, and Salt, mix well and saute.

Add water and continue to cook the chicken until all the water is absorbed and the meat is tender. Approximately for 35-40 mins on medium high heat. Remove from heat and serve this with some steamed rice.

title: Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani
cooking_instructions: In a deep pot, add mutton and the rest of the ingredients required for the marination. Mix it all together till they combine evenly. Let it marinate for 2 hours in the same pot.
Keep the pot with the mutton on the stove and cook the mutton for 10 minutes till it lets out water and it comes to a boil.
In another pan, bring water to boil. Add the whole spices, ghee, salt and bring it to a boil.
Add the basmati rice and let it cook till it is 70% done. Strain the rice immediately. Reserve some of the water for later.
Place the mutton pot on a preheated tawa. Layer it with half of the rice, sprinkle coriander, mint, brown onion on top and add a tablespoon of ghee.
Add the second layer of rice, repeat the same process. Add saffron milk and ¼ cup of the reserved rice water
Cover the pot with silver foil, seal the edges. Place a fitting lid on top. Let it cook on a dum for the first five minutes on a high flame and then for 20 minutes on a low flame.
Serve it hot, wth raita.

title: Tandoori Veg Dum Biryani
cooking_instructions: For the veggie tikkas, heat the mustard oil and add the Kashmiri red chilli powder.

Whisk the hung curd, ginger garlic paste, salt, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, kasuri methi, lemon juice and the Mustard oil with kashmiri red chilli powder. Marinate refrigerated for 30 mins.
Smoke the marinated veggies with coal for about 5 mins.
Cook the veggies on a grill pan until charred and cooked through. Finish with butter, lemon juice and chaat masala and set aside.
For the biryani masala: Heat oil and ghee and add the whole spices, fry until aromatic. Add the sliced onions and fry until golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, green chillies and saute for 2 mins.
Add the tomatoes, cook until mushy and add chilli powder and garam masala.
Add the mint and coriander leaves, Add some salt, water and continue cooking.
Add the cooked tandoori veggies. Mix well and simmer for 2 mins.
Wash and soak the rice for 20 to 30 mins.
Boil the rice in water with 1 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp oil until 70% done and strain it.

Place the pot on a preheated tawa and remove half of the masala. Layer half of the masala and rice alternatively, pour ¼ Cup of water. Garnish with the remaining chopped mint and coriander leaves, kewra and rose water, saffron strands, ghee and a pinch of garam masala.
Cover well and cook on a high flame for 3 mins and a slow flame for 12 mins.
Open the dum and serve hot with raita, laccha onions and mint chutney.

title: Crunchy Peanut Cookies
cooking_instructions: Chop peanuts into coarse crumbs in a blender. Keep aside
In a mixing bowl, add butter, brown sugar, sugar and use a hand blender to cream it. Keep mixing it for 3 minutes until all the sugar is incorporated into the butter.
Add one egg at a time and continue using a hand blender to incorporate eggs into the butter and sugar mixture. Add Vanilla extract to this mix.
Sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt. Add dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix.
Add oatmeal, cornflakes, crushed peanuts and mix until everything is incorporated
Add oatmeal, cornflakes, crushed peanuts and mix until everything is incorporated use an ice cream scoop and drop cookies onto a parchment paper-lined baking tray.
Bake in a preheated oven at 170 C for 10 minutes until slightly puffed and golden brown around the edges.
Cool the cookies for 15 mins on a cooling rack.

title: Karandi Omelette
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the eggs, shallots, green chilli, coriander leaves, pepper powder and salt. Whisk until it is well combined and becomes a little frothy.

Use a small tempering pan for this dish. Heat oil over medium flame. Pour in the eggs. After it starts to set a little, push the egg to one side using a spoon. This is to allow the uncooked part of the egg to move to the side and get cooked evenly. Slowly turn the egg and continue cooking. Keep doing this until the egg is completely cooked.
As an alternative cooking method, similarly, they can be made in paniyaram molds.

title: Tomato Soup
cooking_instructions: To make the Croutons, cut the bread into 1-inch cubes, brush with oil and shallow fry in a Tawa or bake in an oven for 10-15 mins at 200 C.
In a pressure cooker add butter, bay leaf, Kashmiri red chilli, star anise, peppercorns and saute for a minute.
Add 4 garlic cloves, finely chopped onion and saute for a minute.
Add 5 roughly chopped tomatoes, 1 cup of water, fresh coriander leaves and pressure cook for 3 whistles.
Open the pan, remove bay leaf and using a hand blender or mixer grinder, blend this into a smooth puree. Strain this using a strainer.
In another saucepan add the strained mixture, 2 cups of water and bring it to boil. Add sugar and salt.
Add 1 tbsp fresh cream to the soup, simmer for 2 more minutes. And serve hot with croutons.

title: Sweet Corn Vegetable Soup
cooking_instructions: Blend ½ Cup of sweet corn kernels with ¼ cup of water and keep aside.
Heat butter in a pan, add garlic and saute it until raw smell leaves.
Add spring onion white, carrots, beans, green peas, and saute for 3 minutes and add sweet corn kernels.
Pour 4 cups of water and cook all the veggies for 10 minutes in a medium flame until they are cooked.
Add the blended sweet corn paste to the boiling soup and cook for 5 minutes.
Add salt, sugar to the soup.
Mix cornflour with 2 tbsp of water to make a slurry. Add the cornflour mixture to the soup once the vegetables are cooked in the soup.
Season the soup with pepper powder. And add the spring onion greens and remove the soup from the heat. Serve it hot.

title: Traditional Tamilnadu Mutton Biryani
cooking_instructions: Dry Roast and grind the spices under biryani masala and keep aside.
In a mixer grinder grind all the ingredients mentioned under Mutton Masala with some water into a paste.
Wash and Soak the Seeraga samba rice for 30 minutes
In a biryani pot, add the Groundnut oil
Add Coconut oil, bay leaf, shallots and onion to the biryani pot. Fry until the onions turn golden brown.
Add Slit green chilli, lemon juice, ginger paste, garlic paste and cook until the raw smell leaves.
Add Ghee, prepared biryani masala, chilli powder, coriander powder, prepared mutton masala paste in the same order and cook for a couple of minutes.
Add curd, salt, mint leaves and coriander leaves to the pot. Cook for a further 2 minutes.
Add the mutton pieces and cook for 20 minutes adding 2 Cups of water. The gravy would become thick by the time the mutton is cooked.

Now once the mutton is cooked, add the soaked rice and 6 cups of water (1:2 Rice to Water Ratio in case of Seeraga Samba Rice). Simmer this until most of the water is absorbed by the rice. At this point, seal the pot with chapati dough or aluminium foil to prevent steam and heat from going out of the pot. Simmer this closed pot for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes turn off the heat.
Let the biryani rest for another 15 minutes before the pot seal is broken. This will help in finishing off the cooking process.
Now open the pan, fluff the rice and serve hot with Raita.

title: Carrot Cake
cooking_instructions: In a medium-sized mixing bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon powder until everything is combined together.
In another large mixing bowl, whisk the oil, sugar, brown sugar and vanilla. Whisk in the eggs one at a time.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients in three parts, combine it gently using a spatula.
Add the grated carrots to this mixture.
Take two 9 inch baking pans, line the pans with parchment paper, grease it with little butter.
Preheat the oven to 175 C. Transfer the batter equally in the two baking pans.
Bake the cake in a preheated oven at 175 C for 40 mins. To check if the cake is properly cooked, insert a toothpick into the centre of the cake, and it should come out clean.
Cool the cake in the cooking rack for 15 mins.
For the cream cheese frosting, combine the butter and cream cheese in a bowl and beat until creamy using a hand mixer. This should take around 3 mins.
Add Vanilla Extract and mix well.
Add powder sugar in parts and continue mixing using a hand mixer.
Frost the top of one cake layer and place the other cake layer on top. Frost the sides of the cake also. Cut it into wedges and serve.

title: Paal Payasam
cooking_instructions: Heat 2 tsp Ghee in a pan, add the cashews and raisins, once the cashews turn brown and the raisins puff, switch off the heat and keep aside.
Heat a thick-bottomed or a non-stick Kadai, add 2 tsp of ghee. Add the rice and stir for 30 seconds on medium heat.
Bring the milk to a boil and continue simmering on a medium-low flame for 25 mins
Add sugar. Continue simmering for 10 mins or until the quantity is reduced by 30%
Add the cashews and raisins to the payasam and remove it from the heat.
Serve it hot or chill it in a refrigerator and serve cold.

title: Classic Bruschetta
cooking_instructions: Deseed and dice the tomatoes. Add the garlic, salt, pepper, basil, and olive oil to the diced tomatoes, adding the vinegar is optional since tomatoes are acidic naturally.
Allow the tomatoes to seep the juices for 10 mins.
Toast the baguette slices until golden brown and crispy, with some olive oil.
Rub each slice with a pod of garlic to impart some extra flavour.
Top with the tomato mixture, spoon over the juices and garnish with basil sprigs.

title: Tea-Shop Bread Omelette
cooking_instructions: To a small blender jar, add the eggs, garlic, salt, sugar and lemon juice. Blend it for a few seconds to combine.
Drizzle the oil gradually in a thin stream while blending on low speed. Do not over-mix. Stop when the mayonnaise is thick. You can use more or less oil as needed.
Prepare the green chutney by blending together all the ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
Crack the eggs into a bowl. Add salt, pepper and water. Whisk until smooth.
Heat butter in a flat pan. Add the eggs before the oil gets too hot. Spread the eggs around the pan.
Add the bread slices on two sides next to each other. Spread the mayonnaise on one slice of bread. Spread green chutney on the other slice.
Fold in the excess eggs onto the bread. Fold it in half. Cook briefly on both sides and remove from the heat.
Cut it into small squares. Drizzle mayonnaise over the bread omelette and garnish with chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot and enjoy!

title: Green Chicken Curry
cooking_instructions: Soak the cashews in water for 15 minutes.
Heat a frying pan, add 2 tbsp of oil and the thinly sliced onions. Saute the onions on medium heat until they are crispy brown. This should take around 7 mins.
Remove the onions from the pan, transfer them to a mixer grinder jar. Add coriander leaves, mint leaves, soaked cashews, green chillies and ½ Cup of water. Grind this into a smooth paste.
In the same pan, add 1 tbsp of oil. Once the oil is hot, add bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, chopped ginger and garlic.
Add the chicken pieces and saute for 5 mins until the chicken is seared.
Add coriander powder, cumin powder and saute for 2 more minutes.
Add the ground green paste and saute for 2 minutes.
Add salt, sugar, lemon juice, 1 ¼ cup of water. Bring this to a boil and simmer until the chicken is cooked. This should take around 6 minutes.
Add the fresh cream and stir well. Remove the curry from the heat.
In a tempering pan, heat ghee. Add a blade of mace and remove it from the heat after 20 seconds. Add this tempering to the curry and mix well.
Serve hot with Steamed Rice/Naan/Chapati.

title: Fish Fry
cooking_instructions: Clean and wash the fish pieces. Pat dry and keep aside.
In a bowl, add the ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, chopped curry leaves, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, garam masala powder, black pepper powder and salt. Mix well.
Add the besan flour, corn flour and water to the bowl. Mix well to form a paste.
Add the cleaned fish pieces to the Masala paste. Coat each piece of the fish with masala paste and set aside for 15 minutes.
In a deep frying pan, heat the oil.
Once the oil is hot, add the fish pieces and deep fry for 3 mins.
Drain the oil using a paper towel and serve the fish pieces with onion slices and lemon wedges.

title: Banana Chocolate Smoothie
cooking_instructions: In a mixer grinder, add the banana, chocolate piece, milk, honey, ice cubes and cinnamon powder.
Grind the above ingredients into a thick smoothie.
A delicious smoothie is ready to be served.

title: Chicken Ghee Roast
cooking_instructions: In a pan dry roast Kashmiri red chilli, red chilli, coriander, cumin, fennel and pepper.
Grind the dry roasted ingredients with ginger, garlic cloves, lemon juice and tamarind juice to a smooth paste.
Marinate the chicken with the ground paste and curd for 1 hour
In a pan add Ghee, finely chopped onion, once the onions turn golden, add the marinated chicken with the masala and salt.
Cook the chicken for 15 minutes on medium-high heat until the ghee separated and the chicken is coated well with the masala.
Add Jaggery and curry leaves and cook for 1 more minute. Remove from heat and serve with rice/roti/paratha/dosa/appam.

title: Burmese Egg Bhejo
cooking_instructions: Soak the tamarind in hot water for at least 15 minutes.
In a pan, heat the oil. Add the sliced onions and fry them until they turn golden brown. Remove them from the heat.
Add the sliced garlic. Remove them and set aside as soon as they turn golden brown.
Fry the dried red chillies for a few seconds until they barely start to darken. Set the chillies aside and reserve the remaining oil for later use.
Blend the fried chillies into flakes. Combine the fried onion, garlic and chilli flakes.
Mix the salt with water until the salt has dissolved. Keep all the other ingredients prepared.
Slit the boiled eggs halfway through. Stuff the fried onion mixture into the egg.
Pour in a teaspoon of the tamarind extract and the salt mixture, a teaspoon of the remaining oil and a few drops of lemon juice. Garnish with a few sprigs of coriander leaves.

title: Chicken Yakhni Pulao
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 mins.
To make the broth: place all the spices except the fennel seeds and cumin seeds in a clean cheesecloth along with onion, ginger, garlic, green chillies.
Add in a pot with 5 Cups of water, the chicken and salt. Boil it for 10 mins.
Remove the chicken and the spice pouch separately.
To prepare the rice: heat oil in a pot and add the slices onions and brown them.
Add the fennel and cumin seeds and green chillies.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, powdered spices, salt and saute until the tomatoes are soft.
Add the curd, salt and mix well.
Add the chicken and coat well.
Add the rice and 4 cups of the prepared stocks and cook until the water and rice reach the same level.
Cover and cook on a slow flame for 15 mins.
Take off the cover and fluff the rice with a fork and add 1 tbsp of ghee and serve it hot.

title: Paneer Samosa
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add chopped onion, saute until translucent.
Add the green chillies and ginger garlic paste and cook until no longer raw in aroma.
Add tomato, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala powder, cardamom powder and salt to taste, saute till the masalas get cooked.
Add the grated paneer and saute for 2 mins.
Add coriander, mint leaves and the chopped nuts and mix. Remove from the heat and cool the mixture.
For the samosa, prepare a paste of maida and water to use for sticking.
Prepare cones from the samosa sheets, add the paneer stuffing and seal with the maida paste.
Deep fry until golden brown and crispy in medium hot oil. Taket it out, drain the excess oil. Serve it hot

title: Chicken Chinthamani
cooking_instructions: Wash the chicken with ¼ tsp of turmeric and ¼ salt.
Heat a pan or a pot. Add Gingelly Oil. Add mustard seeds and Fenugreek seeds and let it splutter.
Add chopped shallots and red chilli. Cook until the shallots turn golden brown.
Add the curry leaves and add the cleaned and washed chicken. Saute for 2 mins.
Add 2 cups of water ad add ½ tsp turmeric powder and salt to taste.
Cook till the water evaporated and the gravy coats the chicken.
Add coriander leaves and remove from heat. Serve hot with Rice/Idly/Dosa.

title: Falafel
cooking_instructions: Soak the chana overnight or for at least 12-15 hours.

Drain the water. Add it into a food processor/mixer along with onion, garlic, coriander leaves, mint leaves, parsley, salt, cumin powder, black pepper powder and coriander powder. Grind it into a coarse mixture.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. Add baking powder and mix again. Adjust the consistency with Maida.
Shape into balls/patties.
Fry them in oil until they turn brown and crisp on the outside. Serve it hot.

title: Malpua
cooking_instructions: Combine the maida and 1 cup water to get a smooth and free flowing batter.
Soak khoya in a bowl with ½ cup warm water for 5 mins.
Combine the maida batter and the soaked khoya and blend until combined.
Pass the mixture through a strainer and add the remaining ingredients- cardamom powder, salt and crushed fennel seeds.
Combine the sugar and ½ Cup water in a pan. Switch on the flame and cook to 1 string consistency. Add a few strands of saffron, cardamom and lemon juice and switch off the flame.
To fry the malpua, take a shallow kadai and heat oil, reduce to a medium flame and add 1 ladle at a time holding your hand steady. Fry until golden brown on both sides and strain the malpua.
Arrange it on a plate, top it off with sugar syrup and rabadi and serve it warm.

title: Pickled Vegetables
cooking_instructions: Boil the vinegar, salt, sugar and water with the whole spices.
Switch off the pickling liquid and add the vegetables.
Allow the liquid to cool down. Refrigerate once completely cooled.. Ready to be consumed from the next day. Can be stored for upto 2 weeks.

title: Thoothukudi Macaroons
cooking_instructions:
Preheat an oven to 100°c.
Add the cashew to a mixer. Pulse them for a couple of seconds at a time, so that they are coarsely powdered. 
Separate the eggs carefully. Make sure that the yolk doesn’t dissolve into the egg whites at all. 
Add the eggs into a bowl and beat it on low speed until it turns foamy. 
Add the sugar in 3 batches. Add the next spoon only once the sugar is dissolved already. Continue adding and beating on low-medium speed until it forms stiff peaks. 
Add the coarsely powdered cashew into the egg mixture and fold it very gently. 
Add the mixture into piping bags with a large plain tip. Pipe it in cones onto a baking tray lined with a baking sheet/ butter paper. 
Place the tray in the oven and reduce the temperature to 100°c. Bake for 100 minutes. NEVER open the oven door in between. 
Once the baking is done, crack the door open and continue baking for 20 minutes

title: Wedding Style Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions: In a pan, add the sliced onions, whole spices and green chillies. Add oil, turn on the flame and cook the onions till they turn golden brown.
Add the coriander and mint leaves and fry them for a few seconds.
Add the ginger garlic paste, cook it for a minute.
Add the kashmiri chilli and cook it for a few seconds till it brings out a bright red colour.
Add the tomatoes, cook them till they get mashed and oil splutters from the sides. Add salt.
Add curd, mix it well. Add water, mix it well, cover it and bring it to a boil for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, mix it well. Cover and cook it on a medium flame for 10 minutes.

In another pot, boil water, add salt to it and make sure the water tastes slightly salty. Add the rice, cook it till it is 70% done (for about 3 minutes). Strain the rice immediately. Reserve some of the water.
Add the rice to the chicken masala, mix it very gently. If there isn't enough water, pour the reserved rice water till it is almost equal to the level of the rice.
Cover the pot with silver foil and a fitting lid.
Place the pot on a preheated tawa and keep the biryani on dum for 5 minutes on a medium flame and then for 10 minutes on a low flame.
Serve it hot with raita, brinjal curry or chicken 65.

title: Paal Kozhukattai
cooking_instructions: To make the jaggery syrup, add water, jaggery to a pan and bring the water to a boil and simmer until all the jaggery is melted.
Once this cools down, pass it through a metal strainer to strain all the impurities. Let the jaggery cool.
To make the dough balls, add water and milk to a pan and bring it to a boil. Add salt and rice flour. Keep stirring until a smooth, lump-free dough is formed. Add Ghee.
Remove from the heat and let it cool. Grease your hands with little ghee and make small dough balls from the prepared dough.
Grind the coconut with water, filter and extract coconut milk.
To make the milk sauce, heat a pan, add milk and water, bring it to a boil. Add the prepared dough balls to the pan.
Once the dough balls are cooked, they will float to the surface.
Add the jaggery and continue to cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, cardamom powder and switch off the flame.
Add grated coconut mix well and remove from the heat. Serve it as a dessert with lunch or evening snack.

title: Tomato Egg Drop Soup
cooking_instructions: In a pot, pour in the vegetable stock along with grated ginger and garlic. Cover and bring it to a boil.
Add the tomato, tomato ketchup, red chilli sauce, salt and white pepper powder. Bring it to a boil again. Cover and simmer for 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine the cornstarch with the water to form a slurry. Add this to the soup.
Beat the eggs in a bowl. Pour the beaten eggs into the pot in a thin stream, from a height. Simultaneously, keep mixing the soup with a ladle so that the egg forms into thin strands.
Add the chopped coriander leaves and simmer for 1 more minute. Turn off the heat and serve warm.

title: Spanish Omelette
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, whisk 4 eggs with salt and pepper
Heat oil in a pan, add the potatoes and fry, stirring occasionally for 5 mins.
Add the onions. Fry for 2 mins further.
To make the omelette, add the eggs into the same pan. Push the edges down and cook until the base firms up. Cover the omelette and reduce the heat for 3 mins.
Uncover the eggs and place a plate over the pan, flip the eggs onto the plate and slide it back into the pan. Return the pan to high heat for 2 minutes.

title: Chocolate Cheese Sandwich
cooking_instructions: Apply butter on both sides of the bread slices.
