Apply 1 tsp of pizza sauce on each piece. Spread a few pieces of the veggies on it.
Spread some mozzarella cheese on top and sprinkle some oregano and chilli flakes.
Heat some butter in a pan over low heat. Place the bread in the pan carefully.
On low heat, cover and cook for 4-5 minutes, or until the cheese has melted. Serve it hot.

title: Bread Pakoda
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a kadhai and let the mustard seeds splutter, add coriander seeds, ginger, garlic, green chillies and curry leaves. Add hing, salt and turmeric powder.
Add the potatoes, mash and mix well. Add chopped coriander leaves and mix.
For the batter: combine the given ingredients to make a smooth batter.
Fill this mixture in between two slices of bread.
Dip the potato sandwiched bread in the batter and deep fry until golden brown.

title: Chettinad Chicken Momos
cooking_instructions: For the momo dough, knead a firm yet pliable dough with the given ingredients and cover and rest for 20 mins.
In a pan, add all the whole spices and dry roast until they are aromatic. Add the curry leaves and saute until dry. Grind this into a coarse powder using a mixer grinder.
In another pan, heat oil and add the finely chopped onions, finely chopped garlic, and continue to cook until the onions turn translucent.
Add the Ginger Garlic Paste and continue to saute. Add the finely chopped tomato and saute until the tomatoes are mushy. Add the turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt.

Add Chicken to the pan, mix well to coat the Chicken with masala, and continuously stir to prevent the mince from clumping up. Cook the chicken for 10 minutes by stirring in intervals or until the chicken is cooked.
Add the ground spice powder which was prepared earlier, to the pan. Mix well and saute for 2 mins. Add coriander leaves.

Divide the dough and roll out small roundels using cornstarch for dusting and stuff with the mixture by sticking the ends together forming a semi-circle and sticking together the ends of the semi-circle, or by pinching pleats.
Steam for 6 mins.
For Chutney - In a mixer grinder, take the ingredients for the chutney. Add water as needed and blend to a fine paste.
Serve the momos hot with red chilli coconut chutney.

title: Fattoush
cooking_instructions: Cut the Pita bread into small squares. Fry them in oil until they turn crisp. These are the pita chips for the salad.
For the dressing, whisk all the ingredients together.
Mix all the ingredients for the salad along with dressing.
Garnish with mint sprigs, pomegranate seeds and some more pita chips.

title: Beetroot Poriyal
cooking_instructions: In a pan, Heat Oil, add Mustard, Cumin, urad dal,  Dry Red Chillies,  green chilli,Curry Leaves and let them Crackle. Add Asafoetida and mix it well
Add the chopped onions and cook it till they go brown. Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a few seconds.
Add the dry powders, cook it for a few seconds.
Add the diced beetroot, toss it till it coats evenly with the masala.
Add a cup of water, bring it to a boil.
Season it with salt and sugar. Mix it well. Cover it and cook for 10 minutes on a medium flame, Stirring occasionally
Transfer it to a bowl. Garnish it with chopped coriander. Serve it hot.

title: Dal Dhokli
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the dal for 30 mins. Add into a pressure cooker with salt, turmeric powder and water and pressure cook for 3-4 whistles.
Knead a stiff dough with atta, besan and the spices. Roll out into thin sheets and cut into large diamond shapes/ strips.
In a pot, heat ghee and splutter the mustard seeds. Add the cumin seeds, garlic, curry leaves and slit green chillies, asafoetida. Mix it well. Add chilli and turmeric powder and mix it well.
Add the cooked dal and adjust the consistency with water, if needed. Add salt and mix it well.
Add the tamarind and jaggery. Mix it well. Add water, mix it well and bring the mixture to a boil.
Add the dough triangles and simmer for 10 mins until cooked.
Finish with chopped coriander leaves.

title: No-Oven Paneer Stuffed Capsicum
cooking_instructions: Cut the capsicum in half and remove the seeds.
Heat oil in a pan and add the capsicum. Toss on high heat for 2-3 minutes. Remove from the pan.
In the same pan, add the ginger, garlic, and green chilli. Saute lightly and then add the onion and cashew. Saute until translucent.
Add all the powdered spices, salt, and tomato ketchup. Mix well for 2 minutes.
Add paneer, potato, coriander leaves and lemon juice. Mix and remove from the heat.
Fill the capsicum with the stuffing. Press it down tightly.
Grease a pan with oil, and add the stuffed capsicum, stuffing side down. Cook for 2 minutes on low heat.
Flip it carefully, cover and cook for 10-12 minutes on low heat. Move it around occasionally to ensure it does not burn on the bottom. Cook on very low heat only.
Add grated cheese on top of each piece, cover and cook for 5 minutes or until the cheese melts.
Serve this as a starter or a party snack, garnished with coriander leaves and chilli flakes.

title: Pallipalayam mutton
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add garlic, dry red chillies and let it crackle for a few seconds.
Add the shallots and saute till it turns translucent.
Add the mutton and mix it well for a few minutes
Add the chilli powder and turmeric powder. Keep mixing it and let it cook on a medium flame for a minute.
Add water, mix it well. Season it with salt and pepper. Mix it well.
Cover and cook the mutton on a medium flame, stirring occasionally.
Add curry leaves and the sliced coconut and mix it well till all the ingredients combine evenly.
Cook it till it is almost dry
Transfer it to a bowl, garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot.

title: Cooker Vegetable Pulao
cooking_instructions: Wash the basmati rice 3 times and then soak for 10 minutes.
In a pressure cooker, heat ghee and add all the whole spices. Saute until aromatic, then add the green chilli and onion. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the ginger garlic paste and saute, followed by the tomato. Saute until the tomato softens.
Add all the vegetables, mint leaves, coriander leaves, salt and garam masala powder. Saute for 1 minute.
Add the soaked rice, lemon juice and the water. Cover and pressure cook for 1 whistle on medium heat. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Once the steam has settled, fluff up the rice with a fork. Serve with any gravy or with onion raita.

title: Telangana Natu Kodi Kurra
cooking_instructions: Soak the dry red chillies in hot water for 15 minutes.
Take a mixer jar and add in tomatoes, garlic cloves, soaked dry chillies. Now blend this into a paste and set aside.
Take a pressure cooker and add oil and cumin seeds. Saute for a minute. Then add in sliced onions, cook the onions until it turns light brown color

Now add curry leaves & ginger garlic paste. Saute the ginger-garlic paste for 3 minutes.  Add turmeric powder & the prepared chili paste. Saute for 4 minutes on medium to low heat.Then add in coriander powder.
Add Country chicken. Mix well, turn the flame to low, cover with a lid and cook for 15 minutes.
Now add salt & water, pressure cook for 2 whistles on high heat. Then turn the flame to low and cook for 5 whistles.
Once the pressure is released take out the cooker lid let it cook for another 5 minutes on medium flame or until the curry starts getting thick. Add in finely chopped coriander leaves
Serve it hot with piping hot plain rice.

title: Lauki Halwa
cooking_instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and add the lauki and cook for 5 mins.
Add the milk and cardamom powder and boil on a high flame for 15 mins, stirring often.
Add the sugar and continue cooking for 10 mins.
Add the khoya and mixed chopped nuts and cook until it becomes thick.

title: Dindigul Chicken Biryani
cooking_instructions: Heat a pan and dry roast the spices for the biryani masala till it is aromatic. Transfer it to a blender and grind it to a coarse powder.
Blend the ginger and garlic with little water to a fine paste. Keep it aside.

Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes Heat a pot, add groundnut oil and ghee. Add the bay leaves and let it crackle.
Then add the onions and saute till they turn translucent.

Add the green chilli and let it cook in the oil for a minute. Keep mixing it well. Then add the coriander and mint leaves and let it fry till it gives out an aroma. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook it for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook it till it turns soft.
Add the red chilli powder, biryani masala, and cook it till it gives out an aroma. Add the curd, mix it well. Cook it until oil starts floating on top.
Add the chicken pieces and cook it till it is evenly coated with the masala. Add salt to it, and mix it well. Then cover and cook the chicken on a medium flame for 10 minutes.
Add the rice. Mix the rice gently for a minute in the masala. Add water, mix and bring it to a boil and let it cook till the rice and water are at the same level.
Place it on a preheated tawa and cook it on a dum on low flame for 15 minutes. Turn off the flame after 15 minutes and let it rest for another 5 minutes before opening the pot.
Add Ghee to it, fluff the rice and chicken pieces. And remove it from the stove.
Serve it hot with raita and accompaniments of your choice.

title: Nallampatti Chicken
cooking_instructions: In a small pot, boil water and add the red chillies. Boil for 5 minutes.
Take out the chillies and blend them into a fine paste, adding water as required.
In a larger pot, heat gingelly oil and add curry leaves and shallots. Saute until it turns slightly golden brown.
Add the chilli paste and saute for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken, turmeric, salt and mix well. Add water and bring it to a boil. Cover and cook on low heat for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove the lid and add the coconut slices. Cook until the chicken becomes tender and the gravy is thick enough.

title: Gobi Pepper Fry
cooking_instructions: Put the cauliflower florets into a bowl and cover with hot water. Cover with a lid and set aside for 5 minutes.

Drain the cauliflower and add it to a bowl. Add the maida, cornflour, salt, Kashmiri red chilli powder and salt. Mix until there is an even coating on the cauliflower pieces. Sprinkle water as required.
Heat oil in a pan and deep-fry the cauliflower on medium-high heat until golden brown. Remove and set aside.

Heat oil in a pan and add the fennel seeds, followed by the curry leaves, garlic, green chilli and onion. Saute until the onion turns translucent. Add the powdered spices and salt. Saute for 1 minute, then add a splash of water.
Add the fried cauliflower and toss until evenly coated. Add lemon juice and coriander leaves, and give it a final toss.

title: Honey Garlic Chicken Bites
cooking_instructions: Wash and drain the chicken. Transfer it to a bowl, add salt, pepper,msg, garlic powder, maida and egg. Mix it till the chicken is evenly coated with all ingredients.
Coat the chicken in panko crumbs.
Head oil in a kadai, Deep fry the crumbed chicken to a golden brown colour.
In another pan, heat oil, saute garlic and red chilli flakes for a few seconds.
Add honey, soy sauce, water and mix till the honey and soy sauce dissolve in the water.
When the mixture starts to thicken, add the fried chicken and toss it on a high flame.
Garnish it with chopped spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve it hot.

title: White Chocolate Butterscotch Barks
cooking_instructions: Add the butter, sugar, vanilla, salt to a pan with a splash of water and bring it up to a boil. Simmer until the bubbles are thick, the colour will be light golden and check the consistency in a bowl of water. Add 1 drop of this mixture to water, if it solidifies immediately the mixture is ready.
Pour this mixture on the baking sheet and move around to spread evenly.
For the white chocolate, add all but 50 gms, in a microwave-safe bowl and melt in bursts of 30 seconds. Stir in between each session.
Once completely melted, add the remaining chocolate to bring down the temperature. Continue stirring for 1 minute continuously. Heat the chocolate again for 20 seconds.
Add a few drops of color to this mixture and swirl it around to create a marble effect.
Spread half the white chocolate on a separate parchment-lined tray.
De-mold the set butterscotch toffee and wipe the excess butter.
Pour the remaining chocolate on top and spread it into a thin layer.
Sprinkle on top the rose petals, pista, cardamom powder and place some silver leaf. Allow it to set completely, place it for a few minutes in the fridge.
Break into smaller bark pieces and serve.

title: Soya Chilli Hotdogs
cooking_instructions: Soak soya in hot water and salt. Cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Squeeze out the excess water. Add maida and cornflour, and toss lightly to coat evenly.
Heat oil in a pan and fry the soya chunks on high flame until slightly crisp (around 4 minutes). Take it out of the oil.
In a pan add oil, add the garlic, ginger, green chilli and onion. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add red chilli powder, cumin powder and salt. Saute for a minute.
Add the sauces, sugar and mix.
Add the capsicum & fried soya chunks. Mix and cook for 2 minutes on high heat. Take it off the flame.
Make a slit on a hotdog bun. Cut a cheese slice in half and place it inside.
Spoon some of the filling into the bun.
Heat some butter in a pan and toast it for 1-2 minutes, covered with a lid.
Serve with a drizzle of mayonnaise. Garnish with chopped onion and coriander leaves.

title: Chettinad Mutton Chukka Burger
cooking_instructions: In a saucepan, combine water, vinegar, coriander seeds, cardamom, sugar and salt. Bring it to a gentle simmer. Turn off the heat.
In a jar, add the shallots. Add the vinegar, allow it to cool slightly, and then cover.
Dry roast all the spices (except curry leaves) on medium-low heat until aromatic.
Add the curry leaves and continue to dry roast until the leaves turn crispy. Grind this into a fine powder.
Add the chukka masala to the mutton mince along with onion powder, garlic powder, and coriander leaves. Mix until evenly combined.
Divide the mixture into 8 portions. Flatten it well.

Heat a pan to high heat and add oil. Season the patties generously with salt and place them with sufficient space around them. Flatten it with a spatula. Cook for 6 minutes, flipping them occasionally. Remove it from the pan.
Heat ghee in a pan. Crackle mustard seeds in it. Add curry leaves, green chilli, and turmeric powder. Continue cooking for 20 seconds, or until the curry leaves turn crisp.
Add this tempering to mayonnaise, and mix until combined.
In a bowl, beat together eggs, salt, and black pepper.
Heat oil in a pan and add some of the egg mixture. Fold in the eggs from the sides continuously, to form a pouch shape. It should cook only for around 30 seconds. Remove from the pan.

Toast the buns with some ghee. Spread the sauce on both sides of the bun. Add two patties to each burger (or one, if that’s what you prefer). Place the Kalakki and top it off with some of the pickled shallots. Cover it and enjoy!

title: Hyderabadi Dum ka Murgh
cooking_instructions: In a pot of boiling water, add the cashew and almonds. Boil for 5 minutes. Remove the skins of the almonds. Grind it into a paste along with the cashews, desiccated coconut, green chilli and water as needed.
To the chicken, add all the dry ingredients for the marination, lemon juice, ginger garlic paste and mix.
Then mix the curd, khoya, saffron and curd. Mix well. Marinate for 3 hours, or overnight for the best results.
Place the chicken into a heavy bottomed pot. Seal the pot using aluminium foil and the lid.
Heat a Tawa over high heat. Place the sealed pot on the Tawa and cook for 5 minutes.
Reduce the flame and cook for 35 minutes on low heat.
Open the dum. Place a bowl with hot charcoal in the pot. Pour a teaspoon of ghee for the smoke. Cover tightly and rest for 5-7 minutes, depending on the level of smokiness you want in the dish.
Remove the charcoal, cover and rest for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Do Pyaza
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds, bay leaf and black cardamom. Add the onion and saute until it turns golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste, turmeric powder, salt, Kashmiri red chilli powder, cumin powder and coriander powder. Saute for a minute.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 3 minutes, mixing regularly.
Add the chicken and saute for 2 minutes.
Add the cashew paste and mix well to combine. Add water and sugar. Cover and cook for 15 minutes on low heat.
Add the onion and green chilli. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato and ginger julienne. Cook for 2 minutes. Add butter, garam masala powder, Kasuri methi and coriander leaves. Turn off the heat as soon as it starts to simmer.

title: Mangalore Prawn Sukka
cooking_instructions: For the masala, heat oil in a pan over low heat. Add all the ingredients except grated coconut, tamarind and turmeric powder. Roast until it turns aromatic, then remove the spices from the pan. Allow to cool, then grind into a powder.

In the same pan, add the grated coconut and turmeric powder. Roast it very lightly. It should be aromatic but the colour should not change. Add this to the ground powder. Add tamarind also, and grind into a paste, adding water if required. The masala is ready.
Mix the prawns along with salt and turmeric powder. Set aside for 10 minutes.
In a pan, heat coconut oil. Add mustard seeds and allow them to crackle. Add curry leaves and onions. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the marinated prawns, saute and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the prepared masala and mix well. Add salt. Mix, cover and cook for 5 minutes on low heat. Remove the lid and cook until the gravy is thick and semi-dry.
Add coriander leaves, mix and serve with rice.

title: Chicken Malai Tikka
cooking_instructions: Cut the chicken into thin pieces.
Marinate the chicken with the 1st marination and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Soak the cashew nuts in water for 15 minutes. Blend it along with the mace, grated cheese and cream.

In a bowl, add hung curd, green chilli, salt, garam masala powder, cumin powder and cardamom powder. Add the previously prepared paste. Whisk until smooth. Add the marinated chicken and mix well to coat. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat a piece of charcoal on the stove. Place it in a small metal bowl in the marinated chicken. Pour 1 tsp of oil on top and cover. Let it sit for 3 minutes.
Skewer the chicken pieces onto the bamboo skewers.
Heat a pan and grease with oil. Place the skewers and cook on high flame for 2 minutes, turning constantly to get a crust on all sides.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 8 minutes or until cooked through, flipping halfway through.
Remove from the pan, brush with melted butter and sprinkle Chaat masala over the tikka.

title: Kovakkai Poriyal
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, Add mustard, urad dal, dry red chilli, curry leaves and let it crackle.
Add the onions and saute till it turns translucent. Add a pinch of asafoetida, mix it well. Cook the onions till they start to turn light brown.
Add ginger garlic paste, mix it for a few seconds.
Add the red chilli powder and turmeric powder, mix it for about a minute.
Add the kovakkai and saute for a minute.
Add water, salt and sugar. Mix it well. Cover and cook it till all the water is absorbed.
Add grated coconut. Mix it till it combines evenly. Serve it hot as a side with rice and any gravy.

title: Avarakkai Poriyal
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, Add mustard, urad dal, dry red chilli, curry leaves and let it crackle.
Add the onions and saute till it turns translucent. Add a pinch of asafoetida, mix it well. Cook the onions till they start to turn light brown.
Add ginger garlic paste, mix it for a few seconds.
Add the masala, mix it well and let it cook for a minute.
Add the avarakkai, mix it well for a minute.
Add salt, sugar and water. Mix it well. Cover and cook it till all the water evaporates.
Add grated coconut. Mix it well. Serve it hot as a side along with rice and any gravy.

title: Cauliflower Poriyal
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, Add mustard, cumin seeds, chilli, curry leaves and let it crackle.
Add the onions and saute till it turns translucent. Add a pinch of asafoetida, mix it well. Cook the onions till they start to turn light brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a minute.
Add turmeric powder and red chilli powder, mix it well and let it cook for a minute.
Add the cauliflower, mix it till it is coated evenly with the masala.
Add salt, pepper, sugar and a little water. Mix it well. Cover and let it cook till the cauliflower is cooked.
Transfer it to a bowl, garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot with rice/roti etc.

title: Paneer Frankie
cooking_instructions: Mix the ingredients for the Frankie masala and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add the onions and saute till it turns light brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook it for a minute.
Add the dry powders and cook it for a minute on a low flame.
Add the pureed tomatoes and cook until the oil separates from it.
Add green chilies and mix it well. Then add water to it and cook it well
Add the Paneer, mix it gently. Let it cook for 5 minutes in the masala.
Season the mixture, mix it well.
Add the capsicum, mix it well. Keep the filling aside.
Heat a tawa and cook the chapati evenly on both sides. Take it off the tawa.
Spread mayonnaise and ketchup over the chapati. Sprinkle the frankie masala and add the paneer filling.Roll it tightly and serve it hot.

title: Gun Fire Chicken
cooking_instructions: Make a smooth paste using all the ingredients under the ‘for the paste’ section.
Make shallow cuts on the thick parts of the chicken leg. Add the prepared paste and coat fully. Rest for 15 minutes at least.
Heat oil in a pan. Add fennel seeds, green chilli, onion and curry leaves. Saute until the onion starts to brown.
Add the chicken pieces and cook for a couple of minutes.
Add water along with the remaining masala. Add it to the pan. Cover and cook on medium heat for 20 minutes, flipping occasionally.
Remove the lid and cook for 5 more minutes, flipping occasionally, until the masala is dry and just coats the chicken.
Add curry leaves and black pepper powder. Mix it well and then serve hot.

title: Sharjah Shake
cooking_instructions: Place the packet of milk in the freezer. Freeze for 3-4 hours.
Beat the milk packet with a rolling pin or a ladle, to crush the ice.
Cut it open and pour the contents into a blender jar. Add all the other ingredients and blend.
Garnish with some Boost and roasted peanuts.

title: Mushroom Poriyal
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, Add mustard, urad dal, chilli, curry leaves and let it crackle.
Add the onions and saute till it turns translucent. Cook the onions till they start to turn light brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a minute. Then add turmeric powder, mix it well.
Add the mushroom, mix it till it is coated evenly with the masala.
Add salt, pepper, sugar and a little water. Mix it well.
Keep tossing till the mushroom is cooked. Add coriander leaves, mix it well. Then transfer it to a bowl, serve it hot with rice/roti etc.

title: Spicy Prawn Masala
cooking_instructions: In a pan, add the water, turmeric powder and salt. Mix it, cover and cook for 3 minutes on medium heat. Set this aside.
In another pan, heat coconut oil. Add the shallots, green chilli, curry leaves. Saute for 1 minute on medium heat.
Add the cooked prawns (without the water) and mix. Spread them evenly around the pan. Cook for 5 minutes on high heat, flipping it occasionally.
Add salt, red chilli powder, black pepper powder and curry leaves. Mix and then add the remaining water from cooking the prawns.
Stir-fry for 2 minutes on high heat, and then remove from the heat. Serve with rice or parotta.

title: Sizzling Brownie
cooking_instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°c. Grease a 8-inch tray and line with butter paper.
In a large bowl, add the butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla essence. Beat until it turns pale yellow, around 4 minutes.
Place a sift/strainer above the bowl. Add in maida, cocoa powder, salt and baking powder.
Mix using a whisk or a spatula until fully combined.
Pour it into the prepared tray. In a bowl, mix together chocolate chips, almond, cashew and maida. Mix it and sprinkle it on the brownie batter.
Bake for 30 minutes. Check if it is done by inserting a toothpick. It should come out just slightly coated in crumbs, but mostly dry.
Add the chopped chocolate and cream to a bowl. Microwave it for 1 minute. Alternatively, place the bowl over a pot of boiling water and stir until it melts.
Mix until evenly combined. Set aside.
Heat up the sizzler plate until smoking hot.
Place it on the wooden base. Crush some of the chocolate biscuits/cookies and add it in the centre.
Place the brownies followed by the vanilla ice cream. You can also drizzle some of the chocolate sauce on the ice cream.
Pour the chocolate sauce near the brownie for the sizzling effect.

title: Sev
cooking_instructions: Mix the besan and rice flour with powdered spices and salt. Mix with hot oil to get a crumbly texture.
Knead to make a smooth and firm dough, adding water little at a time.
Grease the mold with oil and fill the mixture.
Pipe into medium hot oil/ on a ladle and dip the ladle in oil. Fry for a min until crispy but not changed colour.
Cool and break into small pieces.

title: Fish Tikka
cooking_instructions: To prepare chilli oil, heat a small pan with mustard oil, bring it to a smoking point and turn off the flame.
Let the mustard oil cool down a bit and add kashmiri chilli powder and besan flour to it and mix it well. Keep it aside
To the fish, add lemon juice, ginger garlic paste, chilli oil, ajwain and salt. Mix it till the fish is coated evenly with the marinade. Let it marinate for 25-30 minutes
In another bowl add mustard oil, kashmiri chilli powder and mix it well till the oil becomes red in colour. Add hung curd, and the rest of the ingredients, mix it well. Add the remaining chilli oil
Add the curd mixture to the marinated fish and let it marinate for another 30 minutes.
Heat up a piece of coal, transfer it to a bowl. Place the bowl into the marinated fish bowl and pour a tablespoon of ghee and immediately cover the bowl and seal it from all ends with silver foil.
Let the fish smoke for 5-7 minutes
Skewer the marinated fish.
Heat oil on a grill pan and grill the fish on all sides till it is cooked evenly and grill marks appear.

While taking it off the skewer, rotate the skewer while holding the fish. Take it out one piece at a time to avoid breaking it. Top it off with some butter and chaat masala. Garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot along with mint chutney, sliced onions and a lemon wedge.

title: Naatukozhi Pallipalayam
cooking_instructions: Blend ginger, garlic, green chilli and turmeric powder to a coarse paste.
Add the paste to the chicken along with salt. Mix it well and let it marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan, add garlic, dry red chillies and let it crackle for a few seconds.
Add the shallots and saute till it turns translucent.
Add the chilli powder and turmeric powder. Keep mixing it and let it cook on a medium flame for a minute.
Add the marinated chicken and mix it till it is evenly coated with the masala and it gives out an aroma.
Add water till it is level with the chicken, season the mixture with salt and mix it well. Cover and cook it till the water evaporates, stirring at regular intervals.
Add curry leaves and the sliced coconut
Mix it well till all the ingredients combine evenly. Cook the chicken till it is almost dry and aromatic.
Transfer it to a bowl, garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot.

title: Mutton Kari Dosa
cooking_instructions: Dry roast the spices until aromatic. Blend it into a powder.
Heat oil and add the fennel seeds, curry leaves, onion and green chilli. Saute until the onion starts to turn golden brown.
Add the ginger garlic paste and saute for 1-2 minutes or until the raw smell disappears.
Add the tomato, turmeric powder and salt. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add the prepared masala and the mutton mince and saute for 2 minutes, breaking down any lumps.
Add the water, cover and cook for 20 minutes on low heat, until the meat is cooked and the oil floats on top.
Allow it to cool down. Then crack eggs into it and mix. Set aside.
In a bowl, mix together onion, coriander leaves, and curry leaves. Mix and set aside.
Heat a tawa and grease it lightly with oil. Spread a ladle of Dosa batter slightly thick. Add the mutton mixture, onion mix and black pepper powder on top. Drizzle some gingelly oil on the sides.
Flip it and cook on medium heat for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and serve.

title: Fried Milk
cooking_instructions: In a pan, heat milk, add sugar, vanilla essence and a pinch of nutmeg powder and mix it till the sugar dissolves.

Add cornflour, whisk it till the mixture turns thick. Check the taste for the preferred level of sweetness. Transfer it to a square or rectangular dish, spread it evenly and let it set in the freezer for 8 hours.
Take out the milk mixture, check if it is set. Cut it into batons/cubes and place it in the freezer for 30 minutes.
Coat the milk cubes/batons in flour, then eggs and finally panko crumbs.
Heat oil in a kadai, Gently deep fry the crumbed milk to a golden brown colour. Serve it hot.

title: Japan Paneer
cooking_instructions: Make a batter out of the maida, cornflour, salt, pepper and water.
Coat the paneer cubes and deep-fry on medium-high heat until crispy and golden brown.
Grind the cashews into cashew powder using a mixer grinder.
Heat a pan, add oil and butter. Add garlic and slit green chilli. Saute for a minute.
Add the milk, salt and sugar. Stir and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the cashew powder and let the sauce thicken.
Add the deep-fried paneer pieces to the sauce. Stir fry until the sauce coats the paneer pieces.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot as an appetizer.

title: Mutton Paya
cooking_instructions: Add all the ingredients into the pressure cooker. Cook on high heat for 1 whistle, then reduce the heat to medium and cook for 15 more minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
Make the coconut paste by grinding together the coconut, fennel seeds, poppy seeds and water. Set this aside.

Heat oil in a pan and add the whole spices. Add the onion and green chilli. Saute until the onion turns translucent. Add the salt, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder and ginger garlic paste. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add the mint and coriander leaves. Saute for 1 minute. Add the tomato and saute for 3-4 minutes, or until it softens.
Add the water and bring it to a boil. Cover and cook for 10 minutes, on low heat.
Add the cooked mutton to the pan. Cover again and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the coconut paste, cover and cook again for 10 minutes. Serve with appam, idiyappam or parotta.

title: Beetroot Hummus
cooking_instructions: Soak the chickpeas in water overnight.
Pressure cook them along with water for 6 whistles. Allow the steam to release.
Add the beetroot to a pressure cooker along with 2 cups of water and cook for 5 whistles.
Toast the white sesame seeds in a pan on low heat until the colour starts to change. Grind it in a mixer.
Add the cooked chickpeas, beetroot and all the other ingredients except water into a mixer/food processor. Add water gradually if needed and blend into a fine paste.
Garnish it with olive oil, white sesame seeds and parsley. Serve it with pita bread

title: Creole Chicken
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan, sear the chicken till it turns golden brown on all sides and take it out.
In the same pan, add some more oil, add garlic and satue it for a few seconds.
Add the celery, cook it for a minute, add the onions and saute till it turns translucent. Add the bell peppers and saute them for a few minutes.
Add the herbs and cook it for a few seconds.
Add the Paprika and cook it for 2 minutes. Add the diced tomatoes and cook till it becomes soft.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 5 minutes. Add a cup of water, mix it well and let the tomato puree cook till it isn't raw anymore.
Add the seared chicken and mix it till it coats evenly
Season the dish with salt. Mix it well.
Cover and cook it for 15 minutes.
Garnish it with Fried Basil. Serve it hot.

title: Cookd Dindigul Veg Biryani
cooking_instructions: Transfer the whole spices to a blender and grind it to a coarse powder.
Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes
Heat a pot, add groundnut oil and ghee. Add the bay leaves and let it crackle.
Add the onions and saute till they turn translucent.
Add the ginger garlic paste, green chilli and let it cook in the oil for a minute. Keep mixing it well
Add the tomatoes and cook it till it turns soft.
Add the coriander and mint leaves and let it fry till it gives out an aroma.
Add the curd, mix it well. Cook it until oil starts floating on top.
Add the red chilli powder, biryani masala and cook it till it gives out an aroma. Add salt, mix it well.
Add the vegetables and stir till it is evenly coated with the masala. Add water and bring it to a boil.
Add the rice. Mix the rice gently for a minute in the masala.
Mix and let it cook till the rice and water are at the same level.
Add the lemon juice and mix well.
Close it tightly with a lid. Cook it on a dum on low flame for 15 minutes.
Open the pot, fluff the rice. Finish with ghee.
Serve it hot with onion raita and biryani kathirikai or accompaniments of your choice.

title: Veggie Bean and Corn Burritos
cooking_instructions: Cut the avocado into dices, add lemon juice, mix it well and keep it aside.
Combine the wheat flour, corn flour and salt. Add the vinegar and water and knead a semi hard dough.
Apply oil on the dough and rest it for 15 mins, covered.
For the filling: heat oil in pan and add the garlic, saute for 2-3 mins.
Add all the vegetables at once and saute on a high flame for 2-3 mins.
Add the spice powders, seasonings and the ketchup. Mix well and set aside.
Roll out the dough into flat circles.
Cook them thoroughly on a tava. Apply oil and set aside.
Place the mixture in the centre of the tortilla circles, place a generous serving of cheese on top.
Roll them tightly into cylinders/ rolls.
Cook on a hot tava with some oil until golden brown, crispy on the outside and the cheese has melted. Serve it hot.

title: Aloo Matar Palak Tikki
cooking_instructions: Boil the potatoes and green peas for 4 whistles.
Blanch the spinach and drain.
Roast the besan for 3 mins on a slow flame.
Once the spinach has cooled, chop it finely.
Combine the potatoes, spinach and green peas and mash well. Add the chillies, ginger and powdered spices, besan and mix well.
Apply oil on your hands to prevent the mixture from sticking. Form into roundels and flatten slightly.
Shallow fry until golden brown on both sides.

title: Paneer Schezwan Toast
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add garlic. Saute lightly for a few seconds, until aromatic. Add onion and capsicum. Saute for a minute on high heat.
Add schezwan sauce, paneer and salt. Mix until evenly combined.
Turn off the heat and let it cool slightly. Add coriander leaves and mayonnaise, and mix.
To assemble, take a slice of bread and place a cheese slice on it. Spoon some of the filling onto it. Top it off with some mozzarella cheese and red chilli flakes.
Heat butter in a pan over low heat. Place the bread, cover and toast for 3-4 minutes until the cheese is melted. Serve hot.

title: Parotta
cooking_instructions: In a mixing bowl, add maida, salt, sugar and water.
Combine the flour and mix it to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 15 minutes by continuously folding the dough.
Add 1 tbsp of oil on dough and rest for 60 minutes.
Divide the dough and make individual 2-inch dough balls.
Add 2 tbsp of oil on the dough balls and rest for 30 minutes.
Take a dough ball and flatten as thin as possible by forming a large circle. Apply oil on the spread dough.
Gather rolled dough in one corner and make a spiral. Repeat for all the dough balls.
Roll the spiralled dough using a pin or flatten it into a 3-4 inch circle using hands.
Heat a Tawa, place the flattened parotta on the Tawa. Add oil. Cook on a medium flame for 2 mins and flip. Cook the other side for 2 mins.
By tapping the sides of the parotta right after it is cooked will fluff up the parotta.
Repeat this for all the Parotta. Serve it hot.

title: Chilli Fish
cooking_instructions: Add the fish pieces to a bowl. Add salt, pepper, ginger garlic paste and egg white. Mix it to combine.
Add the cornstarch and mix to form a coating.
Heat oil in a pan and deep-fry on medium heat for 4 minutes, or until it starts to turn golden brown. Take it out of the oil.
Turn up the heat to high. Add the fish back into the oil, and fry for 1 minute. Remove and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan.

Add ginger, garlic and green chilli. Saute for a few seconds until it turns aromatic, onion and capsicum, and saute on high heat for 30 seconds. Mix all the sauces together in a small bowl. Add the prepared sauce mixture to the pan. Add
Add the fried fish. Mix to coat.
Mix the cornstarch and water together. Add the cornstarch slurry, mixing it well once before adding. Heat until it thickens, then add the chopped spring onions.
Serve, garnished with chopped spring onions.

title: Egg Kurma
cooking_instructions: Blend the ingredients for the coconut paste to a fine consistency and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a pan and add the whole spices
Add the sliced onions and saute till they turn golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste, mix it well and cook it for a minute.
Add the masala powders and cook on a medium flame for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook it till it is mashed.
Add water, bring it to a boil.
Add the prepared coconut paste. Mix it well till it combines evenly.
Season the gravy.
Score and add the boiled egg to the gravy. Add coriander leaves and mix it well. Transfer it to a bowl. Garnish it with coriander leaves. Serve it hot with rice, roti, idli or dosa.

title: Toddy Shop Fish Curry
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, mix together the Malabar tamarind and warm water. Allow it to rest for 15 minutes.
In a pan, add coconut oil and crackle mustard seeds, and add fenugreek seeds. Add ginger and garlic and saute for a minute.
Add the shallots, curry leaves and green chilli, and saute until it starts to turn golden brown.
Turn the flame to low. Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder and Kashmiri chilli powder. Saute for a minute.
Add the tamarind water. Increase the heat to medium and bring it to a boil. Add water.
Add the rock salt, cover and cook for 5 minutes. Add the fish, cook for 5 mins and then reduce the flame to low, cook for around 10 minutes, depending on the size of the fish pieces.
Swirl the pot around to mix. Don’t use a spoon or spatula.
Add curry leaves, fenugreek powder and coconut oil. Turn off the heat.
Cover and allow it to rest for at least 2 hours before serving. For best results, serve it the next day.

title: Cookd Mangalore Ghee Roast Potatoes
cooking_instructions:
Wash the potatoes nicely. Heat water in a saucepan, add salt and bring it to a boil. Add the baby potatoes and boil it for 15-20 minutes. Check with a for to see if the potato is cooked through
Strain the potatoes and transfer it to a bowl. Add 1 packet of cookd mangalore ghee roast paste and 1 tbsp of ghee. Mix well till the potatoes are coated with the masala
Air fry the potatoes at 100 degrees for 10 minutes and take it out. Garnish with fried curry leaves and serve it hot

title: Turkey Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the rice for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a big pot, add the whole spices and let it crackle
Add the sliced onions and green chillies and saute it till the onions start to turn golden brown.
Add the mint, and coriander and mix it till aromatic.
Add Kashmiri chilli powder and mix till it becomes nice and red
Add the tomatoes and mix it for 2 minutes.
Add the curd and mix it well and cook till the tomatoes become soft.
Add the turkey and cook it well in the masala for about 10 minutes.
Add water, bring it to a boil.
Add salt, mix it well. Cover and cook the turkey on a medium flame for 40 minutes
Bring the water to a boil, add rice and cook the rice in boiling water for 3 minutes.
Strain it immediately and keep it aside. Reserve a cup of rice water. Once the 40 minutes is up for cooking the turkey, add the par boiled rice to the turkey mixture, and fold it over gently.
Pour ¾  cup of the reserved rice water over the rice and level it.
Cover the pot tightly with silver foil and place the lid and press it down.

Place the pot on a preheated tawa and keep it for dum for 5 minutes on a medium flame and for 10 minutes on a low flame. After 15 minutes, turn off the flame and let the biryani rest for another 5 minutes. And open the pot
Fluff the rice gently. Serve it hot along with raita.

title: Hyderabadi Prawn Biryani
cooking_instructions: In a deep pot, add the prawns and the rest of the ingredients required for the marination. Mix it all together till they combine evenly. Let it marinate for 30 minutes in the same pot.
Keep the pot with the marinated prawns on the stove and cook the prawn for 10 minutes till it lets out water and it comes to a boil.
In another pan, bring water to boil. Add the whole spices, ghee, salt and bring it to a boil.
Add the basmati rice to the boiling water and let it cook for 3 minutes. Strain the rice immediately. Reserve some of the water for later.
Place the prawn pot on a preheated tawa. Layer it with half of the rice, sprinkle coriander, mint, brown onion on top and add a tablespoon of ghee.
Add the second layer of rice, and repeat the same process. Add saffron milk and kewra water
Cover the pot with silver foil, seal the edges. Place a fitting lid on top. Let it cook on a dum for the first five minutes on a high flame and then for 20 minutes on a low flame.
Serve it hot, wth raita.

title: Chicken Hakka Noodles
cooking_instructions: Mix the chicken with all the ingredients until evenly combined. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Fry the chicken for 3-4 minutes. Remove it from the pan and set aside.
In a bowl, beat together eggs with a pinch of salt. Add it to the same pan. Once it starts to solidify, mix it well to scramble. Remove it from the pan and set aside.
Heat another pan or wok until smoking hot. Add oil and then add ginger and garlic followed by all the vegetables. Saute for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and the soy sauce, salt, sugar, vinegar, black pepper powder and MSG. Toss together on high heat for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked chicken and eggs, and toss for another 2 minutes. Finish with chopped spring onions and serve hot.

title: Chicken Frankie
cooking_instructions: Mix the ingredients for the frankie masala and keep it aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add the onions and saute till it turns light brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a minute.
Add the dry powders and cook it for a minute on a low flame.
Add the pureed tomatoes and cook until the oil separates from it.
Add green chillies and mix it well.
Add the chicken and water, mix it well. Let the chicken cook for 10-15 minutes.
Season the chicken, mix it well.
Add the capsicum, coriander leaves and mix it well. Keep the filling aside.
Heat a tawa and cook the chapati to 50% on both sides. Take it off the tawa.

Head oil in the same tawa, add a beaten egg and spread it out evenly. Immediately place the half cooked piece of chapati on top of it and flip it. Let the chapati cook well. Take it off the tawa and place it on a board.
Spread mayonnaise, ketchup and sprinkle some frankie masala on top.
Spoon some of the chicken mixture. Top it off with sliced onions.
Roll it tightly and cover it with butter paper. Serve it hot

title: Kerala Lamb Stew
cooking_instructions: In a pressure cooker, add the mutton cubes with bay leaf, sliced ginger, peppercorns and ¼ tsp of salt. Cook on high flame for 1 whistle, then reduce the flame to low and cook for 10 minutes.
In a pot, heat oil. Add the cardamom and cloves. Then add the sliced onions, slit green chillies and curry leaves. Saute until the onion turns translucent.
Add the 2nd press coconut milk and bring it to a boil. Add the onion, carrot and beans. Season with salt, cover and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the cooked mutton along with the water. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the 1st press coconut milk and turn off the flame as soon as it comes to a boil.

title: Handi Paneer
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a kadai over medium heat. Add the onion and fry until golden brown, stirring regularly. Remove onto a plate lined with tissue paper.
In the same oil, fry cashew on low heat until the colour starts to change. Remove from the oil and set aside.
Grind the fried onion, cashew and curd together into a fine paste. Set aside.
Heat oil in a Handi/earthen pot. Add all the whole spices and stir until aromatic. Add ginger garlic paste and saute for 2 minutes on medium heat.
Add turmeric powder, Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder. Mix for a minute.
Add the tomato puree and salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the onion paste, stir for 2 minutes.
Add water, cover and cook for 5 minutes on low heat.
Add Kasuri methi, ghee, garam masala powder, green chilli and coriander leaves. Mix and add the paneer.
Turn off the heat as soon as it comes to a simmer. Garnish with green chilli, coriander leaves and ginger juliennes. Serve with roti/any Indian bread.

title: Quail Pepper Fry
cooking_instructions: Lightly toast the peppercorn and cumin on medium heat, until it turns aromatic. Grind it into a slightly coarse powder. Set aside.
In a pan, heat gingelly oil and add cinnamon, clove, black peppercorn, cardamom, fennel seeds, dry red chilli, curry leaves and garlic. Saute for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add the shallots and saute until lightly golden brown.
Add the ginger garlic paste and saute for a minute. Add the tomato and salt, and saute until the tomato is softened.
Add red chilli powder, coriander powder and cumin powder. Saute for a minute and then add water. Cook for 4 minutes or until the raw flavour of the masalas disappear.
Add the quail, cover and cook for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Add the prepared pepper powder and mix for 2 minutes.
Stir in the coriander leaves, and serve!

title: Thai Pineapple and Egg Fried Rice
cooking_instructions: Heat Oil in wok, add the beaten egg and scramble till it becomes fluffy.
Add garlic, lemongrass, shallots and red chillies. Saute them for a few seconds on a high flame.
Add the carrot, green peas and toss them for a few seconds on a high flame.
Add the cold rice, toss it till all the ingredients evenly combine. Add soy sauce, salt, pepper and toss it till all the ingredients combine evenly.
Finally add the diced pineapple, toss it for a few seconds on a high flame. Transfer it to a plate, garnish it with spring onion and toasted sesame seeds. Serve it hot.

title: Biryani Kathirikai
cooking_instructions: Dry roast the ingredients for the masala and grind to a fine powder.
Heat oil, add the brinjal and saute for a few mins and set aside.
For the preparation, heat oil in a pot and add the fenugreek and mustard seeds. Add the curry leaves.
Add the onions and ginger garlic paste and saute until light brown.
Add the tomato puree and powdered spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add the masala and water and bring to a boil. Add the salt. Add the tamarind pulp.
Add the brinjal, cover and simmer for 10 mins. Finish with coriander leaves.

title: Tandoori Corn
cooking_instructions: In a pot, add water, salt and corn. Cover and boil for 10 minutes. Once cooked, set aside.
Mix together the ingredients for the marination (except mustard oil and red chilli powder).
For the bright red colour, heat mustard oil in a small pan. Once it is hot, add red chilli powder. Add this to the marinade immediately and mix.
Brush this over the boiled corn.
Place a greased mesh or grill over the stove. Place the corn and cook on medium-low heat until charred on all sides. Keep turning it regularly.
Once done, remove it from the heat. Apply melted butter on it, followed by a sprinkle of chaat masala and coriander leaves.

title: Pachamilagai Mutton Curry
cooking_instructions: In a pressure cooker, heat oil and add cumin and black peppercorn. Add shallots and saute until it turns translucent.
Add ginger garlic paste and green chilli, and saute for a minute.
Add mutton and salt, and saute for 2 minutes.

Add water, cover and pressure cook for 1 whistle on high heat. Reduce the flame to low and cook for 20-25 minutes. Allow the pressure to release, then open. If you want a thicker gravy, you can open the lid and cook until it reaches the desired consistency. Serve hot with Idli/dosa.

title: Masala Egg and Cheese Toast
alternate_titles: Super Easy Masala Egg and Cheese Toast
cooking_instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add the chopped onions, and green chillies and saute for a minute.
Add the dry masala powder and cook them for another minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and saute for a minute
Add the beaten eggs, salt, pepper and coriander leaves. Scramble the eggs till it becomes fluffy. Take it off the flame.
Heat a tawa/pan, Toas one side of the bread, flip it and lower the flame.
Spread some butter on top of the bread, add the scrambled egg and top it off with cheese.

title: Mutton Kheema Samosa
cooking_instructions: Prepare a soft dough with flour, salt, sugar, oil and water. Knead it well and keep it in a bowl covered with dry cloth.
For the filling, heat oil in a kadai, add cumin seeds, chopped garlic and green chillies and let it crackle.
Add the chopped onions and cook it till it’s golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a few seconds.
Add the dry powders and cook them for a few seconds.
Add the minced mutton and mix it well till it is completely coated with the masala.
The mutton will ooze out some water, additionally add some more water and let it cook in it.
Add the seasoning, and cook the mutton dry. Check the taste. Finally Add Chopped Coriander and mix it in.
Take the dough, dust it with flour and roll it out into a thin sheet and cut it into 6 inch rectangles.
Add the mutton mixture on one side of the sheet, apply maida batter on all the sides and fold it into triangles. Repeat the same step for every sheet.

Heat oil in a kadai, deep fry the samosas on a medium flame till they are golden brown and crispy. Take the samosas out using a perforated spoon, draining the excess oil. Transfer it to a plate. Serve it hot along with ketchup or mint chutney.

title: Drums of Heaven
cooking_instructions: Cut the tip of the chicken drumstick. Using a knife, scrape the meat towards one side. Do this for all the drumstick pieces. Marinate the chicken pieces with salt, pepper, Kashmiri chilli powder, soy sauce, vinegar and ginger garlic paste. Refrigerate for 30 minutes at least.
Before frying, add maida and cornflour and mix gently.
Fry on medium heat until it is fully cooked, around 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oil and set aside.
Soak the Kashmiri chillies in hot water for 20 minutes. Grind it into a fine paste along with garlic.
Heat oil in a wok/pan. Add ginger and garlic, saute for 30 seconds.
Add onions and saute for a minute. Add the red chilli paste and cook until the oil starts to float on the sides, around 4-5 minutes.
Add tomato ketchup, soy sauce, black pepper and vinegar. Mix and add the fried chicken.
Add the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken pieces. Serve hot, garnished with spring onions.

title: Kozhi Uppu Kari
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken with all the ingredients. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 20 minutes.
Heat oil in a pot and add the mustard seeds. Once they start to crackle, add the fennel seeds, cinnamon and dry red chillies. Saute for a minute.
Add curry leaves, crushed garlic and shallots. Saute until the shallots begin to turn golden brown.
Add the marinated chicken and mix. Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Open the lid and cook until the remaining moisture has evaporated.
Add black pepper powder and curry leaves. Mix and remove from the heat. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve with any rice dish.

title: Murg Kali Mirch
cooking_instructions: Marinate the chicken with a tbsp of oil, curd, 1 tsp black pepper powder and ¼ tsp pf garam masala powder. Mix well and set aside.
Boil cashewnuts in 1 Cup of water for 5 mins.
Strain and blend to fine paste with ½ Cup of water.
Heat oil a kadhai and add the onion. Cook until translucent.
Add the chopped green chillies and ginger-garlic paste. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add the cumin powder, black pepper powder, garam masala powder, salt and kasuri methi powder. Add ¼ cup of water and cook well.
Add the chicken and mix well.
Add the cashew nut paste, ¼ Cup water. Cover and cook for 8 mins on a medium-low flame.

title: Veg Kizhi Parotta
cooking_instructions: Soak the cashew and poppy seeds in hot water for 10 minutes.
Grind it to a fine paste along with grated coconut. Set aside.
In a pressure cooker, heat oil and add the whole spices, followed by the onion and curry leaves. Saute for 2 minutes.
Add the ginger garlic paste and saute for a minute, followed by the tomato and mint leaves. Mix and add the powdered spices and salt.
Add the potato, carrot, beans and cauliflower. Mix and add lemon juice and the coconut paste.
Give it a stir and then add water. Cover and pressure cook for 2 whistles on medium heat.
Heat oil and add the curry leaves, green chilli and garlic. Saute lightly until aromatic.
Add the mushrooms and mix. Add the powdered spices and salt. Saute for 5 minutes or until it releases moisture and then turns almost dry.
Add the paneer pieces and saute for 2 more minutes.
Add the coriander leaves and mix. Turn off the heat and set aside.
Remove the thick center part of the banana leaf carefully. Heat up the leaves over a direct heat to make it flexible.
In the center, pour some of the salna. Place a parotta followed by more salna. Place some of the paneer & mushroom masala.
Repeat the process again. On top, place a parotta followed by some salna and topped off with chopped onion and coriander leaves.
Cover it with the banana leaf and tie it tightly using some of the banana leaf fiber itself, or using a rope/twine.
Place it on a hot tawa and sprinkle some water around it. Cook for 3 minutes on each side. Open the parcel only while serving.

title: Low-Fat Egg Salad
cooking_instructions: Use the yolks from 2 eggs. Put it into a bowl and mash it. Add the curd, salt, black pepper, garlic, and mixed herbs. Mix well to form the salad dressing.
Chop the egg whites.
Add it to a bowl with all the other ingredients.
Mix it with the dressing until evenly combined. Serve it chilled as it is, or with brown bread.

title: KGF Chicken
cooking_instructions: Add all the ingredients ‘for frying’ to the chicken and mix.
Heat oil and deep fry the chicken on medium-high heat until golden brown and crispy. Remove from the oil and set aside.
In another pan, heat coconut oil and add garlic, red chilli paste, soy sauce and fennel powder. Cook for 3 minutes until the oil starts separating from the sides.
Add the chicken and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, ginger, green chilli and coriander leaves. Toss for a minute and serve as an appetizer.

title: Masala Peanuts
cooking_instructions: In a bowl, add the peanuts. Add salt, Kashmiri chilli powder, cumin powder, asafoetida, ginger garlic paste and mix. Add 1 tbsp of water too, just enough to wet the peanuts. Add besan and rice flour. Mix well to coat evenly, sprinkling water as required.
Heat oil over medium flame. Separate the peanuts and drop them into the oil. Fry until it turns crispy and golden brown. Remove from the oil.
Fry the curry leaves in the same oil. Remove it as soon as it gets crispy, which will only take a few seconds. Set this aside.

In a small bowl, combine together all the ingredients for the spice mix. Add the fried curry leaves also and mix well until evenly combined. Add this to the fried peanuts and toss. Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

title: One Pot Creamy Spring Vegetable Pasta
cooking_instructions: Heat olive oil in a pan, add garlic, saute for a few seconds.
Add the onions and saute till they turn translucent.
Add the carrot, beans and bell peppers, saute them for a few 2-3 minutes.
Add the pasta. Mix it with the vegetables for a minute.

Add water, mix it well and make sure the pasta submerges in the water. Cover and cook it for 8 minutes or until the water almost evaporates. Stirring occasionally. Add the cream and mix it till the pasta is coated evenly. Once the water has almost evaporated, season it with salt, pepper and oregano.
Add the grated cheese, blanched broccoli. Mix it well. Serve it hot.

title: Tomato Chicken
cooking_instructions: Mix the chicken with all the other ingredients for the marination. Marinate for 20 minutes at room temperature (or in the refrigerator if you are marinating for a longer time).
Grind the tomato, garlic, ginger and cardamom into a fine paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add the marinated chicken pieces. Fry for a few minutes on medium-high heat until it is golden brown on all sides. Flip occasionally so that it cooks evenly.
Add the prepared paste and mix. Bring it to a boil. Cover and cook on medium heat for 10-15 minutes until the oil floats on the sides/on top, and the chicken is cooked.
Add mint and a pinch of salt. Serve it with rice/roti, garnished with coriander leaves.

title: Paneer Tikka Biryani
cooking_instructions: Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes
To prepare chilli oil, heat mustard oil to a smoking point, turn off the flame and let it cool down.
To the oil, add kashmiri red chilli powder and mix it well till the oil absorbs the colour. Add besan flour, mix it well and keep it aside.
Prepare the marinade by mixing oil and kashmiri chilli powder first and then add the remaining ingredients required till they combine evenly.
Add the chilli oil to the marinade, mix it well.
Add the paneer cubes to the marinade, mix it till it is coated evenly. Let it marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat water in a pot, add bayleaves, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, ghee and salt to it. Bring it to a boil.
Add the soaked rice and boil it for 3 minutes and strain it immediately
Skewer and cook the paneer over direct fire till charred marks appear.
In a biryani pot, heat oil and ghee, add the whole spices and let it crackle.
Add the sliced onions, green chili and saute till the onions turn golden brown
Add ginger garlic paste and cook it for a minute.
Add mint and coriander leaves, fry the well.
Add kashmiri chilli powder, curd and mix till the onions and oil turn red in colour.
Add water, mix it well and bring it to a boil.
Season the mixture. Reduce the flame.
Start the layering process directly. Add the rice first, then the coriander, mint, fried onion and paneer tikka.
Repeat the process and this time add ghee, kewra water and saffron milk.
Cover the pot with silver foil and close it tightly with a lid.
Keep it for dum, on a high flame for the first 5 minutes and on a low flame for 10 minutes.
Open the pot, fluff the rice and serve it hot.
